PREFACE  序言

THIS book is not meant to be an exhaustive treatise on the aesthetics of the Italian Renaissance. It is intended for the student of Italian painting who may feel that it is not enough to study the concrete works of art left by the painters of that period, but that a fuller comprehension can be gained of these works, and of the different movements in the arts, if we also know what the artists were consciously aiming at. Such knowledge can serve two main purposes: it can often give us a clue to the meaning of tendencies in a form of art which might otherwise be puzzling; and it can be used as a check on the theories which it is only too easy for us to read into the works of art which we have to interpret. If we see a feature in a painting, and then find that it is also set up as an ideal by the theoretical writers of the time, then we are doubly, and even more than doubly, sure that the feature really exists in the painting and is not the creation of our imagination.
本书并非旨在成为关于意大利文艺复兴美学的详尽论著。它面向意大利绘画的学生，后者可能觉得仅仅研究那个时期画家的具体艺术作品还不够，而如果我们也了解艺术家有意识地追求的目标，就能对这些作品及艺术中的不同潮流获得更全面的理解。这类知识有两大主要用途：它常常能为一种艺术形式中看似令人费解的倾向提供线索；同时也可作为对理论的校验，避免我们过于轻易地把自己的理论强加到必须解释的艺术作品上。如果我们在一幅画中看到某一特征，又发现同时代的理论作家也把该特征确立为一种理想，那么我们就能更加确定——甚至超出双重把握——该特征确实存在于画作之中，而非出自我们的想象。
The exact scope of the book should perhaps be defined. It deals with the artistic theory of the Italian Renaissance in its fully developed form, and is therefore primarily concerned with the sixteenth century. No attempt has been made to trace the relation between the theory of the early Quattrocento and that of the Middle Ages, as this subject is one of great complexity and could only be dealt with adequately if a disproportionate amount of space was allowed it. Even the first writers of the Early Renaissance are hardly mentioned, though in some ways they foreshadow theories which later become of importance. Instead Alberti has been chosen as the starting-point, since it is in his writings that a full Humanist doctrine is formulated for the first time, and they are the source from which later ideas mainly derive.
本书的确切范围或许应当加以限定。它处理的是意大利文艺复兴艺术理论的成熟形态，因此主要涉及十六世纪。并未试图追溯早期十五世纪艺术理论与中世纪理论之间的关系，因为这一课题极为复杂，只有给予其不相称的篇幅才能加以充分处理。即便是早期文艺复兴的最初几位作家几乎也未被提及，尽管在某些方面他们预示了后来变得重要的理论。相反，本书以 Alberti 为出发点，因为正是在他的著作中首次完整阐明了人文主义学说，而后来的思想主要源自这些著作。
The last three chapters of the book lead us beyond the Renaissance, in the strictest sense, since they deal with the
本书最后三章将我们带到严格意义上的文艺复兴之外，因为它们讨论了...
theories associated with the movement of Mannerism, which in Italy succeeded the Humanist art of the High Renaissance. But the doctrines of Mannerism form a logical sequel to those of the Renaissance and can conveniently be treated with them. The approximate date of 1600 has been chosen for the upper limit of the book, since after that time the whole character of artistic theory in Italy changes, and an account of it would demand an entirely different treatment, on a far larger scale.
与矫饰主义（Mannerism）运动相关的理论在意大利继承了盛期文艺复兴的人文主义艺术。但矫饰主义的学说在逻辑上是文艺复兴学说的延续，因此可以与之一并论述。本书以上限大致定在 1600 年，因在此之后意大利艺术理论的整体特征发生了变化，若要叙述则需采取完全不同且规模更大的处理方式。
The obligations incurred in the writing of this book are legion. First to the Master and Fellows of Trinity College, Cambridge, for giving me the means, in the form of scholarships and fellowship, to carry out the necessary research; and to the Courtauld Institute of Art, London University, my appointment at which allowed me to finish the work. To the Warburg Institute I also owe practical assistance, but it is overshadowed by a debt of a more spiritual kind. In the process of working with the members of this Institute I have had the inestimable advantage of seeing a really scientific method consistently applied, and any features of this book which are not wholly amateur are due to this example.
在撰写本书过程中所负的恩情不胜枚举。首先感谢剑桥大学三一学院（Trinity College, Cambridge）的院长与研究员们，正是他们通过奖学金与研究金等形式为我提供了开展必要研究的经费；以及伦敦大学考道学院（Courtauld Institute of Art），我在该院的任职使我得以完成此项工作。我亦欠瓦尔堡研究所（Warburg Institute）实际上的帮助，但更重要的是一种精神上的债务。在与该研究所成员共事的过程中，我获得了将真正的科学方法一贯应用的无价优势，本书中任何非完全业余的特点，均归功于此榜样。
To individuals my debts are too wide to be acknowledged adequately. To Mr. A. Gow I owe encouragement and advice at a vital period; to Dr. F. Antal I am indebted for instruction in a method which has, I fear, been applied in an only too slipshod manner in this book and for many ideas on individual points; to Mr. Guy Burgess the stimulus of constant discussion and suggestions on all the more basic points at issue. Dr. Saxl, Dr. Wittkower, Dr. Wind, and Professor Boase have all earned my gratitude by reading either manuscript or proofs and making valuable emendations. Finally I would thank my mother, Miss Margaret Whinney, and Miss Ida Herz for help in the preparation and copying of the manuscript, and my brother and sister-in-law for providing shelter and quiet during the actual writing of the book.
我欠个人的债太多，无法充分表达谢意。对 A. Gow 先生，我在一个关键时期得到他的鼓励和建议；对 F. Antal 医生，我感谢他在一种方法上的指导——我担心这种方法在本书中被应用得过于草率——以及在若干具体问题上提供的许多想法；对 Guy Burgess 先生，则感谢他在所有更为根本的问题上不断讨论并提出建议的激励。Saxl 博士、Wittkower 博士、Wind 博士和 Boase 教授通过阅读手稿或校样并提出有价值的修订，都值得我的感谢。最后我要感谢我的母亲、Margaret Whinney 小姐和 Ida Herz 小姐在准备和抄写手稿时的帮助，以及我的兄弟和弟媳在实际写作期间提供的住所与安静环境。

Chapter I  第一章

Abstract  摘要

ALBERTI

WITH the generation of Brunelleschi, Masaccio, and Donatello in Florence a new ideal of art was realized, which expressed the aspirations of the most progressive minds in Florence at a moment when the city-republic reached a high point in its development. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} As the last remains of Gothic disappear, a style emerges which expresses men’s new approach to the world, their Humanist confidence, and their reliance on the methods of reason. In painting and sculpture naturalism flourished, but a naturalism based on the scientific study of the outside world by means of the new weapons of perspective and anatomy. In architecture the revival of Roman forms was used to create a style which answered to the demands of human reason rather than to the more mystical needs of medieval Catholicism.
随着布鲁内莱斯基、马萨乔和多纳太罗这一代人在佛罗伦萨的出现，实现了一种新的艺术理想，这种理想表达了在城邦共和国达到发展高峰时佛罗伦萨最进步思想者的志向。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 随着哥特式的最后残留消失，出现了一种风格，表达了人们对世界的新观照、他们的人文主义自信以及对理性方法的依赖。在绘画和雕塑中，自然主义蓬勃发展，但这是建立在通过透视和解剖这两种新“武器”对外部世界进行科学研究的自然主义。在建筑上，对罗马形式的复兴被用来创造一种更符合人类理性要求的风格，而不是迎合中世纪天主教更为神秘的需要。

Such a change in the practice of the arts was, of course, accompanied by a similar change in the theories which were held about them. Medieval writers on painting had been predominantly theological in their approach. For them the arts were entirely subject to the direction of the Church; they accepted its general scale of values, which emphasized the spiritual and had no interest in the material; and for this reason they made no demand that artists should imitate the outside world. Their duty was rather to evolve the appropriate symbol to convey the moral and religious lessons of the Church. The painter was a craftsman who performed a practical function under the direction of the Church, and
这种艺术实践的变化当然伴随着对艺术理论的类似变化。中世纪的绘画论著在方法上主要是神学性的。对他们而言，艺术完全受制于教会的指引；他们接受教会的价值体系，该体系强调精神性、对物质没有兴趣；因此他们并不要求艺术家去模仿外部世界。他们的职责反而是设计出恰当的符号以传达教会的道德和宗教教训。画家是一个在教会指示下履行实用功能的工匠，并且

through the organization of the Guilds, like any other kind of craftsman.
通过行会的组织，与其他类型的工匠一样。
The generation of 1420 regarded the arts in a very different spirit. For them painting consisted first and foremost in the rendering of the outside world according to the principles of human reason. Therefore they could no longer acknowledge a theory of the arts which did not allow any place to naturalism or to the scientific study of the material world. The new ideas which they formulated are most fully expressed in the writings of Leon Battista Alberti, whose universal intelligence particularly suited him for expounding a doctrine which affected all branches of human activity-political life, and philosophy, just as much as literature and the arts.
1420 年代的一代人以截然不同的精神看待艺术。对他们来说，绘画首先是按照人的理性原则再现外部世界。因此，他们不再认可那种不容许自然主义或对物质世界进行科学研究的艺术理论。他们所阐述的新思想在 Leon Battista Alberti 的著作中得到了最充分的表达，他的博学多才尤其使他适合阐明一种影响人类各项活动——政治生活与哲学，以及文学和艺术——的学说。
Alberti did not, of course, leap into a wholly unprepared world with a ready-made theory. There had been men before him who had hinted at the doctrines which he was to enunciate with such clarity and completeness. In Cennino Cennini, for instance, we find traces of the new naturalism which was already growing up in the Trecento, and in Lorenzo Ghiberti the new feeling for antiquity makes its appearance. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} But these and the other points of detail which can be traced in writers before Alberti’s time are only indications of what is to come. Their real significance only becomes clear when we consider them in connexion with the whole new view of the arts and of the world as we find it set forth in Alberti.
阿尔伯蒂当然不是带着现成的理论跳入一个完全毫无准备的世界。在他之前已有一些人暗示过他后来以如此清晰和完整阐述的学说。例如在切尼诺·切尼尼（Cennino Cennini）的作品中，我们可以发现已经在十四世纪成长起来的新自然主义的痕迹；在洛伦佐·吉贝尔蒂（Lorenzo Ghiberti）那里，对古代的全新情感也开始显现。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 但这些以及在阿尔伯蒂之前的作家中可追溯到的其他细节，只是对即将到来的事物的提示。只有当我们把它们与阿尔伯蒂所阐述的关于艺术与世界的整套新观点联系起来考虑时，它们的真正意义才变得清晰。
Alberti was the illegitimate son of a Florentine merchant. He was born in 1404 in Genoa, where his father had moved after the decree of exile had been passed on the whole
阿尔伯蒂是佛罗伦萨一位商人的私生子。他于 1404 年出生在热那亚，他的父亲在对整个...颁布放逐法令后迁往那里
Alberti family, one of the richest and most powerful in Florence. He was educated in the north of Italy, principally in Bologna, where he studied Law. He seems to have gone to Florence in 1428, when the ban on his family had been lifted, and the next few years, which must have been of vital importance in his formation, coincided with the end of that period when Florence was dominated by the big merchants, who had achieved a greater power than they had held for nearly a century.
阿尔贝尔蒂家族，是佛罗伦萨最富有、最有权势的家族之一。他在意大利北部接受教育，主要在博洛尼亚学习法律。1428 年家族禁令解除时，他似乎前往了佛罗伦萨，接下来的几年对他的成长至关重要，这一时期恰逢佛罗伦萨由大商人主导的阶段结束，而这些商人所掌握的权力达到了近一个世纪以来的最高点。
The rest of Alberti’s life was spent for the most part either in Florence or following the Papal Court, in which he held a secretarial post from 1432 to 1464. Papal policy was at this period increasingly concentrated on central Italy, and relied largely on the merchant class and its support. The outlook, too, in Papal circles was Humanist in character, so that Alberti found there a similar atmosphere to that of his own city, Florence.
阿尔贝尔蒂其余的大部分生涯要么在佛罗伦萨度过，要么随同教廷行事，他自 1432 年至 1464 年在教廷担任秘书职务。此时教皇的政策越来越集中于意大利中部，并在很大程度上依赖商人阶层及其支持。教廷圈子的思想倾向也具有人文主义特征，因此阿尔贝尔蒂在那里发现了与他故乡佛罗伦萨类似的氛围。
In his width of knowledge, as well as in his rational and scientific approach, Alberti was typical of the early Humanists. He worked apparently with equal ease in the fields of philosophy, science, classical learning, and the arts. He wrote pamphlets or treatises on ethics, love, religion, sociology, law, mathematics, and different branches of the natural sciences. He also wrote verses, and his intimacy with the Classics was so great that two of his own works, a comedy and a dialogue in the manner of Lucian, were accepted as newly discovered writings of the ancients. In the arts, he practised and wrote about painting, sculpture, and architecture. Indeed, his grasp of all forms of learning was so encyclopaedic that he well deserved the praise written by a contemporary copyist in a manuscript of the Trivi: ‘Dic quid tandem nesciverit hic vir?’
在知识的广度以及理性和科学的方法上，Alberti 是早期人文主义者的典型。他在哲学、科学、古典学和艺术等领域显然都能同样自如地工作。他撰写了关于伦理、爱情、宗教、社会学、法律、数学以及自然科学不同分支的小册子或论著。他也写诗，并且他对古典作品的熟悉程度如此之深，以至于他的两部作品——一出喜剧和一篇以卢西安风格写成的对话——曾被当作新近发现的古代著作而被接受。在艺术方面，他实践并撰写了关于绘画、雕塑和建筑的作品。事实上，他对各种学问的掌握如此博洽，以致他完全配得上一位同时代的誊写员在一本 Trivi 手稿里所写的赞誉：‘Dic quid tandem nesciverit hic vir?’
Alberti’s views about the arts are so closely dependent on his general philosophical attitude that it is worth while analysing the latter in some detail. His outlook on life was
Alberti 对艺术的观点与他一般的哲学态度紧密相关，因此值得对后者做一番详细分析。他的人生观是
precisely that of the Humanists of the first half of the fifteenth century, and corresponds to the conception of the city-state as it existed in Florence before the final triumph of Cosimo de’ Medici.
正是十五世纪上半叶人文主义者的观点，与科西莫·德·美第奇最终胜利之前佛罗伦萨所存在的城邦观念相一致。
For Alberti the highest good is the public interest. To this princes and individual citizens are equally bound. The prince must govern in the interests of the citizens, preserve their liberties, and obey the laws of the city, or he becomes a tyrant. Above all the peace of the city must be preserved, and Alberti strongly condemns the factions which arouse civil strife and from which his own family had suffered so much. Those who hold office under the prince must equally seek the general good. The judge, for instance, whose functions Alberti discusses at length, must administer the law with firmness but with moderation and humanity, so that public and private interest may be protected, but so that no greater suffering than is necessary may be inflicted on those who infringe the law. Some of his views on punishment are strangely modern; for though he admits the use of torture as a means of arriving at the truth, he attacks the bad prisons of his time and sets down the principle that prisons are intended to reform, not to destroy, the criminal.
对阿尔伯蒂来说，至高的善是公共利益。为此，君主和普通公民同等负有责任。君主必须为公民的利益而治理，维护他们的自由，并遵守城邦的法律，否则他就会成为暴君。最重要的是必须维护城市的和平，阿尔伯蒂强烈谴责那些引发内乱的党派，这些党派曾让他自己的家族遭受了如此多的苦难。受君主委任的官员同样必须追求公共利益。例如，阿尔伯蒂详尽讨论的法官，必须以坚定但适度和人道的方式执行法律，以便保护公共和私人利益，同时对触犯法律者施加的痛苦不得超过必要。他关于惩罚的某些观点在某种程度上显得颇为现代；虽然他承认使用酷刑作为获取真相的一种手段，但他抨击同时代恶劣的监狱状况，并确立了监狱旨在改造而非毁灭罪犯的原则。
Alberti is not a strict republican. In the fifth book of the treatise on architecture he discusses the different forms of government, and though he approves strongly of the republiccity he does not exclude the idea of government by a prince, provided that he governs in the interests of the city. But when Alberti speaks of the public good, he does not mean the good of some abstract entity, ‘the State’, he means the good of all the individual citizens who make up the State. And he is therefore as much interested in the individual citizen as in the prince or those who govern for the prince.
阿尔伯蒂并非严格意义上的共和主义者。在他的建筑论第五卷中，他讨论了不同的政府形式，尽管他非常赞成共和制，但并不排斥由君主统治的想法，前提是君主以城市的利益为治。可当阿尔伯蒂谈到公共利益时，他并非指某个抽象实体“国家”的利益，而是指组成国家的每一位公民的利益。因此，他对个别公民的关切与对君主或为君主治理者的关切同样重视。
The first aim of the individual is to be a good citizen, that is to say, to serve his fellow-citizens as far as possible. He
个人的首要目标是做一个好公民，也就是说，尽可能为同胞服务。他
can only attain this end by the pursuit of virtue, and it is to methods of acquiring virtue that Alberti devotes most of his purely ethical writings. His rules can be summarized as follows. The individual must seek virtue by the application of the will, by the use of reason, and by following nature. Will supplies the driving force. A man, he says, can achieve as much as he wishes to achieve. But it is only through reason that he can know what he should aim at, and what he should avoid. Finally man must follow nature in the sense that he must know the end for which he was created, and try to attain it; he must discover why nature gave him certain faculties, and develop them, unless he is sure that they are bad. So, for instance, Alberti believes that man must aim at spiritual good and not be bound by the senses and the passions; he must be superior to material things and so be independent of fate. Yet he is strongly opposed to the extreme of Stoicism as represented by the Cynicism of Diogenes, since he finds it contrary to nature. It is inhuman not to be moved by any emotions at all. What man needs is to be moderate in his feelings, and to enjoy the things of this world without being tied to them. In fact, the moderation which is one of the results of following reason is the most significant and often recurring feature of Alberti’s doctrine. It leads to the calm of mind which is for him a necessary condition for the right conduct of life.
只有通过追求美德才能达到这个目的，而阿尔伯蒂在他那些纯伦理著作中主要致力于论述获得美德的方法。他的准则可概括如下。个体必须通过意志的运用、理性的使用以及顺应自然来寻求美德。意志提供推动力。他说，一个人可以实现与他所愿望的相称的成就。但只有通过理性，他才能知道自己应当追求什么，应当避免什么。最后，人必须顺应自然，意即他必须知道自己被创造的目的并努力达成它；他必须弄清自然为何赋予他某些能力并发展这些能力，除非他确知这些能力本身有害。因此，例如，阿尔伯蒂认为人应当以属灵的善为目标，不应被感官和情欲所束缚；人必须超越物质事物，从而不为命运所左右。然而，他强烈反对以第欧根尼的犬儒主义为代表的斯多葛学派极端观点，因为他认为那违背自然。对任何情感全然不动是非人的。 人所需要的是在情感上保持节制，享受世间之物而不为其所累。事实上，节制作为遵循理性的结果之一，是 Alberti 学说中最重要且经常出现的特征。它导致了内心的平静，而这种平静对他而言是正确生活行为的必要条件。
The outstanding characteristic of Alberti’s view of life is this rationalism, based more on ancient philosophy than on the teachings of Catholicism. But this does not imply that he was opposed to Christianity. On the contrary he constantly pays his respects to it, but it is before a curious form of Christianity that he bows, a typical Humanist religion in which elements of pagan and classical philosophy blend without any difficulty with Christian dogmas, in which churches are referred to as ‘Temples’ and in which sometimes ‘the gods’, in the plural, seem to receive as much
Alberti 人生观的突出特征是这种理性主义，更多地基于古代哲学而非天主教教义。但这并不意味着他反对基督教。相反，他不断向基督教致敬，不过他所敬仰的是一种奇特形式的基督教——一种典型的人文主义宗教，在这种宗教中，异教与古典哲学的元素可以毫不费力地与基督教教条融合，其中教堂被称为“Temple”，有时复数形式的“the gods”似乎也同样获得了敬重
honour as the Christian God. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} With this humanized religion Alberti feels himself entirely at home, but he will not give up his right to individual judgement on every matter. Even the ancients, for whom he has a deeper reverence than for any other persons, human or divine, he treats on a level and does not feel himself obliged to follow either their precept or their example if his own judgement tells him otherwise.
对基督之神的尊崇。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 有了这种被人性化的宗教，Alberti 感到完全适应，但他不会放弃在每一件事上作出个人判断的权利。即使是那些古人——他对他们的敬重超过对任何其他人，不论凡人或神祇——他也把他们置于平等地位；当他自己的判断与他们的教诲或榜样相悖时，他并不觉得有义务去遵从。
We shall find many of Alberti’s ideas on these general philosophical and political subjects reflected in his theoretical writings in the aesthetic field, but before we go on to them we must consider the actual works which he left behind him in the arts. In painting and sculpture nothing survives from his hand, but in architecture his contribution is considerable. His position is that of a younger member of the group which, under the leadership of Brunelleschi, dominated Florence at the time of his return there in 1428. He carried on their work and developed many of their principles a stage further.
我们会在他关于审美领域的理论著作中发现许多关于这些一般哲学和政治问题的观点有所反映，但在继续讨论这些著作之前，我们必须考虑他在艺术上留下的实际作品。在绘画和雕塑方面，他的手笔没有流传下来，但在建筑学上他的贡献相当可观。他的地位是属于那一代较年轻成员，这一群体在他 1428 年回到佛罗伦萨时由 Brunelleschi 领导并主导着佛罗伦萨。他继承了他们的工作，并将他们的许多原则进一步发展了一个阶段。
Alberti was a more fully self-conscious classicist than Brunelleschi and his contemporaries. He was more learned in the study of antiquity than they, more scientific in his application of the archaeological knowledge which he had acquired. In architecture he eliminates the last traces of Gothic, which were still so evident in Brunelleschi, especially in the dome of the cathedral. He was far more scrupulous in his treatment of the orders (cf. Plate I); and in the Plaazzo Rucellai he adapted them for use on a façade of more than one story, by using a single order for each-a method which was later universally adopted. In other ways he carried on the tradition of clear design which was an essential feature of Brunelleschi’s work. His design for S. Sebastiano at Mantua is perhaps the most mature centralized church plan of the time, and his S. Andrea, in the same town, was the last word in lucid spacing of the Latin Cross church. The
阿尔贝蒂比布鲁内莱斯基及其同时代人更具有自觉的古典主义倾向。他在古代研究方面比他们更博学，在应用他所获得的考古学知识时也更为科学。在建筑上，他消除了哥特式的最后痕迹——这些痕迹在布鲁内莱斯基身上仍然很明显，尤其是在大教堂的穹顶中。他在处理柱式时更加谨慎（参见图版 I）；在 Rucellai 宫他将柱式用于多层立面时采用了为每层使用单一柱式的做法——这一方法后来被普遍采用。在其他方面，他延续了布鲁内莱斯基作品中那种清晰设计的传统。他为曼图亚设计的圣塞巴斯蒂亚诺教堂或许是当时最成熟的集中式教堂平面，而同城的圣安德烈亚教堂则是在拉丁十字教堂的明朗空间处理方面的最后定论。


O
latter was of dominant importance in church design for several centuries.
后者在几个世纪的教堂设计中占有主导地位。
His theoretical ideas on the arts are to be found principally in three works. The earliest is the treatise on painting, Della Pittura di Leon Battista Alberti Libri tre, written in 1436 probably in Latin, but translated by Alberti himself for Brunelleschi’s benefit into Italian. The second and the most considerable of the treatises consists of the ten books of architecture, De Re Aedificatoria, which Alberti began probably about 1450, but to which he went on making additions and alterations till the time of his death in 1472 . The last work is the pamphlet on sculpture, De Statua, written probably shortly before 1464.
他关于艺术的理论思想主要见于三部著作。最早的是关于绘画的论文《Della Pittura di Leon Battista Alberti Libri tre》，作于 1436 年，可能最初以拉丁文写成，但由 Alberti 本人为布鲁内莱斯基的利益将其译成意大利文。第二部且最重要的论文是十卷的建筑著作《De Re Aedificatoria》，Alberti 可能始于约 1450 年，但他不断对其加以增补和修改，直至 1472 年去世。最后一部作品是关于雕塑的短文《De Statua》，大概写于 1464 年之前不久。
Since architecture is the art most closely connected with the practical needs of man, it is in Alberti’s architectural theories that his general social ideas are most visibly reflected. He thinks of architecture entirely as a civic activity. In the preface to his treatise, which is a sort of apologia for architecture, he speaks above all of the glory which it brings to the city, in utility and in ornament. Architecture serves commerce, of which, as we should expect, Alberti speaks in the highest terms; it enables the city to defend itself against its enemies, and, by inventing aggressive machines of war, even helps it to extend its dominion. From architecture the city derives its splendid public buildings, its private houses, and the monuments which keep alive the memory of its great men.
由于建筑与人的实际需要关系最为密切，因此阿尔伯蒂的建筑理论最明显地反映了他的一般社会思想。他把建筑完全视为一项城公共活动。在他那部可被看作是为建筑辩护的论文的前言中，他首先谈到的是建筑为城市带来的荣耀，无论在实用性还是装饰性方面。建筑服务于商业，正如我们所料，阿尔伯蒂对商业给予了极高的评价；建筑使城市能够抵御敌人，并且通过发明进攻性的战争机器，甚至帮助城市扩展其统治权。城市从建筑中获得壮丽的公共建筑、私人住宅以及那些使其伟人记忆得以延续的纪念物。
It is the principles of such a civil architecture that Alberti expounds in his treatise, not an architecture for private patrons or ecclesiastical purposes only, though, of course, the needs of both the individual and the Church are carefully considered. The novelty in his method is that he proposes a scheme for the building of an entire town, and every detail in his suggestions is made subordinate to the main design of the town as a whole.
阿尔伯提在他的论述中阐述的正是这种市政建筑的原则，而不是仅为私人委托人或教会用途而建的建筑，尽管当然个人和教会的需求都被仔细考虑。他的方法新颖之处在于他提出了整个城镇建造的方案，他建议中的每一项细节都从属于城镇总体设计的主旨。
The first three books of the treatise are given up to purely
论述的前三卷完全献给纯粹的
technical matters; the first to the use of drawings in architecture, the second to the choice of materials, and the third to the principles of structure. After this preliminary Alberti attacks at once the problems which concern the town as a whole, first of all the question of its site. This must be healthy, in a temperate climate, conveniently placed for water-supply, easy to defend, and so on. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Next it must be clearly laid out, with good main streets conveniently connected with the bridges and gates of the town. The streets must be wide enough not to be congested but not so wide as to be too hot. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Moreover, Alberti proposes that if possible the streets shall be so designed that symmetry may reign between the houses on the two sides of the street, and that a standard design may be repeated for a whole street 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} (Plate 2). This is a piece of large-scale planning which reveals Alberti’s astonishing civic-mindedness, for this suggestion was not put into general practice till the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, when town life had reached a far more advanced stage of development. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} It is in marked contrast to the medieval method of town planning, against which Alberti explicitly protests, according to which each family built a palace and a tower without any consideration of its neighbours, except one of rivalry. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
技术问题；第一是关于在建筑中使用图纸，第二是关于材料选择，第三是关于结构原理。在这一初步论述之后，Alberti 立刻着手处理有关整个城镇的问题，首先是选址问题。选址必须健康，气候温和，便于供水，易于防守，等等。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 其次，城镇必须有明确的布局，主街要宽阔并与城镇的桥梁和城门方便地相连。街道必须足够宽以避免拥堵，但又不能宽得令人感到过于闷热。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 此外，Alberti 建议如果可能的话，街道应当这样设计，使得街道两侧房屋之间保持对称，并且整条街可以重复采用统一的标准设计 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} （图版 2）。这是一个大尺度的规划方案，显示出 Alberti 令人惊讶的公民意识，因为这一建议直到十七、十八世纪才被普遍采纳，那时城镇生活已发展到更为高级的阶段。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 这与中世纪的城镇规划方式形成鲜明对比，Alberti 明确反对那种规划方式；在那种方式下，每个家庭都建造自己的宫殿和塔楼，除了出于竞争之外，完全不考虑邻居。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
Figure 1: Design for a market place. From Alberti's De Re Aedificatoria, 1550
图 1：集市广场设计。摘自 Alberti 的 De Re Aedificatoria，1550
Having thus settled the questions which affect the whole layout of the town, Alberti proceeds to consider the different kinds of buildings which are to be put up in it. He divides these into three groups: public buildings, the houses of the important citizens, and the houses of the people. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Over the first type he is very thorough and gives the fullest details about the planning and construction of squares, towers, bridges, halls of justice, churches, and theatres, which must all be carried out with the greatest possible splendour as befits the dignity of the city. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The houses of the leading citizens must also be dignified, but they must avoid all ostentation, and rely more on beauty of design and convenience of disposition than on size or ornament. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Otherwise they will arouse the envy of their neighbours, and the harmony of the whole design will be disturbed. The houses of the poorer citizens should be built on the same scheme as those of the richer, but in a smaller and more modest manner, so that the difference between the positions of the richer and poorer citizens will not be too strongly marked. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} In each of these cases Alberti gives fairly complete rules for the buildings which he proposes, so that the same principles appear in each detail as in the whole scheme of the town.
在这样解决了影响全镇总体布局的问题之后，Alberti 开始考虑要在镇上兴建的不同类型的建筑。他将这些建筑分为三类：公共建筑、重要市民的住宅以及平民的住宅。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 对于第一类，他非常详细，提供了关于广场、塔楼、桥梁、法庭大楼、教堂和剧院的规划与建造的最详尽细节——这些都必须以尽可能的宏伟来实施，以符合城市的尊严。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 主要市民的住宅也必须庄重，但应避免一切炫耀，更多依靠设计之美和布局的便利，而不是依靠规模或装饰。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 否则，它们会引起邻居的嫉妒，并破坏整体设计的和谐。较贫穷市民的住宅应按与富人相同的方案建造，但规模更小、更加朴素，以使富民与穷民之间的差异不过于明显。 在这些情况下，Alberti 都为他所提议的建筑给出了相当完整的规则，因而在每一细节中都出现与城镇整体方案相同的原则。
In Alberti’s other writings on the arts his social and ethical views are not so clearly reflected, but in all of them we find the spirit of rational Humanism which is characteristic of his philosophical works.
在 Alberti 关于艺术的其他著作中，他的社会与伦理观并没有如此清楚地反映出来，但在所有这些著作中我们都能发现理性人文主义的精神，这正是其哲学著作的特征。
Certain of his predecessors, such as Cennini and Ghiberti,
他的若干前辈，如 Cennini 和 Ghiberti，
had maintained that the artist was an independent individual, who needed to be acquainted with the liberal arts, and no one could have carried out this principle more thoroughly in practice than Alberti. His conception of the architect appears most clearly in the definition which he gives in the preface to the book on architecture:
他主张艺术家是一个独立的个体，须熟悉文科诸学，而在实践中没有人比 Alberti 更彻底地贯彻了这一原则。他对建筑师的概念在他为《建筑论》一书所作序言中的定义中最为清晰地显现：
‘Before I go any further I think it will be convenient to say whom exactly I mean to call an architect; for I will not set up before you a carpenter and ask you to regard him as the equal of men deeply versed in the other sciences, though it is true that the man who works with his hands serves as an instrument for the architect. I will call an architect one who, with a sure and marvellous reason and rule, knows first how to divide things with his mind and intelligence, secondly how rightly to put together in the carrying out of the work all those materials which, by the movements of weights and the conjoining and heaping up of bodies, may serve successfully and with dignity the needs of man. And in the carrying out of this task he will have need of the best and most excellent knowledge.’
“在我继续之前，认为有必要确切地说明我所谓的建筑师为何人；因为我不会在你们面前举起一个木匠并要求你们视他与那些深谙其他学科之人相提并论，尽管确实从事体力劳动的人在建筑师手下担任工具的角色。我称建筑师为这样的人：他以确定而奇妙的理性与规矩，首先知道如何用心智与智慧来划分事物；其次知道在施工中如何恰当地组合所有那些材料，这些材料通过重量的作用以及体块的结合与堆叠，能够成功且有尊严地服务于人的需要。在完成此任务时，他将需要最良好且最卓越的知识。”
He is less elaborate in his definition of the painter, but here again he wishes him to be acquainted with all the forms of knowledge which are relevant to his art, particularly history, poetry, and mathematics. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
他在对画家的定义上不那么详尽，但在这里他仍希望画家熟知与其艺术相关的所有知识形式，尤其是历史、诗歌和数学。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
This is the most complete definition of the artist as a man engaged in a scientific occupation that can be found in the Early Renaissance; and this conception runs through the whole of Alberti’s writings. Each of the treatises on the arts begins with a statement of the scientific basis of the art in question. In the case of architecture, for instance, the first book is mainly given up to the importance of drawings, which Alberti regards as the link between architecture and mathematics. The second deals with the knowledge of the materials necessary to building, and the third to methods of construc-
这是早期文艺复兴时期关于艺术家作为从事科学性职业之人的最完整定义；这种观念贯穿于 Alberti 的全部著作。每一部关于诸艺术的论文都以阐明该艺术的科学基础开始。例如在建筑学方面，第一卷主要论述图纸的重要性，Alberti 认为图纸是建筑与数学之间的联系。第二卷处理建造所需材料的知识，第三卷则论述构造的方法。
tion. These three books cover the two aspects of the scientific study of architecture-first the purely theoretical and then the technical. In the treatise on painting the first book is devoted to mathematics and to the application of geometry to painting in the form of perspective.
这三卷涵盖了建筑科学研究的两个方面——首先是纯理论，其次是技术。在关于绘画的论文中，第一卷专注于数学以及以透视形式将几何应用于绘画。
On this solid foundation of science Alberti builds up a structure of the arts which is no less scientific. ‘The arts’, he says, 'are learnt by reason and method; they are mastered by practice, ’ 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and this could almost be taken as the motto of the book. According to him the artist must grasp the fundamental principles of his art by means of reason; he must study the best works that have been produced by other artists before his time; and by this means he will be able to formulate precepts about the practice of the arts, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} which, however, must always be combined with practical experience.
在这一坚实的科学基础上，Alberti 构建起一个同样科学的艺术体系。“艺术，”他说，“以理性与方法来学习；以实践来掌握，” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这几乎可以作为本书的座右铭。依他看来，艺术家必须通过理性把握其艺术的基本原则；必须学习在他之前由其他艺术家所创造的最佳作品；通过这种方式他将能够制定关于艺术实践的准则， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 但这些准则必须始终与实践经验相结合。
Alberti’s scientific approach is only part of his general Humanism, for science is the finest fruit of the application of human reason to the study of the world. There is hardly a trace in him of the theological preoccupations which dominated the thought of medieval writers. His definitions of the arts do not include any reference to religion and are entirely framed in human terms. In the case of architecture he does not talk of its use in the service of the Church, except by the way. His basic proposition is that ‘Buildings have been made because of men’, and he develops this idea by saying that buildings are made either to satisfy the needs of life or for the convenience of men’s occupations, or for their delight. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} His attitude towards painting is the same. For him history painting, i.e. subject painting of any kind, as opposed to that of single figures, is the noblest kind of painting, partly because it is the most difficult genre and one which demands proficiency in all the others, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} but also because
阿尔伯蒂的科学方法只是他总体人文主义的一部分，因为科学是将人的理性应用于研究世界所结出的最美好的果实。他几乎没有表现出中世纪作家那种以神学为中心的忧虑。他对艺术的定义不包含任何关于宗教的参照，完全以人的角度来表述。就建筑而言，他并不谈论建筑为教会服务的用途，至多只是顺带提及。他的基本命题是“建筑是为了人而造”，并通过指出建筑要么为满足生活需要，要么为便于人们的职业活动，要么为取悦人们来阐述这一思想。他对绘画的态度也是如此。对他来说，史诗画，即任何题材的叙事绘画，与单独人物像相对，是最高贵的绘画类型，部分原因是它是最难的流派，需要在其他所有流派上都具备娴熟的技艺，但也因为
it gives a picture of the activities of man, like a written history. ‘And I may well stand looking at a picture . . . with no less delight to my mind than if I was reading a good history; for both are painters, one painting with words and the other with the brush.’ 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} A history painting affects the spectator deeply because the emotions which he sees represented in it will be stirred in him; he will laugh, cry, or shiver according as those in the painting show joy, sorrow, or fear. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} For this reason Alberti attributes great importance to the ability of the painter to explain an action and to render the emotions by means of gesture and by the expression of the face. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
它描绘了人的活动，就像一部书面史。“我观看一幅画时，也许会像读一本好史书一样，心中生出同样的愉悦；因为两者都是画家，一个用文字作画，另一个用画笔作画。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 一幅历史画能深深打动观者，因为画中所呈现的情感会在观者心中被激起；观者会随画中人物表现出的欢乐、悲伤或恐惧而笑、哭或颤栗。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 因此，Alberti 非常重视画家解释一个动作的能力，以及通过手势和面部表情来渲染情感的技巧。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
In the arts as in all other fields this Humanism is combined with a strong admiration for classical antiquity. Ghiberti had expressed his admiration for the ancients in general terms and quoted them often, but he had not the absolute cult for them which characterizes Alberti. It has already been said that in style Alberti’s actual buildings are more strictly in accordance with the practice of ancient Roman architecture than any works of his predecessors, and in his theoretical writings we find the same spirit. The ancients appear at every turn. The picture which he gives of the ideal town is almost entirely made up of elements taken from antiquity. 'The models which he quotes for the buildings, public or private, are almost always those that he has seen in Rome or read about in ancient writers; and the authorities to whom he refers for any method which he recommends are the historians and philosophers of Greece and Rome. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
在艺术上与其他所有领域一样，这种人文主义与对古典古代的强烈钦佩相结合。Ghiberti 曾以笼统的方式表达他对古人的钦佩并经常引用他们，但他并不具有那种标志着 Alberti 的对古人的绝对崇拜。前面已说过，就风格而言，Alberti 的实际建筑比他的任何前辈的作品都更严格地遵循古罗马建筑的做法，在他的理论著作中我们也发现了同样的精神。古人处处可见。他所描绘的理想城几乎完全由取自古代的元素构成。“他为公共或私人建筑所引用的范例几乎总是他在罗马见过的或在古代著作中读到的；而他在推荐任何方法时所引用的权威则是希腊和罗马的历史学家与哲学家。” 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
We can see from his descriptions that he had an intimate knowledge of the remains of ancient architecture in Italy,
从他的描述中我们可以看出他对意大利古代建筑遗迹有深入的了解，
and that he had studied them first of all from the point of view of structure and planning. He wished to understand the real principles of Roman architecture, not merely to be able to produce a building which looked classical on the outside but underneath was Gothic in design. This does not, however, mean that he neglected the question of ornament and decoration, and one of the most typical features of the treatise is that it contains the first exposition of the use of the Five Orders in Italy since classical times. Brunelleschi and his contemporaries had used them in their buildings, but always with great freedom, and there was evidently no recognized canon for the proportions of their different parts. Compared with later theoretical treatments of the orders Alberti’s seems simple and cursory, but it gave a new foundation for their correct use.
并且他首先从结构和布局的角度研究了它们。他希望理解罗马建筑的真实原则，而不仅仅是能够建造一座外表古典但内部在设计上却是哥特式的建筑。然而，这并不意味着他忽视了装饰和陈设的问题，该论文的一个最典型特征是，它包含了自古典时代以来意大利对五柱式使用的首次阐述。布鲁内莱斯基及其同时代人在他们的建筑中使用过五柱式，但总是非常随意，明显没有对其各部分比例的公认规范。与后来的关于柱式的理论论述相比，阿尔伯蒂的论述显得简洁而粗略，但它为柱式的正确使用奠定了新的基础。
But though Alberti was possessed of a really extensive and first-hand knowledge of ancient architecture, he was never either pedantic or slavish in his application of it. He considers the ancients as the best models, but he never encourages the modern architect to imitate them blindly. On the contrary, he advises him to try always to introduce into his designs something entirely of his own invention. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} He says that he found the information supplied by Vitruvius of great use, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} but he is far from setting him up as the final authority. In fact in one place he speaks of him with very little respect, complaining that his style is so obscure and confused that it is almost impossible to understand what he means. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} In this as in all other matters, therefore, Alberti reserves the right to judge every problem which comes before him on its own merits.
尽管 Alberti 对古代建筑有着真正广泛且第一手的了解，但在运用这些知识时他从未显得迂腐或盲从。他把古人为最佳范本，但从不鼓励现代建筑师盲目模仿他们。相反，他建议建筑师在设计中始终尽力加入完全由自己发明的元素。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 他说自己发现 Vitruvius 提供的信息非常有用， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 但他远非把他视为最终权威。事实上在某处他对 Vitruvius 的评价颇为轻蔑，抱怨他的文体晦涩混乱，以致几乎无法理解其本意。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 因此在此事以及其他所有问题上，Alberti 都保留根据各案自身优劣独立判断的权利。
The rational and scientific method which, as we have seen,
正如我们已见，那种理性和科学的方法
Alberti pursues in architecture appears in connexion with painting and sculpture in the form of a new conception of realism. The core of his views about the representational arts is to be found in his theory of the imitation of nature, and it is here that his realism can be most clearly traced.
阿尔伯蒂在建筑学上的追求与绘画和雕塑相联系，表现为一种新的写实观念。他关于再现艺术的观点核心在于他的自然模仿理论，而正是在这里可以最清楚地追溯到他的写实主义。
In certain contexts he defines painting in terms of an absolutely unqualified naturalism: ‘The function of the painter is to render with lines and colours, on a given panel or wall, the visible surface of any body, so that at a certain distance and from a certain position it appears in relief and just like the body itself.’ ′ ′ ^('){ }^{\prime} But on other occasions he is more scientific and defines painting as the imitation of a section of the pyramid which any body subtends at the eye of an observer. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} He even invented a device for recording the appearance of such a section, namely, a net which the painter held between himself and the object to be painted, and on which he could trace exactly the outlines which appeared through it. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} This idea of the pyramid leading from the object seen to the eye is the foundation of linear perspective, so that Alberti’s net is only a method for recording the correct view of an object according to linear perspective; it has, however, the disadvantage that it can only be applied to scenes which are visible to the eye. When the painter came to construct compositions of things which he had not actually seen, he had need of a more efficient device, and this was supplied by the full theory of perspective which Alberti expounds in the first two books of his treatise on painting.
在某些语境下，他把绘画绝对地、不加限制地定义为自然主义：“画家的职能是在给定的画板或墙面上用线条和色彩描绘任何机身的可见表面，使之在一定距离和一定位置看起来有浮雕感，宛如物体本身。” ′ ′ ^('){ }^{\prime} 但在其他场合他更为科学，将绘画定义为对任何物体在观察者眼中所张示的金字塔截面的模仿。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 他甚至发明了一种记录此类截面外观的装置，即画家将一张网置于自己和待画物体之间，通过网可以准确描绘出透过网看到的轮廓。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 由物体朝向眼睛的金字塔这一构想是线性透视的基础，因此 Alberti 的网只是根据线性透视记录物体正确视图的一种方法；然而它的缺点是只能用于肉眼可见的场景。 当画家要构建他并未亲眼见过的事物的构图时，他需要一种更有效的装置，而这是由阿尔伯蒂在他的《论绘画》前两卷中阐述的完整透视理论所提供的。
But though the exact imitation of nature is the first function of painting it has another and more important duty. The painter must make his work beautiful as well as accurate, and beauty does not necessarily follow from exactness of imitation as Alberti shows by the example of the ancient painter Demetrius, ‘who failed to obtain the highest praise, because he paid much more attention to making paintings which were true to nature than to making them beautiful’. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Beauty, therefore, is a quality which is not necessarily inherent in all natural objects, though nature is the only source from which the artist can derive it. The artist, therefore, must not use nature indiscriminately: ‘We must always take what we paint from nature and always choose from it the most beautiful things.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} This process of selection is essential because ‘it is very rarely granted even to Nature herself to produce anything absolutely perfect in every part’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
但尽管对自然的准确模仿是绘画的首要职能，它还有另一项更重要的职责。画家必须使他的作品既准确又优美，而美并不必然由模仿的精确性产生，正如阿尔伯蒂通过古代画家德米特里乌斯的例子所示：“他未能获得最高的赞誉，因为他过于注重创作忠于自然的画作，而不是使它们变得优美。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 因此，美是一种不一定内在于所有自然物的品质，尽管自然是艺术家可以从中汲取美的唯一来源。因此，艺术家不得不对自然加以不加区分地使用：“我们必须始终以自然为绘画的取材，并总是从中选择最美的事物。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 这一选择过程是必要的，因为“即便是自然自身也很少被赋予在各部分都绝对完美的产物。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Alberti does not explicitly define and describe this beauty which is not attainable in art by mere imitation. In the treatise on painting he does not pursue the matter, but evidently assumes that his readers will know beauty when they see it. In the later and much more elaborate De Re Aedificatoria he gives two definitions of beauty which are roughly those to be found in Vitruvius. In one case he describes beauty as ‘a certain regular harmony of all the parts of a thing of such a kind that nothing could be added or taken away or altered without making it less pleasing’. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} In the second definition he says: 'Beauty is a kind of harmony and concord of all the parts to form a whole which is constructed according to a fixed number, and a certain relation and order, as symmetry, the highest and most perfect law of nature, demands. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Perhaps more important is another
阿尔伯蒂并未明确定义和描述这种仅凭模仿无法在艺术中达到的美。在他的《论绘画》中，他并未深入探讨此问题，但显然假定读者看到时会认识到美。在后来更为详尽的《建筑论》中，他给出了两个大体上与维特鲁威斯相似的美的定义。在一种情况下，他将美描述为“某物的所有部分之间的一种规则和谐，以至于不能增减或改变任何部分，否则便会使其不那么令人愉悦”。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 在第二个定义中，他说：“美是一种各部分的和谐与一致，使之构成一个整体，该整体按一定的数目、某种关系与秩序构造，正如对称——自然的至高无上和最完美的法则——所要求的。” 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 也许更重要的是另一个观点
passage in the same treatise in which he expands the idea, again with reference to architecture:
在同一篇论著中，他在引用建筑时再次扩展了这一思想的段落：
'What pleases us in the most beautiful and lovely things springs either from a rational inspiration of the mind, or from the hand of the artist or is produced by nature from materials. The business of the mind is the choice, division, ordering and things of that kind, which give dignity to the work. The business of the human hand is the collecting, adding, taking away, outlining, careful working and things of that kind, which give grace to the work. From nature things acquire heaviness, lightness, thickness and purity." 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
“在最美丽可爱之物中使我们感到愉悦的，或源于心灵的理性启发，或出自艺术家的手，或由自然以材料生成。心灵的工作是选择、划分、排列及此类能赋予作品尊严的事物。人手的工作是收集、增减、描绘、精细加工及此类能赋予作品优雅的事物。事物从自然获得沉重、轻盈、厚度与纯净。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
We may suppose, I think, that Alberti would admit a parallel view of painting in which the mind controlled the disposition, the hand contributed skill in technique, and nature added richness of material; though from what he says elsewhere about those who waste their time using gold and rich colours in painting and pay little attention to skill in using them, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} it seems probable that, unlike medieval artists, he attributed small importance to the part which nature plays in painting by supplying good materials.
我想，我们可以假定阿尔伯蒂会承认对绘画有类似的看法：心灵控制构图，之手在技法上贡献技能，自然增添材料的丰富；不过从他在别处对那些在绘画中挥霍金粉与艳丽色彩却很少注意使用技艺的人所说的话来看， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 与中世纪艺术家不同，他很可能认为自然通过提供良好材料在绘画中所起的作用并不重要。
Alberti considers that beauty gives pleasure to the eye, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and it is partly by this means that we can recognize it. But he does not identify the recognition of beauty with this feeling. In the treatise on architecture he explicitly distinguishes between the two processes of liking a thing and judging it to be beautiful. He is talking of people’s tastes in women, how some prefer them fat, others thin, others medium:
阿尔伯蒂认为美使眼睛愉悦， 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 我们部分通过这种方式来识别它。但他并不把对美的识别等同于这种感受。在《论建筑》一书中他明确区分了喜欢某物与判断其为美之间的两种过程。他在谈论人们对女性的品味，有些人偏爱丰满的，有些偏爱瘦的，有些偏爱中等的：
'But, because you like one kind or another more, will you maintain that the others are not noble and beautiful in form? Certainly not. That you liked this particular woman depends on some cause, but what that cause is I will not try to discover. But when you judge about beauty, that does not depend on mere
“但因为你更喜欢这一种或那一种，你就会坚持认为其他的在形体上不高贵、不美丽吗？当然不会。你喜欢这个具体的女人有某种原因，但那原因是什么我不会试图去发现。但当你对美作判断时，那并不依赖于单纯的
opinion but on a certain judgement innate in our minds’ (animis innata quaedam ratio). 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
观点而非基于某种根植于我们心灵的判断（animis innata quaedam ratio）。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
And elsewhere he differentiates between personal taste and the judgement that a thing is beautiful:
而在别处他区分了个人品味与认为某物美的判断：
‘Many . . . say that our ideas of beauty and architecture are wholly false, maintaining that the forms of buildings are various and changeable according to the taste of each individual and not dependent on any rules of art. This is a common error of ignorance, to maintain that what it does not know does not exist.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
“许多人……认为我们对美与建筑的观念完全错误，主张建筑的形式多样且随各人品味而变化，并不依赖任何艺术法则。这是一种无知的常见错误，断言它所不知者不存在。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
All this can be summed up by saying that Alberti believes that man recognizes beauty not by mere taste, which is entirely personal and variable and judges of attractiveness, but by a rational faculty which is common to all men and leads to a general agreement about which works of art are beautiful. Beauty, in fact, is detected by a faculty of artistic judgement.
这一切可归结为：Alberti 认为人并非凭借纯粹的品味来识别美——品味完全个人化且可变，只判断吸引力——而是凭借一种人人共有的理性能力，从而达成关于哪些艺术作品是美的普遍共识。事实上，美是由一种艺术判断能力所识别的。
The artist must take pains to introduce as much of the beautiful and as little of the ugly as possible into his paintings. First of all he must cover up or leave out any imperfections in his model; and this concealing of flaws is said by Alberti to be the particular function of ornament. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} In the next stage the artist must carefully select from the various models before him all the most beautiful parts in order to combine them into a single faultless whole: ‘He must take from all the beautiful bodies those parts which are particularly praised… which will be difficult because perfect beauty is never to be found in any one body but is scattered and dispersed in many different bodies.’ 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
艺术家必须尽力在他的画作中尽可能多地引入美的因素、尽可能少地引入丑的因素。首先他必须遮盖或省略模特身上的任何缺陷；Alberti 说这种掩饰瑕疵正是装饰的特殊功能。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 在下一阶段，艺术家必须从眼前各种模特中小心挑选出所有最美的部位，以便将它们组合成一个无瑕的整体：“他必须从所有美丽的身体中取出那些特别受赞誉的部位……这将是困难的，因为完美的美从来不会出现在任何一个身体中，而是散布并分散在许多不同的身体中。” 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
In the book on sculpture this theory is further developed. The book ends with a table of the proportions of a man, which is prefaced with the following passage:
在关于雕塑的那本书中，这一理论得到了进一步的发展。该书以一张人的比例表结束，表之前有如下引言：
'We have taken the trouble to set down the principal measure-
“我们费了心思记录下主要的度量——”
ments of a man. We did not, however, choose this or that single body, but as far as possible we have tried to note and set down in writing the highest beauty scattered, as if in calculated portions, among many bodies. . . . We have chosen a number of bodies considered by the skilful to be the most beautiful and have taken the dimensions of each of these. These we compared together, and leaving aside the extreme measurements which were below or above certain limits, we chose out those which the agreement of many cases showed to be the average." 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
我们没有选择这一具或那一具单独的身体，而是在尽可能的范围内，努力记录并写下散布在多个人体之间、仿佛被划分成可计算部分的最高美……我们选择了若干被技艺高超者认为最美的身体，并测量了每一具的尺寸。我们将这些相互比较，撇开低于或高于某些极限的极端测量值，挑选出那些在多种情况下显示出一致性、被认为是平均值的样本。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
This shows a new feature in Alberti’s theory of imitation, namely, the desire to make his figures conform not only to the most beautiful in nature but to the most usual, the most general, or the most typical.
这在 Alberti 的摹仿理论中展示了一个新特征，即不仅希望使他的形象符合自然中最美的典型，而且要符合最常见的、最一般的或最具代表性的类型。
This identification of the beautiful with the typical in nature implies a belief in the Aristotelian view of nature as an artist striving towards perfection and always hindered from attaining it by accident. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} According to this view the artist, by eliminating the imperfections in natural objects and combining their most typical parts, reveals what nature is always aiming at but is always frustrated from producing. Alberti has simplified Aristotle’s views on this point, for he arrives at the type-beauty by a process of more or less arithmetical averaging, whereas in Aristotle some faculty nearer to the imagination is involved.
将美与自然中的典型相等同，意味着一种亚里士多德式的自然观：自然如同一位追求完美的艺术家，但总被偶然因素阻碍而无法达到完美。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 按照这一观点，艺术家通过消除自然物中的不完美并结合其最典型的部分，显露出自然一直在追求但始终无法产生的目标。Alberti 在这一点上简化了亚里士多德的观点，因为他通过或多或少算术平均的过程得出类型之美，而在亚里士多德那里则涉及一种更接近想象力的能力。
This very matter-of-fact averaging technique, however, is characteristic of Alberti and illustrates how far he was removed from any sort of idealistic or Neoplatonic conceptions. From what he says about choosing the best and the typical from nature it follows that the artist can create a work which is more beautiful than anything in nature. But with Alberti this can only be done by a series of processes all of which keep the artist in the closest touch with nature, and it is done without any appeal to the imagination. The impor-
然而，这种非常实事求是的平均技术正是 Alberti 的特点，并说明了他与任何形式的唯心主义或新柏拉图主义概念相去甚远。从他关于从自然中选择最佳和典型的论述可推断出，艺术家可以创造出比自然中任何事物都更美的作品。但在 Alberti 看来，这只能通过一系列过程来完成，而这些过程都使艺术家与自然保持最密切的接触，且在此过程中不诉诸想象力。该项工...
tance of this will appear when the development of aesthetics in the sixteenth century is considered. For the moment it is enough to notice how consistent Alberti is in his fidelity to nature. Towards the end of the treatise on painting, after he has been advising the artist only to select the best from nature, he is immediately frightened that he may have gone too far and puts in a warning to those who think they can neglect nature and rely on their own skill and imagination. They will fall into bad ways, he says, from which they will never be able to free themselves. r r ^(r){ }^{\mathrm{r}}
当考虑十六世纪美学的发展时，这一点的重要性将显现出来。暂且只需注意阿尔伯蒂在忠实于自然方面的一贯性。在《论绘画》一书的末尾，当他只建议艺术家从自然中取其精华时，他立刻又担心自己可能过了头，因此对那些认为可以忽视自然、依靠自身技巧和想象的人提出了警告。他说，他们将陷入恶习，并永远无法自拔。 r r ^(r){ }^{\mathrm{r}}
Alberti varies a little in the meaning which he attaches to the word ‘nature’. In the early treatise on painting he generally seems to mean by it simply the sum of all the material objects not made by man. In the later works on sculpture he seems to assume the vaguely Aristotelian view discussed above. One of the most curious results to which Alberti’s acceptance of this definition of nature leads him is to describe architecture as an imitation of nature, just as much as the directly representational arts. The idea underlying this view is that nature acts according to certain general laws and on an orderly method. The aim of the architect is, therefore, to infuse into his works something of this order and method which is to be found in nature. Ancient architects, he says, ‘rightly maintained that nature, the greatest of all artists in the invention of forms, was always their model. Therefore they collected the laws, according to which she works in her productions as far as was humanly possible, and introduced them into their method of building.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The principles to which Alberti refers are defined by such qualities as harmony (concinnitas), proportion, symmetry. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
阿尔伯蒂在“自然”一词的含义上有些许不同。在早期关于绘画的论著中，他通常似乎仅指所有非人为制造的物质对象的总和。在后来的关于雕塑的作品里，他似乎采纳了上文所述的那种模糊的亚里士多德式观点。阿尔伯蒂接受这种自然定义后导致的最奇特结果之一，是他将建筑描述为对自然的模仿，正如那些直接再现的艺术一样。支撑这一观点的思想是：自然按照某些普遍规律并以有序的方法行事。因此，建筑师的目标就是在他的作品中注入自然中所能发现的这种秩序和方法。他说，古代的建筑师“有理地坚持认为，自然——在形态创造上最伟大的所有艺术家——一直是他们的范本。因此他们把自然在其作品中运作的规律，在人力所及的范围内加以收集，并把这些规律引入他们的建造方法中。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 阿尔伯蒂所指的原则可由诸如和谐（concinnitas）、比例、对称等特性来界定。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
There is nothing startlingly original in this view, which is made up of ideas taken from Aristotle and Vitruvius, but Alberti was not primarily interested in abstract aesthetic
这种观点并无惊世之处，主要是从亚里士多德和维特鲁威那里借来的观念，但阿尔伯蒂并不主要关心抽象的美学
3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Ibid.   3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 同上。
speculation, and when he comes to discuss these very general qualities he often takes over traditional theories from the ancients. He himself distinguishes the laws governing the beauty of buildings as a whole which are derived from philosophy from those dealing with the parts of the building which, based on experience, are the proper business of the architect and the real foundation of architecture. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
思辨，而当他讨论这些非常一般的品质时，他常常沿用古人的传统理论。他自己区分了两类关于建筑之美的规律：一类源自哲学，适用于整体建筑之美；另一类则处理建筑的各个部分，基于经验，属于建筑师的正当事务并构成建筑学的真正基础。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
When Alberti first evolved his philosophy he was in close agreement and sympathy with many of the best thinkers in Florence. But when he again came into contact with Florentine society in the last years of his life, between 1464 and 1472, he found that life and culture there had changed. The Medici were now in complete control of the city, and, under their autocratic rule, life had grown more luxurious. Men’s philosophy, too, had changed. For Florentine culture of the later Quattrocento was dominated by the Neoplatonists led by Marsilio Ficino and Pico della Mirandola.
当阿尔伯蒂最初形成他的哲学时，他与佛罗伦萨许多最优秀的思想家观点一致并深有同感。但在他晚年重返佛罗伦萨社会的最后几年（1464 年至 1472 年），他发现那里的生活与文化已有所改变。美第奇家族现在完全控制了这座城市，在他们的专制统治下，生活变得更加奢华。人们的哲学观也随之改变。晚期十五世纪的佛罗伦萨文化被由马西利奥·菲奇诺和皮科·德拉·米兰多拉领导的新柏拉图主义者所主导。
Alberti’s relation to Platonism is somewhat complex. Many of the fundamental ideas in his philosophy are ultimately Platonic in origin, and Alberti very likely derived them from the Florentine followers of Plato in the fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries, such as Petrarch or Bruni. His faith in man and in the human will, his doctrine of following nature, his conception of the prince, and many others of his opinions are to be traced in the writings of the early Humanist admirers of Plato such as Salutati. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} But by the end of the fifteenth century the philosophy of the Platonists in Florence had entirely changed. Under the influence of Cosimo and Lorenzo de’ Medici the Platonic Academy had developed, but it had tended to pay even more attention to the writings of the Alexandrian exponents of Plato than to the philosopher himself. Ficino and Pico are soaked in mysticism, derived partly from Plotinus and partly from oriental origins. This
阿尔伯蒂与柏拉图主义的关系有些复杂。他哲学中的许多基本观念最终源自柏拉图，而阿尔伯蒂很可能从十四世纪和十五世纪早期佛罗伦萨的柏拉图追随者那里获得这些观念，例如彼特拉克或布鲁尼。他对人的信仰和对人类意志的信念、他追随自然的学说、他对君主的观念以及许多其他观点，都可以在早期人文主义者对柏拉图的崇拜者如萨卢塔蒂的著作中找到渊源。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 但到十五世纪末，佛罗伦萨的柏拉图主义者的哲学已完全改变。在科西莫和洛伦佐·德·美第奇的影响下，柏拉图学院得以发展，但它反而更倾向于重视亚历山大学派对柏拉图的阐释者的著述，而非柏拉图本人。菲奇诺和皮科浸润于神秘主义之中，这种神秘主义部分源自普罗提诺，部分源自东方起源。
mystical Neoplatonism was encouraged by Lorenzo de’ Medici, perhaps to some extent for political reasons. At any rate it certainly served his ends; for the Neoplatonists at this time laid much more emphasis on the contemplative than on the active life; and it suits an autocrat to keep thinking men as far as possible out of active politics in order that he may enjoy his absolute power undisturbed.
洛伦佐·德·美第奇鼓励神秘的新柏拉图主义，或许在某种程度上出于政治原因。不管怎样，这确实有利于他的目的；因为那时的新柏拉图主义者更强调沉思的生活而非行动的生活；而对于一个独裁者来说，尽可能将有思想的人排除在政治活动之外，使他能在不受打扰的情况下享有他的绝对权力，是十分合适的。
Alberti seems to have felt little sympathy either with the methods of Lorenzo or with the mystical kind of Neoplatonism which he encouraged. He is sometimes claimed as a supporter of the Neoplatonists on the grounds that he was involved in many of their discussions. But his agreement with them appears to be limited to the doctrines which they held in common with earlier Platonists, and did not extend to those more mystical ideas which Ficino and Pico had added. Nothing could be less mystical than Alberti’s way of thought. He believed above all in the importance of the active life, and thought that the citizen should contribute tangibly and materially to the good of the city. I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} Indeed, to the Florentines of the late 1460’s Alberti must have seemed a relic of the heroic period of thirty years before. In his last work, the De Iciarchia, he condemns the luxury of the city, and attacks the Medici almost openly, saying that great power awakens vices in a man, and reminding them that the prince is subject to the laws of the city and must preserve its liberties.
阿尔伯蒂似乎对洛伦佐的作法以及他所鼓励的那种神秘的新柏拉图主义都鲜有同情。他有时被认为是新柏拉图主义者的支持者，理由是他参与了他们的许多讨论。但他与他们的共识似乎仅限于那些与早期柏拉图主义者共有的教义，并未扩展到菲奇诺和皮科所加入的那些更为神秘的观念。阿尔伯蒂的思维方式再不神秘不过了。他首先相信积极生活的重要性，认为公民应在有形和物质上为城市的良善作出贡献。确实，对于 1460 年代末的佛罗伦萨人来说，阿尔伯蒂必定被视为三十年前那个英雄时代的遗存。在他的晚作《De Iciarchia》中，他谴责城市的奢靡，几乎公开地抨击美第奇家族，称巨大的权力会唤醒人的恶习，并提醒他们君主受制于城市的法律，必须维护其自由。
Seen in relation to his predecessors, Alberti’s most striking characteristics are his rationalism, his classicism, his scientific method, and his complete faith in nature. In relation to the Neoplatonists of the later Quattrocento, the feature which stands out most is the complete absence of the idea of
与他的前辈相比，阿尔伯蒂最引人注目的特征是他的理性主义、古典主义、科学方法以及对自然的完全信任。与晚期十五世纪的新柏拉图主义者相比，最突出的特点是他的著作中完全缺乏想象力的观念。
imagination in his writings. Everything is attributed to reason, to method, to imitation, to measurement; nothing to the creative faculty. And this is quite logical. The artists of the early Quattrocento whose ideas he expresses were entirely occupied with exploring the visible universe which they had so recently discovered. What they needed was practical advice, not abstract speculation; and that is exactly what Alberti gave them. It was not till the next century that the doctrines of Neoplatonism came into real contact with the theory of painting, most notably in the person of Michelangelo, whose first training was received in the circle of Lorenzo de’ Medici. With him the artist becomes for the first time ‘the Divine’, and Alberti’s practical conception of the arts gives place to a loftier doctrine.
一切都归于理性、方法、模仿、测量；没有什么归于创造力。这是完全合乎逻辑的。早期十五世纪那些其思想为他所表达的艺术家，完全致力于探索他们刚刚发现的可见宇宙。他们需要的是实用的建议，而不是抽象的思辨；这正是阿尔伯蒂给予他们的。直到下一个世纪，新柏拉图主义的学说才真正与绘画理论发生联系，最显著的例子是米开朗基罗，其最初的训练是在洛伦佐·德·美第奇的圈子里完成的。在他这里，艺术家第一次成为“神圣”的存在，阿尔伯蒂对艺术的实用观念让位于更高远的学说。

Chapter II  第二章

LEONARDO  列奥纳多

A p A p A^(p)\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{p}}PART from Michelangelo, Leonardo is the only great painter of the Italian Renaissance who has left in writing any quantity of material dealing with the arts, and we should expect that the opinions and ideas of such a man would throw more light on Renaissance art-theories than all the systematic and philosophical treatises of the laymen who wrote in the sixteenth century. Many of his theories do, of course, give us information about the methods and ideas of the period which we cannot derive from other sources, but the confusion of the surviving manuscripts and the lack of plan in the notes make it impossible to deduce a really coherent theory of the arts from Leonardo’s written works.
米开朗基罗之外，莱昂纳多是意大利文艺复兴时期唯一一位留下大量有关艺术书面材料的伟大画家，因此我们本应期望这样一位人物的观点和思想，比十六世纪那些非宗教作家所写的所有系统性和哲学性论述更能阐明文艺复兴的艺术理论。当然，他的许多理论确实为我们提供了关于当时方法和观念的信息，这些信息是其他来源无法得出的，但存世手稿的混乱以及笔记中缺乏条理，使得无法从莱昂纳多的著述中推导出真正连贯的艺术理论。
Leonardo evidently intended to write a full-dress treatise on painting, and, according to Luca Pacioli, some sections of it at least were finished by 1498. If this is so, the parts in question are lost, but many schemes for the general plan of the treatise, not all of them consistent with each other, survive in the existing material. What we actually have left of Leonardo’s writing is an enormous mass of notes, mostly jotted on the margins of sketch-books. These notes are either passages which Leonardo copied down from what he read, or original ideas embodying a personal theory or observation.
显然，莱昂纳多打算写一部完整的绘画论著，而且据卢卡·帕西奥利所说，至少其中的一些章节在 1498 年之前已经完成。如果情况确实如此，那么有关的部分已遗失，但在现存材料中保留着许多关于该论著总体构想的方案，且这些方案并不全相互一致。我们实际上保留下来的莱昂纳多著述是一大堆笔记，主要记在素描本的边缘。这些笔记要么是莱昂纳多从所读之书中抄录下来的段落，要么是体现个人理论或观察的原创观点。
The datable manuscripts cover a period from 1489 to 1518 . The originals are to be found in many public and private libraries, particularly in Paris and at Windsor, and most of them have been published. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Even more important, however,
可定年手稿涵盖了 1489 年至 1518 年这段时期。原稿散见于许多公私图书馆，尤其是在巴黎和温莎，其中大多数已被刊行。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 然而，更为重要的是，
for the present purpose is a copy of the originals, now in the Vatican Library, made by a sixteenth-century student, evidently with the idea of publication, in which the notes are to some extent arranged by subjects. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The first printed edition, based on two other manuscript copies, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} was published in Paris by Dufresne in 1651. It is of little importance for the study of the text, since it is incomplete and inaccurate, and its chief interest lies in the engravings illustrating it, which were made after drawings executed by Poussin in order to explain points in Leonardo’s writings.
就目前目的而言，这是对原件的抄本（现藏于梵蒂冈图书馆），由一位十六世纪的学生所作，显然带有出版之意，其中笔记在某种程度上按主题排列。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 第一版印刷本基于另外两份手稿抄本， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 由 Dufresne 于 1651 年在巴黎出版。该版对文本研究意义不大，因为它不完整且不准确，其主要价值在于附带的插图，这些版画是根据 Poussin 所绘的图稿制作，以便解释 Leonardo 著作中的要点。
Leonardo was born in 1452, and as he grew up in Florence the main intellectual influence in the city was that of the Neoplatonists who were discussed in the last chapter. But though they dominated the philosophical field, the old scientific method in the arts, which we have seen in the work of Alberti, survived in the form of a studio tradition, above all through painters such as Verrocchio, under whom Leonardo studied.
Leonardo 出生于 1452 年，他在佛罗伦萨长大，该城的主要思想影响来自上章讨论的现代新柏拉图主义者（Neoplatonists）。但尽管他们主导了哲学领域，艺术中的旧有科学方法——我们在 Alberti 的作品中已见过——以画室传统的形式得以保留，尤其通过像 Verrocchio 这样的画家传承下来，Leonardo 就是在其门下学习的。
The basis of Leonardo’s scientific observations, which covered every branch of the study of natural phenomenazoology, anatomy, botany, geology, as well as mechanical and mathematical problems-was a profound belief in the value of experiment and of direct observation. It was by what he actually saw-in the human body, in plants, or in the formation of rocks-that he entirely outstripped his contemporaries, even the experts in the various sciences which he studied. His knowledge of human anatomy was not attained by members of the medical profession for half a
达·芬奇科学观察的基础——这些观察涵盖了自然现象学、动物学、解剖学、植物学、地质学，以及机械与数学问题的各个分支——是对实验价值和直接观察的深刻信念。正是通过他亲眼所见的事物——无论是人体、植物，还是岩石的形成——他完全超越了同时代人，甚至超越了他所研究的各门科学中的专家。他对人体解剖的认识，是医学界的从业者直到半个世纪之后才达到的。
century after his death, and many of the facts which he observed had to wait still longer before they could be properly fitted into man’s scheme of the universe.
在他去世后的一个世纪里，他所观察到的许多事实还要更久才能被恰当地纳入人类的宇宙观。
He expresses his faith in experiment on many occasions. In one group of notes he attacks the abstract speculations of the Scholastics. He exactly reverses the medieval canon that a science is only certain if it is purely speculative and merely mechanical if it comes into contact with the material universe:
他在多次场合表达了对实验的信任。在一组笔记中，他抨击了经院哲学家的抽象臆断。他完全颠倒了中世纪的教条——即只有当一门科学纯粹是思辨性的才是确定的，而一旦与物质世界接触就只是机械的。
‘They say that any knowledge is mechanical if it is the product of experiment, that it is scientific if it begins and ends in the mind, and that it is semi-mechanical if it springs from pure knowledge and ends in a manual activity. But it seems to me that those sciences are vain and full of error which do not spring from experiment, the source of all certainty, and which do not lead to experimental truth, of which, that is to say, neither the beginning, the middle nor the end is dependent on one of the five senses. And if we doubt the certainty of everything which comes to us through the senses, how much more should we doubt those things which cannot be tested by the senses, such as the nature of God and of the soul and such things.’ 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
“他们说任何知识如果是实验的产物就是机械的，如果它始于心智并终于心智就是科学的，如果它源于纯粹知识而终结于手工活动就是半机械的。但在我看来，那些不源于实验——一切确定性的源泉——且不通向经验证实的真理的学问，是虚妄且充满错误的。所谓经验证实的真理，是指其开端、中间与结尾都不依赖于五感之外的任何东西。如果我们怀疑一切通过感官传达给我们的事物的确定性，那么我们更应怀疑那些无法通过感官检验的事物，例如关于上帝与灵魂的本性等。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Here Leonardo’s faith in the material world and in the evidence of the senses has led him to opinions which in less secure times would have brought trouble from the Church authorities, but the passage shows how deeply he was opposed to speculation not based on experiment. His real feeling is summed up in the formula, borrowed from Aristotle, ‘All our knowledge has its origin in our perceptions’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
在这里，列奥纳多对物质世界及感官证据的信赖使他形成了在更不稳定的时期可能会招来教会当局麻烦的观点，但这段话显示了他对不以实验为基础的推测有多么深恶痛绝。他的真实观点可用从亚里士多德借来的公式概括：“我们一切知识都起源于感知。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
Leonardo applied the same argument to the principle of authority as to the method of abstract speculation: 'Many will think they may reasonably blame me by alleging that my proofs are opposed to the authority of certain men held in the highest reverence by their inexperienced judgements; not considering that my works are the issue of pure and simple
莱昂纳多对权威原则所作的论证，与他对抽象推测方法的论证相同： “许多人会认为他们可以合理地指责我，声称我的论证与某些为无经验判断而备受尊崇之人的权威相抵触；却不考虑到我的著作是纯粹且简单的
experiment, which is the one true mistress.’ 'This is an extension of the personal test for truth which Alberti and the early Humanists had already substituted for the test of authority. 'Any one who in an argument appeals to authority uses not his intelligence, but his memory." 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
实验的产物，而实验是唯一真正的女主人。” “这是对个人真理检验的一种扩展，Alberti 和早期人文主义者已经用它取代了权威的检验。 ‘在论证中援引权威的人用的不是他的理智，而是他的记忆。’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
In a sense Leonardo carried on the scientific principles which Alberti had applied to the arts; but there are important differences between their methods. Whereas Alberti applies the ordinary processes of deduction to the facts which he observes in order to arrive at general laws, Leonardo’s strength lies in the actual observation of phenomena, and he is little given to deducing general laws from his observations. Moreover, such generalizations as he does make are usually closely based on the work of his predecessors, above all on the medieval philosophers.
在某种意义上，莱昂纳多延续了 Alberti 应用于艺术的科学原则；但他们的方法之间存在重要差异。Alberti 把普通的演绎过程应用于他观察到的事实以得出一般规律，而莱昂纳多的强项在于对现象的实际观察，他很少从观察中推导出一般规律。此外，他所作的此类概括通常严格基于前人的工作，特别是中世纪哲学家的著作。
For Leonardo, as for Alberti, painting is a science because of its foundation on mathematical perspective and on the study of nature. It is based on ‘scientific and true principles’; 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} but these principles are derived from observation, as appears when Leonardo, after putting down a series of practical hints for the painter, says that they are ‘the issue of sound experience, the common mother of all the Sciences and Arts’. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
对莱奥纳多而言，正如对阿尔伯蒂一样，绘画是一门科学，因为它建立在数学透视和对自然的研究之上。它基于“科学而真实的原则”； 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 但这些原则来自观测，正如莱奥纳多在给画家的若干实用提示之后所说的那样，它们是“健全经验的产物，一切科学与艺术的共同母体”。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
Considered as a kind of knowledge, the art of painting is to be judged by two standards: the certainty of its premisses and methods, and the completeness of the knowledge represented by its productions.
作为一种知识，绘画艺术应以两个标准来评判：其前提和方法的确定性，以及其作品所呈现知识的完备性。
The certainty of painting depends on various facts: first it depends on the eye, which is the least easily deceived of all the senses; 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} secondly the painter does not rely wholly on the eye but checks its judgements by actual measurement; 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} and thirdly painting is based on the principles of geometry. 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7}
绘画的确定性取决于若干事实：首先取决于眼睛，眼睛是在所有感官中最不易被欺骗的； 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 其次画家并不完全依赖眼睛，而是通过实际测量来检验其判断； 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 第三，绘画还基于几何学的原则。 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7}
The importance which Leonardo attaches to the completeness with which an art represents nature, to the comprehensiveness of its particular kind of truth, comes out most clearly in the disputes about the relative dignity of the various arts, the significance of which will be discussed later. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} In arguing with the defenders of poetry Leonardo maintains that painting is the finer art because ‘it makes images of the works of nature with more truth than the poet’, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and in other passages he expresses the same view in different ways. Painting is to poetry as reality to the shadow, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and elsewhere he says: 'Write up in one place the name of God, and put a figure representing him opposite, and see which will be the more deeply reverenced. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} The same idea comes out when Leonardo claims superiority for painting over sculpture because the latter cannot use colour, or aerial perspective, or depict luminous or transparent bodies, clouds, storms, and many other things. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} All this suggests that the completeness with which an art represents nature is, after the certainty of its methods, one of the standards by which it is to be judged.
列奥纳多所强调的艺术对自然再现的完整性、以及其所呈现之特定真理的全面性，在关于各艺术相对尊严的争论中最为清晰，这些争论的重要性将在后文讨论。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 在与诗歌支持者的辩论中，列奥纳多主张绘画是更高雅的艺术，因为“它比诗人更真实地描绘自然的作品”， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 在其他段落他以不同方式表达了相同观点。绘画之于诗歌，如现实之于影子， 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 在别处他又说： “在一处写上上帝的名字，并在对面放一幅代表他的形象，看看哪个会被更深地崇敬。” 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 当列奥纳多主张绘画优于雕塑，因为后者无法使用色彩、或空气透视、或描绘发光或透明的物体、云、风暴以及许多其他事物时，同一思想也显现出来。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 这一切表明，艺术对自然再现的完整性，继其方法的可靠性之后，是评判艺术的标准之一。
Since painting is a kind of science, its processes must be checked by rational judgement at each stage. ‘He is a sorry master whose works are ahead of his judgement; but that master will go forward to the perfection of his art whose judgement exceeds his work.’ 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} And the fact that judgement in art is a rational process is made even clearer in another section where Leonardo advises the artist to listen to the opinion of all his friends about his paintings: 'Be ready therefore to hear with patience the opinions of others; and consider well and think carefully whether he that blames your work has cause or not to do so. If you find that he has, correct it; if not, pretend not to have understood him, or, if he is a man of merit, make him understand by reasoning (per ragione) that he is mistaken. 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7}
既然绘画是一门科学，其每一阶段的过程都必须通过理性判断来检验。“作品先于判断的画家可悲；但判断领先于作品的画家，将朝着其艺术的完美前进。” 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 而且在另一段中，列奥纳多建议艺术家倾听所有朋友对其画作的意见时，更清楚地表明了艺术判断是一个理性过程：“因此要准备耐心听取他人的意见；并且要好好思考、仔细判断，责备你作品的人是否有理由这样做。若你发现他有理由，就改正；若无，则假装不理解他，或者如果他是有见识的人，就用理性（per ragione）使他明白他错了。” 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7}
Painting, therefore, is a science, but it is different from other sciences because it involves the production of a material work of art. In an important passage Leonardo enumerates those elements, like perspective, which compose the science of painting and ‘which exist in the mind of those that think about it. From this springs the execution (operatione), which is much nobler than the thinking or science’. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This is a remarkable inversion of the current idea, which Leonardo seems to accept on other occasions, that the actual execution was manual and for that reason despicable.
因此，绘画是一门科学，但它不同于其他科学，因为它涉及物质艺术品的创作。在一段重要的论述中，莱昂纳多列举了构成绘画科学的那些要素，例如透视，‘这些存在于思考它者的心中。从此产生了施行（operatione），这比思考或科学要高贵得多’。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这是对当时观念的一个显著颠倒；莱昂纳多在其他场合似乎接受的观点是，实际的施行是体力性的，因此可以被蔑视。
According to Leonardo, then, painting is a science having as its material product a work which is a reproduction of some part of nature. So we are back to the idea of painting as the scientific imitation of nature, though it will be seen later that Leonardo’s ideas on this imitation are different from Alberti’s.
因此在莱昂纳多看来，绘画是一门以某种再现自然局部的作品为其物质成果的科学。所以我们回到了将绘画视为对自然的科学模仿的观念，尽管稍后将看到，莱昂纳多关于这种模仿的观点与 Alberti 的不同。
Leonardo constantly emphasizes the fact that artistic imitation is a scientific act and not a mere mechanical process. He has particular scorn for those who ignore theory and think that by mere practice they can produce works of art: ‘Those who devote themselves to practice without science are like sailors who put to sea without rudder or compass and who can never be certain where they are going. Practice must always be founded on sound theory.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} He also disapproves of those who rely on devices for exact imitation, like Alberti’s net or the method of painting on a piece of glass held in front of the view. These should only be used as short-cuts and labour-saving tricks by those who have enough knowledge of theory, that is to say above all of perspective, to be able to check their work according to scientific standards. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
列奥纳多不断强调艺术模仿是一个科学行为，而不仅仅是一个机械过程。他特别鄙视那些忽视理论、认为仅凭实践就能创作艺术作品的人：‘那些专注于无科学的实践的人，就像出海却没有舵或罗盘的水手，永远无法确定他们要去何方。实践必须始终建立在健全的理论基础上。’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 他也不赞成依赖于精确模仿装置的人，比如 Alberti 的网或将玻璃片置于视野前方进行绘画的方法。这些应仅作为有足够理论知识者的捷径和省力技巧使用，也就是说，首先应当具备透视等理论，以便能够根据科学标准检验他们的作品。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
As with all Leonardo’s ideas the originality of his conception of the imitation of nature can only be seen in his treatment of specific problems. A very large part of the notes is devoted to scientific observation of facts relevant to the
与列奥纳多所有思想一样，他对自然模仿的独创性观点只有在他对具体问题的处理上才能看出。大量笔记致力于对与…相关事实的科学观察。
painter. In some of them, for instance in those dealing with linear perspective, he is on ground which had already been covered by earlier authors, but in most of the subjects his observations are entirely original and of astonishing acuteness. In those sections in which he writes of the movements of a man and the attitudes which he will take up in performing different actions, he is perhaps only putting down what was to some extent the common property of Florentine painters, and following up the investigations of men like the Pollaiuolo brothers. His notes on botany, particularly on the growth of trees, are much more personal, for before his time men had paid little attention to the scientific study of inanimate nature for its own sake.
画家。在其中的一些部分，例如涉及线性透视的那些，他所述的内容已经被早期作者所涉及，但在大多数主题上，他的观察完全是原创的，且敏锐程度令人惊讶。在那些他写到人的动作以及在执行不同行为时所采取的姿势的段落里，他或许只是记录下某种程度上属于佛罗伦萨画家共有的东西，并延续了像 Pollaiuolo 兄弟那样的人物的研究。他关于植物学的笔记，尤其是关于树木生长的部分，则更具个人特色，因为在他之前，人们很少为了自身目的而对无生命的自然进行科学研究。
But the notes in which the exactness of his observation is most startlingly apparent are those dealing with light and shade and those on aerial perspective. To the former he attaches great importance because without the correct disposition of light and shade a painting will not have the appearance of relief. The details of his treatment of the subject are not relevant here, but one specimen will give an idea of how carefully he observed nature. He noticed that shadows cast by the sun on a white surface are blue, I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} an idea which was not taken up again till the second half of the nineteenth century, when it became one of the fundamental discoveries of Impressionism. Unfortunately, however, this did not lead Leonardo to experiment further with the theory of colours in which he was not particularly interested. In aerial perspective Leonardo appears as a complete innovator. Earlier writers, such as Alberti, were apparently quite unaware that the edges of objects become less clearly defined and the details on them less distinct as they get farther away. They seem not even to have noticed or not to have been interested in the fact that hills are blue in the distance, and, though some painters before Leonardo, or independent
但最能突显他观察精确性的注释，是那些关于明暗处理和大气透视的篇章。他把前者看得非常重要，因为如果明暗布置不正确，画作就不会显现出立体感。他对该主题的具体处理在此不必赘述，但举一个例子便可说明他观察自然有多么细致。他注意到太阳在白色表面上投下的阴影呈蓝色， I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} 这一观点直到十九世纪下半叶才被重新提起，并成为印象派的基本发现之一。不幸的是，这并没有促使列奥纳多在他并不特别感兴趣的色彩理论上做更多实验。在大气透视方面，列奥纳多显得完全具有创新性。早期的作者，如 Alberti，显然并未意识到物体的边缘随着距离的增加会变得不那么清晰，其上的细节也会变得不那么明确。 他们似乎甚至没有注意到，或对远处群山呈蓝色这一事实不感兴趣，尽管在列奥纳多之前的一些画家，或像佩鲁吉诺这样的同时代独立艺术家，
contemporaries like Perugino, hint in their paintings at the possibilities of this kind of perspective, it is only in a very vague way. Leonardo was the first to carry out a really systematic study of the subject, the effects of which appear in his paintings and no less in his theoretical writings.
在他们的画作中以非常含糊的方式暗示了这种透视可能性，但真正系统地研究这一课题的人是列奥纳多，他的研究成果出现在他的画作中，也同样体现在他的理论著作里。
These examples of Leonardo’s scientific observation illustrate the importance which he attached to the certainty of methods in painting, and the care with which he established this certainty in direct experiment with nature. Other details in his theory are relevant to his other standard, that painting must be as complete as possible in its representation of nature.
列奥纳多这些科学观察的例子说明了他对绘画方法确证性的重视，以及他如何通过与自然的直接实验来周密地建立这种确证。他理论中的其他细节与他的另一项标准有关，即绘画在再现自然方面必须尽可能完整。
Leonardo’s belief in the exact imitation of nature is even greater than Alberti’s. He constantly sets up this exactness as the final test of painting, as, for instance, when he says: "That painting is the most to be praised which agrees most exactly with the thing imitated’ 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and though in other passages his opinion on this seems to differ, he certainly considers if of great importance, since he recommends the painter always to carry with him a mirror and to see whether the reflection in it agrees exactly with his painting, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and elsewhere he refers to the reflection in a mirror as ‘the true painting’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
列奥纳多对精确模仿自然的信念甚至比阿尔伯蒂更强烈。他不断将这种精确性作为绘画的最终考验，例如当他说：“那幅画最值得称赞，便是最精确地与所模仿之物相符的那幅” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} ，尽管在其他段落中他的观点似乎有所不同，但他无疑认为这一点极为重要，因此他建议画家随身携带一面镜子，以观察镜中反射是否与他的画作完全一致， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 并且在别处他把镜中反像称为“真实的画”。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
The artist, therefore, is to imitate nature exactly and he must not try to improve on it, for this will only lead him to be unnatural and mannered. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} In this matter Leonardo is even more whole-heartedly opposed to any idealism than Alberti. In his practical advice to the painter there is no trace of it, and he never suggests that the artist must make nature conform to some idea which exists in his mind, though nature herself, of course, is subject to general laws.
因此，艺术家应当精确地模仿自然，不应试图改良自然，因为那只会使作品显得不自然和矫揉造作。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 在这一点上，列奥纳多比阿尔伯蒂更彻底地反对任何理想主义。在他对画家的实际建议中没有任何理想主义的痕迹，他从未暗示艺术家必须使自然服从于他头脑中某种观念，尽管自然本身当然服从于一般规律。
Leonardo lays little emphasis on Alberti’s process of selection of the most beautiful from nature. From passages
列奥纳多很少强调阿尔伯蒂从自然中选取最美之物的过程。从以下段落
quoted above it is evident that he wishes the painter to copy all that is in nature and not to limit himself by leaving out certain classes of things; and in many other notes he talks of the beauty of all the works of nature without making any distinction of different degrees of beauty. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} From other sections, however, we can see that he is aware that all nature is not equally beautiful, but he believes it to be all equally worthy of imitation by the painter nevertheless. Both the painter and the poet describe ‘the beauty or ugliness of a body’, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and the introduction of ugliness even serves a definite purpose because the contrast of beautiful and ugly parts serves to show up each with greater intensity. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Contrast, which is elsewhere recommended by Leonardo as a quality always to be sought after, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} is a very important element in his theory and may be connected with one of the most general features of his thought: that he is primarily interested not in the beautiful but in the individual and the characteristic. In this way he is entirely opposed to Alberti, who, with his search after perfect proportion, the generalized type of human figure and so on, was always in pursuit of the beautiful. Leonardo seems to feel that, provided he can make his figures real, individual, and living, it will not matter if they do not conform to some absolute standard of harmony. In his practice Leonardo consistently followed this principle, as as is shown by the extraordinary series of caricatures in the sketch-books. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
如上所引可见，他希望画家复制自然中的一切，而不要通过省略某些类别的事物来限制自己；在许多其他段落中，他谈到自然万物的美而不区分美的不同级别。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 然而，从其他章节我们可以看到，他意识到并非所有自然事物都同样美，但他仍认为这些均同样值得画家模仿。画家和诗人都描述“一个躯体的美或丑”， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 而丑的引入甚至具有明确目的，因为美与丑部分的对比能使各自更为突出。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 对比——在其他地方被列奥纳多推荐为应当始终追求的品质—— 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 在他的理论中是一个非常重要的要素，并且可能与他思想中最普遍的特征之一相关：他主要感兴趣的不是美，而是个体性与特征性。 在这一点上，他完全反对 Alberti。Alberti 追求完美的比例、一般化的人体类型等等，总是追逐“美”。莱昂纳多似乎认为，只要他能把人物表现得真实、个性化、有生命，即使这些人物不符合某种绝对的和谐标准也无妨。莱昂纳多在实践中始终遵循这一原则，这一点由习作本中那一连串非凡的讽刺画可见一斑。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
Leonardo disagrees with Alberti’s pursuit of only the beautiful in nature and also of his pursuit of the typical and the general which is closely associated with it. This follows from what has just been said of his interest in the individual
莱昂纳多不同意 Alberti 只追求自然中的“美”以及与之紧密相关的典型性和一般性的做法。这一点可从前文关于他对个体兴趣的描述中得出。
and the characteristic. It appears partícularly when he discusses the proportions of the human figure. Alberti had tried to fix a single canon of proportion to apply to all human figures. Leonardo goes about it in exactly the opposite way.
