He concentrates on the infinite variety which nature shows in the human figure: 'A man can be well proportioned if he is thick and short, or tall and thin, or medium; and whoever does not observe this variety will always make his figures on a single model, so that they will all look like brothers, which is greatly to be condemned. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Leonardo finds himself compelled to admit that the proportions of a man are fixed in height (presumably by a false deduction from the fixed length of the bones), but he urges the painter to make them vary as much as possible in breadth. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} What is vitally important is not that the limbs of a figure should obey a fixed rule of proportion, but that they should be harmonious among themselves and that you should not see, for instance, a woman’s hand on a muscular arm. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
以及特征。尤其当他讨论人体比例时，这一点表现得尤为明显。Alberti 试图确定一个适用于所有人体的单一比例规范。Leonardo 则完全相反。他专注于自然在人体上表现出的无限多样性：“一个人可以是粗短而匀称，也可以是高瘦而匀称，或中等；凡不注意这种多样性的人，总会用单一范式来塑造人物，使他们看起来都像兄弟，这实在大有可谴。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Leonardo 不得不承认人的高度比例是固定的（可能因从骨骼固定长度做出错误推断），但他敦促画家尽可能使宽度发生变化。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 至关重要的不是人物的四肢遵从某一固定的比例规则，而是它们彼此和谐，例如你不应看到一只女性的手长在肌肉发达的手臂上。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
The contrast between the views of Leonardo and Alberti on the subject of proportion corresponds to certain changes which had taken place in painting in the fifteenth century. In the time of Alberti, when artists were still working back to realism after the non-realistic style of the Middle Ages, it was necessary in the interests of realism to establish what were roughly the proportions of a man, this not having been in the Middle Ages a matter of importance to artists. Alberti’s theories of proportion, therefore, were a weapon for establishing the first stage of realism. But in the time of Leonardo the situation was changed. Realism had been fully established, and artists knew the correct proportions of the human body only too well. Their tendency was to use them mechanically and to produce an academic uniformity, so that it was necessary to give the contrary advice to that which Alberti had rightly given. Therefore, in opposition to the stylization
关于比例问题，列奥纳多与阿尔伯蒂观点之间的对比，反映了十五世纪绘画中发生的某些变化。在阿尔伯蒂时期，艺术家们还在从中世纪非写实风格回归写实，在追求写实的过程中，必须大致确定人的比例，而在中世纪这对艺术家并不是重要的问题。因此，阿尔伯蒂的比例理论成了确立写实第一阶段的武器。但到列奥纳多时代，情况已然改变。写实已被完全确立，艺术家们对人体的正确比例了解得过于透彻。他们倾向于机械地运用这些比例，导致学究式的单一化，因此有必要给出与阿尔伯蒂当年正确建议相反的劝告。因此，为了反对程式化
and monotony into which Florentine artists were threatening to slip, Leonardo emphasized the importance of variety in the proportion of the human figure.
为了防止佛罗伦萨艺术家陷入单调乏味，莱昂纳多强调了人体比例多样性的重要性。
Leonardo’s whole-hearted faith in nature makes him disapprove of those who devote themselves to imitating the style of other masters: ‘Never imitate the manner of another painter, or you will be called a grandson and not a son of nature in your art.’ 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} He makes an exception for the young painter, who must study the work of the masters as a training but must give up the practice as soon as possible. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The danger of copying the style of another painter is that it leads to mannerism, and that, in Leonardo’s eyes, is one of the worst sins, since mannerism excludes naturalism. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Mannerism in general springs from constantly repeating a trick of any kind without referring back to nature, so that in the end an unconscious habit is formed and the artist is unaware that he is going against nature. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} The same sort of fate is likely to befall an artist who relies on his memory instead of studying nature directly. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
列奥纳多对自然的全心信赖使他不赞成那些致力于模仿其他大师风格的人：“切勿模仿另一位画家的作风，否则在艺术上你会被称为自然的孙子而不是儿子。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 他为年轻画家作了例外，认为他们必须把研习大师作品作为训练，但应尽快放弃这种做法。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 模仿他人风格的危险在于它会导致矫揉造作，而在列奥纳多看来，这是最严重的罪过之一，因为矫揉造作排斥自然主义。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 一般来说，矫揉造作源于不断重复某种技巧而不回归自然，最终形成一种无意识的习惯，艺术家自己却未察觉违背了自然。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 同样的命运也可能降临依赖记忆而不直接研究自然的艺术家身上。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
One other small point illustrates Leonardo’s views about the imitation of nature, namely, the importance which he attaches to relief in a painting. If a painting has not the appearance of relief it has not satisfied the very first condition necessary for likeness to the thing depicted. For Leonardo this quality is of greater importance than beauty of colour, or correctness of drawing: 'The first business of the painter is to make a plane surface appear to be a body raised and standing out from this surface, and whoever excels the others in this matter deserves the highest praise. And this study, or rather this summit of our learning, depends on lights and shades. ′ 6 ′ 6 ^('6){ }^{\prime 6} This is high praise for the mere appearance of relief, but it is for Leonardo a quality so essential to any kind
另一个小例子说明了列奥纳多关于模仿自然的观点，即他对画面凸显感的重视。如果一幅画没有呈现出凸起的外观，就未能满足与所描绘对象相似的最基本条件。对列奥纳多而言，这一特性比色彩之美或线描之准确更为重要：“画家的首务是使平面看起来像一个从该平面上凸起并突出的实体，凡在此方面超越他人者，应受最高的赞誉。而这门学问，或者说我们学习的顶峰，依赖于明暗。”这对单纯凸显外观是极高的评价，但对列奥纳多来说，这是任何艺术品质中如此根本的一项，...
of good painting that nothing that he can say is too good for it, and he comes back to it over and over again in his notes. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
对优秀绘画的赞誉之词，他所能说的再好也不过分，并且他在笔记中反复回到这一点。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
Leonardo’s view of the world is anthropocentric, but much less narrowly so than Alberti’s. The latter thinks of everything in terms of man, whereas Leonardo was deeply interested in animals and plants for their own sake, and not merely for their utility to man. When, therefore, Leonardo says that painting imitates all nature he includes not only man but also all other living creatures and inanimate nature as well. We know that he devoted one section of his treatise to the proportions of the horse, and a very large number of the surviving fragments deal with trees and with the general aspects of landscape. ‘How to paint night’, ‘How to paint a storm’ are typical chapter headings, and all the notes dealing with aerial perspective are directed towards a more complete rendering of landscape. Without a knowledge of landscape the artist would never be universal, and his imitation of nature would be incomplete.
列奥纳多的世界观以人为中心，但比阿尔伯蒂的视角要宽广得多。后者把一切都以人为尺度来考量，而列奥纳多则对动物和植物本身就有深厚的兴趣，而不仅仅关心它们对人的用途。因此，当列奥纳多说绘画模仿全部自然时，他不仅包括人，也把所有其他生物和无生命的自然一并包括在内。我们知道他在论著中专门用一章论述马的比例，现存的许多片段都涉及树木和风景的一般面貌。“如何画夜景”“如何画暴风雨”是典型的章节标题，所有关于大气透视的笔记都旨在更完整地再现风景。不了解风景，艺术家就不可能达到普遍性，他对自然的模仿也将不完整。
History painting, in which the artist is required to show all the aspects of his talent, is the highest and noblest kind of painting. It demands universal knowledge, though the most important element in it is the painting of man. This, however, involves the painting not only of his body but also of his mind: "The good painter must paint principally two things, which are man and the ideas in man’s mind. The first is easy, the second difficult, because they can only be expressed by means of gestures and the movements of the limbs. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} It is for this purpose that Leonardo develops his whole theory of Expression, to which he devotes much space and which was to be taken up and developed by almost all
历史画——画家需要展示其才能的各个方面——是最高尚、最崇高的一类绘画。它要求广博的知识，尽管其中最重要的元素是人的绘画。然而，这不仅涉及对人体的描绘，还涉及对心智的描绘：“优秀的画家必须主要绘制两样东西，即人以及人心中的观念。第一样容易，第二样困难，因为后者只能通过姿态和四肢的动作来表现。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 正是为此，列奥纳多发展了他整套关于表情的理论，他为此投入了大量篇幅，这一理论后来被几乎所有人继承并发展”
later theorists, particularly in France. Leonardo repeats over and over again the importance of showing the emotions and the ideas in a person’s mind by means of his gestures and facial expression, and he gives various indications how this can be done. It is typical of his reliance on nature that his chief advice is that the painter should study people as they argue, or grow angry or look sad, or show any other emotion to see by what gestures they express their feelings, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} taking care at the same time that they do not know that they are being watched and do not therefore become self-conscious. He adds to this advice, however, by writing down the way in which certain emotions should be expressed, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and though, no doubt, these details are based on his own observation, this seems to be a beginning of that systematization of gesture and expression which was carried to its highest point by the French theorists of the seventeenth century. An even further step in the same direction, however, is marked by his suggestion that the appropriate gestures can be found by studying the dumb, who have only the language of gesture by which to express their feelings. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
后来的理论家，尤其是在法国。列奥纳多一再重复通过手势和面部表情来展示一个人内心情感和思想的重要性，并且给出各种如何做到这一点的指示。他依赖自然的典型体现是，他的主要建议是画家应当研究人们在争论、发怒、悲伤或表现任何其他情绪时，通过哪些手势来表达他们的感受， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 同时注意他们不知道自己被观察，以免因此变得自我意识。他在此建议之外还写下了某些情绪应如何表达的方式， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 尽管这些细节无疑基于他的观察，但这似乎是对手势和表情进行系统化的开端，这一体系在十七世纪的法国理论家那里达到了最高点。然而，同一方向上更进一步的一步是他提出可以通过研究聋哑人来发现适当的手势，聋哑人只有手势语言来表达他们的感情。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Closely connected with Expression is another theory which had a great success later and which is to be found in Leonardo for the first time, the theory of Decorum. The gestures which a figure makes must not only show his feelings but must be appropriate to his age, rank, and position. So also must be his dress, the setting in which he moves, and all the other details of the composition.
与“表情”密切相关的还有另一种后来大为流行、并在列奥纳多处首次出现的理论——端庄得体（Decorum）理论。人物的姿势不仅要表现其感情，而且必须与其年龄、等级和身份相称。服饰、人物所处的环境以及构图中的其他所有细节也同样如此。
'Observe Decorum, that is to say the suitability of action, dress, setting and circumstances to the dignity or lowliness of the things which you wish to present. Let a king be dignified in his beard, his mien and his dress; let the place be rich, and let the attendants stand with reverence and admiration, in clothes worthy of and appropriate to the dignity of a royal court. . . . Let the movements
“当注意端庄得体，也就是说行为、服饰、环境与情景要与所要表现事物的尊贵或卑微相适合。让国王在胡须、仪态和服饰上显得庄重；让场所富丽堂皇，让侍从们怀着敬畏与钦佩之情立于一旁，所穿衣物应配得上王室宫廷的尊严和体面……让
of an old man not be like those of a youth, nor those of a woman like those of a man, nor those of a man like those of a child. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
老人的动作不要像青年，女人的举止不要像男人，男人的举止不要像孩子。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
In the hands of Leonardo decorum is simply an element in the complete rendering of the outside world, without which history painting would be incomplete and unconvincing. Later the theory was made to serve entirely different purposes. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
在列奥纳多手中，端庄得体只是完整呈现外部世界的一个要素，缺了它，历史画就显得不完整且不令人信服。后来这一理论被用来服务于完全不同的目的。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
All the notes so far quoted from Leonardo bear on his conception of the artist as a scientist. But opposite to this figure stands that of the artist as creator and inventor. However great may be Leonardo’s feeling that painting is a scientific activity, he realizes that it is not simply a science, and that certain faculties are needed by a good painter which are not necessary to the scientist. The young artist has need of a natural talent, whereas, according to Leonardo the student of mathematics can learn by sheer application. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} The impossibility of producing works of art solely by scientific means is also implied when he says of geometry and arithmetic that ‘these two sciences only extend to a knowledge of quantity . . . but they do not concern themselves with quality, which forms the beauty of the works of nature and the glory of the world’. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Painting, however, ‘studies with philosophical and subtle speculation the qualities of every form’. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Moreover, the painter must ‘by means of drawing show to the eye in visible form the idea and invention which exists first in his imagination (nella sua immaginativa)’. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} And in another chapter he says more generally: 'in fact, whatever exists in essence, in material form or in imagination, all this the artist has first in his mind and then in the work of his hand. 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} He even compares this inventive faculty in one case
到目前为止引用的所有莱昂纳多的笔记都与他将艺术家视为科学家的观念有关。但与这一形象相对立的，是将艺术家视为创造者和发明者的形象。无论莱昂纳多多么强烈地认为绘画是一项科学活动，他也意识到绘画并不仅仅是科学，优秀画家需要某些科学家不必具备的能力。年轻的艺术家需要一种天赋，而据莱昂纳多说，数学的学生可以通过纯粹的应用来学习。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 当他谈到几何和算术时也暗示了单靠科学手段不可能创作出艺术作品：“这两门科学只延伸到对数量的认识……但它们并不涉及质量，质量构成了自然作品之美与世界之荣光”。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 然而，绘画“以哲学和微妙的思辨来研究一切形态的特性”。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 此外，画家必须“通过素描以可见的形式向眼睛展示首先存在于他想象中的观念和发明（nella sua immaginativa）”。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 在另一章中他更概括地说：“事实上，无论在本质上、在物质形态上或在想象中存在的所有事物，艺术家首先在他的头脑中有过，然后才在他的手的作品中显现。” 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} 他甚至在一处将这种发明能力
with the power of God in creating the world: 'that divine power, which lies in the knowledge of the painter, transforms the mind of the painter into the likeness of the divine mind, for with a free hand he can produce different beings, animals, plants, fruits, landscapes, open fields, abysses, terrifying and fearful places. ¹ ¹  ^("¹ "){ }^{\text {¹ }}
比作上帝创造世界的力量：“那种神圣的力量，存在于画家的知识中，将画家的心智变成神性心智的相似物，因为他可以用自由的手创造出不同的存在、动物、植物、果实、风景、开阔的田野、深渊、令人恐惧和可怕的地方。” ¹ ¹  ^("¹ "){ }^{\text {¹ }}
The painter is, therefore, not merely a scientist who copies nature, he is also a creator; he can draw ‘not only the works of nature, but infinitely more than those which nature produces’, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and he excels nature ‘by the invention (fintione) of endless forms of animals and herbs, plants and landscapes’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} In another chapter Leonardo gives examples of the kinds of things which the artist can invent-monsters, unknown landscapes, mountains, plains, and so on. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
因此，画家不仅仅是一个复制自然的学者，他也是一个创造者；他可以绘制“不仅仅是自然的作品，而是远比自然所产生的更多的东西”， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 并且他通过发明（fintione）无尽的动物与草本、植物与风景的形态而超越自然。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 在另一章中，列举了艺术家可以发明的事物类型的例子——怪物、未知的风景、山脉、平原，诸如此类。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
But Leonardo never encourages the artist to give free play to his imagination. What he invents must always have the most exact foundation and justification in nature. Even if it does not actually exist, it must appear to the spectator as if it could exist. If the imagined vision is not built up of material collected directly from nature it will be vague and incomplete because ‘the imagination does not see such splendour as the eye sees’, 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} and ‘the imagination stands in the same relation to reality as the shadows to the body which casts it’. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} Even if the artist wants to paint a purely fantastic monster he must build it up from limbs observed in different animals, or it will not be convincing. 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} Therefore Leonardo gives the following final advice to the artist on the method of stocking and stimulating his imagination:
但列奥纳多从不鼓励艺术家随意放纵想象力。他所发明的一切必须始终有最精确的自然基础与正当理由。即使它实际上并不存在，也必须在观者眼中显得仿佛可能存在。如果想象的意象不是由直接从自然中收集的材料构成，就会显得模糊不全，因为“想象所见不如眼睛所见那般辉煌”， 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 并且“想象与现实的关系，如同影子与投射其影的身体的关系”。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 即便艺术家想要画一个纯粹的奇幻怪物，他也必须把它由在不同动物身上观察到的肢体构成，否则就不会令人信服。 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} 因此列奥纳多就储备与激发想象力的方法给艺术家以下最终建议：
'Knowing that you cannot be a good painter unless you are a universal master capable of imitating with your art all the qualities of the forms which nature produces, and that you will not be able to do this unless you see them in your mind and copy them from there, when you go through the fields turn your mind to different
“知道你若不是一位能够用艺术模仿自然所出诸形态一切品质的通才，就不能成为优秀的画家；而你若不在心中见到这些并从心中临摹，也做不到这一点。因此当你走过田野时，应将心思转向不同的事物”
objects, and study them one after another, making a bundle of selected and chosen things. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
将对象一一研究，逐一考察，选取并汇集成一束精心挑选的事物。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
In this way the artist will fill his mind with images based on the exact knowledge of nature and his imagination will have a sure foundation for its inventions.
通过这种方式，艺术家将以对自然的精确认识为基础充实他的心象，他的想象力也将有一个可靠的发明基础。
This double conception of the artist’s function, as scientific observer and as imaginative creator, is found perfectly expressed in the paintings and, above all, in the drawings of Leonardo. Here the material collected by the minute study of natural phenomena seems to have been transmuted by the imagination by an almost magical process of which Leonardo gives no account in his writings.
作为科学观察者与想象创造者这两重艺术家功能的观念，在列奥纳多的画作，尤其是在他的素描中得到了最完美的体现。在这里，通过对自然现象细致研究所收集的素材似乎经过想象的几乎魔幻般的转化过程，而列奥纳多在著述中并未对此做出任何解释。

Chapter III  第三章

COLONNA: FILARETE: SAVONAROLA
科隆纳：菲拉雷特：萨沃纳罗拉

CERTAIN other works produced during the Quattrocento are relevant to the development of theory in Italy. The most important is the curious and celebrated romance attributed to Fra Francesco Colonna, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} entitled Hypnerotomachia Poliphili, first published by Aldus Manutius in 1499 in an edition principally famous for its woodcuts. Colonna, who was born in 1433, was a monk in the monastery of SS. Giovanni e Paolo in Venice and also for a time at his native Treviso. The Hypnerotomachia is dated 1467, but the author probably went on working at it till the date of its publication. This romance is of interest because it is the only work dealing with the Fine Arts produced in Venice during the Quattrocento, and therefore the only direct clue to the views which the Venetians held about aesthetics at that time.
在十五世纪四百年间创作的某些其他作品与意大利理论的发展有关。其中最重要的是一部归于修士 Francesco Colonna 的奇特且著名的长篇小说， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 题为 Hypnerotomachia Poliphili，首次由 Aldus Manutius 于 1499 年出版，该版本以其木刻插图著称。Colonna 生于 1433 年，曾在威尼斯的 SS. Giovanni e Paolo 修道院为僧，也曾在他的故乡特雷维索短暂居住。Hypnerotomachia 标注为 1467 年，但作者很可能一直工作到出版之时。这部小说之所以引人注意，是因为它是四百年间威尼斯唯一一部涉及美术的作品，因此是当时威尼斯人关于美学观点的唯一直接线索。
A very large element of Gothic survives in the painting and architecture of Venice in the late fifteenth century; for the Gothic tradition was too deeply established to be completely dislodged by the cult of Antiquity which spread to Venice from Florence and Rome. The classical style was taken up, but it was treated in a romantic and irrational spirit. Painters like Mantegna imitated ancient statues with enthusiasm, but they combined what they derived from them with a Gothic emotionalism. Architects such as the Lombardi used the classical orders, but in combination with Gothic structure and with an almost oriental use of rich marbles.
在十五世纪末的威尼斯绘画和建筑中，哥特式的大量要素仍然保留着；因为哥特传统根深蒂固，不会被从佛罗伦萨和罗马传入威尼斯的古典崇拜完全取代。古典风格被采纳进来，但以浪漫且非理性的精神来对待。像曼特尼亚这样的画家热衷模仿古代雕像，但他们将从中汲取的元素与哥特式的情感主义结合起来。像伦巴第人这样的建筑师使用古典柱式，但与哥特式结构相结合，并几乎以东方式的方式大量使用华丽的大理石。
The same mixture of medieval and classical elements appears in the Hypnerotomachia. In form it is a Gothic romance, of the type of the Roman de la Rose, but taken more directly from the Amorosa Visione of Boccaccio. The wanderings of the unhappy lover Poliphilus in search of his Polia are accompanied by all the adventures and allegories traditional in the romances of the Middle Ages. But the author has used this medieval form to express above all his overwhelming passion for antiquity. Every episode, every allegory is dressed up in classical phraseology. The language and names are a bastard mixture of Italian, Latin, and Greek; the buildings described are in the ancient manner; the monuments are covered with Latin or Greek inscriptions, or with hieroglyphics which the author painstakingly transcribes and explains; every ceremony is dedicated to a classical god or goddess.
在《梦幻情斗记》中同样出现了中世纪与古典元素的混合。在形式上它是一本哥特式爱情小说，属《玫瑰之书》那一类，但更多直接取材于薄伽丘的《爱情幻景》。不幸的恋人波利菲勒斯为寻找他的波莉娅而四处漂泊，伴随他的有中世纪浪漫小说中常见的一切冒险与寓言。然而作者利用这种中世纪的形式，主要是为了表达他对古代的炽热热情。每一段情节、每一个寓言都以古典的辞格装扮。语言与人名是意大利语、拉丁语与希腊语的杂糅；所描绘的建筑皆为古制；纪念性建筑上刻满拉丁文或希腊文铭文，或刻着作者细心抄录并加以解释的象形文字；每一场仪式都献给某位古典的神或女神。
The author evidently set himself to recreate an atmosphere which he believed to be ancient. But his method and, indeed, his whole attitude to antiquity are fundamentally different from that of a Florentine Humanist like Alberti. Whereas the latter is rational and severely archaeological, Colonna interprets his knowledge of antiquity imaginatively, with no great regard for accuracy of detail. He is not interested in the philosophical and moral ideas of the ancients; he wishes only to take from antiquity those elements which will help him to build up a dream; and this dream, one feels, became for him more important than the ordinary conduct of life. His view is summed up in the sub-title of the book: ‘Ubi humana omnia non nisi somnium esse ostendit’.
作者显然试图重现他所认为的古代氛围。但他的方法以及他对古代整体的态度，根本上不同于像 Alberti 这样的佛罗伦萨人文主义者。后者理性且具有严格的考古学倾向，而 Colonna 则以想象的方式解读他对古代的知识，对细节的准确性并不十分在意。他对古人的哲学和道德思想不感兴趣；他只希望从古代汲取那些能帮助他构筑梦境的元素；而这个梦，对于他而言，似乎比日常生活的行为更为重要。他的观点在书的副标题中得以概括：“Ubi humana omnia non nisi somnium esse ostendit”。
But the dream which he spun was a very sweet one, in which he could enjoy all those things which were unattainable to him in real life. Among these is the ideal of perfect love, which is expressed in a very strong erotic element throughout the book. This is usually discreetly clothed in allegory, but the covering is sometimes of the thinnest and the symbolism of the most direct kind.
但他所编织的梦非常甜美，在其中他可以享受现实生活中无法得到的一切。其中包括完美爱情的理想，这一理想贯穿全书并以强烈的情色元素表达出来。这通常以寓言的方式含蓄表述，但这种掩饰有时却非常薄弱，象征性也往往极为直接。
Figure 2: The Ruins of Polyandrion. From the Hypnerotomachia Poliphili, 1499
图 2：Polyandrion 的废墟。出自《Hypnerotomachia Poliphili》，1499

The author’s imaginative attitude also extends to matters of pure archaeology, in which he seems not to bother about either accuracy or consistency. When he describes the ritual which is performed in the various temples which Poliphilus visits, there is often a strong tinge of Christian usage ; so that, for instance, the attendants in the temple of Venus say ‘So be it’, at the end of each prayer. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The architectural descriptions, which are the most important part of the book from the present point of view, do not contain the same mixture of non-classical elements, but, compared with Alberti’s business-like analyses, they are fantastic and irrational. At first sight the author seems to be very precise in the giving of dimensions, which he piles up for every building that he describes. But these are apparently not supplied for the benefit of an architect who might wish to carry out the schemes, but merely to give the reader an impression of vast size and elaboration. The buildings are so fantastic that few have attempted to put Colonna’s ideas into execution. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
作者的想象态度也扩展到纯考古学问题上，在这些方面他似乎并不在意准确性或一致性。当他描述 Poliphilus 所访问的各个神庙中所举行的仪式时，常常带有强烈的基督教用法色彩；例如，在维纳斯神庙中侍从在每次祈祷结束时会说“愿如是”。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 从当前视角来看，书中最重要的部分是建筑描写，这些描写并不包含同样的非古典元素混杂，但与 Alberti 那种事务化的分析相比，它们显得奇幻而不合常理。乍看之下，作者在给出尺寸方面似乎非常精确，他为所描述的每一座建筑都堆砌了大量尺寸数据。但这些显然不是为了方便某位可能想要实施这些方案的建筑师，而仅仅是为了给读者一种宏大与精细的印象。那些建筑如此幻想，以致很少有人试图将 Colonna 的想法付诸实施。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
One of the most remarkable of the buildings which he describes is the great monument crowned with an obelisk, illustrated on Plate 4. Colonna’s description is evidently a free imaginative version of ancient accounts of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} but with many elements of his own invention. The base of the building was a block forty paces high on a square of 1,200 paces. On this was built a pyramid of I , 400 I , 400 I,400\mathbf{I}, 400 steps, crowned by a cube of stone on a side of four paces, which supported a huge obelisk, in a single shaft fourteen paces high. Finally the whole monu-
他描述的最为显著的建筑之一是顶端饰以方尖碑的大型纪念碑，如图版 4 所示。科隆纳的描述显然是对哈利卡纳苏斯陵墓古代记述的自由想象性改写， 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 但其中包含许多他自己发明的元素。建筑的基座是一个高四十步、边长为 1200 步的方体。在此之上建有一座由 I , 400 I , 400 I,400\mathbf{I}, 400 级台阶组成的金字塔，金字塔顶端置有一侧长四步的石方块，支撑着一根高十四步的单体巨大方尖碑。最后，整个纪念碑——
ment was topped by a great statue of gilded bronze, representing Occasio, so arranged that it was turned on its axis by the wind, with a terrifying noise. There is in this description something of the fear which men of the Middle Ages felt before the vast ruins of Roman times; but it is combined with an intense desire to recreate their glories, though only in the imagination.
顶端安放着一座巨大的镀金青铜雕像，代表着“机遇”，被安置成可随风转动，发出可怖的声响。这段描写中带有中世纪人面对浩大古罗马遗迹时的某种恐惧；但同时也夹杂着一种强烈的欲望，想要重现它们的光辉，尽管只是存在于想象之中。
In many other cases, however, Colonna shows a different view about the remains of antiquity. Many of the buildings which he describes are in a state of ruin, and in talking of them he betrays a romantic feeling quite unlike the serious archaeological approach of the early Quattrocento Florentines. Brunelleschi and Alberti, for instance, spent much time on the study of the remains of ancient Rome, but only in order to find out what they had been like when they were complete. For them the ruins were a school for the modern builder. Colonna takes an actual delight in the fact that they are ruins and not complete buildings. He describes their decay with real feeling, and he makes them an excuse for reflections on the frailty of human life and love, and on the destructive passage of time. When Poliphilus comes upon the ruins of Polyandrion (Plate 3), the ancient temple of Pluto, Polia says to him: 'Look a while at this noble relic of things great in the eyes of posterity, and see how it now lies in ruins and has become a heap of fragments of rough and humpy stones. In the first age of man it was a splendid and magnificent temple. . . . 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Colonna is in fact here indulging in that sentimental and melancholy delight in ruins as symbols of the impermanence of things which became so fashionable at a later date, particularly in the eighteenth century.
然而在许多其他情况下，Colonna 对古代遗迹却表现出不同的观点。他所描述的许多建筑都处于荒废状态，在谈论它们时流露出一种浪漫的情感，这与十五世纪初佛罗伦萨人的严肃考古方法大为不同。例如，Brunelleschi 和 Alberti 花了大量时间研究古罗马的遗迹，但只是为了弄清它们在完整时的样子。对他们而言，那些废墟是现代建筑师的课堂。Colonna 则对它们是废墟而非完整建筑这一事实感到由衷的欣喜。他带着真情描述它们的毁坏，并以此为借口反思人生与爱情的脆弱，以及时间的摧毁性流逝。当 Poliphilus 遇见 Polyandrion（图版 3），即古代的冥王神庙的废墟时，Polia 对他说：‘且细看这在后世眼中曾极为壮丽的遗物，如今如何凋零，已成为一堆粗糙不平的石块。在人类的最初时代，它是座华丽而宏伟的神庙……’ 科隆纳在这里实际上沉湎于那种把废墟视为万物流转的象征的感伤与忧郁的欣赏，这种情绪在后来尤其是十八世纪变得非常流行。
The Hypnerotomachia was not of great use to architects who wished to learn about the methods and structure of ancient building, but to the painters, sculptors, engravers, and maiolica painters it was an endless source of themes.
《恋梦狂斗记》对那些想学习古代建筑方法与结构的建筑师帮助不大，但对画家、雕塑家、版画家和马约利卡陶瓷画师来说，它是一个取之不尽的题材来源。
Figure 3: PLATE 4  图 3：图版 4
The Pyramid. From the Hypnerotomachia Poliphili, 1499
金字塔。《恋梦狂斗记》（Hypnerotomachia Poliphili），1499 年
The hieroglyphics which Colonna describes were perhaps the most popular part of the book, and Aldus set the fashion by taking one representing a dolphin curled round an anchor as his printer’s mark. Other parts were also borrowed. Some painters, for instance, copied the subjects on the reliefs which Poliphilus finds in his wanderings; others illustrated scenes from the story in paintings. In these various ways the novel could be of use to all those who felt that antiquity was a sort of ideal existence which could be reconstructed in imagination. For those whose approach was more sharply archaeological or more severely moralizing it was not of much service.
科隆纳所描述的象形文字或许是这本书中最受欢迎的部分，Aldus 通过采用一个卷绕在锚周围的海豚作为他的印刷商标而引领了这一潮流。其他部分也被借用。例如，一些画家临摹了 Poliphilus 在游历中发现的浮雕题材；另一些则在绘画中描绘故事场景。通过这些不同的方式，这部小说对那些认为古代是一种可以在想象中重构的理想存在的人们有用。对于那些采取更明确的考古学方法或更严格说教态度的人来说，它帮助不大。
Some of the same elements that appear in the Hypnerotomachia are to be found in the treatise on architecture written by Antonio Averlino, called Filarete. The author was a Florentine sculptor and architect, born about 1400, who worked mainly in Rome and Milan, his best-known works being the bronze doors of Old St. Peter’s. His treatise was written between 1460 and 1464 in Milan, where Filarete was attached to the court of Francesco Sforza. The author has given it a semi-romantic form, in which he describes the building of an imaginary city, ‘Sforzinda’. The vastness of the conception, the descriptions of the pageantry accompanying the founding of the city, the time of which is chosen in accordance with astrological observation, the passionate but uncritical admiration for antiquity, are all elements which bring Filarete’s work close to the Hypnerotomachia. On the other hand, underneath the dilettante surface there is more rationalism than is to be found in Colonna. Filarete was a serious defender of ancient architecture in a town where the Gothic continued to have a firm grip till well into the sixteenth century. His ideas on town planning, which recall Alberti (by whom they may have been partly inspired), are whole-heartedly anti-medieval, and the author lays great emphasis on regularity of disposition and on the importance of having large squares. The treatise ends with three books
在《Hypnerotomachia》中出现的一些要素也可以在安东尼奥·阿韦利诺（Antonio Averlino），即所谓的 Filarete，所著的建筑论著中找到。作者是一位出生于约 1400 年的佛罗伦萨雕塑家兼建筑师，主要在罗马和米兰工作，他最著名的作品是老圣彼得大教堂的青铜门。他的论著写于 1460 年至 1464 年间，地点在 Filarete 隶属弗朗切斯科·斯福尔扎（Francesco Sforza）宫廷的米兰。作者赋予该书一种半浪漫的形式，书中描述了一个虚构城市“Sforzinda”的建造。构想的宏大、随城建成而来的盛大仪仗的描述、按占星观察选定的建城时辰、对古代的热烈但不加批判的崇拜——所有这些要素都使 Filarete 的作品接近《Hypnerotomachia》。另一方面，在这位玩味者式的表面之下，隐含着比科隆纳（Colonna）更为理性主义的倾向。Filarete 是古代建筑在一座直到十六世纪中叶哥特式仍占主导的城市中的严肃捍卫者。 他关于城市规划的观点让人想起 Alberti（或许部分受其启发），完全反对中世纪风格，作者非常强调布局的规律性以及设置大型广场的重要性。该论述以三卷书结束
on drawing in which, however, the author only repeats the mathematical and technical commonplaces of earlier writers.
关于绘画，但在这些书中，作者只重复了早期著作中的数学和技术陈词滥调。
In the same town as Filarete’s Trattato there was produced in 1497 the curious work De Divina Proportione of the mathematician Fra Luca Pacioli. Pacioli was a pupil of Piero della Francesca, from whom he learnt mathematics and perspective. He was also a friend of Alberti and Leonardo, but his outlook was very different from theirs. Springing from a tradition of scientific artists who used mathematics as a weapon for studying nature, Pacioli absorbed their learning but applied it to wholly different purposes. He devoted his attention to the abstract side of mathematics, thinking entirely of theory and not at all of the foundation of his theory in nature. His attitude is almost Pythagorean, for to him numbers have a mystical significance, with which the idea of beauty is closely associated. There are passages in the D e D e DeD e Divina Proportione which might almost have been written in the thirteenth century, and Pacioli’s favourite authorities are not the Classics but St. Augustine or Duns Scotus. With the mystical play with numbers are intermingled certain ideas which are more closely Neoplatonic.
在与 Filarete 的 Trattato 同一城镇，于 1497 年出现了数学家 Fra Luca Pacioli 的奇特著作 De Divina Proportione。Pacioli 是 Piero della Francesca 的学生，从他那里学得数学和透视。他也是 Alberti 和 Leonardo 的朋友，但他的观点与他们大不相同。源于一传统——那些把数学作为研究自然的武器的科学艺术家，Pacioli 吸收了他们的学识，但将其应用于全然不同的目的。他把注意力奉献给数学的抽象一面，完全只考虑理论，而根本不考虑其理论在自然中的基础。他的态度几乎是毕达哥拉斯式的，因为在他看来，数字具有神秘的意义，与美的观念密切相关。在 De Divina Proportione 中有些段落几乎可以说是十三世纪写的，而 Pacioli 最喜爱的权威不是古典作家，而是圣奥古斯丁或敦斯·司各特。在对数字的神秘戏耍中夹杂着一些更接近新柏拉图主义的思想。
There is no need to analyse Pacioli’s writings in detail. Their importance here depends on their being an example of the application to the theory of painting of the medieval and Neoplatonic ideas which gradually spread over Italy as the early city-republics broke up and were replaced by tyrannies. The earlier philosophers of this group had speculated on the nature of beauty, but Pacioli’s treatise brings the doctrines closer to the arts. The significance of this movement, however, becomes clearer in the sixteenth century, and it will be discussed later. I I ^(I){ }^{\mathbf{I}}
无需详细分析帕西奥利的著作。它们在此处的重要性在于作为一个范例，展示了中世纪与新柏拉图主义思想如何被应用到绘画理论上——这些思想随着早期城邦的解体并被暴君统治取代而逐渐在意大利传播。该群体中较早的哲学家曾对美的本质进行过推测，但帕西奥利的论文将这些学说更贴近于艺术。然而，这一思潮的意义在十六世纪变得更加清晰，稍后将予以论述。 I I ^(I){ }^{\mathbf{I}}
Before going on to the sixteenth century something must be said of a writer who is not generally associated with theory of the Fine Arts, namely, Fra Girolamo Savonarola. Historians often think that, when they have mentioned Savonarola’s burning of those paintings and statues which he considered incitements to sin, they have given his whole view on the arts. But from passages in the Sermons it is clear that, though Savonarola feared the evil effects which might come from the wrong kind of art, he had the greatest faith in the good which could be done by the right kind. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
在进入十六世纪之前，必须提到一位通常不与美术理论联系在一起的作家，即弗拉·吉罗拉莫·萨沃纳罗拉。史学家们常常认为，当他们提到萨沃纳罗拉焚毁那些他认为会引人犯罪的画作和雕像时，就已涵盖了他对艺术的全部看法。但从他布道中的段落可以看出，尽管萨沃纳罗拉害怕不当艺术可能带来的恶劣影响，他对恰当艺术能够带来的善果却怀有最大的信心。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
It is not surprising that Savonarola’s views on art should be almost medieval. The whole basis of his work and teaching was a protest against the worldly and capitalist Papacy of Alexander Vl, and an attempt to restore something of the purity which he associated with medieval life and doctrine. At the same time his preaching was directed towards the artisan classes and not to the feudal aristocracy, which, with the upper middle classes, opposed his efforts.
萨沃纳罗拉对艺术的观点几乎呈中世纪式并不令人惊讶。他全部工作的基础和教导都是对亚历山大六世那世俗化且资本主义的教皇制度的抗议，以及试图恢复他与中世纪生活与教义相联系的某种纯洁性。同时，他的布道面向的是工匠阶层，而非封建贵族；封建贵族与上层中产阶级一道，反对他的努力。
His conception of beauty is based on the assumption that the spiritual is superior to the material. Perfect beauty resides in God, and below Him in varying degrees come the beauty of the saints, the soul of man, and the body. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Some of Savonarola’s definitions are like those of St. Thomas. Beauty lies in proportion, in the harmony of forms and colours. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Others are more Neoplatonic: the beauty of simple things consists in Light. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Since the forms of all created things proceed ultimately from God, beauty in the material world is a reflection of the divine. Therefore Socrates was
他对美的观念基于一种假设：精神优于物质。完美的美存在于上帝，次之的是圣人的美、人的灵魂和肉体，依次下降（程度各异）。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 萨沃纳罗拉的一些定义类似于圣托马斯的看法。美存在于比例中，存在于形与色的和谐中。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 另一些则更具新柏拉图主义色彩：简单事物的美在于光。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 既然一切受造物的形态最终来自上帝，物质世界的美就是对神圣的反照。因此，苏格拉底是
able to contemplate the divine beauty through the beauty of young men. Savonarola does not entirely recommend this method, which is, he says, tempting God, but he quotes it as an example of how material beauty can be used for the perception of the divine. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
能通过年轻人的美来沉思神圣的美。萨沃纳罗拉并不完全赞同这种方法，他说这是对上帝的诱惑，但他引用它作为物质之美可用于感知神圣的例证。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
Savonarola’s conception of beauty is, therefore, in agreement with medieval ideas. His view of the function of the arts is no less so. Painting is to be the Bible of the Illiterate. In one sermon Savonarola recommends his hearers to read the Scriptures, and adds: 'And you who cannot read, go to paintings and contemplate the life of Christ and of His Saints. 12 12 ^(12){ }^{12} And elsewhere he says that ‘figures represented in churches are the books of women and children’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
因此，萨沃纳罗拉对美的概念与中世纪观念一致。他对艺术功能的看法也同样如此。绘画应成为不能读书之人的圣经。在一次布道中，萨沃纳罗拉建议听众阅读圣经，并补充道：“你们这些不能读书的，去看画，沉思基督及其圣徒的生平。” 12 12 ^(12){ }^{12} 在别处他又说，“教堂里所描绘的人物是妇女和儿童的书籍”。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Though Savonarola was medieval in his outlook, he lived surrounded by the worldliness of the Renaissance, and he was therefore impelled, unlike the writers of the Middle Ages, to attack the sinful kinds of painting put into churches in his time. Since painting is such a powerful weapon for good or evil by its effects on the spectator, all indecent or mundane pictures must be taken from churches. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Savonarola makes, however, an interesting addition to this demand. He wishes all paintings to be removed which by their incompetence may arouse the laughter of those who see them. ‘Indecent figures must first be taken away, and then no composition should be allowed which arouses laughter by its mediocrity. In churches only the greatest artists should be allowed to paint, and they should only paint decent subjects.’ 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Savonarola was therefore far from being indifferent to artistic qualities, and the view expressed in this passage is in almost exact agreement with the opinion of Michelangelo reported by Hollanda. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6}
萨沃纳罗拉的观点虽然属于中世纪式的，但他生活在文艺复兴的世俗氛围之中，因此不像中世纪的作家那样，只是抽象地谴责道德败坏，他还具体抨击当时被放入教堂的那些有罪的绘画。因为绘画以其对观者的影响，既能够成为行善的强大武器，也能成为作恶的工具，所有下流或世俗的画作都必须从教堂中移除。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 然而，萨沃纳罗拉在这一要求上做了一个有趣的补充。他希望所有那些因技艺拙劣而会引起观者发笑的画作也一并移走。“应先拿走下流的人物，然后不应容许任何因平庸而招人发笑的构图。在教堂里只应允许最伟大的艺术家作画，而且他们只应描绘端庄的题材。” 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 因此萨沃纳罗拉绝非对艺术品质漠不关心，这段话所表达的观点与 Hollanda 所记载的米开朗基罗的看法几乎完全一致。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6}
But Savonarola does not always speak of the moral purpose
但萨沃纳罗拉并不总是谈论道德目的
of painting, or even of the skill of the artist. There is one passage in the De Simplicitate Vitae Christianae in which he talks in terms of the most naïve naturalism. 'Art prefers the works of nature to its own creations, for it seeks to imitate nature as closely as possible. . . . If works of art please men they do so in proportion as they imitate nature. And in praising a painting one says: “These animals seem to be alive, these flowers look real.” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This is a curious point of view to find among the Scholastic talk about beauty, but it can be explained by the popular basis of Savonarola’s appeal. All through the later Middle Ages popular ideas expressed themselves in the arts by means of realism, but a naïve realism not at all like the scientific realism of the Renaissance, and a realism that is often found in conjunction with purely medieval elements of fantasy and symbolism; as, for instance, in the tradition of Diableries leading up to painters like Bosch or Grünewald. One would therefore expect in any expression of a popular late medieval view of art a mixture of idealist and simple naturalistic theories. And, though he preached almost at the height of the Renaissance, it is as a representative of the later Middle Ages that Savonarola speaks.
绘画，甚至是艺术家技巧的价值。在《基督徒简朴生活论》中有一段，他以极为朴素的自然主义表述道：“艺术偏爱自然的作品胜过自身的创造，因为它力求尽可能地模仿自然……若艺术作品取悦人们，则其程度与模仿自然的程度成正比。赞美一幅画时人们会说：‘这些动物看起来像活的，这些花看起来很真实。’”在关于美的经院式论述中出现这种观点，着实令人惊讶，但可以用萨沃纳罗拉诉求的民众基础来解释。在整个中世纪晚期，民众思想通过现实主义在艺术中得以表达，但那是一种朴素的现实主义，完全不同于文艺复兴时期的科学现实主义，而且这种现实主义常常与纯粹中世纪的幻想和象征元素并存；例如，从“妖魔画”（Diableries）的传统延续到像博斯或格吕内瓦尔德这样的画家。因此，在任何反映民众晚期中世纪艺术观的表达中，我们都应预期理想主义与朴素自然主义理论的混合。 尽管他几乎在文艺复兴的鼎盛时期传道，萨沃纳罗拉却以晚期中世纪代表人物的身份发声。

Chapter IV  第 IV 章

THE SOCIAL POSITION OF THE ARTIST
艺术家的社会地位

MENTION has already been made in connexion with Leonardo of the struggle of painters, sculptors, and architects to attain recognition of their professions as liberal arts. With their new scientific methods they began to claim superiority over mere craftsmen, and tried to establish for themselves a better social position.
在关于列奥纳多的论述中已提到过画家、雕塑家和建筑师为争取将其职业确认为自由艺术而进行的斗争。随着新的科学方法的出现，他们开始主张自己优于普通工匠，并努力为自己确立更高的社会地位。
In practice the position of the artist was considerably higher in the fifteenth century than it had been before. Ghiberti and Brunelleschi both held important administrative posts in Florence, the latter being even a member of the Signoria. In general the public respect for artists had increased immeasurably and was to become even greater in the sixteenth century when the adjective divine was applied to Michelangelo. However, there continued to be theoretical opposition to the admission of painting and sculpture among the liberal arts. In the middle of the fifteenth century Lorenzo Valla excludes them from his list, and much later both Cardanus and Vossius class them as mechanical. Pinturicchio leaves them out in his frescoes of the liberal arts in the Borgia apartments of the Vatican, painted in the last decade of the fifteenth century. It is hard for us to realize the importance attached to these disputes about the liberal arts, but it is brought home to us by a story told by Baccio Bandinelli, who records in his Memoriale a duel fought between his cousin and the Vidame de Chartres because the latter accused the Florentine nobles of practising manual arts in that they took an active interest in painting and sculpture. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
在实践中，艺术家的地位在十五世纪比以前高得多。Ghiberti 和 Brunelleschi 在佛罗伦萨都担任过重要的行政职务，后者甚至成为了 Signoria 的一员。总体而言，公众对艺术家的尊重已大为增加，并在十六世纪变得更加显著，那时“divine”这一形容词被用来形容 Michelangelo。然而，在理论上，绘画和雕塑被纳入自由艺科的做法仍然遭到反对。十五世纪中叶，Lorenzo Valla 在他的名单中将它们排除在外；更晚一些，Cardanus 和 Vossius 都将它们归类为机械艺科。Pinturicchio 在十五世纪最后十年为梵蒂冈的 Borgia 套房所绘的自由艺科壁画中也将它们省略。 我们很难体会到当时对这些有关自由艺术的争论所赋予的重要性，但 Baccio Bandinelli 在他的《Memoriale》中记载的一个故事让这一点变得清晰：他记述了他的表亲与 Chartres 副主教之间为此而发生的一场决斗，后者指责佛罗伦萨贵族从事手工艺，因为他们对绘画和雕塑表现出积极兴趣。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
The claims of artists to a better social position sometimes simply take the form of showing that in earlier times the
艺术家为获得更高社会地位所提出的主张，有时仅表现为证明在过去绘画艺术曾备受尊崇。
art of painting had been held in great respect. Theoretical writers on painting in the fifteenth century searched out every instance in antiquity and in more recent times of favour shown to painters by kings, princes, or popes. The greatest value was attributed to cases in which it could be found that a great man had actually practised painting. For the distinction between the liberal and mechanical arts was that the former were practised by free men, the latter by slaves; and an art acquired much reflected glory from being practised by a royal artist. I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}}
十五世纪关于绘画的理论作家穷尽一切古代与近代的例证，寻找国王、诸侯或教皇对画家的青睐。那些能够证明伟人亲自从事绘画的案例被赋予最高价值。因为自由艺术与机械艺术的区别在于前者由自由人从事，后者由奴隶从事；而若一位王室人物亲自从事某门艺术，则该艺术会因此获得巨大的荣耀。 I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}}
In general, however, the principal aim of the artists in their claim to be regarded as liberal was to dissociate themselves from the craftsmen, and in their discussions on the subject they make it their business to bring out all the intellectual elements in their art. In later fifteenth-century theoretical writings it becomes a commonplace that painting depends on a knowledge of mathematics and of different branches of learning. The early critics argue this matter in quite general terms, but later their claims become more precise and exaggerated.
总的来说，艺术家们声称自己属于自由职业者的主要目的，是与工匠划清界限；在关于这一点的讨论中，他们着力突出艺术中的所有理性成分。到十五世纪后期的理论著作中，绘画依赖于数学和各类学科知识这一观点已成为常见说法。早期批评家以相当笼统的方式论证这一点，但后来他们的主张变得更为具体和夸张。
The part which mathematics played in the painting of the Early Renaissance has already been discussed. In the form of linear perspective it provided one of the most important scientific weapons for the study of nature, and it is as a learned science that the theorists appeal to it. Mathematics was included in the narrow circle of the liberal arts, and if the painters could show that their art involved a knowledge of it, this would be a strong argument for their own art to be considered liberal. Alberti and Ghiberti explain the kinds of mathematics of which a painter must be master, but they do not explicitly connect the matter with the question of the liberal arts. Leonardo is the earliest writer to do so. He first of all says in general terms: 'Practice must always be founded on sound theory, and to this perspective is the guide and gateway; and without this nothing can be done well in the
前文已讨论了数学在早期文艺复兴绘画中所起的作用。以线性透视的形式，它为研究自然提供了最重要的科学武器之一，理论家们正是以一种博学的科学来援引它。数学被包括在狭义的文科自由学科圈内，如果画家们能够证明他们的艺术需要掌握数学知识，这将成为他们的艺术被视为自由艺术的重要论据。Alberti 和 Ghiberti 解释了画家必须精通的数学类型，但他们并未明确将此事与古代文艺自由学科的问题相联系。Leonardo 是最早提出这种联系的作者。他首先总体上说：“实践必须始终建立在牢固的理论之上，而透视学是其指南和门户；没有它，在……方面就无法做好任何事。”
matter of painting.’ I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} But in another passage he alludes directly to the ennobling qualities of mathematics in connexion with perspective: 'Among all the studies of natural causes and reasons light chiefly delights the beholders; and among the great features of mathematics the certainty of its demonstrations is what pre-eminently tends to elevate the mind of the investigator. Perspective therefore must be preferred to all the discourses and systems of human learning. ′ 2 ′ 2 ^('2){ }^{\prime 2}
绘画的问题。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 但在另一个段落中他直接提到数学在透视方面的高贵品质：‘在所有关于自然原因与理性的研究中，光主要取悦观者；在数学的重要特征中，其论证的确定性最能提升研究者的心智。因此，透视应被置于所有人类学问的论述与体系之上。 ′ 2 ′ 2 ^('2){ }^{\prime 2}
The emphasis which Leonardo here lays on the certainty of mathematical demonstration is typical of the use which painters of the Quattrocento made of perspective. As has already been said, it was by means of perspective that they got beyond the naïve and tentative imitation of the natural world and were able to reconstruct it with the sureness which comes from reliance on absolute rules. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
莱昂纳多在此强调数学论证的确定性，这正是十五世纪画家使用透视的典型做法。如前所述，正是通过透视，他们超越了对自然界的幼稚和试探性的模仿，能够以依赖绝对规则而来的把握性重构自然。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
In their claim to knowledge in other branches of science the painters were probably urged on to greater audacity by the rivalry which they felt with the architects. Vitruvius
在对其他科学分支知识的主张上，画家们很可能因与建筑师之间的竞争而更敢冒进。维特鲁威斯
had claimed that the architect must be acquainted with many branches of knowledge, I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} and Renaissance writers from Ghiberti onwards repeat his demands. The painters could not allow themselves to be beaten by this claim, and they simply incorporate the sciences which Vitruvius mentions into their list of requirements for the painter. They do not evolve their full list till the end of the Mannerist period, but the tendency to exaggerate their claims appears earlier. Cellini, for instance, maintains that a sculptor must know about the art of war and must be himself a brave man if he is to make a successful statue of a brave soldier. In the same way he must know about music and rhetoric to represent a musician or an orator. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} To this demand, which can be extended indefinitely, he was probably provoked by an opinion expressed by Plato, who argues that the painter is a mere illiterate imitator: ‘The painter will paint a shoemaker, a carpenter, or any other craftsman, without knowing anything about their trades; and notwithstanding this ignorance on his part, let him be but a good painter, and if he paints a carpenter and displays his painting at a distance he will deceive children and silly people by making them think that it really is a carpenter.’ 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} This scornful opinion clearly offers the painter an opportunity to retort in the way suggested by Cellini, whose view is otherwise hard to explain.
曾宣称建筑师必须通晓多门学科， I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} 自吉贝尔蒂起的文艺复兴作家们便重复这一要求。画家们不甘示弱，便把维特鲁威所提到的那些科学纳入画家的必备学科清单中。他们直到矫饰派末期才形成完整的清单，但夸大自身要求的倾向早已出现。例如切利尼主张，雕刻家若要成功塑造一位英勇士兵的雕像，必须了解战争艺术并且本人须为勇敢之人。同样地，他要表现一位音乐家或演说家，必须懂得音乐和修辞。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 对于这一可以无限延伸的指责，他可能是被柏拉图所表达的一种观点所激怒，柏拉图认为画家不过是文盲式的模仿者：‘画家会画一个鞋匠、木匠或任何其他工匠，而对他们的手艺一无所知；尽管他对此一无所知，只要他是个好画家，如果他画了一个木匠并把画从远处展示出来，他就会通过让孩子和愚蠢的人以为那真的是一个木匠来欺骗他们。’ 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 这种蔑视的观点显然给了画家以回击的机会，正如切利尼所建议的那样，否则很难解释他的看法。
But the painters and sculptors did not content themselves with a general claim to learning; they explicitly demanded equality with the poets. Poetry and rhetoric were accepted as liberal arts, and the painters and sculptors evidently felt that, if they could show that their arts were as noble as that of the poets, they would have proved their claim to be liberal artists also. The first difficulty which they had to overcome was that painting and sculpture seemed to be more manual
但画家和雕塑家并不满足于对学识的笼统主张；他们明确要求与诗人平等。诗歌和修辞被承认为自由艺术，画家和雕塑家显然认为，如果他们能够证明自己的艺术与诗人的艺术同样高贵，他们也就证明了自己是自由艺术家。首先他们必须克服的困难是，绘画和雕塑似乎更偏向手工劳动。
than literature. Equicola, for instance, says: "Therefore, however worthy of praise painting, modelling and sculpture may be, nevertheless they must be considered far inferior to poetry in dignity and authority. Painting is a work and a labour more of the body than of the mind, and is, more often than not, exercised by the ignorant. 1 1 1 1 ^(1)^(1){ }^{1}{ }^{1} Leonardo, however, has a reply ready for this kind of argument; and in defence of painting he says: 'If you call it mechanical because it is, in the first place, manual, and that it is the hand which produces what is to be found in the imagination, you writers also set down manually with the pen what is devised in your mind. ′ 2 ′ 2 ^('2){ }^{\prime 2}
比文学更低。例如，Equicola 说：“因此，无论绘画、塑造和雕刻多么值得称赞，然而在尊严和权威上它们仍应被视为远不及诗歌。绘画是一种更多属于身体而非心灵的工作与劳作，而且往往由无知者来从事。 1 1 1 1 ^(1)^(1){ }^{1}{ }^{1} 然而，列奥纳多对这种论点已有回应；为捍卫绘画他说：‘如果你们称之为机械的，因为它首先是手工的，且是手产生了想象中所见之物，你们这些作家也用笔手写出在你们心中构思的东西。 ′ 2 ′ 2 ^('2){ }^{\prime 2} ’”
Having dealt with this attack, Leonardo goes on to claim that the painter can achieve no less than the poet. Painting can represent an action as completely, more completely even, than poetry; and, in particular, painting can attain the same moral ends on which poetry prides itself:
在应付了这一攻击之后，列奥纳多继续主张画家所能达到的并不比诗人少。绘画能够比诗歌更完整地表现一个动作，甚至在某些方面更为完整；尤其是，绘画能够达到诗歌引以为傲的同样的道德目的：
'And if a poet should say: “I will invent a fiction with a great purpose”, the painter can do the same, as Apelles painted Calumny. . . . If poetry deals with moral philosophy, painting deals with natural philosophy. Poetry describes the action of the mind, painting considers what the mind may effect by the motions [of the body]. If poetry can terrify people by hideous fictions, painting can do as much by depicting the same things in action. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
“如果诗人说：‘我要虚构一个具有伟大目的的故事’，画家也可以照做，正如 Apelles 所画的《诽谤》……若诗歌处理的是道德哲学，绘画则处理自然哲学。诗歌描写心灵的行动，绘画考察心灵通过（身体的）动作可以产生的效果。若诗歌能以可怕的虚构使人惊恐，绘画通过描绘同样的事物在动作中也能达到同样的效果。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Painting, that is to say, can attain its moral end by showing human action through the use of gesture and facial expression, and Leonardo is therefore able to press his favourite theory of expression into the defence of his art. But his argument was not always accepted. Equicola still decides against painting on the grounds that it cannot go beyond the simple imitation of nature: 'Painting has no other concern
也就是说，绘画能够通过手势和面部表情来展示人的行为，从而实现其道德目的，因此列奥纳多能够将他最喜欢的表现理论用于为他的艺术辩护。但他的论点并不总是被接受。Equicola 仍然反对绘画，理由是它不能超越对自然的简单模仿：“绘画没有别的关切”
except with copying nature with various appropriately chosen colours. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} I And Castelvetro later repeats the same argument: 'That which in poetry is first and of most account, the imitation of a human action, as it ought to be, is the last in painting and of no account, namely, that which painters call history. 22 22 ^(22){ }^{22} It was, we may imagine, against arguments of this type that Leonardo was directing one of his notes which refers to the phrase traced back to Simonides which describes painting as muta poesis and poetry as pictura loquens: 'If you call painting dumb poetry, the painter may call poetry blind painting. Now which is the worse defect? to be blind or dumb?'3
除了用各种恰当选择的颜色来复制自然之外。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 我 而 Castelvetro 后来也重复了同样的论点：‘在诗歌中首先且最重要的，那就是对人类行动的模仿，按应有的方式，而在绘画中这是最后且无足轻重的，也就是画家所谓的史画。 22 22 ^(22){ }^{22} 我们可以想象，正是针对这类论点，达·芬奇在他的某条笔记中所指的是可追溯到西蒙尼德斯的话，称绘画为 muta poesis，诗歌为 pictura loquens：‘如果你称绘画为哑的诗，那么画家可以称诗歌为盲的绘画。现在哪个缺陷更糟？失明还是哑口？’3
As soon, however, as the visual arts became generally accepted as liberal, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} the protagonists began to quarrel among themselves about which of them was the noblest and most liberal. Leonardo, in particular, was much concerned with defending painting from the attacks of the sculptors, and many of his notes deal with this question. In these Leonardo first argues, as he did with the poets, that painting can give a more complete description of nature than the rival art. To this the sculptors reply that their art actually creates objects in three dimensions, whereas painting merely gives the illusion of the third dimension. Leonardo, however, turns this argument to his advantage by showing that this illusion is created by intellectual means, whereas the threedimensional quality of sculpture depends simply on the
然而，一旦视觉艺术普遍被接受为文科， 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 各派主将便开始相互争论谁更高贵、更有教养。尤其是达·芬奇，非常关心为绘画辩护以抵制雕塑家的攻击，他的许多笔记都涉及这个问题。在这些论述中，达·芬奇首先像与诗人争辩时那样主张，绘画比竞争艺术能够更完整地描述自然。对此，雕塑家反驳说，他们的艺术实际上创造了三维的对象，而绘画仅仅给出第三维的幻象。达·芬奇却将此论据转为己用，指出这种幻象是由智力手段创造的，而雕塑的三维性仅仅依赖于材料：
material: 'Sculpture shows with little labour what in painting appears a miraculous thing to do; to make what is impalpable appear palpable, flat objects appear in relief, and near objects seem distant," 11 11 ^(11){ }^{11} all this being achieved by means of linear and aerial perspective.
材料：“雕塑用很少的劳力就展示出在绘画中看似奇迹般才能做到的事；使无形之物显得可触，使平面之物呈现浮雕效果，使近物看起来遥远，” 11 11 ^(11){ }^{11} 所有这些都通过线性透视和空气透视手段实现。
An argument of the same kind occurs later in one of the Lezioni of Benedetto Varchi, who tried to settle the rivalry between the painters and sculptors by collecting the opinions of a selected group of masters 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and combining them into a single discourse of his own. He succeeded in showing that painting and sculpture are equally noble arts, because fundamentally their aims and methods are the same. During his exposition, however, he mentions the argument put forward by the sculptors that their art is more difficult. But, following a suggestion of Bronzino, Varchi distinguishes between two kinds of difficulty: manual and intellectual. He admits that the sculptor has more manual or technical difficulties to deal with, by reason of the material in which he works, but he regards this as an ignoble kind of difficulty. The only noble difficulties are intellectual problems, such as those which confront the painter when he has to deal with proportion or with the two perspectives.
同样性质的论点在贝内代托·瓦尔基的一篇 Lezioni 中也出现过。他试图通过收集一组选定大师的意见 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 并将其综合成自己的单一论述来平息画家与雕塑家之间的争论。他成功地证明了绘画与雕塑同为高贵的艺术，因为从根本上说它们的目的和方法是相同的。然而，在他的陈述中，他提到了雕塑家提出的其艺术更为困难的论点。但按照布朗齐诺的建议，瓦尔基区分了两种困难：手工的和智力的。他承认雕塑家因所用材料而面临更多的手工或技术难题，但他认为这是一种卑微的困难。唯一高贵的困难是智力问题，比如当画家必须处理比例或两种透视时所面临的那些问题。
Implicit in these arguments is a belief in the superiority of the intellectual over the manual or mechanical, which corresponds to the desire of artists at this time to shake themselves free from the accusation of being merely craftsmen, manual labour being considered in the society of the Renaissance as ignoble as it had been in the Middle Ages. The pride which artists took in not being involved in much manual labour appears in the contrasted description which Leonardo gives of the sculptor and the painter. The former
这些论点中隐含着一种观念，即智力劳动优于体力或机械劳动，这与当时艺术家希望摆脱仅仅被视为工匠的指控相呼应；在文艺复兴社会里，体力劳动像中世纪一样被认为是不光彩的。艺术家以不从事大量体力劳动为傲，这一点在列奥纳多对雕塑家与画家的对比描述中表现得尤为明显。前者


goes through an exhausting labour with hammer and chisel, is covered with dust and sweat so that he looks like a baker and not like an artist, whereas ‘the painter sits in great comfort before his work, well dressed, and wields his light brush loaded with lovely colours. He can be dressed as well as he pleases, and his house can be clean and filled with beautiful paintings. He often works to the accompaniment of music, or listening to the reading of many fine works. And all this can be heard without being drowned with the sounds of hammering or other uproar.’ 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This gentlemanly kind of painting recalls the representations of the arts on the Campanile basreliefs in Florence in which the calm and dignity of every profession are the qualities which the artist seeks to render. (See Plates 5 a 5 a 5a5 a and b b bb.)
经历着用錾和锤的艰苦劳作，满身尘土和汗水，看起来像个面包师而不像艺术家；而“画家则舒适地坐在作品前，衣着考究，挥动着蘸满美丽色彩的轻巧画笔。他可以随意穿着得体，居所可以干净并陈列着精美的画作。他常在音乐伴奏下工作，或一边听许多佳作的朗读。所有这一切都不会被锤击声或其他喧闹声淹没。” 这种绅士化的绘画风格让人想起佛罗伦萨钟楼浮雕中对各类工艺的表现，在那些作品里，每种职业的平和与尊严正是艺术家试图呈现的特质。（见图版 5 a 5 a 5a5 a 和 b b bb 。）
The upshot of all these disputes was that the painter, sculptor, and architect obtained recognition as educated men, as members of Humanist society. Painting, sculpture, and architecture were accepted as liberal arts, and are now grouped together as activities closely allied to each other and all differing fundamentally from the manual crafts. The idea of the ‘Fine Arts’ comes into existence this way, though a single phrase is not attached to them till the middle of the sixteenth century, when they come to be known as the Arti di disegno. At the same time critics begin to have the idea of a work of art as something distinct from an object of practical utility, as something which is justified simply by its beauty and which is a luxury product.
所有这些争论的结果是，画家、雕塑家和建筑师获得了作为有学识人士、作为人文主义社会成员的认可。绘画、雕塑和建筑被接受为自由艺术，并且现在被归为彼此紧密相关的活动，根本上有别于手工艺。这样“美术”的观念便由此产生，尽管直到十六世纪中叶才有一个统一的称呼把它们连在一起，那时它们被称为 Arti di disegno。与此同时，评论家们开始把艺术作品看作有别于实用物品的东西，视其为仅凭美而自洽的、属于奢侈品范畴的存在。
The arguments about the liberal arts were, therefore, the theoretical side of the artists’ struggle for a better position. The practical side of this was a struggle against the old organization of the guilds, by which artists felt themselves tied. By the end of the fifteenth century they had almost thrown off restraint, and the painter had become a
关于自由艺术的争论，因此，是艺术家为获得更好地位而进行斗争的理论层面。这场斗争的实践层面则是反对行会的旧有组织，因为艺术家感到被其束缚。到十五世纪末，他们几乎摆脱了这些限制，画家已成为一位
free, educated individual co-operating with other men of learning.
自由的、有学识的个体，与其他学识人士合作。
In his new freedom the artist was no longer a purveyor of goods which every one needed and which could be ordered like any other material goods, but an individual facing a public. Both Alberti and Leonardo talk of the importance of pleasing the public. "The painter in his work seeks to please the crowd (tutta la moltitudine)’, says Alberti, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and Leonardo recommends the artist to take the advice of all his friends, who can at any rate judge of the likeness of the painting to nature. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Leonardo, however, still has in mind only an educated public, for in a passage already quoted he speaks scornfully of those painters who aim at pleasing the ignorant. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} His view of the right of those who do not paint to judge painting is of only limited democracy. But by the beginning of the sixteenth century it became a generally accepted idea that the educated layman could give a useful opinion on the arts, and there was even a small outcrop of treatises on the arts written by laymen which will be referred to in a later chapter. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
在获得新自由后，艺术家不再是提供人人需要且可以像其他物质商品那样订购的货物的供应者，而是面对公众的个体。阿尔伯蒂和达·芬奇都谈到取悦公众的重要性。阿尔伯蒂说：“画家在他的作品中寻求取悦群众（tutta la moltitudine）”， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 达·芬奇则建议艺术家采纳所有朋友的意见，毕竟他们至少能判断画作与自然的相似程度。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 然而，达·芬奇心中仍然只考虑受过教育的公众，因为在一段已被引用的文字中，他轻蔑地谈到那些以取悦无知者为目标的画家。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 他关于不作画者有权评判绘画的观点只是有限的民主。但到十六世纪初，人们普遍接受这样的观点：受过教育的外行人可以对艺术提出有用的意见，甚至出现了一小批由外行人写的艺术论著，后文章节将提及这些论著。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
The artist was now faced with a wide public consisting of educated people, not merely of Church officials and a few princes, which he attempted to attract by his art; and in this spirit of competition he began to carry out works other than those directly commissioned. We are here at the beginning of those modern ideas which make of the artist a creator who works for himself alone, but in the Cinquecento these views were only in their infancy. The artist was still closely tied to his public, and most of his work was commissioned. The days of exhibitions were yet a long way off.
艺术家现在面对的是由受过教育的人组成的广大公众，不再仅仅是教会官员和少数诸侯，他试图通过艺术吸引这些观众；带着这种竞争精神，他开始创作那些并非直接受委托的作品。在这里，我们看到了那些将艺术家视为只为自己创作的现代观念的萌芽，但在十六世纪这些观点仍处于初期阶段。艺术家仍然与其公众紧密相连，大部分作品仍是受委托而作。展览的时代还遥遥无期。
But once the old organizations were abandoned as out of date, it became clear that artists needed some sort of institution for guarding their interests and training young artists.
但一旦旧的组织被认为过时而被废弃，便显而易见艺术家需要某种机构来维护他们的利益并培养年轻艺术家。
Consequently in the second half of the sixteenth century there began to grow up those academies which were later to form the whole structure of artistic education. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The earliest was the Accademia del Disegno, founded by Vasari in Florence in 1562, but this was soon followed in Rome, where the Guild of St. Luke was transformed into an academy in 1577. The essential difference between the guilds and the academies was that the latter treated the arts as scientific subjects to be taught theoretically as well as practically, whereas the guilds had mainly aimed at fixing a technical tradition. In the early days the academies allowed individual competition and did not crush every rival as the guilds had done, but later they in their turn became tyrannical.
因此在十六世纪下半叶，那些后来构成整个艺术教育体系的学院开始出现。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 最早的是 1562 年由 Vasari 在佛罗伦萨创立的 Accademia del Disegno，但很快在罗马也出现了类似机构，那里圣卢克公会在 1577 年被改组为学院。公会与学院的根本区别在于，学院将艺术作为既要理论教学又要实践教学的科学学科来对待，而公会主要旨在确立一种技术传统。早期学院允许个人竞争，并不像公会那样摧毁所有对手，但后来它们反过来也变得专制起来。
The guilds were defeated, but there is one curious instance of their attempt to reassert their rights. As late as 1590 the Guild of Genoa tried to prevent Giovanni Battista Paggi from practising painting in the city because he had not gone through the regular training. Legally they were perfectly justified, but the decision went againt them, and this case became a sort of legal admission of the artist’s new status and freedom. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
公会被击败了，但有一个有趣的例子显示了它们试图恢复权利的努力。直到 1590 年，热那亚公会还试图阻止 Giovanni Battista Paggi 在该城从事绘画，因为他没有经过正规的培训。从法律上说他们完全有理，但裁决对他们不利，这一案件成为对艺术家新地位和自由的一种法律承认。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}

Chapter V  第 V 章

MICHELANGELO  米开朗基罗

OUR sources of knowledge for Michelangelo’s views on the Fine Arts are varied. Of his own writings, the letters contain almost nothing of interest from the point of view of theory, since they are nearly all personal or business notes to his family or his patrons. The poems, on the other hand, are of great importance, for though they contain few direct references to the arts, many of them are love poems from which it is possible to deduce in what terms Michelangelo conceived of beauty.
我们关于米开朗基罗对美术观念的认识来源多样。在他自己的著作中，书信从理论角度几乎没有什么有趣的内容，因为它们几乎全是写给家人或资助人的私人或事务性便条。另一方面，诗歌却极为重要，尽管其中直接提到艺术的内容很少，但许多诗是情诗，从中可以推断出米开朗基罗对于美的概念用什么样的措辞来表达。
In addition to his own writings we have the evidence of three of his contemporaries. The first of these is the Portuguese painter Francisco de Hollanda, who came to Rome in 1538 and worked his way for a time into Michelangelo’s circle. He was probably never very intimate with the latter, and his dialogues 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} were almost certainly written to glorify himself and to show how closely he associated with the master. But however great his conceit may have been, his evidence is of importance, since it deals with a period of Michelangelo’s life on which we are not otherwise well informed by his biographers. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
除了他自己的著述外，我们还有三位同时代人的证言。其中第一位是葡萄牙画家弗朗西斯科·德·霍兰达（Francisco de Hollanda），他于 1538 年来到罗马，并一度进入米开朗基罗的朋友圈。他可能从未与米开朗基罗非常亲近，他的对话录 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 几乎可以肯定是为歌颂自己并显示他与大师的密切来往而写的。但无论他的自负有多大，他的证言仍然重要，因为它涉及米开朗基罗生活中的一个时期，而这一时期我们从传记作家那里并未得到充分的了解。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
The second contemporary source is the biography of Michelangelo in Vasari’s Lives. It was first published in 1550, but was greatly enlarged and almost entirely rewritten for the second edition of 1568 . It contains less material than might be expected, but it gives some account of his methods of working and records some of his opinions.
第二个当代来源是瓦萨里的《名人传》中关于米开朗基罗的传记。该书最初于 1550 年出版，但在 1568 年第二版时大幅扩充并几乎全部重写。内容比人们预期的要少，但它对米开朗基罗的工作方法有所记载，并记录了他的一些观点。
More important is the third authority, Ascanio Condivi, a pupil of Michelangelo, who published a biography of his master in 1553. The life seems to have been written to correct certain false statements made by Vasari; and, though Condivi was a somewhat naïve character, he is probably more reliable than either Hollanda or Vasari when he reports Michelangelo’s own views and statements.
更重要的是第三个权威——阿斯卡尼奥·康迪维，他是米开朗基罗的学生，1553 年出版了其师的传记。该传记似乎是为纠正瓦萨里所作的某些错误陈述而写；尽管康迪维为人有些天真，当他报道米开朗基罗的亲自观点和陈述时，他可能比霍兰达或瓦萨里更可靠。
Michelangelo lived to a great age, and his views were constantly developing and changing, so that it is impossible to treat his theories as a single consistent whole. Born in 1475, he was trained under masters who still belonged to the Quattrocento. His earliest works in Rome represent the full blooming of the High Renaissance, but before he died in 1564 Mannerism was firmly established. It is impossible to divide his works or his ideas into sharply separate compartments, but for the present purpose they can be roughly grouped in three periods, if we ignore the very early years from which no documents survive.
米开朗基罗寿命很长，其观点不断发展变化，因此不可能把他的理论视为一个单一的一致整体。他出生于 1475 年，接受的训练师承仍属于十五世纪初期风格（Quattrocento）。他在罗马的早期作品代表着高文艺复兴的盛期，但在 1564 年去世之前，矫饰主义（Mannerism）已牢固确立。无法将他的作品或思想划分为截然分明的各个部分，但就当前目的而言，如果忽略那些没有存留文献的早年时期，可以粗略地将其分为三个时期。
In the first period, ending roughly in 1530 , Michelangelo’s view of the arts is that of High Renaissance Humanism. It is most clearly typified in the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, the Pietà in St. Peter’s (Plate 6 a), and the early love-poems. In these works the various elements which made up Michelangelo’s early training are clearly visible. Like Leonardo he was heir to the scientific tradition of Florentine painting, but he was also affected by the atmosphere of Neoplatonism in which he grew up. His highest allegiance, however, was to beauty rather than to scientific truth; and although in his early years at least he felt that the attainment of beauty depended in large part on the knowledge of nature, he did not feel the urge to undertake the investigation of natural causes for their own sake. Consequently the observation of nature which he absorbed in the studio of Ghirlandaio could fairly easily be fused with the doctrines of beauty which he learnt from the circle of Lorenzo de’ Medici. But there was another
在第一个时期，大约结束于 1530 年，米开朗基罗的艺术观属于高文艺复兴的人文主义。它在西斯廷礼拜堂的天顶画、圣彼得大教堂的《哀悼基督》（图版 6a）和早期的情诗中表现得最为典型。在这些作品中，构成米开朗基罗早期训练的各种要素清晰可见。像列奥纳多一样，他继承了佛罗伦萨绘画的科学传统，但他也受到了他成长环境中新柏拉图主义氛围的影响。然而，他最高的忠诚对象是美而非科学真理；虽然至少在早年他认为美的实现很大程度上依赖于对自然的认识，但他并不觉得有必要为了自身去探究自然的因果。因此，他在吉尔兰达约的画室中吸收的自然观察，可以相对容易地与他从洛伦佐·德·美第奇圈子学到的美的教义融合起来。但还有另一个因素
factor which favoured Michelangelo in comparison with Leonardo. Neither Florence nor Milan could provide the latter with the atmosphere of buoyancy which alone can produce a great synthesis such as had been achieved in Florence in the early years of the fifteenth century. In Rome, on the other hand, Michelangelo found a city at the height of its wealth and politically in a leading position for the whole of Italy. In this atmosphere the artist felt at ease with the world, at which he could look out steadily, and which he could reflect directly in his works. A training in Neoplatonism led to a belief in the beauty of the visible universe, above all in human beauty, which was no longer coloured by the nostalgic mysticism of Florence. The grandeur of the figures on the Sistine ceiling depends on far more than the simple imitation of natural forms, but its idealization is based on a close knowledge and study of these forms. Whatever heroic quality is added, the foundation is a worship of the beauty of the human body.
这是一个有利于米开朗基罗而不利于列奥纳多的因素。佛罗伦萨或米兰都无法为后者提供那种只有在其中才能产生伟大综合体的轻快氛围——正如十五世纪初佛罗伦萨所实现的那种综合体。另一方面，在罗马，米开朗基罗遇到的是一个处于极盛繁荣并在整个意大利政治上处于主导地位的城市。在这种氛围中，艺术家对世界感到从容，他可以稳健地眺望世界，并能在作品中直接反映它。新柏拉图主义的训练导致了对可见宇宙之美，尤以人体之美的信仰，这种信仰不再带有佛罗伦萨那种怀旧的神秘主义色彩。《西斯廷天顶画》中人物的宏伟不仅仅依赖于对自然形态的简单模仿，其理想化是建立在对这些形态的深入了解和研究之上的。不论添加了怎样的英雄气质，其基础都是对人体之美的崇拜。
In the field of thought the two apparently conflicting systems of Christianity and paganism are still perfectly fused in the Rome of the High Renaissance. The iconographical scheme of the Sistine ceiling frescoes is based on the most erudite theology, but the forms in which it is clothed are those of pagan gods. In Raphael’s frescoes in the Stanza della Segnatura the four themes of Theology, Pagan Philosophy, Poetry, and Justice are intricately blended. The catalyst, however, is no longer the hard reason of the Florentines like Alberti, but rather the elaborate Neoplatonism of the later Quattrocento stripped of its more nostalgic elements. In Michelangelo the two faiths were both perfectly sincere. From the days when he was first influenced by the teaching of Savonarola he was a good member of the Catholic Church, though at first without that passionate self-abnegation which came into his faith in the last years of his life.
在思想领域中，在盛期文艺复兴时期的罗马，基督教与异教这两种表面上看似冲突的体系仍然完美融合。西斯廷天顶壁画的图像方案基于最博学的神学，但其所采用的形象却是异教诸神的形式。在拉斐尔位于 Stanza della Segnatura 的壁画中，神学、古典哲学、诗歌与大法官（Justice[Legal]）这四个主题交织融合。然而，催化剂已不再是佛罗伦萨人如 Alberti 那样的冷峻理性，而是后来十五世纪晚期那种剥去了更多怀旧成分的精细新柏拉图主义。在米开朗基罗身上，这两种信仰都是真诚存在的。从他最初受 Savonarola 教导影响的时期起，他就是天主教会的良好成员，尽管起初并没有在其生命后期出现的那种充满激情的自我否定般的信仰。
Michelangelo’s belief in the beauty of the material world was very great. His early love-poems reflect this feeling in
米开朗基罗对物质世界之美的信仰极为强烈。他早期的情诗反映了这种感受于
Figure 4: PLATE 6  图 4：第 6 版画

their expression of strong emotional and often physical passion, directed as much towards visible beauty as towards the spiritual beauty of which the Neoplatonists spoke. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Moreover, Michelangelo’s contemporaries tell us that he did not merely look at nature, but, throughout his life, studied it scientifically. Condivi speaks of his knowledge of perspective, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and both he and Vasari record the care which he devoted to anatomy, not merely learning it at second-hand but dissecting bodies himself. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
他们表现出强烈的情感和常常带有肉体激情的表达，这种激情既指向可见的美，也指向新柏拉图主义者所说的精神之美。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 此外，米开朗基罗的同时代人告诉我们，他不仅仅是观察自然，而是在他的一生中以科学的方式研究自然。Condivi 提到他对透视的知识， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 他和 Vasari 都记载了他对解剖学的用心，不仅仅是间接学习，而是亲自解剖尸体。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Michelangelo did not, however, believe in the exact imitation of nature. Vasari says that he made a pencil drawing of Tommaso de’ Cavalieri ‘and neither before nor afterwards did he take the portrait of anyone, because he abhorred executing a resemblance to the living subject, unless it were of extraordinary beauty’. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} According to Hollanda his scorn for Flemish painting was based on the same idea: 'In Flanders they paint with a view to external exactness . . . without reason or art, without symmetry or proportion, without skilful choice or boldness. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} This view that the artist must select from nature is in agreement with Alberti, though it is unlikely that the latter would have protested so vigorously against Flemish naturalism. His standards were not the same as those of Michelangelo. Alberti acted according to a strictly rational choice, and sought the typical. Michelangelo pursued the beautiful. Condivi describes his methods as follows, alluding to Zeuxis’s painting of the Crotonian Venus:
然而，米开朗基罗并不相信对自然的精确模仿。瓦萨里说他为托马索·德·卡瓦列里画过一幅铅笔素描“此后也未曾为任何人画过肖像，因为他厌恶描绘活体的相貌，除非那是非凡的美人”。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 根据霍兰达的说法，他对佛兰德画派的鄙视基于相同的观点： “在佛兰德，他们作画追求外在的精确……没有理性或艺术，没有对称或比例，没有巧妙的取舍或大胆。” 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 这种认为艺术家必须从自然中选择的观点与阿尔伯蒂一致，尽管阿尔伯蒂不太可能像米开朗基罗那样强烈反对佛兰德的自然主义。他的标准与米开朗基罗不同。阿尔伯蒂按严格的理性选择行事，追求典型性。米开朗基罗则追求美。孔迪维如此描述他的创作方法，并暗指泽克西斯所画的克罗托尼亚维纳斯：
ful thing . . . choosing the beauty in nature, as the bees gather honey from the flowers using it afterwards in their works, as all those have done who have ever made a noise in painting. That old master who had to paint a Venus was not content to see one virgin only, but studied many, and taking from each her most beautiful and perfect feature gave them to his Venus. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} I
完整的事情……在大自然中选择美，就像蜜蜂从花中采蜜并在它们的作品中使用一样，所有那些在绘画上曾有名声的人都是这样做的。那位必须画维纳斯的古老大师并不满足于只看到一位处女，而是研究了许多，从每一个人那里取其最美、最完美的特征赋予他的维纳斯。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} I
For Michelangelo it is by means of the imagination that the artist attains to a beauty above that of nature, and in this he appears as a Neoplatonist compared with the rational Alberti. To him beauty is the reflection of the divine in the material world. In an early poem he speaks of God’s revelation through beauty:
对于米开朗基罗来说，艺术家通过想象力达到一种超越自然的美，在这点上，他相比于理性的阿尔伯蒂显得更像一位新柏拉图主义者。对他而言，美是神在物质世界中的反映。在一首早期诗中，他谈到通过美显现的上帝：
Colui, che ‘l tutto fe’, fece ogni parte
那创造万物者，造就了每一部分
E poi del tutto la più bella scelse
随后从整体中选出最美的一部分
Per mostrar quivi le sue cose eccelse,
以在此展示他那崇高的作品，
Com’ ha fatto or, con la sua divin’ arte. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
正如他如今以其神圣的艺术所为。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
And from another passage it is clear that the human figure is the particular form in which he finds this divine beauty most clearly manifested:
并且从另一个段落可以清楚看出，人体是他发现这种神圣之美最清晰显现的特殊形式：
Non posso or non veder dentr’ a chi muore
我不能，或无法在临终者体内看见
Tua luce eterna senza gran desio. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
你那永恒的光芒却并未引起强烈渴望。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
In other cases he talks of the inward image which the beauty of the visible world arouses in his mind. The idea of beauty set up in this way is superior to material beauty, for the mind refines the images which it receives, and makes
在其他情况下，他谈到可见世界之美在他心中唤起的内在形象。以这种方式确立的美的观念优于物质之美，因为心灵净化它所接收的形象，并使
them approach more nearly the Ideas which exist in it by direct infusion from God:
这些形象更接近那些通过上帝直接注入而存在于心中的理念：
Mentre ch’alla beltà, ch’i’ viddi in prima
当我初见那美丽
Apresso l’alma, che per gli occhi vede,
紧随其后的，是那因眼而见的灵魂，
L’immagin dentro crescie, e quella cede
心中形象增长，那形象又退却
Quasi vilmente e senza alcuna stima. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
几近卑微且毫无尊重。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
But at this time Michelangelo still firmly believes that the inward image is dependent on the existence of beauty in the outside world which is transformed by the mind into something nobler. In an early sonnet, written in the form of a dialogue, he asks Love:
但此时米开朗基罗仍然坚信，内在的意象依赖于外在世界中美的存在，而这美经心智转化为更高贵之物。在一首以对话体写成的早期十四行诗中，他向爱发问：
Dimmi di grazia, Amor, se gli occhi mei
请告诉我，爱神，若我的眼睛
Veggon ‘1 ver della beltà, ch’aspiro, O s’io l’ho dentro, allor che, dov’ io miro,
看到我渴望的美的真实，或是我把它心怀其中，当我凝视之处，
Veggio scolpito el viso di costei. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
我看见她的脸被雕刻出来了。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
And Love answers:  爱回答说：
  • La beltà che tu vedi, è ben da quella,
    你所见的美，确实来自那位，
Ma crescie, poi ch’a miglior loco sale,
但随着上升到更高之处，它愈发增长，
Se per gli occhi mortali all’ alma corre.
如果对凡人的眼睛，灵魂也奔向。
Quivi si fa divina, onesta e bella,
在那里它变得神圣、庄重而美丽，
Com’ a sè simil vuol cosa immortale.
如同它自己所愿成为的不朽之物。
Questa e non quella a gli occhi tuoi precorre. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
这一种而非那一种先在你的眼前显现。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
These passages may be compared with Raphael’s letters to Castiglione, referring to his fresco of Galatea in the Farnesina,
这些段落可与拉斐尔写给卡斯蒂廖内的信相比较，信中提及他在法尔内西纳的《伽拉蒂亚》壁画，

Michelangelo’s views, therefore, in his first period are still related to those of Alberti, but with a strong tinge of Neoplatonic idealism. For Alberti the artist is entirely dependent on nature in his work, and he can only improve on it by attempting to reach the types at which nature aims. For Michelangelo, on the other hand, the artist, though directly inspired by nature, must make what he sees in nature conform to an ideal standard in his own mind. Compared with Alberti this approach may seem already somewhat unrealistic, but compared with Michelangelo’s later views it represents a close and direct connexion with nature.
因此，米开朗基罗在他的第一个时期的观点仍与阿尔伯蒂有关，但带有强烈的新柏拉图主义理想色彩。对阿尔伯蒂而言，艺术家在创作中完全依赖于自然，只有通过努力达到自然所追求的范型，才能对自然加以改进。另一方面，对米开朗基罗来说，艺术家虽直接受自然启发，但必须使他在自然中所见在自己心中的一种理想标准下得以符合。与阿尔伯蒂相比，这种方法可能已显得有些不切实际，但与米开朗基罗后期的观点相比，它代表了一种与自然的密切而直接的联系。
By about 1530 the attempts of the Papacy to form a powerful secular State in Italy had failed. The Reformation had split the Church and incalculably weakened the position of the Pope. Financial disorders of every kind added to the confusion, and the greatest single blow of all had come with the Sack of Rome in 1527, which left Clement VII almost powerless. The whole social structure on which the Humanist art of High Renaissance Rome was based was swept away. Instead of a sense of security men felt the general disturbance of events, which seemed to threaten the existence of the Catholic Church and, with it, of the whole of Italian society.
到约 1530 年，教皇试图在意大利建立一个强大的世俗国家的努力已经失败。宗教改革分裂了教会，极大地削弱了教皇的地位。各种财务混乱加剧了混乱，而最严重的一击来自 1527 年的劫掠罗马事件，使克莱蒙七世几乎失去权力。构成高文艺复兴时期罗马人文主义艺术基础的整个社会结构被摧毁。人们不再有安全感，而是感到普遍的动荡，这种动荡似乎威胁到天主教会的存在，进而威胁到整个意大利社会。
This changed situation affected different generations in different ways. The older Humanists, men of Michelangelo’s age, had felt that the Roman Church was in need of reform, and had anticipated many of the Pauline features in Luther’s theology. The latter forms in some respects a parallel to Italian Humanism, for, if the Humanists asserted the rights of individual reason, Luther asserted those of individual conscience. The Italian Humanists were too closely involved
这种变化对不同世代产生了不同影响。年长的人文主义者——如米开朗基罗那个时代的人——认为罗马教会需要改革，并预示了路德神学中的许多保罗主义特征。在某些方面，后者与意大利人文主义形成了平行关系，因为如果人文主义者主张个人理性的权利，路德则主张个人良知的权利。意大利人文主义者过于紧密地卷入其中

with the Church of Rome as an institution to follow Luther when it became a question of schism in the Church, but, as long as it appeared possible to combine the more moderate doctrines of reform, particularly Justification by Faith, with fidelity to Rome, many of them were in sympathy with the demands of the German reformers. In this way there was formed a party of Humanists who aimed at an internal reform of the Roman Church and a compromise with the Protestants. This party, which later received the official support of Paul III, was led by men like Contarini, Pole, and Sadoleto, with whom were associated as close followers and supporters Vittoria Colonna and Michelangelo. The religion of the latter now became fervent, and took on the form of a serious but not fanatical piety, consonant with his humanistic principles, but gradually modifying them. He belongs, that is to say, to those who wanted to build up a new and spiritualized Catholicism by means of such reforming doctrines as did not destroy the basis of the Roman Church.
在教会出现分裂的问题上，他们并未像路德那样主张与罗马教廷对立，但只要似乎可以将较温和的宗教改革教义，尤其是“因信称义”，与对罗马的忠诚相结合，许多人就同情德国宗教改革者的要求。这样，一群人文学者形成了一个派别，旨在对罗马教会进行内部改革并与新教徒达成妥协。这个派别后来得到保禄三世的官方支持，领导者有孔塔里尼、波尔和萨多莱托，紧密的追随者和支持者包括维多利亚·科隆纳和米开朗基罗。后者的宗教信仰变得热切，呈现出一种严肃但不狂热的虔诚，与他的人文主义原则相一致，但又逐渐修正这些原则。也就是说，他属于那些希望通过不破坏罗马教会基础的改革教义，来建立一种新的、精神化的天主教的人。
This change of outlook naturally affected Michelangelo’s art, and the change is most clearly shown in the great work of this period, the fresco of the Last Fudgement over the altar of the Sistine Chapel, painted for Clement VII and Paul III between 1534 and 1541. This fresco is the work of a man shaken out of his secure position, no longer at ease with the world, and unable to face it directly. Michelangelo does not now deal directly with the visible beauty of the physical world. When he made the Adam on the Sistine ceiling (Plate 7) he was aiming at a rendering of what would in actual life be a beautiful body, though it was idealized above reality. In the Last Fudgement his aim was different. Here again Adam appears, but his figure is heavy and lumpish, with thick limbs, lacking in grace (Plate 8). The truth is not, as has sometimes been said, that Michelangelo’s hand was failing, but that he was no longer interested in physical beauty for its own sake. Instead he used it as a means of
这种观念的变化自然影响了米开朗基罗的艺术，而这一变化在这一时期的伟大作品中表现得最为清晰，即 1534 年至 1541 年间为克莱门特七世和保禄三世绘制于西斯廷礼拜堂祭坛上的《最后的审判》壁画。这幅壁画出自一个已被动摇的人的手笔，他不再处于安稳的状态，不再对这个世界感到自在，也无法直接面对它。米开朗基罗现在不再直接描绘物质世界的可见之美。当他在西斯廷天顶画出亚当时（图版 7），他的目的是呈现在现实生活中会被视为美的身体，尽管这种呈现高于现实而被理想化。在《最后的审判》中，他的目的则不同。这里同样出现了亚当，但他的形象沉重笨拙，四肢粗壮，缺乏优雅（图版 8）。事实并非如有时所说，米开朗基罗的手艺衰退了，而是他不再单纯为物理美本身而感兴趣。相反，他将其作为一种手段来...
conveying an idea, or of revealing a spiritual state. Judged on the Humanist standard of 1510 the Last Fudgement is a failure, and it is not surprising that the admirers of Raphael could not stomach it. But as the most profound expression of the spiritualized Catholicism which Michelangelo practised, it is a masterpiece of equal importance with the ceiling. The ideals of classic beauty which were relevant in the Sistine ceiling are no longer valid in the Last Fudgement. Such classical features as there are, like the Charon and Minos group, are seen through the eyes of Dante and are given a new spiritual significance. The most fundamental principle of the High Renaissance seems here to have been neglected, for there is little reconstruction of the real world, no real space, no perspective, no typical proportions. The artist is intent only on conveying his particular kind of idea, though the means by which he conveys it is still the traditional Renaissance symbol, the human figure.
传达一个观念，或揭示一种精神状态。按 1510 年的人文主义标准来评判，《最后的审判》是失败的，因此拉斐尔的崇拜者无法接受它也就不足为奇。但作为米开朗基罗所实践的那种精神化天主教最深刻的表达，它与天顶画同样是重要的杰作。西斯廷天顶画中相关的古典美理想在《最后的审判》中已不再有效。像卡戎和米诺斯那样的古典元素，经过但丁的视角被重新解读并赋予新的精神意义。这里似乎忽略了高文艺复兴最根本的原则，因为几乎没有对真实世界的重建，没有真实的空间，没有透视，没有典型的比例。艺术家只专注于传达他特有的观念，尽管他所用的传达手段仍是传统的文艺复兴符号——人体。
The new approach to life and to art which is to be found in the Last Judgement can also be traced in Michelangelo’s writings. In the poems of the thirties and early forties a new attitude towards beauty and towards the problem of love is visible. At this time one of the poet’s most frequent themes is that physical beauty passes away, so that love directed towards it cannot give complete satisfaction and is degrading to the mind:
在《最后的审判》中呈现的这种对生活和艺术的新方法，也可以在米开朗基罗的著述中找到踪迹。在三十年代和四十年代初的诗作中，对美与爱情问题的一种新态度已经显现。那时，诗人最常表现的主题之一是：肉体的美会消逝，因此以之为对象的爱情不能带来完全的满足，且有损心智：
