But this element of bitterness and gloom is balanced by a more optimistic Neoplatonic belief. Love of physical beauty is a cheat, but the true love, that of spiritual beauty, gives perfect satisfaction, does not fade with time, and elevates the mind to the contemplation of the divine. This feeling is expressed most clearly in the poems to Tommaso de’ Cavalieri, who dominates Michelangelo’s emotional life from 1532 onwards. The artist was evidently overwhelmed by the physical beauty of the young man, but he regarded it as an outward sign of spiritual and mental beauty, and the friendship was built upon that basis, though the violence of Michelangelo’s passion was no less than in his earlier affections. This is summed up in a sonnet to Cavalieri:
但这种苦涩与阴郁的成分被一种更为乐观的新柏拉图主义信念所平衡。对肉体之美的爱是欺骗，但真正的爱——对精神之美的爱，能给予完全的满足，不随时间消逝，并提升心智以观想神圣。这种情感在献给托马索·德·卡瓦列里的诗作中表达得最为清晰，自 1532 年起他主导了米开朗基罗的情感生活。艺术家显然被这位青年人的外在美所震撼，但他把这视为精神与心灵之美的外在标志，友谊就在此基础上建立，尽管米开朗基罗激情的强烈程度并不亚于他早年的感情。这一点在献给卡瓦列里的十四行诗中得以概括：

But it must not be supposed that Michelangelo’s view of beauty is wholly incorporeal and spiritualized. Visible beauty is still for him of the greatest significance, since it is the most effective symbol for the true spiritual beauty, and the beauty of man leads more easily than any other means to the contemplation of the divine. Love is stirred up most easily through the eye, which, according to the Neoplatonists, was the noblest of the senses:
但不应假定米开朗基罗对美的看法完全是无形和精神化的。可见之美对他仍具有最大的意义，因为它是指向真正精神之美的最有效的象征，而人的美比任何其他方式更容易引导人进入对神性的凝视。爱情最容易通过眼睛被激发，根据新柏拉图主义者的观点，眼睛是感官中最崇高的：

At this period of his life, therefore, Michelangelo’s poems show strongly the influence of the more mystical elements of Neoplatonism. The strong physical passion of the early love poems has given place to doctrines which make of love the contemplation of an incorporeal beauty. This is only another manifestation of the same tendency which we have traced in the paintings of the second period, such as the Last Fudgement. It is also the equivalent of the spiritualized form of religion with which Michelangelo was associated in the thirties and forties. In all branches of his art and thought we feel a withdrawal from that direct contact with life which characterized the early period.
因此，在他人生的这一时期，米开朗基罗的诗歌强烈表现出新柏拉图主义中较为神秘元素的影响。早期爱情诗中强烈的肉体激情已让位于把爱情视为对无形之美的沉思的学说。这不过是我们在第二时期的绘画（如《最后的审判》）中所追溯到的同一倾向的另一种表现形式。它也是与米开朗基罗在三十至四十年代所结缘的那种精神化宗教形式的等价物。在他艺术和思想的各个分支中，我们都感到他在逐渐远离那种以早期为特征的与生活直接接触。
It may be suggested that this tendency away from the material and towards the things of the spirit can really be put down to the fact that Michelangelo was growing old. No doubt this provides a part of the explanation, but not the whole of it. Not all old men become spiritually minded. They only become so in certain circumstances, and Michelangelo’s mysticism was a mode of escape from finding that his own world had crumbled about him. Age played its part, because had he been younger Michelangelo might have been able to fit himself to the changed circumstances, and have been
可以说，这种从物质转向精神之物的倾向确实可以归因于米开朗基罗日渐衰老。毫无疑问，这构成了解释的一部分，但并非全部。并非所有老人都会变得以精神为重。他们只有在特定环境下才会如此，而米开朗基罗的神秘主义是一种逃避方式，逃避那种发现自己所处的世界已经四分五裂的现实。年老确实起了作用，因为如果他更年轻，米开朗基罗也许能够适应变化的环境，并被
drawn into the Counter-Reformation movement. But the general situation also played its part in breaking up the foundation on which his life was built.
吸引到反宗教改革运动中去。但总体形势也在瓦解他人生所基于的根基方面起了作用。
In those passages of Michelangelo’s poems which refer directly to the art of painting and sculpture we find a change corresponding to that in his ideas on beauty in the abstract.
在米开朗基罗诗歌中那些直接涉及绘画和雕塑艺术的段落里，我们发现了与他关于抽象美的观念变化相对应的转变。
In the first place Michelangelo is much more explicit about the religious function of the arts. Hollanda records a conversation in which Michelangelo explains his idea of the religious painter, who according to him must be skilful in his art and at the same time a man of pious life:
首先，米开朗基罗对艺术的宗教功能表述得更加明确。Hollanda 记载了一次对话，米开朗基罗在其中阐明了他对宗教画家的看法：在他看来，宗教画家必须既有精湛的技艺，又是一个虔诚生活的人：

Often badly wrought images distract the attention and prevent devotion, at least with persons who have but little; while those which are divinely fashioned excite even those who have little devotion or sensibility to contemplation and tears, and by their austere beauty inspire them with great reverence and fear. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
“为了在某种程度上效法我主那庄严的形象，仅仅成为一名画家、一位伟大而熟练的师傅是不够的；我相信人还必须生活无可指责，若可能的话甚至成为圣人，以便圣灵能启发人的理解……常常做得拙劣的图像分散注意力并妨碍虔敬，至少对那些虔敬心不深的人是这样；而那些由神所造的图像即便激发的是少许虔敬或感受的人，也能引起他们的沉思与泪水，并以其朴素的美感激发他们深切的敬畏与惧怕。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}

In the more purely aesthetic part of Michelangelo’s writings on the arts the dominant influence in this period is that of Neoplatonism, which affects his view of the relation of painting to the visible world. Painting is no longer talked of as an imitation of nature, and the artist’s interest is diverted almost entirely towards the inward mental image,

Michelangelo’s theory of sculpture can be deduced from some of the poems, particularly the sonnet beginning:
米开朗基罗的雕塑理论可以从一些诗作中推断出来，尤其是以以下十四行诗开头的那首：
Non ha l’ottimo artista alcun concetto, Ch’un marmo solo in sè non circoscriva Col suo soverchio, e solo a quello arriva La man, che ubbidisce all’ intelletto. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}

The explanation of this idea is to be found in the fact that when Michelangelo speaks of sculpture he always has in mind sculpture in marble or stone and not modelling in clay. ‘By sculpture I mean the sort that is executed by cutting away from the block: the sort that is executed by building up resembles painting.’ 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} For Michelangelo the essential characteristic of sculpture is that the artist starts with a block of stone or marble and cuts away from it till he reveals or discovers the statue in it. This statue is the material equivalent of the idea which the artist had in his own mind; and, since the statue existed potentially in the block before the artist began to work on it, it is in a sense true to say that the idea in the artist’s mind also existed potentially in the block, and that all he has done in carving his statue is to discover this idea.
这一思想的解释在于，当米开朗基罗谈论雕塑时，他始终想到的是大理石或石雕，而不是用粘土塑造。“我所说的雕塑是那种通过从整块材料上切削出来实现的：通过堆积而成的那类则更类似于绘画。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 对米开朗基罗而言，雕塑的本质特征在于艺术家以一块石头或大理石为起点，从中切削，直至显现或发现其中的雕像。这个雕像是艺术家心中观念的物质对应物；并且，由于雕像在艺术家开始工作之前就在石块中潜在存在，从某种意义上可以说，艺术家心中的观念也在石块中潜在存在，他在雕刻雕像时所做的不过是发现这一观念。

This ‘double birth’ corresponds exactly to what we know of Michelangelo’s methods as a sculptor. In general he did not make a full-size clay version for a marble statue, but worked instead from a small model, perhaps only a foot high, which kept before him the idea which he had in his mind. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Starting from this he attacked the block directly, literally uncovering the statue, so that an unfinished figure like the St. Matthew (Plate 9) gives the impression that it is all in the block and that one could just knock off the superfluous marble and reveal the complete statue.
这种“双重诞生”与我们所知的米开朗基罗作为雕塑家的工作方法完全一致。一般来说，他并不为大理石雕像制作全尺寸的粘土模型，而是从一个小模型出发，可能只有一英尺高，这个小模型在他面前保留着他心中构思的形象。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 从此出发，他直接进攻石料，字面意义上是揭示雕像，因此像未完成的《圣马太》（图版 9）这样的作品给人的印象是雕像就存在于石块之中，人们只需敲掉多余的大理石就能显露出完整的雕像。
Certain opinions of Michelangelo’s which are recorded by his immediate followers show that he had almost consciously broken with the ideals of the earlier Humanists. He was opposed, for instance, to the mathematical methods which formed an important part of Alberti’s or Leonardo’s theory. Lomazzo records a saying of his that 'all the reasonings of geometry and arithmetic, and all the proofs of perspective
米开朗基罗的一些观点由其直接追随者记录下来，表明他几乎是有意识地与早期人文主义者的理想决裂。例如，他反对作为 Alberti 或 Leonardo 理论重要组成部分的数学方法。Lomazzo 记录了他的一句名言：“几何与算术的所有推理，以及所有透视的证明
Figure 5: PLATE 9  图 5：图板 9

were of no use to a man without the eye’, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and Vasari attributes to him the saying that ‘it was necessary to have the compasses in the eyes and not in the hand, because the hands work and the eyes judge’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} He disapproved further of the importance which Alberti and the early Renaissance artists attributed to rules in painting, and he seems not to have sympathized at all with their idea that nature was based on general rules and a general orderliness. He condemns Dürer’s treatment of proportion in the human figure as too rigid, saying that this is a matter ‘for which one cannot make fixed rules, making figures as regular as posts’ ; 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and, according to Vasari, 'he used to make his figures in the proportion of nine, ten, and even twelve faces, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} seeking nought else but that in putting them all together there should be certain harmony of grace in the whole, which nature does not present. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} These opinions all show how far Michelangelo in his later period relied on imagination and individual inspiration rather than on obedience to any fixed standards of beauty. The same is true of his attitude towards architecture, for Vasari writes that
对一个没有眼睛的人来说毫无用处’， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 而瓦萨里把这句话归给他，称‘必须把圆规放在眼里而不是手里，因为手在做工而眼在判断’。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 他进一步不赞同阿尔伯蒂和早期文艺复兴艺术家在绘画中对规则所赋予的重要性，而且他似乎根本不同情他们那种认为自然基于普遍规则和普遍秩序的观点。他谴责丢勒在人像比例处理上的过于刻板，称这是一个‘不能制定固定规则的问题，把人物做得像柱子一样规则’； 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 并且据瓦萨里所述，‘他过去常把人物按九、十、甚至十二个头的比例来画， 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 别无所求，只是希望把这些部份组合在一起时在整体上呈现某种优雅的和谐，而自然并不展现出这种东西。’ 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 这些看法都表明米开朗基罗晚期多么依赖想象力和个人灵感，而不是服从任何固定的美的标准。他对建筑的态度也是如此，因为瓦萨里写道：
'he departed not a little from the work regulated by measure, order and rule which other men did according to a common use and after Vitruvius and the antiquities, to which he would not conform . . . wherefore the craftsmen owe him an infinite and everlasting obligation, he having broken down the bonds and chains by reason of which they had always followed a beaten path in the execution of their works. 36 36 ^(36){ }^{36}
“他在相当程度上偏离了那些由度量、秩序和规则所规范的作品，其他人则依照通用做法并遵循维特鲁威及古物的准则行事，而他却不愿顺从……因此工匠们对他负有无尽且永恒的恩情，正是他打破了那些使他们在作品执行中总是沿袭老路的束缚与枷锁。” 36 36 ^(36){ }^{36}
This independence of all rule and the individualism that accompanied it account for the opinion which was generally held in the middle of the sixteenth century that Raphael was the ideal balanced painter, universal in his talent, satisfying all the absolute standards, and obeying all the rules which were supposed to govern the arts, whereas Michelangelo was the eccentric genius, more brilliant than any other artists in his particular field, the drawing of the male nude, but unbalanced and lacking in certain qualities, such as grace and restraint, essential to the great artist. Those, like Dolce and Aretino, who held this view were usually the survivors of Renaissance Humanism, unable to follow Michelangelo as he moved on into Mannerism. That this difference of aim was apparent to Michelangelo himself is evident from his remark recorded by Condivi that ‘Raphael had not his art by nature but acquired it by long study’. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
这种不受任何规矩约束的独立性以及随之而来的个人主义，解释了为何在十六世纪中叶普遍认为拉斐尔是理想的平衡画家：才华通达，满足所有绝对标准，遵守被认为应当统摄诸艺术的各种规则；而米开朗基罗则被看作是古怪的天才，在他特定的领域——男性裸像的素描——比任何其他艺术家都更出众，但不够均衡，缺乏某些对伟大艺术家至关重要的品质，如优雅与克制。持此观点者，如 Dolce 和 Aretino，通常是文艺复兴人文主义的残存者，无法随米开朗基罗进入矫饰主义而继续跟进。Condivi 记载的米开朗基罗自己的一句评语表明他注意到这种目标的差异：“Raphael had not his art by nature but acquired it by long study”。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
In the last fifteen or twenty years of his life we can trace a further change in Michelangelo’s art and ideas, though in some ways this change consists in an intensification of the characteristics of the art and ideas of the late thirties and early forties.
在他生命的最后十五到二十年里，我们可以追踪到米开朗基罗艺术与思想的进一步变化，尽管在某些方面，这种变化只是对三十年代末与四十年代初艺术与思想特征的一种强化。
After about 1545 the situation of the Papacy changed. The schism with Protestantism had reached a more acute stage, and since the Diet of Ratisbon it had become apparent that any kind of compromise was impossible. Therefore the position of the moderate party to which Michelangelo was attached was steadily weakened. The Church could no longer hope to save itself by their methods and was forced to adopt a much more drastic policy. Even Paul III found himself compelled in his last years to give up his attempts at conciliation and to allow the more fanatical CounterReformers to put their ideas into practice. At the Council of Trent the survivors of the Contarini party were defeated,
大约在 1545 年以后，教皇制度的局势发生了变化。与新教的分裂已进入更为尖锐的阶段，自从拉策布隆议会以来，任何妥协已显得不可能。因此米开朗基罗所属的温和派地位逐步被削弱。教会再也无法指望通过他们的方法自我挽救，不得不采取更为严厉的政策。即便保禄三世在晚年也被迫放弃和解尝试，允许更狂热的反宗教改革者将他们的主张付诸实践。在特伦特会议上，Contarini 派的幸存者被击败，
and their rivals, the Jesuits and Caraffa, had their way, gradually establishing their system of blind belief in authority, strict obedience, and absolute rigidity of doctrine.
而与他们对立的耶稣会和 Caraffa 占了上风，逐步确立了对权威的盲目信仰、严格的服从以及教义的绝对僵化的体系。
One result of this change was that the moderates found themselves stranded. They could not sympathize with the new and drastic policy, and yet their own methods seemed useless. Their position was, in fact, hopeless, and for this reason their mysticism gradually takes on a more introspective colour.
这一变化的一个结果是温和派发现自己陷入僵局。他们既不能同情新的严厉政策，又觉得自己的方法无济于事。事实上，他们的处境已无可挽回，因此他们的神秘主义逐渐呈现出更内省的色彩。
Michelangelo’s most representative work in this period is the last group which he carved, the Rondanini Pietà (Plate 6 b 6 b 6b6 b ), left unfinished at his death, in which he seems to have deprived his human symbols of all corporeal quality and to succeed at last in conveying directly a purely spiritual idea. Like most of the other works of this period, such as the Pietà in the Cathedral of Florence, and the group of late drawings, it is concerned with the central features of the Christian faith, the events of the Passion. Michelangelo has given up classical subjects, but even the religious themes which he treats are no longer those which he preferred in his younger days. Then he chose for his subjects either Old Testament figures, like David, or themes from the New Testament, like the Holy Family, which had a direct and general human appeal. When he carved a Pietà, as in St. Peter’s, it was conceived as a human tragedy, without much indication of the supernatural implications (Plate 6a). The Pietà of the last years is an expression of violent, personal, mystical Christian faith, which appears with equal intensity in the drawings for the Crucifixion of the same period.
米开朗基罗在此时期最具代表性的作品是他最后雕刻的一组作品——Rondanini Pietà（第 6 b 6 b 6b6 b 板），遗作未完成。他在其中似乎剥夺了人类符号的一切物质性，最终成功地直接传达出一种纯粹的精神观念。像该时期的大部分其他作品一样，例如佛罗伦萨大教堂的 Pietà，以及那一时期的一组晚期素描，这些作品都集中于基督信仰的核心特征——受难的事件。米开朗基罗已放弃古典题材，即便他处理的宗教主题也不再是年轻时代所偏好的那些。当时他选择的题材要么是旧约人物，例如大卫，要么是具有直接且普遍人类吸引力的新约题材，例如圣家。当他雕刻 Pietà时，如在圣彼得大教堂的那件，构思上是作为一出人类悲剧，较少表明超自然的含义（第 6a 板）。晚年之 Pietà则是强烈的、个人化的、神秘主义的基督信仰的表达，这种强烈在同一时期为受难所做的素描中同样可见。
A corresponding change takes place in Michelangelo’s writings. Much of what has been said about his views in the middle period of his life applies even more strongly to his last years. His approach to the world and the arts becomes even more spiritual, but at the same time more specifically
米开朗基罗的著作中也发生了相应的变化。关于他生命中期观点的大部分论述，在他晚年适用性更强。他对世界和艺术的态度变得更加精神化，但同时也更加具体化
Christian. His religious feeling now combines the mystical conception of Neoplatonism with the intense belief in Justification by Faith which he learnt from Savonarola and the Contarini group. But he talks less of an abstract divine essence and more of a God whom he addresses personally. We may suppose that his comment on the paintings of Fra Angelico, which shows how much importance he attributed to Christian piety in an artist, was made about this time: "This good man painted with his heart, so that he was able with his pencil to give outward expression to his inner devotion and piety, which I can never achieve, since I do not feel myself to have so well disposed a heart.
