In Michelangelo we have an example of that rare phenomenon, the great artist who is both able and willing to put in writing what he feels about his art. The value of these writings to us depends largely on the light which they throw on the artist’s work in painting and sculpture. It is possible to enjoy and even to understand the frescoes on the Sistine roof without reading any of the sonnets, but the appreciation of both the poetry and the paintings can be increased by the comparison of the one with the other; and in the case of Michelangelo’s latest works, like the Rondanini Pietà, the exposition in words in the late sonnets of the ideas expressed more obscurely, but not less completely, in the carved forms of the statue may provide a clue to the meaning of the latter, for which any one unacquainted with the poems might long search without success. We could deduce the changes traceable in Michelangelo’s view of life from his paintings and sculpture, but the evidence of the written word is more compelling, because less liable to misinterpretation; and an hypothesis based on the former is more than doubled in strength when it is confirmed by the latter. The changes that have been traced above, however, are not merely those of a single individual. For Michelangelo was the type of those men who belonged to the Renaissance but lived on into the early stages of the Counter-Reformation. The development in his ideas, therefore, follows the change from one epoch to another, and prepares the way for the art and doctrines of Mannerism.
在米开朗基罗身上，我们看到一种罕见现象的范例：这位伟大的艺术家既有能力又愿意把他对艺术的感受写出来。这些著述对我们的价值，很大程度上取决于它们为我们理解他在绘画与雕塑方面的作品所提供的启示。即便不读任何十四行诗，也可能欣赏甚至理解西斯廷教堂天顶壁画，但将诗歌与绘画相互比较，能增加对二者的鉴赏；而在米开朗基罗晚期作品如罗丹尼尼悲悯像（Rondanini Pietà）的情况下，晚年十四行诗中用文字阐述的那些在雕像雕刻形式中以更为晦暗但并不逊色的方式表达的思想，可能为后者的意义提供线索，否则不熟悉这些诗的人可能会徒劳无功地长时间探寻。我们可以仅从米开朗基罗的绘画与雕塑推断出他人生观的可追溯变化，但书面语的证据更具说服力，因为它不易被误解；若基于前者形成的假设又被后者所证实，其论证力便不止倍增。 然而，上文所追溯到的变化并非仅属于某一位个人。因为米开朗基罗正是那类属于文艺复兴却延续至反宗教改革早期的人的典型。 因此，他思想的发展遵循了从一个时代向另一个时代的转变，并为矫饰主义的艺术与学说铺平了道路。

Chapter VI  第六章

THE MINOR WRITERS OF THE HIGH RENAISSANCE
盛期文艺复兴时期的次要作家

IN general the High Renaissance in Italy did not produce the outburst of theoretical works which might have been expected from it. The reason may be that in the early sixteenth century the arts were at a peak in their development when theory for a moment seemed unnecessary. In the Quattrocento the ideas which artists were working out were so new and exciting that they demanded theoretical treatment. In the early Cinquecento the newly discovered territory had been thoroughly absorbed. There was little to dispute in the field of the arts, since all were agreed on a more or less fixed set of doctrines worked out by the previous generation. Critics, therefore, could only go on copying down in palatable form a common stock of accepted ideas. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
总体上，意大利的盛期文艺复兴并没有产生可能被预期的大量理论著作。原因可能在于十六世纪初，各种艺术已经达到发展的高峰，理论一时显得不必要。十五世纪的艺术家们所探索的思想如此新颖且振奋人心，以至需要理论化的处理。而十六世纪初新发现的领域已被彻底吸收。在艺术领域几乎没有争论可言，因为所有人对前一代人提出并确立的一套或多或少固定的学说基本上达成了一致。因此，评论家们只能以悦耳的形式继续记录这一共同的被接受的思想库。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
More interesting than these popularizers is a small group of Venetian critics who wrote about the middle of the century. The Disegno of the Florentine Antonio Francesco Doni, published in Venice in 1549, provides nothing of theoretical interest, but from the works of three other writers we can form some idea of what the Venetians thought about painting in the middle of the Cinquecento. These writers are Paolo Pino, whose Dialogo di Pittura appeared in 1548; Michelangelo Biondo, who published his Della Nobilissima Pittura in the next year; and Lodovico Dolce, whose dialogue
比这些通俗化作者更有趣的是一小群在世纪中叶撰述的威尼斯批评家。佛罗伦萨人 Antonio Francesco Doni 的 Disegno 于 1549 年在威尼斯出版，理论价值不大，但从另外三位作家的作品中我们可以大致了解十六世纪中期威尼斯人对绘画的看法。这三位作家是 Paolo Pino（其 Dialogo di Pittura 见于 1548 年）；Michelangelo Biondo（次年出版了他的 Della Nobilissima Pittura）；以及 Lodovico Dolce，其对话
THE MINOR WRITERS OF THE HIGH RENAISSANCE 83
高文艺复兴时期的次要作家 83
L ′ L ′ L^(')L^{\prime} Aretino, printed in 1557 , will be chiefly discussed in the chapter on religious painting.
L ′ L ′ L^(')L^{\prime} Aretino，印于 1557 年，关于宗教绘画的内容将在相应章节中主要讨论。
These treatises were written at the moment when Venetian painting was hovering on the edge between the Renaissance and the Mannerist periods. Titian, the great figure of the older generation, was slowly changing his style, abandoning his early sensuous manner, and turning towards a more dramatic, emotional, and religious style. Among the younger artists Tintoretto, Paris Bordone, and the Bassani were tending whole-heartedly towards Mannerism, while a few major figures such as Veronese continued in the earlier Venetian tradition.
这些论文写作于威尼斯绘画在文艺复兴与矫饰主义时期边缘徘徊之时。提香，作为老一代的巨匠，正在慢慢改变他的风格，放弃早期感官化的笔触，转向更具戏剧性、情感性和宗教性的风格。在年轻一代艺术家中，丁托列托、巴黎·博尔多内和巴萨尼家族则全心倾向于矫饰主义，而像维罗内塞这样的一些重要人物则继续沿袭早期的威尼斯传统。
We find the same division of feeling and the same hesitation among the critics. Much of what they say is simply the traditional matter of earlier Renaissance treatises. Pino, Dolce, and Biondo all three draw extensively on Alberti, Biondo even copying several chapters from him almost word for word, and the commonplaces from Pliny and other ancient writers fill a large part in each of the treatises.
我们在批评家中也发现了相同的情感分歧和犹豫。他们所说的许多内容其实只是早期文艺复兴论文的传统材料。皮诺、多尔切和比翁多三人都大量借鉴了 Alberti，比翁多甚至几乎逐字逐章地抄袭了他，而来自普林尼和其他古代作家的陈词滥调在每一篇论文中都占有很大比重。
Although his dialogue was the latest of the three in date, Dolce belongs more closely to the Renaissance than the other two critics. The theme of his dialogue is that Michelangelo is not so great a master as is generally supposed, and that Raphael and Titian at least are his superiors. It will be seen later that Dolce, who was largely acting as a mouthpiece for Aretino in this dialogue, had personal reasons for wishing to decry Michelangelo whom he certainly admired, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} but probably he genuinely thought that Michelangelo was a one-sided artist in comparison with Raphael, and that in his later work, particularly in the Last Fudgement, he was falling off from his earlier standard. It would be consistent with his strictly Renaissance view to regard the Mannerist idiosyncrasies of the Last Fudgement as freaks and signs of decadence. To him Raphael was the perfect example of a balanced Humanist
尽管他的对话在三者中成书最晚，Dolce 却比另两位批评家更贴近文艺复兴。其对话的主题是米开朗基罗并不像人们普遍认为的那样是多么伟大的大师，拉斐尔和提香至少在某些方面优于他。后文将看到，Dolce 在这部对话中在很大程度上充当了 Aretino 的代言人，他有个人理由想要贬低他确实欣赏的米开朗基罗， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 但他大概真心认为与拉斐尔相比，米开朗是一个偏颇的艺术家，而且在晚期作品中，尤其是在《最后的审判》中，他已经不如早期水平。根据他严格的文艺复兴观点，将《最后的审判》中的风格怪癖视为怪现象和颓废的迹象是合乎情理的。对他来说，拉斐尔是和谐人文主义者的完美典范

84 THE MINOR WRITERS OF THE HIGH RENAISSANCE
84 高文艺复兴时期的小作家

artist, skilful in all the branches of his art, and not devoting himself to the pursuit of one quality only as Michelangelo concentrated, according to him, on the drawing of the nude. But even above Raphael he places Titian as the greatest painter of the period, a balanced artist, with supreme mastery of colour. In certain passages Dolce protests against practices which are particularly associated with Mannerism. He disapproves of the use of foreshortening when it is introduced irrelevantly only to display the skill of the artist; 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} also of the habit of making every figure affectedly elegant, a trick of the Mannerists who followed Parmigianino. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Dolce has great respect for the ancients, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and prefers the easy elegance of Raphael to the terribiltà of Michelangelo-a distinction which at this date is equivalent to the opposition of Renaissance to Mannerism. One point is discussed explicitly in Dolce which had only been indirectly dealt with by earlier writers, namely, the right of the layman who does not himself paint to judge in questions of art. Earlier writers of the Renaissance seem to have assumed that the educated layman was competent to judge everything except the technical part of a painting, but Dolce expresses this opinion clearly. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} This view, based on the idea that painting is a learned pursuit and the sister of poetry, is again typical of Dolce’s Humanist outlook.
艺术家，精通其艺术的各个分支，而不是像米开朗基罗那样只专注于追求某一品质——据他说米开朗基罗专注于裸体的造型。但即便超过拉斐尔，他仍将提香列为本时期最伟大的画家，一位均衡的艺术家，具有对色彩的绝对驾驭力。在某些段落中，Dolce 反对一些特别与矫饰主义（Mannerism）相关的做法。他反对在没有必要的情况下使用透视缩短，仅仅为了炫耀画家的技巧；也反对把每个人物都刻意描绘得优雅做作，这是追随 Parmigianino 的矫饰派的把戏。Dolce 非常尊重古人，并且更偏爱拉斐尔那种轻松的优雅，而不是米开朗基罗的惊世之气——在这个时期，这一区别等同于文艺复兴与矫饰主义的对立。Dolce 明确讨论了一个要点，早期作家们只曾间接涉及，即不亲自作画的外行人在艺术问题上进行评判的权利。 早期的文艺复兴作家似乎认为有教养的门外汉有能力判断一切，除了绘画的技术部分，但多尔切明确表达了这种观点。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 这种观点基于绘画是一门有学问的追求并且是诗歌的姊妹这一观念，再次体现了多尔切的人文主义视角。
Paolo Pino is more divided in his attitude. He has the proper Humanist feeling that the painter must be born with a natural talent for his art; 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} and in his attitude on the matter of facility, to which the Mannerists attributed such importance, he is still on the side of the Renaissance, maintaining that great speed and great slowness are both to be avoided. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} On the other hand, he speaks more as a Mannerist when he demands that the artist shall display his virtuosity by in-
保罗·皮诺在态度上更加分裂。他具有正统的人文主义情怀，认为画家必须天生具有艺术天赋； 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 在关于技巧熟练度的问题上——这是矫饰派极为重视的方面——他的立场仍倾向于文艺复兴，主张既要避免极快亦要避免极慢。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 另一方面，当他要求艺术家通过……来展示其技艺时，他的论调更像矫饰派。
THE MINOR WRITERS OF THE HIGH RENAISSANCE
文艺复兴盛期的次要作家
genious foreshortenings in his paintings. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} In another passage he hints at the theory of Eclecticism, when he says that if Titian and Michelangelo could have combined their talents they would have made the perfect artist. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} This is an idea which constantly recurs in later Mannerist writings, and it is also reported as a maxim of Tintoretto.
在他的画作中有天才般的透视缩短技巧。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 在另一段中，他暗示了折衷主义的理论，当他说如果提香和米开朗基罗能够结合他们的才能，他们本可以造就完美的艺术家。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 这是一个在后来的矫饰主义著作中经常出现的观点，并且据说也是丁托列托的一句格言。
Michelangelo Biondo is in general a mere plagiarist with no feeling for painting at all. All his ideas are borrowed from traditional Renaissance sources, but the treatise ends with the description of ten subjects for paintings, in the manner of Philostratus, in which the writer shows himself much closer to Mannerist ideals. The descriptions are a mixture of Neoplatonic imagery, freely interpreted mythology, and scholastic symbolism-in fact, just the elements which we shall later see brought together in the pure Mannerist writings on the arts.
米开朗基奥·比翁多总体上只是一个缺乏绘画感觉的剽窃者。他的所有想法都借自传统的文艺复兴来源，但这篇论著以对十个绘画题材的描述结束，采用菲洛斯特拉托斯式的风格，在这些描述中，作者表现得更接近矫饰主义的理想。这些描述混合了新柏拉图主义意象、自由阐释的神话和经院符号学——事实上，正是后来我们将在纯粹的矫饰主义美术著作中看到的那些要素。
2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Ibid., p. 24.   2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 同上，第 24 页。

Chapter VII  第七章

VASARI  瓦萨里

THE political disturbances of the early sixteenth century affected different parts of Italy in different ways. Something has already been said of the chaos produced in Rome by the Sack of 1527. In Florence this episode was the signal for a new outburst of popular feeling. The Medici were driven out, and for a time a popular government ruled the city. But by 1531 the Medici were reinstated, and this time they took care to destroy even those traces of democracy which they had tolerated before 1527. The government of the city became undisguisedly autocratic, and nothing but the name remained of the old republic. During the pontificate of Clement VII and the early years of Paul III the connexion between Florence and Rome was strong, but when the Papacy, about 1545, launched out into the militant phase of the Counter-Reformation the tie grew steadily weaker. For several decades Florence was less affected than most Italian cities by the spirit which inspired reformers of the Caraffa type. Its government remained purely secular, and even the Inquisition was subject there to state control. There was never felt in Florence that bitter spiritual disillusionment which came over Michelangelo in Rome, nor the fighting Christian spirit personified in St. Ignatius.
十六世纪早期的政治动荡对意大利不同地区产生了不同影响。前面已谈到过 1527 年洗劫罗马所造成的混乱。在佛罗伦萨，这一事件成为新一轮民众情绪爆发的信号。美第奇家族被驱逐，城市一度由民众政权统治。但到 1531 年，美第奇复位，这一次他们注意摧毁那些在 1527 年前曾容忍的民主痕迹。城市的统治公开变得专制，旧共和国不过只剩名称而已。在克莱门特七世教宗在位期间和保禄三世的早年，佛罗伦萨与罗马的联系仍然紧密，但大约自 1545 年教廷进入反宗教改革的好战阶段后，这一联系逐渐削弱。数十年间，佛罗伦萨受卡拉法那类改革者所激励的精神影响比大多数意大利城市轻，其政权仍保持纯粹世俗化，甚至宗教裁判所也在那里受国家控制。 在佛罗伦萨，从未感受到米开朗基罗在罗马经历的那种痛苦的精神幻灭，也没有像圣依纳爵那样具象化的战斗基督教精神。
The art of Florence in the mid-sixteenth century is therefore a pure court art. The constitution of the city was too autocratic for it to produce a Humanist art like that of Rome under Julius II, but it was also too secular to produce the spiritualized painting of Michelangelo in his later years, or of later Roman Mannerism. Florentine Mannerism, as represented in the painting of Vasari or Bronzino, has neither the rationalism of early Quattrocento Florentine painting, nor
因此，十六世纪中叶的佛罗伦萨艺术纯粹是一种宫廷艺术。该市的宪制过于专制，无法产生像尤利乌斯二世时期罗马那样的人文主义艺术，但又过于世俗，无法产生米开朗基罗晚年那种精神化的绘画，或后期罗马矫饰主义的风格。以瓦萨里或布朗齐诺绘画为代表的佛罗伦萨矫饰主义既没有十五世纪早期佛罗伦萨绘画的理性主义，也没有
the emotional intensity of Michelangelo’s Last Judgement, nor the organized didacticism of Taddeo Zuccaro.
米开朗基罗《最后审判》的那种情感强度，也没有塔德奥·祖卡罗那样的有组织的教化性。
It is still a form of Renaissance art in the sense that many elements of classicism survive in it, but they are all transformed to suit the court tone which painting had assumed. The classical culture of the Florentine Mannerists has lost its aggressive quality. It is no longer progressively rational, but has become elegant and ingenious. Artists generally turn for their subjects either to the glorification of the Medici or to allegorical mythology, so involved that a volume is needed to explain a fresco cycle such as Vasari’s in the Palazzo Vecchio. Religious subjects are treated in much the same way. Bronzino’s frescoes in the chapel of Eleanor of Toledo in the Palazzo Vecchio are variations on the theme of the human figure, entirely freed from any spiritual significance; and Vasari’s religious paintings are of the same kind. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} The actual style grows elegant, sweet, and affected. Nothing survives from the real High Renaissance style except its skill and its worldliness. Its energy and rationalism have gone.
它仍然是一种文艺复兴艺术，因其保留了许多古典主义元素，但这些元素都被改造以适应绘画所采用的宫廷风格。佛罗伦萨矫饰主义者的古典文化已失去其锋芒。它不再是进步的理性，而是变得优雅而巧妙。艺术家通常以颂扬美第奇家族或寓言式神话为题材，如此复杂，以至于需要一卷书来解释像瓦萨里的帕拉佐·韦基奥壁画那样的壁画循环。宗教题材也以类似方式处理。布朗齐诺在帕拉佐·韦基奥为埃莉诺·德·托莱多小教堂所作的壁画，是对人体主题的变奏，完全摆脱了任何精神意义；瓦萨里的宗教画也是同一类型。实际的风格变得优雅、柔美且矫揉造作。除了技巧和世俗性之外，真正的盛期文艺复兴风格已无所保留。它的活力和理性主义已不复存在。
As is to be expected in the art produced in a court of this kind, it was only in portraiture that any real discoveries were made. Here Pontormo and still more Bronzino evolved a new style in which elegance was combined with a certain formalism of pose and minute naturalism of detail.
正如在这种宫廷所产生的艺术中可预料的那样，真正的发现只出现在肖像画领域。在这里，Pontormo，尤其是 Bronzino，发展出一种新风格，将优雅与某种姿态上的程式化以及细节上的细微写实结合起来。
The equivalent in theory to Florentine painting of the mid-sixteenth century is provided by the writings of Vasari. There are other sources, such as Cellini’s treatises on the goldsmith’s and the sculptor’s arts, or Benedetto Varchi’s Lezioni, but these are too slight to be of use except in supplementing and confirming what we find in Vasari. Of Vasari’s own works only the Lives are of serious interest from
与十六世纪中期佛罗伦萨绘画在理论上的等价物是 Vasari 的著作。还有其他来源，例如 Cellini 关于金匠与雕塑艺术的论述，或 Benedetto Varchi 的 Lezioni，但这些著作过于零碎，除了补充和证实我们在 Vasari 中所发现的内容外，别无大用。就 Vasari 本人著作而言，只有 Lives 从理论角度具有重要意义，
the point of view of theory, since the Ragionamenti only contain an exposition of the allegories in a single cycle of paintings, and the letters are not in general illuminating. From the Lives, on the other hand, it is possible to form some idea of what Vasari thought about the arts.
因为 Ragionamenti 只是对单一绘画系列中寓意的阐述，而书信通常并不具有启发性。另一方面，从 Lives 中可以对 Vasari 对艺术的看法形成一些认识。
The material, however, is not convenient to handle. The Lives were first published in 1550 under the title LeVite de’ più eccellenti Architetti, Pittori et Scultori Italiani, and were reissued in 1568 in very much enlarged form. Apart from the actual biographies, in which scattered comments on the function of the arts can be found, there are certain sections of the work devoted mainly to theoretical discussion. Of the two prefaces the first contains the arguments about the superiority of painting over sculpture, and the second a history of art from the earliest times up to Cimabue. There are also three introductions devoted to painting, sculpture, and architecture respectively, in the main filled with technical details, but containing also some general comments. Finally there is a proemio to each of the three parts into which the Lives are divided, and in these the general characteristics of the period in question are discussed.
不过，这些材料不便于处理。《名家传》（Le Vite de’ più eccellenti Architetti, Pittori et Scultori Italiani）首次出版于 1550 年，1568 年以大幅增补的版本重刊。除去实际的传记（其中可找到零散的关于艺术功能的评论）外，书中还有若干章节主要用于理论讨论。两篇前言中，第一篇论证了绘画优于雕塑的观点，第二篇则叙述了从最早时期直到契马布埃的艺术史。书中还分别有三篇关于绘画、雕塑和建筑的导言，主要充斥着技术细节，但也包含一些概论性的评论。最后，传记分为三部分，每一部分都有一篇开篇论述（proemio），在这些开篇中讨论了所涉时期的一般特征。
At first sight there seem to be many remains of High Renaissance theory in Vasari, but when they come to be examined it appears that all the elements surviving have been altered and given a new meaning.
乍一看，瓦萨里的著作中似乎保留了许多盛期文艺复兴理论的遗存，但细加考察便会发现，所有幸存的要素都被改造并赋予了新的意义。
For Vasari, as for Alberti, the foundation of any theory of painting is that this art consists in the imitation of nature. One of his highest forms of praise for a painting is to say that the figures are so natural that they seem alive, and in the preface to the Lives he says: 'Our art is all imitation, of nature for the most part, and then, because a man cannot by himself rise so high, of those works that are executed by those whom he judges to be better than himself. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This quotation is typical, for when Vasari says ‘imitate nature’ he nearly always
对瓦萨里而言，正如对阿尔伯蒂一样，任何绘画理论的基础在于这种艺术是对自然的模仿。他对一幅画的最高赞誉之一，就是说人物如此逼真，仿佛活着一样；在《艺人传》的前言中他写道：“我们的艺术全是模仿，大多是模仿自然，其次，因为人不能单凭自己达到那么高的境界，就模仿那些他认为比自己更优秀之人的作品。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这一引语具有代表性，因为当瓦萨里说“模仿自然”时，他几乎总是
qualifies it in such a way that in the end the reader is left with the impression that there are many other things more important for the artist to pursue than the rendering of nature. It is at least as vital, for instance, that he should learn from studying other painters, for, as Vasari says with reference to Titian, whose style is too naturalistic for his taste: 'He who has not drawn much nor studied the choicest ancient and modern works cannot . . . improve the things that he copies from life, giving them the grace and perfection in which art goes beyond the scope of nature. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This view that art can excel nature is evidently one in which Vasari believed firmly, for it is repeated in several contexts throughout the Lives. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} He is therefore far from agreeing with Leonardo that the only hope of the artist lies in the greatest possible truth to nature. In fact in the life of Domenico Puligo he implies an actual contrast between beauty and naturalism:
将其限定为一种方式，最终让读者产生这样的印象：对于艺术家来说，有许多比再现自然更重要的追求。例如，他至少同样需要通过研究其他画家来学习，正如瓦萨里在谈及提香时所说的，提香的风格对他而言过于自然化：“没有大量素描也没有研究精选的古今作品的人，不能……改进从生活中临摹来的事物，赋予它们那种艺术超越自然范围的优雅与完美。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这种艺术可以超越自然的观点显然是瓦萨里坚信的观点，因为在《名人传》的多个语境中都有重复出现。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 因此，他远非同意列奥纳多所持的观点，即艺术家唯一的希望在于对自然达到最大的忠实。实际上，在多梅尼科·普利戈的传记中，他暗示了美与自然主义之间的实际对立：
'I have seen some heads portrayed from life by his hand, which, although they have, for example, the nose crooked, one lip small and the other large, and other such like deformities, nevertheless resemble the life, through his having well caught the expression of the subject; whereas, on the other hand, many excellent masters have made pictures and portraits of absolute perfection with regard to art, but with no resemblance whatever to those that they are supposed to represent. And to tell the truth, he who executes portraits must contrive, without thinking of what is looked for in a perfect figure, to make them like those for whom they are intended. When portraits are like and beautiful, then they may be called rare works, and their authors truly excellent craftsmen. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
“我曾见过他亲手根据生活描绘的一些头部作品，尽管这些作品中有的鼻子歪斜，有的一侧嘴唇小而另一侧大，及其他类似的畸形，但因他能准确捕捉被摄者的神情，仍然与现实相似；另一方面，许多杰出的画家在艺术上可能画出绝对完美的构图和肖像，但却与他们应当表现的人毫无相似之处。说实话，画肖像的人必须设法使其像被画者，而不去考虑在完美人体中所追求的那些东西。当肖像既相似又美丽时，它们才能称得上是稀世之作，其作者才是真正卓越的工匠。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Alberti admitted that exact imitation was not in itself enough to produce perfect beauty, but he would never have allowed the direct contrast between likeness and beauty made by Vasari.
阿尔伯蒂承认，单纯的精确模仿本身不足以产生完美的美，但他绝不会像瓦萨里那样把相似与美对立起来。
The latter’s attitude towards nature is illustrated by another small point. One of his principal reasons for recommending the careful study of nature is that it is the only means by which the artist can reach a stage where he can draw anything from memory with ease and without reference to the model.
后者对自然的态度可以由另一个小细节说明。他推荐仔细观察自然的主要原因之一是，这是艺术家达到能够轻松地、不参考模特就从记忆中绘制任何事物的唯一途径。
'The best thing is to draw men and women from the nude and thus fix in the memory by constant exercise the muscles of the torso, back, legs, arms and knees, with the bones underneath. Then one may be sure that, through much study, attitudes in any position can be drawn by help of the imagination without one’s having the living forms in view. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
“最好的方法是以裸体绘制男女，从而通过不断练习把躯干、背部、腿、臂和膝盖的肌肉，以及其下的骨骼，牢牢固定在记忆中。这样，人便可以确信，经过大量研究后，借助想象力可以在没有观察活体的情况下绘出任何姿势。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
The study of nature is not therefore an end in itself, but a means to efficiency in drawing from memory. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
因此，对自然的研究本身并不是目的，而是为了能够高效地从记忆中作画的手段。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
There are passages in the Lives which at first sight recall Alberti, particularly when Vasari is talking of the necessity of choosing from nature: 'Manner then attained to the greatest beauty from the practice which arose of constantly copying the most beautiful objects, and joining together these most beautiful things, hands, heads, bodies, and legs, so as to make a figure of the greatest possible beauty. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} But in reality the meaning of such a passage is different from that which Alberti would have given it. For the selection from nature is now to be made according to an entirely different principle from his. The artist is now no longer to choose the reasonable mean, the general and the typical; he is to choose according to his judgement. And with Vasari judgement is
在《传记》中有些段落乍看之下会让人联想到 Alberti，尤其是当 Vasari 谈到从自然中取材的必要性时：“风格遂因不断临摹最美之物、并将这些最美的事物——手、头、躯体与腿——拼合在一起以构成可能的最美形象而达到至高之美。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} ”但实际上，此类段落的含义与 Alberti 所赋予的不同。因为从自然中取舍如今应遵循与他完全不同的原则。艺术家不再选择合理的中庸、普遍与典型；他应按其判断来选择。而在 Vasari 那里，判断是
not, as with Alberti, a rational faculty; it is rather an instinct, an irrational gift, allied to what we call taste, and residing not so much in the mind as in the eye.
不是像阿尔贝蒂那样的理性能力；它更像是一种本能，一种非理性的天赋，与我们所称的品味相近，更多地存在于眼睛而非心灵中。
It will be remembered that with Alberti the perfection of proportion in the human body was arrived at by a more or less mathematical computation, by averaging the measurements which were the foundation of all the proportions which he gave. Vasari draws a contrast between the results arrived at by measurement and those reached by judgement, which seems to work independently of any such rational mode of calculation. In talking of the artists of the Quattrocento he says: 'In proportion there was wanting a certain correctness of judgement, by means of which their figures, without having been measured, might have, in due relation to their dimensions, a grace exceeding measurement. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} And in the introduction on sculpture he makes the situation even clearer: 'But no better standard can be applied than the judgement of the eye; for even though a thing is perfectly measured, if the eye is still offended, it will not cease to censure it. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
应当记得，在 Alberti 那里，人体比例的完美是通过或多或少的数学计算得到的，即通过对构成他所给出的一切比例基础的测量值取平均。Vasari 将通过测量得出的结果与通过判断得出的结果作了对比，后者似乎独立于任何此类理性计算方式而起作用。在谈到十五世纪的艺术家们时他说：“在比例上缺少某种判断的准确性，借助这种准确性，他们的人物即使未经测量，也能在与其尺寸相称的关系中，展现出超越测量的优雅。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 而在关于雕塑的序言中他把情况说得更清楚：“但没有比目光的判断更好的标准；因为即便某物被完美地测量过，若仍得罪于眼，眼也不会停止责难它。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
This final appeal to the eye is typical of Florentine Mannerist painting and of Vasari’s outlook. For the group of artists which he represents, painting had ceased to be the intensely serious intellectual pursuit that it had been for the artists of the High Renaissance. It had become rather a game of skill, appealing to a love of ingenuity and leaving the rational faculties undisturbed.
这种最终对视觉的诉求是佛罗伦萨矫饰主义绘画和瓦萨里的观点的典型表现。对他所代表的那群艺术家来说，绘画不再是高文艺复兴时期艺术家们所从事的那种极为严肃的智性追求。相反，它更像是一种技巧的游戏，诉诸于对独创性的喜爱，同时不去打扰理性机能。
Several characteristics in the main group of Florentine Mannerists and in Vasari bring out this lowering of the intellectual and emotional tone of art. For a painter like Bronzino or a theorist like Vasari painting consists primarily in the rendering of the naked human form, whereas an earlier Renaissance artist like Leonardo made human action and emotion his principal interest. To Michelangelo the naked
佛罗伦萨主要矫饰派群体和瓦萨里身上有若干特征，凸显出艺术在智性和情感基调上的这种降低。对像布隆齐诺这样的画家或像瓦萨里这样的理论家而言，绘画主要在于表现裸体人体形，而早期文艺复兴艺术家如莱昂纳多则把人体的动作和情感作为他的主要兴趣。对米开朗基罗而言，裸体
human body was certainly the first object for the artist’s consideration, but, as we have seen, he saw in it a reflection of a spiritual and divine beauty, and in his later years he used it to convey intensely tragic feelings. For Vasari the nude was simply the unit in a jig-saw puzzle, to be twisted and fitted into a decorative scheme. Of course the artist needed some excuse for painting the nude, and therefore he became ingenious in finding stories which could be supposed to involve naked figures, but the imagination was allowed much latitude in this. In a letter to Aretino, Vasari, speaking of a painting he had executed, says: 'As you will see, I have painted a group of naked figures fighting, first to show my skill in art, and secondly to follow the story, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and it appears later that there is no reason at all to suppose from the story that the characters were not fully dressed.
人体无疑是艺术家首先考虑的对象，但正如我们所见，他在其中看到的是一种精神与神圣之美的映照，而在晚年又用它来传达强烈的悲剧情感。对 Vasari 而言，裸像仅仅是拼图中的一个单元，要被扭曲并嵌入装饰构图中。当然，画家需要某种借口来描绘裸体，因此他在寻找可被设想为包含裸体人物的故事时变得足智多谋，但在这方面想象力被赋予了很大的自由。在写给 Aretino 的一封信中，Vasari 谈到他所作的一幅画时说：“如你所见，我画了一组裸人搏斗，首先是为了展示我的艺术技巧，其次是为了遵从故事， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 而后来看来根据故事完全没有理由认为这些人物不是全副衣着的。”
The drawing of the nude was, therefore, an object in itself, and it is remarkable how Vasari’s obsession with it obscures his judgement of other artists’ work. When he talks of Michelangelo’s Last Judgement, which he admires deeply, he seems to be describing an academic exercise in trick drawing. It is for him ‘an exemplar in foreshortenings and all the other difficulties of art’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The point of the Last Fudgement to him is that it ‘opened out the way to facility in this art in its principal province, which is the human body’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} The expression of the passions is only mentioned by the way, and the emotional significance of the painting is not spoken of at all.
因此，裸体素描本身就是一个独立的对象，值得注意的是，瓦萨里对它的痴迷如何模糊了他对其他艺术家作品的判断。当他谈到他非常钦佩的米开朗基罗的《最后的审判》时，他似乎在描述一种学院派的透视技法练习。对他来说，那是“透视缩短以及艺术中所有其他难点的范例”。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 在他看来，《最后的审判》的要点在于它“为这种艺术的主要领域——人体——的熟练开辟了道路”。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 激情的表达只是顺带提到，画作的情感意义根本未被谈及。
But this dislike of any kind of emotion in art appears in Vasari’s comments on other artists as well. It is characteristic that he strongly disapproves of Pontormo’s Certosa frescoes, in which is expressed the religious intensity of the early attempts at reform in Florence. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} The effect of tragedy, which Pontormo could only convey in forms borrowed from northern late Gothic art, was strongly distasteful to Vasari who pre-
但这种对艺术中任何情感的不喜，在瓦萨里对其他艺术家的评论中也有体现。他强烈不赞同庞托尔莫的卡托尔萨（Certosa）壁画这一点很有代表性，后者表达了佛罗伦萨早期改革尝试中的宗教强度。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 悲剧效果，庞托尔莫只能借用北方晚期哥特式艺术的形式来传达，这让瓦萨里极为反感，因他更倾向于...
ferred his placid early works, painted under the influence of Andrea del Sarto. For the same reasons he dislikes Beccafumi’s later paintings in which, he maintains, the heads show ‘an expression of terror by no means agreeable’. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
偏爱他早期的宁静作品，那些在 Andrea del Sarto 影响下创作的。出于同样的原因，他不喜欢 Beccafumi 后期的画作，认为这些画中人物的头部“流露出极不讨人喜欢的惊恐表情”。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
The crucial feature in the whole of Vasari’s theory is the appearance of the new quality of grace, la grazia. This word had, of course, been applied to painting before Vasari’s time, but only in a sense vaguely interchangeable with beauty or differing at most in degree from beauty. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} With Vasari it takes on a quite new function; it is distinguished from beauty and even contrasted with it. It is never clearly defined in the Lives, but by bringing together different passages we can see that beauty is a rational quality dependent on rules, whereas grace is an undefinable quality dependent on judgement and therefore on the eye. It also very soon becomes apparent that it is in grace and not in beauty that Vasari is most genuinely interested. He speaks of ‘delicacy, refinement and supreme grace’ as ‘the qualities produced by the perfection of art’, and if these are lacking it is not enough in a figure that ‘the limbs as a whole are in accordance with the antique and have a certain correct harmony in the proportions’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Correctness cannot produce grace. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
在瓦萨里的整个理论中，关键特征是新的品质“优雅”（la grazia）的出现。当然，这个词在瓦萨里之前已被用于绘画，但只是以一种可以与美互换或至多在程度上与美有所不同的含义存在。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 在瓦萨里这里，它获得了全新的功能；它与美相区分，甚至与之对立。虽然在《名人传》中它从未被明确定义，但通过汇集不同段落我们可以看到，美是一种依赖规则的理性品质，而优雅是一种依赖判断、因此依赖于眼力的难以言明的品质。很快也显而易见，瓦萨里真正感兴趣的更多是优雅而非美。他将“细腻、精致与至高的优雅”称为“由艺术完美所产生的品质”，而如果缺乏这些，仅仅一个人物“整体四肢符合古代风格且在比例上有某种正确的和谐”是不够的。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 正确性无法产生优雅。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
A passage quoted above in connexion with Vasari’s use of the word ‘judgement’ is so relevant to the meaning which he attaches to grace that it must be referred to again. It is
上面引用的一段话与瓦萨里使用“判断”一词所联系的含义密切相关，因而必须再次提及。那段话是
his summing up on the masters of the Quattrocento: 'In proportion there was wanting a certain correctness of judgement, by means of which their figures, without having been measured, might have, in due relation to their dimensions, a grace exceeding measurement. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The dependence of grace on judgement and therefore ultimately on the eye is established in this sentence; and in other passages Vasari gives a number of more revealing hints about the nature of grace.
他对十五世纪大师的总结：“在比例上缺乏某种判断的正确性，借此他们的人物在未被测量的情况下，仍能与其尺寸适当关联，表现出超越测量的优雅。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这句话确立了优雅依赖于判断、从而最终依赖于目光；在其他段落中，瓦萨里还给出了许多更能揭示优雅本质的暗示。
Grace is, for instance, usually contrasted with the serious and the sublime. In comparing Leonardo and Raphael, Vasari says that though the latter could not equal Leonardo in ‘a certain sublimity of ideas and grandeur of art’, yet he approached near to him in sweetness, in facility, and in ‘the grace of colouring’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} And elsewhere he speaks of ‘those who, delighting little in the highest and most difficult flights of art, love things that are seemly, simple, gracious and sweet’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
例如，优雅通常与庄重和崇高形成对比。在比较列奥纳多与拉斐尔时，瓦萨里说虽然后者在“某种思想的崇高性和艺术的宏伟上”不能与列奥纳多相匹敌，但在甜美、流畅以及“色彩的优雅”方面却接近于他。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 在别处他又谈到“那些很少沉醉于艺术最高且最艰难的飞跃，而喜爱体面、简洁、优雅与甜美之物的人”。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
This connexion of grace with sweetness and softness is regular in Vasari. In the life of Masolino it is closely associated with morbidezza and sfumato effects; 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} a work of Giullo Romano is said to lack grace because of its dark and heavy colouring; 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} and the figures of Quattrocento artists are said not to show the muscles ‘with that sweet and facile grace which hovers midway between the seen and the unseen’. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} The same conclusion, that grace springs from sweetness and elegance, can be drawn from the list of artists whom Vasari particularly praises for this quality: Raphael, Parmigianino, and Perino del Vaga.
在瓦萨里作品中，这种将优雅与甜美和柔和相连的说法是常见的。在马索利诺的传记里，这与 morbidezza 和 sfumato 效果密切相关； 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 朱里奥·罗马诺的一件作品被认为缺乏优雅，因为其用色阴暗沉重； 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 四十世纪艺术家的形象被认为没有以“那种介于可见与不可见之间盘旋的甜美而轻巧的优雅”来表现肌肉。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 同样可以从瓦萨里特别称赞具有这种品质的艺术家名单得出结论：拉斐尔、帕尔米贾尼诺和佩里诺·德尔·瓦加。
But what, in the last resort, gives the clearest idea of grace in the sense used by Vasari is its connexion with facility. Rapidity and ease of execution were not qualities pursued by Quattrocento artists for their own sake or recommended by the theorists of that period. On the contrary, care and exactness in working seem to be their first object, and speed
但从根本上讲，最能体现瓦萨里所用“优雅”意义的，是它与熟练的联系。迅速与轻松的表现并非四十世纪艺术家为了自身目的而追求的品质，也非那个时期理论家所推荐的。相反，细致与精确的工作似乎是他们的首要目标，而速度
or slowness seems to be a matter of relative indifference to them. The Mannerists, however, prided themselves that they could establish records in covering wall-space. In his autobiography Vasari boasts that he executes his works ‘not only with the greatest possible rapidity, but also with incredible facility and without effort’, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and that this is no empty boast is proved by his performance in the Palazzo della Cancelleria in Rome, where he frescoed the big hall in a hundred days. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
或缓慢对他们来说似乎是相对无关紧要的。然而，矫饰主义者却以能在覆盖墙面方面创下纪录为荣。在他的自传中，瓦萨里自夸他“不仅以尽可能最大的速度完成作品，而且以令人难以置信的轻松与毫不费力的方式”完成， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 瓦萨里在罗马的枢密院宫（Palazzo della Cancelleria）的大厅里以一百天完成壁画的事实证明这并非空话。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
Any trace of laboriousness, any evidence that the artist has sweated over his work will destroy the grace of a painting, and will give to it what in Vasari’s judgement is the fatal quality of dryness. The whole Quattrocento is condemned by Vasari as dry. The artists of that day gave ‘proof of diligent study’ in finishing their paintings, but ‘study when it is used in that way to obtain finish, gives dryness to the manner’, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and it was only after Leonardo that painters were able to achieve that ‘perfect grace, brought about by the disappearance of a certain dryness, hardness and sharpness of manner which had been left to our art by the excessive study of Piero della Francesca’ and others. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Uccello is the artist most strongly reproved for his excessive industry, particularly in perspective, his obsession for which showed lack of judgement. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
任何费力的痕迹，任何显示出艺术家为作品流过汗水的证据，都会破坏一幅画的优雅，并会赋予它在 Vasari 判断中那种致命的枯燥特质。整个十五世纪被 Vasari 谴责为枯燥不堪。彼时的艺术家在完成画作时表现出“刻苦学习的证据”，但“当学习被用来追求精致时，会使风格变得枯燥”， 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 而且直到达·芬奇之后，画家们才得以达到那种“完美的优雅，这是通过消除某种由 Piero della Francesca 等人过度研究所遗留给我们艺术的枯燥、生硬和尖锐的风格而实现的”。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Uccello 因其过度的勤勉而受到最严厉的指责，尤其在透视方面，他对透视的痴迷显示了判断力的缺乏。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
The artist must therefore pursue ‘the grace and facility that give most pleasure to the eye’. But facility will not only produce grace; it has other advantages, such as bringing with it boldness: 'Many painters . . . achieve in the first sketch of their work, as though guided by a sort of fire of inspiration, something of the good and a certain measure of boldness;
因此艺术家必须追求“给予眼睛最大愉悦的优雅与流畅”。但流畅不仅会产生优雅；它还有其他优点，比如伴随而来的大胆：“许多画家……在作品的第一稿中，仿佛受某种灵感之火引导，达成了某种良好与一定程度的大胆；
but afterwards, in finishing it, the boldness vanishes. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Any undue effort or strain will destroy the effect of inspiration. It was disastrous, for instance, in the case of Uccello: ‘for the spirit of genius must be driven into action only when the intellect wishes to work and when the fire of inspiration is kindled, since it is then that excellent and divine qualities and marvellous conceptions are seen to issue forth.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
但随后在完工时，这种大胆就消失了。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 任何过度的努力或勉强都会破坏灵感的效果。例如在乌切罗的情况下就是灾难性的：‘因为天才之灵只能在理智愿意工作并且灵感之火被点燃时被驱使行动，正是在那时才能见到卓越与神圣的品质以及奇妙的构想显现出来。’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
From what has already been said of Vasari’s conception of grace and facility it will not be surprising to find that he makes them both derive from a natural gift which cannot be acquired by pains and study. 'Very great is the obligation that is owed to Heaven and to Nature by those who bring their works to birth without effort and with a certain grace which others cannot give to their creations either by study or by imitation. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} On the other hand, an artist is to be blamed if he does not take the trouble to cultivate his natural talent. Parmigianino, for instance, is taken to task by Vasari for this reason: 'If Francesco, who had from nature a spirit of great vivacity, with a beautiful and graceful manner, had persisted in working every day, little by little he would have made such proficiency in art, that, even as he gave a beautiful, gracious and most charming air to his heads, so he would have surpassed himself and the others in the solidity and perfect excellence of his drawing. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
根据前面关于瓦萨里对“恩赐”（grace）与“灵便”（facility）观念的论述，不难发现他把两者都归因于一种无法通过刻苦和学习获得的天赋。 “那些不费力便能孕育出作品，并以一种他人既不能通过学习也不能通过模仿赋予其创作的某种优雅的手法，使人对天与自然负有极大的感激之情。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 另一方面，如果艺术家不费心去培养他的天赋，则应受到谴责。例如，瓦萨里就以此责备帕尔米贾尼诺：‘若弗朗切斯科自天赋有极为生动的精神，且具有优美而雅致的风格，若能坚持每日作画，渐渐地他在艺术上本会取得如此的造诣，以致他在赋予人物头部以优美、雅致及极其迷人的神态方面，必同时在描绘的稳固性与完美卓越上超越他自己和他人。’ 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} ”
Vasari, therefore, approves of careful study and hard work in one way and disapproves of them in another. His solution to the problem of combining grace with the more solid excellence of draughtsmanship is as follows: 'As a result of the study and practice of many years the hand must be free and skilled in drawing and copying whatever nature has produced. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} That is to say, the artist must train himself by careful study and diligent copying to attain complete efficiency in drawing and painting natural objects. Over this he can
因此，瓦萨里在某种意义上赞同细致的学习和辛勤的工作，而在另一种意义上又不赞同。他对如何将优雅与更为扎实的绘图技巧结合起来的问题的解决如下：“通过多年的学习和实践，手必须在绘制和临摹大自然所造之物时变得灵活且熟练。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 意即，艺术家必须通过刻苦学习和勤勉临摹来训练自己，以在描绘和绘画自然物体方面达到完全的熟练。在此之上，他可以”
spend indefinite pains and care; but, when it comes to the actual execution of a particular work, he must act as rapidly as possible so that no traces of his effort may appear on the canvas. When he has reached perfect proficiency the artist will be able to draw whatever he wants from memory, without reference to the model at all.
要付出无数不定的辛劳和细心；但在具体作品的实际执行上，他必须尽可能迅速地行动，以便在画布上不显露任何劳动的痕迹。当他达到完美的熟练程度时，艺术家将能够完全凭记忆绘出他想要的任何东西，根本不需要参照模特。
Vasari was the first writer to elaborate the theory of grace in connexion with painting, but in itself it was no invention. For Vasari only applied to the arts the conception of grace as a necessary part of behaviour which had been evolved by the writers on manners, particularly by those of the Neoplatonic school, such as Castiglione. Indeed, the account of grace in its social sense in the Cortegiano is so close to Vasari’s view of it applied to the arts, that we may conclude that he derived the idea direct from this source.
瓦萨里是首位将“优雅”理论与绘画联系起来详加阐述的作家，但这一概念本身并非他所发明。瓦萨里只是将作为行为必要部分的“优雅”这一观念应用到艺术上，该观念由论述礼仪的作家们发展而来，尤其是新柏拉图学派的作家，如卡斯蒂廖内。事实上，《宫廷之人》中关于“优雅”的社会意义的论述与瓦萨里将其应用于艺术时的观点极为接近，因此我们可以断定他是直接从这一来源汲取了这一思想。
In the first book of the Cortegiano Castiglione gives instructions which the courtier must follow in his relations with other men. At the end of these one of the speakers in the dialogue says: "The Courtier ought to accompany all his doings, gestures, demeaners, finally all his motions with a grace. And this, me thinke, ye put for a sauce to everie good thing, without which all his other properties and conditions were litle worth. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} Grace, therefore, is that extra quality which is added to the more solid ‘properties’ and ‘conditions’ which can be acquired by precept. Grace, on the other hand, cannot be learnt; it is a gift from heaven; and it comes from having a good judgement. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} It will vanish if a man takes too much pains to attain it, or if he shows any effort in his actions. Nothing but complete ease can produce it. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} And the only effort which should be expended in attaining it is an effort to conceal the skill on which it is based; 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} and it is from
在《宫人论》第一卷中，卡斯蒂廖内讲述了宫廷人在与他人交往时必须遵循的准则。在这些准则的结尾，对话中的一位发言者说道：“宫廷人应当以一种优雅伴随他的一切行为、手势、举止，最后甚至是一切动作。我认为，你们把它当作任何美好事物的调味品，缺少它，他的一切其他属性和条件都不值一提。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 因此，优雅是一种额外品质，附加在那些可通过教诲获得的更为稳固的‘属性’和‘条件’之上。另一方面，优雅无法被学会；它是来自天赐的礼物；它源于良好的判断力。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 若一个人为追求它而过于费力，或在行为中显露任何用力之态，它就会消失。唯有完全的从容才能产生它。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 而在获得它时，唯一应付出的努力是努力掩饰构成它的技艺； 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 并且它源自于”
sprezzatura, or recklessness, as Hoby translates it, that grace springs. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} These are almost exactly the principles which Vasari lays down for the acquisition of grace in painting; and the parallel is completed by the comparison which Castiglione makes of the grace which he recommends and the methods of ancient painters: 'They say that also, it hath been a proverb among some most excellent painters of olde time, that Too much diligence is hurtfull, and that Apelles found fault with Protogenes, because he could not keepe his handes from the table (i.e. panel). ′ 2 ′ 2 ^('2){ }^{\prime 2} The fact that Vasari’s grace derives from a book of court manners shows the real significance of the idea in his works. With Humanists of the Quattrocento, painting had reached the position of being a learned art; with Vasari it was acquiring good manners.
sprezzatura，或如 Hoby 所译的那样“鲁莽”，正是优雅产生的来源。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这些几乎正是 Vasari 为获得绘画中的优雅所提出的原则；而 Castiglione 将他所推荐的那种优雅与古代画家的方法相比较，则使这一类比更加完整：‘他们还说，古时有些最杰出的画家中流传着一句谚语，过分的勤勉有害，而 Apelles 曾责备 Protogenes，因为他无法把手从画板（即面板）上收回来。’ ′ 2 ′ 2 ^('2){ }^{\prime 2} Vasari 的“优雅”源自一本宫廷礼仪书，这一点表明了这一观念在他作品中的真实意义。对十五世纪的人文学者来说，绘画已成为一门博学的艺术；而在 Vasari 这里，绘画则在获得良好的礼仪。
Since, however, Vasari’s main importance is not as a theorist but as an historian of art, something must be said of his historical approach. In its general lines his attitude is that traditional among Florentine historians from Villani and Ghiberti onwards. Art rose to its highest point in ancient Greece and Rome; it declined with the fall of the Roman Empire, sinking lower and lower during the period of barbarian domination; it made its first steps to recovery in Tuscany with Cimabue, and each of its successive advances was made by a Florentine artist-first by Giotto, then by Masaccio in painting, and Brunelleschi in architecture. Vasari merely carries on the line by putting another great Florentine, Michelangelo, as the peak to which the whole development of the arts led.
然而，瓦萨里的重要性主要不在于作为理论家，而在于作为艺术史家，因此必须谈一谈他的历史方法。总体而言，他的态度延续了从维拉尼（Villani）和吉贝尔蒂（Ghiberti）等佛罗伦萨史学家以来的传统。艺术在古希腊和古罗马达到顶峰；随着罗马帝国的灭亡而衰落，在野蛮人统治时期越来越低落；在托斯卡纳，随着契马布埃（Cimabue）开始出现复兴的初步迹象，而其后每一次进步都是由佛罗伦萨的艺术家推动——首先是乔托（Giotto），然后是马萨乔（Masaccio）在绘画方面，以及布鲁内莱斯基（Brunelleschi）在建筑方面。瓦萨里只是延续了这一脉络，将另一位伟大的佛罗伦萨人米开朗基罗（Michelangelo）置于整个艺术发展所指向的顶峰。
At moments Vasari’s patriotism becomes childish, or, at least, disturbs his historical judgement. He tries, for instance, to persuade himself that the arts originated not in Chaldaea or in Egypt, as was generally maintained, but in his native Etruria. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} In the life of Costa he admits rather grudgingly
在某些时刻，瓦萨里的爱国主义显得幼稚，或者至少干扰了他的历史判断。例如，他试图说服自己，艺术并非像通常认为的那样起源于迦勒底或埃及，而是起源于他的故乡伊特鲁里亚（Etruria）。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 在科斯塔（Costa）传记中，他相当勉强地承认了
that there have been good artists who were not Tuscans, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} but he rarely treats them with the respect which he allows to the men of his own country. Duccio, for instance, only gets two pages as against Giotto’s twenty-five; and in writing of artists like Titian his prejudice constantly bursts out.
他承认也有非托斯卡纳的好艺术家， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 但他很少像对待本国人那样尊重他们。例如，Duccio 只有两页，而 Giotto 却有二十五页；在写到像 Titian 这样的艺术家时，他的偏见也常常暴露出来。
But in certain other ways he shows much greater balance in his judgement than would be expected. He realizes that an artist must be judged in connexion with his historical setting, and that it is foolish to condemn a painter of the Trecento for not being as realistic as one of the Cinquecento. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 'My intention has always been to praise not absolutely but, as the saying is, relatively, having regard to place, time and other similar circumstances. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Therefore artists of the earlier period can receive due praise for their contribution towards the general movement of painting from the barbarism of the Middle Ages to the cultured naturalism of the Renaissance. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
但在某些其他方面，他的判断却表现出比人们预期的更大的平衡。他意识到艺术家必须联系其历史背景来评价，而去指责一位十四世纪的画家不如十六世纪的画家写实是愚蠢的。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} “我的意图向来不是绝对地赞美，而是如俗语所说，作相对的评价，考虑到地点、时间及其他类似情况。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 因此，早期时期的艺术家可以因他们在将绘画从中世纪的野蛮状态推进到文艺复兴的有教养的自然主义这一总体运动中的贡献而得到应有的赞扬。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
Vasari’s attitude, however, is not absolutely constant, and certain differences can be traced between the views expressed in the 1550 edition and those which appear in the much enlarged edition of 1568 . In his treatment of history there is a tendency in the second edition for the author’s patriotism to be a little less evident than in the first. The first is constructed solely to praise Florentine artists, with the life of Michelangelo as the climax. In the later edition nonFlorentine artists are allowed more generous treatment, and though Michelangelo is still quite clearly the author’s favourite, others are allowed to have approached, or even equalled him in certain respects. Raphael in particular, though he is not allowed to compete with Michelangelo in the field of drawing, is admitted to be a more balanced artist,
然而，Vasari 的态度并非一成不变，在 1550 年版与大幅增补的 1568 年版之间可以追溯出若干差异。在处理历史时，第二版中作者的爱国主义倾向比第一版略显淡化。第一版完全以歌颂佛罗伦萨艺术家为构架，以米开朗基罗的生平作为高潮。在后来的版本中，对非佛罗伦萨艺术家的待遇更为宽厚，尽管米开朗基罗仍然明显是作者最喜爱的，但其他人被允许在某些方面接近甚至与他并驾齐驱。特别是拉斐尔，虽然在素描领域并不被允许与米开朗基罗竞争，但被承认是一个更为均衡的艺术家，
and even the Venetians whose main interest was in colour are more kindly treated in 1568 than in 1550 .
甚至那些主要兴趣在色彩方面的威尼斯画派在 1568 年比 1550 年受到的对待也更为友善。
In the matter of theory there is one important passage added in the second edition to the chapter on painting in the introduction. This passage is the only one in which Vasari attempts anything approaching a general and abstract definition, and, though the result is not at all clear, the passage is of interest. He tries to define drawing, and he says of it that
在理论方面，在引言中关于绘画的一章的第二版中增加了一段重要的论述。这段话是瓦萨里唯一一次尝试进行接近一般性和抽象性定义的内容，虽然其结果并不十分清晰，但这段话仍然值得注意。他试图定义素描，并这样描述它：
‘proceeding from the intellect it extracts from many things a universal judgement, like a form or idea of all the things in nature. . . . From this knowledge there proceeds a certain idea or judgement, which is formed in the mind, and this idea to which expression is given by the hands is called drawing. It can therefore be concluded, that this drawing is simply a visible expression and manifestation of the idea which exists in our mind, and which others have formed in their mind and created in their imagination.’
“出自理性，它从许多事物中抽取出一个普遍的判断，像是自然万物的某种形式或观念……从这种知识产生一种特定的观念或判断，这在心中形成，而这种由手去表达的观念就称为素描。因此可以得出结论，这种素描仅仅是我们心中存在的观念以及他人也在他们心中形成并在想象中创造的观念的一种可见的表达和显现。”
Vasari is ill at ease among these abstract terms, but it is significant that he attempts to give some theoretical foundation to the arts. This account is based on Aristotelian ideas, and forms a prelude to the revival of abstract aesthetics among the later Mannerists. The prominence given to the Idea prepares us for the theories of Lomazzo and more particularly of Federico Zuccaro, whose version of Aristotelian doctrines will be discussed in a later chapter. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
瓦萨里在这些抽象术语面前感到不自在，但值得注意的是他试图为艺术提供某种理论基础。这一论述以亚里士多德的思想为依据，并为后期矫饰派中抽象美学的复兴作了序幕。对“理念”的强调为洛马佐，特别是费德里科·祖卡罗的理论铺垫了道路，后者那种亚里士多德学说的版本将在后一章中讨论。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
The tradition of criticism which Vasari had inaugurated in Florence was carried on by a small group of followers. None of these has anything of great originality to contribute to aesthetics, but they are just worthy of mention. The most important is Raffaello Borghini, whose long treatise, Il Riposo, published in 1584, is the best source for the biographies of the later Florentine Mannerists. From the theoretical point of view it is less interesting, for Borghini takes his ideas almost word for word from Vasari. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} The one point worth noting about the book is that Borghini is writing not only for artists but also for those who, without actually painting themselves, yet want to be in a position to judge works of art. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} No writer of a full-dress treatise on painting before Borghini had set out with this intention.
瓦萨里在佛罗伦萨开创的评论传统由一小群追随者继续发扬。虽然后来者在美学上并无重大原创贡献，但仍值得一提。最重要的是拉斐尔·博尔吉尼（Raffaello Borghini），其长篇论著《Il Riposo》，发表于 1584 年，是关于晚期佛罗伦萨矫饰派艺术家传记的最佳资料。从理论角度看则趣味甚微，因为博尔吉尼几乎逐字采纳了瓦萨里的观点。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 这本书值得注意的一点是，博尔吉尼的写作对象不仅限于艺术家，也包括那些虽不亲自作画但希望能够评判艺术作品的人。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 在博尔吉尼之前，还没有哪位撰写完整绘画专论的作者以这种意图开篇。
Even Vasari always addresses himself to his fellow artists, and the same is true of all earlier critics, except those like Equicola who only write of painting incidentally. In other ways Borghini continues along the lines laid down by Vasari. He talks little of the imitation of nature, and much of the importance of such qualities as grace. His formula for achieving this is in exact agreement with the practice of most Florentine Mannerists: give your figures small heads and long limbs, and they will have the required elegance. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
即便是瓦萨里也总是对同为艺术家的同行们讲话，早期所有评论家也是如此，只有像 Equicola 那样只是顺便写到绘画的人除外。在其它方面，Borghini 继续沿着瓦萨里所奠定的路线前进。他很少谈论模仿自然，而更多谈论诸如优雅这类品质的重要性。他对达成这种效果的公式与大多数佛罗伦萨矫饰主义者的做法完全一致：把人物的头画小，四肢画长，这样他们就会具有所需的优雅。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
Vincenzo Danti was a Perugian by birth, but his devotion to the manner of Michelangelo attaches him to the Florentine group. Of the fifteen books in which he composed his treatise on proportion only one was published, in 1567 . The sole purpose of the writer seems to have been to expound the ideas of Michelangelo, whose authority is quoted on every page, and whose works are the foundation for every law that is laid down. The third member of the group is Francesco
Vincenzo Danti 生于佩鲁贾，但他对米开朗基罗风格的崇敬将他归入佛罗伦萨流派。在他所撰写的关于比例的十五卷著作中，只有一卷于 1567 年出版。作者的唯一目的似乎是阐述米开朗基罗的理念，其权威在每一页中被引用，其作品成为所提出每一条法则的基础。该流派的第三位成员是 Francesco

VASARI  瓦萨里

Bocchi, who wrote one of the earliest guide-books to Florence, and also published a short work entitled Eccellenza della statua di S. Giorgio di Donatello. This pamphlet contains little that is new or interesting, but it is typical of Florentine Mannerism in the stress which it lays on movement as the greatest source of beauty in the human figure.
博奇（Bocchi）撰写了最早的佛罗伦萨导游书之一，并出版了一本名为《Eccellenza della statua di S. Giorgio di Donatello》的短册子。该小册子鲜有新颖或有趣之处，但典型地体现了佛罗伦萨矫饰主义（Mannerism），强调动作是人体美的最大来源。

Chapter VIII  第八章

THE COUNCIL OF TRENT AND RELIGIOUS ART
特伦特会议与宗教艺术

THE kinds of painting which are commonly grouped together under the term ‘Mannerism’ are far from being uniform. Different parts of Italy, being at different stages of development and affected in different ways by the political disasters of the sixteenth century, produced styles as varied as those which they evolved in the early Renaissance. In Michelangelo’s later work we saw the tragic mystical form of Mannerism; Vasari represents the aristocratic version of the style suited to the court of the Medici. In this section we shall consider the official style of religious art, which came into existence under the influence of Rome and Trent, and the theories which accompanied it. The various forms of Mannerism differ in many ways among themselves, but, compared with the art of the High Renaissance, they have much in common with each other; for they were all produced against the common background of the political and religious reaction which the alliance of the Papacy with Spain made possible after 1530 . It will therefore be necessary before going further to consider this historical situation out of which Mannerism arose.
通常被归入“矫饰主义”（Mannerism）一词下的绘画类型远非单一。同一时期意大利不同地区处于不同的发展阶段，且在 16 世纪政治灾难的影响下各有不同，因此产生的风格与早期文艺复兴时期一样多样。在米开朗琪罗的晚期作品中，我们看到了矫饰主义的悲剧性神秘形式；瓦萨里则代表了适合美第奇宫廷的贵族化风格。本节我们将考察在罗马与特伦特影响下形成的官方宗教艺术风格及其伴随的理论。各种矫饰主义形式彼此之间有诸多差异，但与盛期文艺复兴艺术相比，它们之间有许多共通之处；因为它们都是在 1530 年后教皇与西班牙结盟使之可能的政治与宗教反动的共同背景下产生的。因此，在进一步讨论之前，有必要考察这一产生矫饰主义的历史背景。
Paradoxically, the ultimate results of the events centring round the Sack of Rome was to strengthen rather than to weaken the power of the Papacy in Italy. Clement, almost more frightened by the revolution in Florence than by the Sack itself, realized that resistance to Charles was useless, and that his only hope lay in an alliance with Spain. The old foundations on which Italian greatness was built were gone. The great merchant republics, like Florence and Venice, had been doomed since the fall of Constantinople and the discovery
具有讽刺意味的是，围绕洗劫罗马事件的最终结果是加强而不是削弱了教皇在意大利的权威。克莱孟对佛罗伦萨的革命几乎比对洗劫本身更为惊恐，他意识到抵抗查理是徒劳的，唯一的希望在于与西班牙结盟。意大利伟大所建立的旧基础已经消失。像佛罗伦萨和威尼斯这样的伟大商贸共和国，自从君士坦丁堡陷落和新航路的发现以来就已注定衰落。
of America had destroyed the command of the Mediterranean over the most important trade-routes, and Rome itself was ruined by the schism in the Church. If Italy was to keep any position in Europe it would clearly have to be by new means, and the alliance with Spain seemed to offer just the right opportunity.
美洲的发现已摧毁了地中海对最重要贸易航线的控制，教会的分裂也使罗马本身衰败不堪。如果意大利要在欧洲保有任何地位，显然必须通过新的手段，而与西班牙的联盟似乎正好提供了这样的机会。
After 1530 the Papacy was still the most powerful single State in Italy, but it was a changed Papacy, for its policy was now dominated by its new ally. Now, compared with the Italian republics or with the States of north-western Europe, Spain was socially and politically behind the times. It was still more than half feudal, and was only just emerging as a modern State. Therefore by its change of policy about 1530 the Papacy moved from a leading place among the progressive States of Italy to one of reaction. It still aimed at dominating the whole peninsula, but it was going to do so with the support, not of the merchants and bankers, but of a foreign power with almost feudal ideas and methods.
1530 年以后，教皇国仍然是意大利最强大的单一国家，但已经成为一个改变后的教皇国，因为其政策现在被新盟友所主导。与意大利的诸共和国或西北欧的各国相比，西班牙在社会和政治上已落后于时代。它仍有一半以上保留封建性质，才刚刚作为一个现代国家出现。因此，约在 1530 年通过其政策转变，教皇国从意大利进步诸国中的领导地位转向了反动一方。它仍然以统治整个半岛为目标，但将不再依靠商人和银行家的支持，而是依靠一个持有几乎封建观念和方法的外国强权。
The aim of Papal policy in the second half of the sixteenth century was not to strengthen the State of which the Popes of the High Renaissance had laid the foundations, but to establish ecclesiastical absolutism as far as possible in Italy; and to achieve this aim it was prepared to use any means, gentle or forcible. In its ultimate results the most fatal action of the Papacy at this time was probably the introduction of the suicidal Spanish system of taxation, for it hurried on the economic collapse which must in any case soon have overtaken Italy. But from the more general point of view the essential characteristic of the earlier stage of the CounterReformation is that it is an attempt to return to the ecclesiastical domination which the Church had held during the Middle Ages.
十六世纪下半叶教皇政策的目标并非加强高文艺复兴时期教皇们所奠定的国家，而是在意大利尽可能建立教会专制；为了达到这一目标，它准备采用一切手段，无论温和或强制。从最终结果来看，那时教皇权最致命的举措大概是引入了自杀性的西班牙税收制度，因为此举加速了本来迟早会降临意大利的经济崩溃。但从更一般的角度看，反宗教改革早期阶段的本质特征在于它试图回归教会在中世纪所拥有的统治地位。
In the intellectual field this meant that the movement was opposed to all the achievements of Renaissance Humanism. The individual rationalism of Humanism had played
在思想领域，这意味着该运动反对文艺复兴人文主义的一切成就。人文主义的个人理性主义已经发挥了
a considerable part in the development of the Reformation, and Humanism was therefore anathema to the CounterReformers. It was their aim to undo all that the Renaissance had achieved, and to get back to a feudal and medieval state of affairs. The movement was just as much a CounterRenaissance as a Counter-Reformation, and it set itself to destroy the human scale of values in which the Humanists believed and to replace it once again with a theological scale such as had been maintained during the Middle Ages.
在人文主义在宗教改革发展中发挥了相当大的作用，因此人文主义对反宗教改革者来说是被诅咒的。他们的目标是撤销文艺复兴所取得的一切，回到封建和中世纪的状态。该运动既是一次反宗教改革，也是一次反文艺复兴运动，其旨在摧毁人文主义者所信奉的人类价值尺度，并再次以中世纪时期所维持的神学尺度取而代之。
One of the first objects of the Counter-Reformers was to abolish the right of the individual to settle all problems of thought or conscience according to the judgement of his own personal reason. They wished instead to set up the acceptance of authority, which was exactly the principle that the Humanists had succeeded in destroying. Their attitude can best be seen from the weapons which they used to enforce their ideas. Of these the most powerful were the Inquisition and the Society of Jesus. The assumption underlying the former was that no latitude could be allowed in matters of dogma, in which the decisions of the Church were to be blindly followed. The latter was built up like a military organization on the basis of absolute, unquestioning obedience. The effect of institutions like this and of the spirit that lay behind them was the destruction of individual thought. As has been said, ‘the sacrifice of the intellect was demanded, not its dedication’, and therefore those few thinkers who were courageous enough to go on with their speculations either took to purely innocuous and abstract fields, or like Bruno, came into conflict with the authorities.
反宗教改革者的首要目标之一是废除个人按其个人理性判断解决一切思想或良心问题的权利。他们反而希望确立对权威的服从，这恰恰是人文主义者所成功摧毁的原则。他们的态度可从他们用以强制推行思想的武器中最佳地看出。其中最有力的是宗教裁判所和耶稣会。前者的前提是教义问题上不能容许任何自由度，必须盲目遵从教会的裁决。后者则以绝对的、毫无质疑的服从为基础，建立起类似军事组织的体制。像这样的机构及其背后的精神的效果就是对个人思想的摧毁。如前所述，“要求的是对智力的牺牲，而非其奉献”，因此那些仍有勇气继续进行思辨的少数思想家，要么转向完全无害且抽象的领域，要么像布鲁诺那样，与当局发生冲突。
This is, of course, only the negative side of the CounterReformation, of which the positive is provided by the intense desire of men like Caraffa to reform the Church, and by the passionate and unselfish devotion of the Jesuits to the spreading of what they believed to be the truth.
这当然只是对反宗教改革的消极一面，其积极方面则由像卡拉法（Caraffa）这样的人士对教会改革的强烈愿望，以及耶稣会士为传播他们认为的真理所表现的热情而无私的奉献所体现。
On the arts the effect of the Counter-Reformation was the
对艺术而言，反宗教改革的影响是
same as in other branches of culture and thought. After about 1530 the Humanist school of painting which had flourished in Rome at the beginning of the century gradually falls into decay. Artists no longer make new discoveries about the outside world. Their work is largely controlled by the Church, and, even when they are allowed a certain freedom, they seem to have lost their interest in what lies around them. Their preoccupation is no longer with the reconstruction of the visible universe, but with developing new methods of drawing and composition. They are not breaking new ground, but rather exploiting what their predecessors had discovered for them and turning their discoveries to new purposes. They abandon the Renaissance ideals of convincing space and normal proportions, and make almost as free use as a medieval artist of arbitrary construction and deliberate elongation. For the restrained and realistic colouring of the Renaissance they substitute tones which appeal directly to the emotions rather than to the mind. In fact, in many ways the Mannerists are nearer to the artists of the Middle Ages than to their immediate predecessors. And this is true not only of matters of technique but also of the subjects which artists seem to choose for preference. At the time of the High Renaissance artists preferred those which had a wide appeal. Even when they painted religious subjects, they were able to find those, such as the Holy Family, which could be treated almost as secular themes with all the emphasis on the human significance. The Mannerists, on the other hand, prefer subjects in which they can emphasize the theological or supernatural aspects.
与文化和思想的其他分支情况相同。大约自 1530 年起，世纪初在罗马蓬勃发展的以人文主义为主的绘画学派逐渐衰落。艺术家们不再对外部世界有新的发现。他们的作品在很大程度上受教会控制，即便被允许有一定自由，也似乎对周围事物失去了兴趣。他们关注的已不再是对可见世界的重建，而是发展新的绘画与构图方法。他们不是在开拓新领域，而是在利用前辈为他们发现的东西并将这些发现转用于新的目的。他们放弃了文艺复兴时期令人信服的空间感和正常比例，几乎像中世纪艺术家那样随意运用任意构造和刻意拉长。取代文艺复兴时期克制而写实的色彩的是直接诉诸情感而非理性的色调。事实上，在许多方面，矫饰派艺术家更接近中世纪的艺术家，而非他们的直接前辈。 这不仅适用于技巧问题，也适用于艺术家似乎偏好选择的题材。在盛期文艺复兴时期，艺术家偏好那些具有广泛吸引力的题材。即使他们描绘宗教题材，也能找到诸如圣家族这样的题材，几乎可以作为世俗主题来处理，完全强调人的意义。另一方面，矫饰主义者更偏好那些可以强调神学或超自然方面的题材。
In the following sections we shall constantly come upon features of Mannerist painting or theory which are only intelligible if we bear in mind the reaction which was going on during the second half of the sixteenth century to the ideas of the Renaissance in religion and politics-for the two cannot be separated and the reaction in the Church was only
在下文各节中，我们将不断遇到宫廷风格绘画或理论的特征，只有当我们铭记十六世纪下半叶在宗教和政治领域对文艺复兴理念所发生的反动时，这些特征才有意义——二者不可分割，而教会内部的反动仅仅是..
another manifestation of the social and political movement which accompanied it.
这是伴随其发生的社会和政治运动的另一种表现。
In their attempts to purge the Church of abuses the Protestants come near to denying altogether the value of any kind of religious art. Images and paintings smelt of idolatry, while the decoration of churches and the impressive ritual of the Mass were examples of that worldliness into which Satan had lured the Catholic Church. As soon, therefore, as the Roman Church gave up its attempt at compromise with the Protestants, and followed the course of strengthening traditional doctrines and methods in defiance of Luther and Calvin, it became necessary for theologians to underpin the foundations on which religious art was built, and to prove that, far from being idolatrous, sacred images were an incitement to piety and a means of salvation. So the first works on the arts produced by the Counter-Reformation are a series of treatises in which all the arguments used by earlier theologians in the Iconoclastic struggles are revived and turned against the Protestants. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
在试图清除教会弊端的过程中，新教徒几乎完全否定了任何形式宗教艺术的价值。图像与绘画带有偶像崇拜的嫌疑，教堂的装饰和弥撒那种壮丽的礼仪则被视为撒旦引诱天主教会陷入的世俗化表现。因此，一旦罗马教会放弃与新教徒妥协的尝试，转而在对抗路德与加尔文时加强对传统教义与方法的维护，神学家们就有必要为宗教艺术所建立的基础提供理论支持，并证明神圣图像非但不是偶像崇拜，反而能激发虔诚并成为得救的手段。于是，反宗教改革初期有关艺术的首批著作，就是一系列论文，在这些论文中，早期神学家在破像运动中使用的所有论点被重新提起并用来反驳新教徒。
Old phrases, like Gregory’s description of religious painting as ‘the Bible of the Illiterate’, reappear and occur in every writer on the arts during the later sixteenth century, and before the end of the Council of Trent art was not only saved for religion but was acknowledged as one of its most valuable weapons in propaganda.
旧有的说法，例如格里高利将宗教绘画称为“文盲的圣经”，在十六世纪后期的每位艺术作家中反复出现，在特伦特会议结束前，艺术不仅被保留为宗教之用，还被公认为其宣传中最有价值的武器之一。
When in its last session in December 1563 the Council discussed the problem of religious art its conclusions were as follows:
当该理事会在 1563 年 12 月的最后一次会议上讨论宗教艺术问题时，其结论如下：
'That the images of Christ, of the Virgin Mother of God, and of the other Saints, are to be had and retained, particularly in
“耶稣基督、圣母（上帝之母）以及其他诸圣的图像，应当保有并保存，尤其是在
churches, and that due honour and veneration are to be given them; not that any divinity, or virtue is believed to be in them on account of which they are to be worshipped; or that anything is to be asked of them; or that trust is to be reposed in images, as was done of old by the Gentiles who placed their hope in idols; but because the honour which is shown them is referred to the prototypes which those images represent; so that by the images which we kiss and before which we uncover our heads and prostrate ourselves we adore Christ, and we venerate the Saints whose likeness they bear; as by the decrees of Councils, and especially of the second Synod of Nicaea, has been defined against the opponents of images.
教堂中对它们应给予适当的尊崇和敬礼；但并非因为这些像中有任何神性或美德，因而应被崇拜；也非应向它们祈求什么；也非应像古代外邦人那样将信托寄托于偶像，把希望寄托于偶像；而是因为对这些像所表现的尊荣是归于那些原型；因此通过我们亲吻并在其前脱帽与俯伏的圣像，我们崇拜基督，并尊敬这些像所描绘的圣人；正如公会议的法令，尤其是尼西亚第二次大公会议的判决，已针对图像的反对者所阐明的那样。
'And the bishops shall carefully teach this: that, by means of the stories of the mysteries of our Redemption, portrayed by paintings or other representations, the people are instructed and confirmed in the habit of remembering, and continually revolving in mind the articles of faith; as also that great profit is derived from all sacred images, not only because the people are thereby admonished of the benefits and gifts bestowed upon them by Christ, but also because the miracles which God has performed by means of the Saints and their salutary examples are set before the eyes of the faithful; that they may give God thanks for those things, may order their own lives and manners in imitation of the Saints; and may be excited to adore and love God and to cultivate piety. 11 11 ^(11){ }^{11}
主教们应当谨慎教导这一点：通过描绘我们救赎奥迹的故事的油画或其他表现形式，人民被教导并被巩固起记忆的习惯，不断在心中反复思考信仰条目；同样，从所有圣像中也能获得巨大益处，不仅因为人们因此被提醒基督赐予他们的恩惠与恩赐，而且因为上帝借着圣人及其有益榜样所行的奇迹在信徒眼前显现；以便他们为这些事感谢上帝，仿效圣人来规范自己的生活与言行；并被激励去崇拜与爱慕上帝，培育虔敬之心。 11 11 ^(11){ }^{11}
But, having decided that images were to be retained and having justified them against the charges of idolatry, the Church had to take care that only the right kinds of religious paintings and statues were allowed and that nothing should be found painted or carved which might either mislead Catholics or give the Protestants a weapon against the Church of Rome. Great trouble was therefore taken to keep churches clear of any heretical or secular paintings, or of any which might be open to the charge of profanity or indecency.
但是，既然决定保留圣像并且为它们辩护以反驳偶像崇拜的指控，教会就必须确保只允许正确类型的宗教画作和雕像，且不会出现任何可能误导天主教徒或给新教徒提供反对罗马教会的把柄的绘画或雕刻。因此教会极为费心地清除教堂内任何异端或世俗的画作，或任何可能被指控为亵渎或猥亵的作品。
The attitude of the Church towards heretical paintings varied at different periods, but was in general surprisingly
教会对异端画作的态度在不同时期有所变化，但总体上令人惊讶地...
broadminded before the Counter-Reformation. In the Middle Ages the Church was so powerful that it could afford to be lax. Rather than risk excluding people from its body, it preferred to allow popular aspirations to express themselves in the broad humour of the Miracle plays and in the imaginative freedom of Gothic sculpture. It allowed stories to be acted or depicted, even if they were legendary or invented, provided that they did not directly go against any ecclesiastical practice or doctrine. During the Renaissance the same broad-mindedness prevailed. Pagan doctrines and symbols were incorporated into Christianity, and the revival of classical ideals was not only tolerated but actively furthered by most of the Popes from Nicholas V to Clement VII. So close was the fusion of Classical and Christian ideas that it surprised no one that Raphael should paint the ancient poets and the ancient philosophers opposite the Christian theologians in decorating one of the central rooms of the Vatican.
在反宗教改革之前思想相当开明。中世纪时教会权力如此强大，以至于它可以放宽要求。与其冒着把人排除在其体系之外的风险，它更倾向于允许民众的愿望在奇迹剧的滑稽表现和哥特雕塑的想象自由中得到表达。它允许故事被表演或描绘，即使这些故事是传说性的或虚构的，只要它们不直接违背任何教会的惯例或教义。文艺复兴时期同样盛行这种宽容。异教的教义和符号被纳入基督教，古典理想的复兴不仅被容忍，而且从尼古拉五世到克莱孟七世的大多数教皇都积极推动。古典与基督教思想的融合如此紧密，以致拉斐尔在装饰梵蒂冈的一间主要厅室时，把古代诗人和古代哲学家与基督教神学家对置，也不足为奇。
During the fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries only one case is known in which official action was taken against heretical painting. The painting in question was Botticini’s Assumption, now in the National Gallery, which was based on the ideas of Matteo Palmieri and was supposed to contain certain heresies derived from Origen and repeated in Palmieri’s Città di Vita. The ecclesiastical authorities ordered the painting to be covered, apparently between 1485 and 1500 , and the chapel in which it hung was still under an interdict in the middle of the eighteenth century. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
在十五世纪和十六世纪早期，只有一起已知的对异端绘画采取官方行动的案例。涉事画作是现藏于 National Gallery 的 Botticini 的《Assumption》，其基于 Matteo Palmieri 的思想，被认为包含源自 Origen 并在 Palmieri 的 Città di Vita 中重复出现的某些异端观点。教会当局下令将该画遮盖，似乎是在 1485 年至 1500 年之间，而挂画的礼拜堂在十八世纪中叶仍处于禁令之下。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
Such cases, however, must have been very rare at the time of the Renaissance, and it was not till the middle of the sixteenth century that the Church decided to see that all religious paintings were strictly orthodox. The tightening up of doctrine and of discipline which was one of the prin-
然而，此类案例在文艺复兴时期必定极为罕见，直到十六世纪中叶教会才决定确保所有宗教画作严格正统。教义和纪律的收紧是当时的主要...
cipal results of the Council of Trent applied in this field as much as in any other, and in the Acts of the Council we read: ‘No image shall be set up which is suggestive of false doctrine or which may furnish an occasion of dangerous error to the uneducated. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} It is typical of the firm control which the Church intended to exercise at this time that the Act adds later: "That these things may be the more faithfully observed the Holy Synod decrees that no one be allowed to place or cause to be placed any unusual image in any place or church . . . unless it has been approved by the Bishop.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
特伦特会议在这一领域所施行的主要成果与其它领域同样重要，在会议记录中我们读到：“不得树立任何暗示错误教义或可能给无学识者带来危险误解的图像。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这反映出教会在此时意图实施严格控制的典型态度，会议决议随后又补充道：“为了更忠实地遵守这些规定，圣会议裁定，除非经主教批准，任何人不得在任何地点或教堂放置或使人放置任何不寻常的图像……。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
This decree, like most of those dealing with religious art, was repeated and expanded by that group of writers who made it their business to publish the decisions of the Council. St. Charles Borromeo will have nothing which disagrees with Holy Scripture or the tradition of the Church. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Cardinal Gabriele Paleotti, Archbishop of Bologna, bans anything ‘superstitious, apocryphal, false, idle, new, unusual’. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} The Fleming Molanus demands that even pictures or representations of heretics should be destroyed. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
这一法令——像处理宗教艺术的大多数法令一样——被一群致力于公布会议决定的著述者重复并扩展。圣查理·博罗梅奥绝不容许有与圣经或教会传统相抵触之物。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 博洛尼亚总主教加布里埃莱·帕莱奥蒂枢机主教禁止一切“迷信的、伪经的、虚假的、无益的、新奇的、不寻常的”事物。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 弗拉芒人莫拉努斯要求甚至连异端者的图画或描绘也应被毁灭。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
But it was not enough for the artist to avoid incorporating established heresies into his paintings; he was constrained further to keep very closely to the Biblical or traditional story which he was treating and not let his imagination add ornaments to it for the sake of making it more attractive. The picturesque or familiar details with which Gothic painters filled their works, and the impressive accompaniments in which the Venetians set their Biblical scenes, were equally condemned. The painter must concentrate his attention on depicting the story in the clearest and most accurate manner possible. 但艺术家仅仅避免在画作中加入既有的异端还不够；他还必须严格遵守所描绘的圣经或传统故事，不得为了使其更具吸引力而让想象为其增添装饰。哥特画家用以充实作品的如画或生活化细节，以及威尼斯画家在圣经场景中安排的壮丽伴景，都同样受到谴责。画家必须把注意力集中在以尽可能清晰和准确的方式描绘故事上。以此观点可与特伦特公会议对宗教音乐的态度相比较，来自
which were swept away the elaborate counterpoint, the improvisations and diminutions which obscured the words of the Mass and made of the music a jig-saw puzzle of sound. The aim of Church music should be not to produce ‘a vain delight for the ears’, but to provide such a setting ‘that the words may be heard by everyone’. The same demand for clarity appears in connexion with painting in the importance attached to certain external details by which the figures could be represented. Angels must have wings; saints must have haloes and their particular attributes, or if they are really obscure, it may even be necessary to write their names below them to avoid any confusion. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} If allegory is used it must be simple and intelligible, for, as Gilio da Fabriano says: 'A thing is beautiful in proportion as it is clear and evident. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}

All the direct exponents of the decrees of Trent already mentioned emphasize the need for accuracy in the representation of religious subjects, and they are joined by others whose primary interest is in painting but who show how far the influence of the Council spread during the later sixteenth century. Raffaello Borghini, for instance, in the Riposo, published in 1584, wishes the artist to ‘paint subjects derived from Holy Scripture simply and purely’, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and others write in the same spirit. These authors are all forced to admit that the artist cannot confine himself absolutely to the Biblical story, that there may be gaps which he is compelled to fill and details which he must add to make the story comprehensible. But they are unanimous in urging him always to consider whether any detail which he adds is suitable and essential to his theme, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} and when they come to define the liberties which they are prepared to allow they are seen to be small enough. Certain other concessions are, however, made.
