The extraordinary attention which critics and theologians paid to details in religious paintings can best be seen in the censures of Gilio da Fabriano on Michelangelo’s Last Fudgement or in Borghini’s comments on Florentine Mannerist paintings, particularly on Pontormo’s frescoes in S. Lorenzo. Gilio’s criticisms go farther towards the ludicrous than Borghini’s, for he was a priest and a professional theologian and took purely doctrinal errors intensely to heart, but Borghini comes very close to him and proves that laymen and not only priests were profoundly influenced by the Tridentine reforms. A few of Gilio’s objections to the Last Fudgement are perhaps worth quoting in detail to give the tone of his dialogue. Michelangelo, he says, has represented the angels without wings. Certain of the figures have draperies blown about by the wind, in spite of the fact that at the Day of Judgement wind and storm will have ceased. The trumpeting angels are shown all standing together,
评论家和神学家对宗教画细节的异常关注，在吉利奥·达·法布里亚诺对米开朗基罗的《最后审判》的谴责或博尔吉尼对佛罗伦萨矫饰主义画作，尤其是庞托尔莫在圣洛伦佐的壁画的评论中可以看到最清楚的一面。吉利奥的批评比博尔吉尼的更接近可笑，因为他是牧师和职业神学家，对纯粹教义性的错误极为关切，但博尔吉尼也非常接近他，并证明不仅牧师，世俗人士也深受特伦特改革的影响。为了呈现其对话的语气，吉利奥对《最后审判》的若干反对意见或许值得详细引用。米开朗基罗，他说，把天使画成没有翅膀的。有些人物的衣褶被风吹得扬起，尽管在审判日风暴将已平息。吹号的天使却都站在一起，
whereas it is written that they shall be sent into the four corners of the earth. Among the dead rising from the earth some are still bare skeletons, while others are already clothed with flesh, though according to the Biblical version the general Resurrection will take place instantaneously. (In the dialogue this view is elaborately disputed, but is finally admitted.) I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} Gilio also protests against the fact that Christ is shown standing, instead of seated upon His throne of glory. One of the speakers justifies this on the grounds that it is symbolical, but his defence is disallowed by the leader of the argument in a sentence which sums up the whole feeling of the dialogue: 'Your opinion may be right, that he intended to interpret the words of the Gospel mystically and allegorically; but first of all the literal meaning should be taken, whenever this can properly be done, and then the others, keeping to the letter as often as possible. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
却又写着他们要被送到地的四角。自地而起的死人中有些仍是光秃的骸骨，有些已被肉身包裹，尽管根据圣经版本，普遍的复活将会瞬间发生。（在对话中对此观点有详尽争辩，但最终被承认。） I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} Gilio 还抗议基督被描绘为站着，而不是端坐在祂的荣耀宝座上。发言者之一以这是象征性的为由为此辩护，但在论点领袖的一句总结全篇对话情感的话中，这种辩护被驳回：‘你的观点可能是对的，即他意在神秘和寓意地解释福音的话；但首先应取字面意义，只要恰当可行，然后才取其他意义，尽量多保持字面意思。’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
This represents not only the attitude of Gilio to Michelangelo but that of his whole generation to the great figures of thirty years before. Caraffa turned against the liberal Reformers, like Contarini and Pole, who attempted to bring a new spirit into the Church without bothering about the letter of dogma; and the supporters of the Council of Trent turned against Michelangelo, who evolved a new spiritualized art and sometimes preferred a moral allegory to the letter of Biblical accuracy. In the face of the Protestant menace, both Pole and Michelangelo might have provided a weapon against the Church of Rome and therefore could not be tolerated.
这不仅代表了 Gilio 对米开朗基罗的态度，也代表了他那一代人对三十年前伟大人物的总体看法。Caraffa 转而反对那些不拘泥教条文字、试图将新精神带入教会的自由改革者，如 Contarini 和 Pole；而支持特伦特议会的人则转而反对米开朗基罗——他发展出一种新的精神化艺术，有时更偏爱道德寓意而非圣经文本的逐字准确。在新教威胁面前，Pole 和米开朗基罗都可能成为对抗罗马教会的武器，因此无法被容忍。
The Counter-Reformers, however, were not only concerned to clear religious art of theological inaccuracies; it was at least as important to eliminate from it everything secular or pagan. Again, their action in connexion with painting and sculpture is parallel with their purge of Church music. In the early sixteenth century it was a regular custom to sing parts of the Mass to the tunes of popular songs, and it some-
然而，反宗教改革者不仅致力于清除宗教艺术中的神学错误；同样重要的是将其中所有世俗或异教的内容剔除。再者，他们在绘画和雕塑方面的行动，与他们清除教会音乐的举措是相似的。十六世纪早期，把弥撒的部分乐章用流行歌曲的调子来演唱是一种常见的做法，而且有时—
times happened, even in the Papal choir, that one of the voices was allowed to sing the words ordinarily associated with the tune while the others sang the words of the Mass. The reforms enjoined by the Council of Trent and by the Commission of Cardinals which dealt with Church music in 1564 forbade all these practices and insisted that words and music should be entirely religious. In the same way the Church insisted that paintings in churches should be entirely free from secular elements, particularly from traces of Greek or Roman paganism.
有时会发生这样的情况，即便在教皇合唱团中，也允许其中一声部唱与曲调通常相关的歌词，而其他声部则唱弥撒文。特伦特会议及 1564 年负责教会音乐的枢机委员会所要求的改革禁止了所有这些做法，并强调词与乐应完全宗教化。同样，教会也坚持认为教堂内的绘画应完全没有世俗元素，尤其应杜绝希腊或罗马异教痕迹。
The reasons which the Counter-Reformers had to fear the worship of classical antiquity have already been explained, and it is not therefore surprising to find Gilio da Fabriano objecting to Michelangelo’s introduction of Charon into the Last Fudgement. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} It is agreed in the dialogue that Michelangelo was here acting on the authority of Dante, but this defence is not allowed to stand, and it is typical of the change of spirit in the Church that what would not have been challenged in the time of Dante could not be risked in 1560 .
反宗教改革派之所以害怕崇拜古典古物的理由已在前文说明，因此看到 Gilio da Fabriano 反对米开朗基罗在《最后的审判》中引入卡戎并不令人惊讶。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 对话中一致认为米开朗基罗此举是依据但丁的权威，但这种辩护未被接受，这也反映了教会精神的变化：在但丁时代不会受到质疑的事，到 1560 年已不敢冒险。
The most austere moralists go farther and would not allow the preservation of pagan images and paintings even in their own houses. According to Possevino the sight of pagan images is abhorrent to the saints in heaven, and Pius V and Sixtus V were therefore right in their attempts to remove and destroy ancient statues or convert them to Christian uses. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Molanus takes the line that pagan statues should not please Christians, but that those which teach a good moral lesson in accordance with Christian ethics may usefully be preserved. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
最严厉的道德主义者走得更远，甚至不允许在自己家中保存异教的塑像和画作。根据 Possevino 的说法，异教图像的存在令天堂中的圣徒憎恶，因此 Pius V 和 Sixtus V 力图移除和摧毁古代雕像或将其改用于基督教用途是正确的。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Molanus 的立场是，异教雕像不应取悦基督徒，但那些按照基督教伦理传授良好道德教训的雕像则可以有益地保存。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
It is, however, clear that these extreme views were not universally accepted and that the Church was ready to make
然而，很明显这些极端观点并未被普遍接受，教会也准备做出
some concessions. Classical antiquity had passed into the habits of thought of the Italians so deeply that nothing could have eradicated it completely. The Church, therefore, set itself to eliminate only the more dangerous forms of classical influence and to devise adequate excuses for allowing the rest. St. Charles Borromeo, for instance, in his instruction for the building of churches, permits the use of the classical orders ‘for the sake of structural durability’. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} In general, however, the Church decided that the innocuous part of classicism was its mythology. It was frightened of the philosophical systems of antiquity which might lead to serious conflict with Christian principles, but mythology was a harmless enough means of satisfying the Italians’ romantic feeling for antiquity.
作出了一些让步。古典古代的思想已经深深融入意大利人的思维习惯，已无从彻底根除。因此，教会只着手消除古典影响中更危险的形式，并为允许其余部分寻找足够的借口。例如，圣查尔斯·博罗梅奥在关于建造教堂的指示中，允许出于“结构耐久性”的缘故使用古典柱式。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 然而总体上，教会认为古典主义中无害的部分是其神话学。教会畏惧古代的哲学体系，这些体系可能与基督教原则发生严重冲突，但神话学作为满足意大利人对古代浪漫情结的手段则足够无害。
In the later sixteenth century, therefore, fresco cycles of mythological themes are common, but they are no longer treated in the spirit in which Raphael painted them. The classicism survives in the stories and symbolism, but the Humanist seriousness which accompanied them at the time of the High Renaissance has gone. This rationalism, which was combined to perfection with classicism in the School of Athens, was the real bugbear of the Church since it led to Protestant reforms or free thought; and, once separated from this, once derationalized, classicism was harmless. Even so severe a critic as Gilio does not altogether ban mythological painting, for he divides painters into three kinds-historical, poetical, and mixed 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}-and under the poetical class he evidently intends to include those who treat mythological scenes, since he refers to Raphael’s decoration of the Farnesina.
因此，到十六世纪后期，神话题材的壁画周期相当普遍，但对待这些题材的精神已不再是拉斐尔绘画时的那种风格。古典主义在故事和象征上仍然存在，但伴随它们在盛期文艺复兴时期的那种人文主义的严肃性已经消失。这种理性主义，在雅典学院中与古典主义达到完美结合，正是教会的真正心腹大患，因为它导致了新教的改革或自由思想；一旦与此分离，一旦被去理性化，古典主义便无害了。即便是像吉里奥这样严厉的批评者也并不完全禁止神话题材绘画，他把画家分为三类——历史的、诗性的和混合的——在诗性类别下，他显然打算把那些处理神话场景的画家包括在内，因为他提到了拉斐尔对法尔内西娜的装饰。
In religious painting the Church did not limit its attention to the exclusion of classical or pagan elements. It disapproved of the introduction of the secular in any form. We are lucky enough to have the full details of one incident in which it took action against an artist in this matter, and the account
在宗教绘画方面，教会并不只是把注意力局限于排斥古典或异教元素。它反对以任何形式引入世俗内容。我们有幸得到一件教会就此对某位艺术家采取行动的事件的详细记录，叙述是
is worth quoting at some length, since it throws light on the official view and on the state of mind of a certain group of artists. In July 1573 Paul Veronese was summoned before the Tribunal of the Inquisition to defend his painting of the ‘Feast in the House of Levi’, executed for the refectory of SS. Giovanni e Paolo, and now in the Academy in Venice. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} The main objections made by the Inquisitors to the painting were that Veronese had introduced into it dogs, dwarfs, a fool with a parrot, men armed in the German manner, and a servant whose nose is bleeding-all details which are not mentioned in the Biblical story and are not suitable to a religious painting. Veronese at first argues ingeniously that Levi was a rich man and no doubt had servants, soldiers and dwarfs about him, but he is rapidly forced to his real explanation. When he was asked whom he supposed to have been actually present at this feast, he answered: ‘I believe that Christ and the apostles were there. But, if in a painting there is space left over, I fill it with figures from my imagination.’ And again: ‘My commission was to make this picture beautiful according to my judgement, and it seemed to me that it was big and capable of holding many figures.’ His explanations were not accepted and he was ordered to make certain alterations in detail, which he duly carried out. It is typical of the methods of the Counter-Reformation that the Inquisition in this case was satisfied with certain changes of detail which left the painting exactly as worldly in feeling as it was before. But the replies of Veronese are even more instructive. His ideas are entirely those of the Renaissance. He thinks in terms of beauty not of spiritual truth, and his object was to produce a magnificent pageant painting, not to illustrate a religious story. The explanation is that, compared with most other parts of Italy, Venice was little affected by the Tridentine phase of the Counter-Reformation. The
值得较长地引用这段话，因为它阐明了官方观点及某些艺术家群体的心态。1573 年 7 月，保罗·威罗内塞（Paul Veronese）被传召到宗教裁判所法庭（Tribunal of the Inquisition）面前，为他为 SS. Giovanni e Paolo 斋堂创作的《利未家筵席》（Feast in the House of Levi）作辩护，该画现收藏于威尼斯学院（Academy）。宗教裁判官对这幅画的主要异议是，威罗内塞在画中加入了狗、侏儒、带鹦鹉的傻瓜、以德国式方式持械的人以及一位鼻子流血的仆人——这些细节在圣经故事中没有提及，也不适合出现在宗教画中。威罗内塞最初巧妙地辩称利未是个富人，显然身边会有仆人、士兵和侏儒，但很快被逼到他的真实解释。当被问及他认为谁实际出席了这场筵席时，他答道：“我相信基督和门徒在那里。但若画面中留有空隙，我就用我想象中的人物来填补。”“再者：‘委托我画这幅画是要按我的判断把它画得漂亮，我认为它很大，能容纳许多人物。’”他的解释没有被接受，他被命令对某些细节作出修改，他也照办了。反宗教改革方法的典型之处在于，这种情况下宗教裁判所满足于对细节作出某些变动，而这些变动并没有改变画作原有的世俗感。更有启发性的是维罗内塞的答辩。他的观念完全属于文艺复兴时期。他以美为思考出发点，而非精神真理，他的目的在于创作一幅壮丽的盛会画，而不是去阐述一个宗教故事。原因在于，与意大利大部地区相比，威尼斯较少受到特伦特会议时期反宗教改革的影响。这
Jesuits were never firmly established there and the Inquisition was subject to State control. Certain painters, like Tintoretto, absorbed the new ideas and their paintings are filled with the turbulent spirituality of the CounterReformers, but they were in a minority, and it was still possible in the later sixteenth century for artists like Veronese or Palladio to work on principles which are fundamentally those of the Renaissance.
耶稣会并未在那里牢固建立，宗教裁判所受国家控制。某些画家，如丁托列托，吸收了新的理念，他们的画作充满了反宗教改革者的动荡灵性，但这类人只占少数；在十六世纪后期，像维罗内塞或帕拉第奥这样的艺术家仍然可以按照根本上属于文艺复兴的原则进行创作。
The last problem connected with religious painting with which the Church was concerned was that of decency. Before the Council of Trent this question had never been of any great moment. In the Middle Ages the Church allowed as much freedom to popular humour as to popular legends, and both expressed themselves within the range of religious art. In the fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries there are cases of objections being made to works of art on the grounds of decency. Jean Gerson, Chancellor of Paris University at the beginning of the fifteenth century, protested against the effects of naked figures in church decoration, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and in Italy Savonarola caused all the voluptuous paintings that he could lay hands on to be burnt, though, as we have seen, he did not disapprove of the arts in general provided they were directed according to the principles of religion. Vasari records that a St. Sebastian by Fra Bartolommeo had to be moved from a church because it had inspired impure thoughts in certain members of the congregation, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and he also tells how Sodoma got into trouble, but only after he had deliberately painted an indecent scene to irritate the monks for whom he was working. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
与宗教绘画有关、教会所关心的最后一个问题是端庄。特伦特会议之前，这个问题从来没有受到太大重视。在中世纪，教会对民间幽默和民间传说都给予了相当的自由，两者都在宗教艺术的范围内表达出来。十五世纪和十六世纪早期，有些艺术作品因不端庄而遭到反对。十五世纪初巴黎大学校长让·热尔松曾抗议教堂装饰中裸体人物的影响， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 在意大利，萨沃纳罗拉把他能找到的所有纵欲画作都付之一炬，尽管如我们所见，他并不反对艺术本身，只要艺术是根据宗教原则来引导的。瓦萨里记载，Fra Bartolommeo 的一幅圣塞巴斯蒂安画像曾被从教堂移走，因为它曾在某些会众中激发出不洁的念头， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 他还讲到索多玛如何陷入麻烦，但那是因为他故意画了一幅猥亵场景以激怒他所为之工作的修士。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
But these cases are isolated, and it is clear from the frequent occurrence of nudes in religious paintings till the middle of the sixteenth century that before the Counter-Reformation the Church was not prepared to take any steps beyond seeing
但这些情况是个别的，而且从宗教画中裸体人物在十六世纪中叶之前频繁出现这一点可以清楚看出，在反宗教改革之前，教会并不准备采取任何超过仅仅观看的措施
that nothing grossly indecent was introduced into church decoration. But after the Council of Trent the situation was entirely changed, and the decency of religious paintings was watched as carefully as their orthodoxy. The Tridentine decree on this subject is very general: 'Finally all lasciviousness must be avoided; so that figures shall not be painted or adorned with a beauty inciting to lust. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} But this was made the text of long and detailed expositions by the propagators of the reforms. Borromeo and Paleotti merely expand the theme, adding to it only the view that indecency must be avoided not only in churches but in the decoration of private houses also. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Gilio da Fabriano considers in some detail the question of nudity, and decides that even when from the Biblical narrative it is clear that the figures should be naked, the artist must at least equip them with loin-cloths. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Molanus is shocked by the representation of the Infant Christ naked, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} and Possevino is horrified at the idea of any nude appearing in any painting anywhere, since ‘if a man has any decency in his heart, he will hardly dare to look at himself naked’. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
教堂装饰中不得引入任何严重猥亵的内容。但在特伦特会议之后，情况完全改变了，宗教画作的端庄性受到与其正统性同样严格的监控。特伦特关于此题的法令非常笼统：“最后一切淫荡必须避免；以致人物不得被描绘或装饰成引人起淫的美。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 然而，这成为改革推动者们长篇详细阐述的文本。博罗梅奥和帕莱奥蒂只是扩展了这一主题，仅补充了这样一种观点：不得仅在教堂中避免不端，也应在私人住宅的装饰中加以避免。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 法布里亚诺的吉里奥相当详细地考虑了裸体问题，并断定即便圣经叙事明确人物应为赤身，艺术家至少也必须给他们配上遮裆布。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 莫拉努斯对描绘赤裸的婴孩基督感到震惊， 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 波塞维诺则对于任何裸体出现在任何画作中的想法感到恐惧，因为“如果一个人心中还有丝毫羞耻，他几乎不敢赤身面对自己”。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
As in the disputes over heresy, so in those over decency, Michelangelo’s Last Fudgement came in for the most violent attacks. Its position in the Sistine Chapel gave it an importance which made it a good test case, and in the question of nudity it provided ample material for discussion. It was not only exposed to written attacks, but on several occasions was in danger of complete destruction and only escaped with serious mutilation. Even before it was finished, the master of the ceremonies to Paul III, Biagio da Cesena, protested against it; but the Pope stood by the artist, who took an easy revenge by painting his opponent as Minos in Hell. Paul IV
正如在异端争论中一样，在有关端庄的问题上，米开朗基罗的《最后审判》也遭到最猛烈的攻击。它在西斯廷礼拜堂中的位置赋予了它重要性，使其成为一个很好的试验案例，而在裸体问题上它提供了大量讨论材料。它不仅受到书面攻击，而且在几次情况下濒临被完全毁坏的危险，仅以严重残缺逃过一劫。甚至在完成之前，教宗保禄三世的礼仪官比亚乔·达·切塞纳就对其提出抗议；但教皇支持这位艺术家，艺术家也轻松地报了复仇，把他的反对者画成地狱中的米诺斯。保禄四世

threatened to destroy the whole fresco and finally ordered Daniele da Volterra to paint draperies over some of the figures. Pius IV was still dissatisfied and had the draperies increased in number, while Clement VIII was only prevented from completely destroying the painting by the appeals of the Academy of St. Luke. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} The violence which Michelangelo’s work aroused is shown by a Florentine criticism, quoted by Symonds, in which the artist is described as ‘that inventor of filthiness’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The official ecclesiastical writers were less forcible in their language, and, as will appear later, the only other critics to speak without any restraint were not disinterested in their attacks (Plates io a a aa and b b bb ).
威胁要摧毁整幅壁画，最终命令 Daniele da Volterra 在部分人物上绘上衣饰。庇护四世仍不满意，要求增加更多衣饰，而克莱门八世则仅因圣卢卡学院的上诉才未能彻底摧毁这幅画。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 米开朗基罗作品引发的激烈反应可见于一则佛罗伦萨批评（由 Symonds 引用），其中将这位艺术家称为“那位污秽的发明者”。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 官方教会作家在措辞上较为委婉，正如后文将会显现的，唯一另一些毫不克制地尖锐批评者在发动攻击时并非无私。 (图版 io a a aa 和 b b bb )
The Church exerted much the same control over literature as over painting, but even more systematically. In the fifteenth century the Papacy was cautious but broad-minded. Sixtus IV forbade the publication of any book till it had been licensed by the ecclesiastical authorities, but little more was done till the last years of Paul III when, owing to the influence of Caraffa, it was made a criminal offence to print, sell, or own any forbidden book. The first official list of such books was published, in harmony with the Tridentine decrees, at Rome in 1564. The rules laid down in this Index Expurgatorius, and in later editions of the work, were close to those which the Council had imposed on painting: prohibition of all heresy, profanity, indecency, and of anything attacking Papal supremacy. As in the case of painting, the ecclesiastical authorities paid more attention to the letter than to the spirit; and they were compelled to make some concessions over the Classics. They were also far fiercer against anti-clerical than
教会对文学的控制与对绘画的控制大体相同，但更为系统。十五世纪教皇制度谨慎而开明。西斯图斯四世禁止出版任何未经教会当局许可的书籍，但直到保罗三世末年才有更严厉的措施出现；在卡拉法的影响下，印刷、出售或拥有任何被禁书籍被定为刑事罪。第一部此类官方书目与特伦特会议的法令相一致，于 1564 年在罗马公布。这部《删节索引》（Index Expurgatorius）及其后版本中规定的规则，与宗教会议对绘画所施加的要求接近：禁止一切异端、亵渎、不雅，以及任何攻击教皇权威的内容。与对绘画的情况一样，教会当局更注重字面形式而非精神实质；他们也被迫在古典作品问题上作出一些让步。他们对反教士倾向的镇压也远比对...
against immoral writers, as can be seen from the so-called expurgated editions, approved by the congregation, of authors like Bandello and Folengo. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} The Papal authorities, therefore, showed the same curious mixture of piety and policy with regard to literature as over painting, and the development of the movement leading to the Index runs parallel with the tightening of control over religious art.
针对不道德作家的打击，从所谓经会批准的删节版（如 Bandello 和 Folengo 等作者的作品）即可看出。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} 因此，教皇当局在文学问题上表现出与对绘画问题相同的虔诚与权谋交织的奇特混合，而导致《Index》运动的发展与对宗教艺术控制的收紧同时并行。
So far almost all the authorities quoted in connexion with the reforms in religious art have been either priests or men directly dependent on ecclesiastical control. But there is no question that, whether or not they really approved of the decisions of Trent, the artists of the later sixteenth century were affected by them and forced in general to follow them. For instance, when Durante Alberti was elected President of the Roman Academy of St. Luke in 1598, he brought with him to the first meeting a Jesuit, who exhorted the Academicians to paint ‘decent and praiseworthy subjects, and to avoid everything lascivious or improper’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The unworldliness of some Mannerist painting has already been discussed, and even in works which are not entirely spiritual in feeling the external laws of decency were observed by painters in the later sixteenth century. Nudes are practically never found in religious art in this period and even figures only partially draped are considerably rarer. There is, indeed, one case of an artist showing as strong a horror of the nude as any of the ecclesiastical critics. This is the sculptor Bartolommeo Ammanati, who in 1582 wrote a letter to the members of the Academy of Drawing in Florence in which he laments all the statues of naked men and women which he had made in earlier years, and, since he cannot destroy these works, wishes to make public confession of his repentance for having carved them. Finally, he urges his brother artists to paint and carve fully draped figures, which, he says, are just as beautiful and
到目前为止，几乎所有与宗教艺术改革有关的权威人士要么是神职人员，要么直接依赖教会控制的人。但毫无疑问，无论他们是否真正赞同特兰特会议的决定，十六世纪后期的艺术家都受到这些决定的影响，并且总体上被迫遵循它们。例如，1598 年当 Durante Alberti 当选为罗马圣卢克学院（Roman Academy of St. Luke）院长时，他在第一次会议上带来了一位耶稣会士，后者督促院士们绘制“端庄且值得称赞的题材，避免一切淫秽或不当之物”。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 已经讨论过某些矫饰主义绘画的非世俗性，即使在那些情感上并非完全精神化的作品中，十六世纪后期的画家也遵守了外在的端庄规范。此时期的宗教艺术中几乎看不到裸体画，甚至仅部分裹布的人物也少得多。事实上，有一位艺术家对裸体表现出与任何教会评论家一样强烈的厌恶。 这是雕塑家巴托洛梅奥·阿马纳蒂，1582 年他给佛罗伦萨素描学院的成员写信，哀叹自己早年所作的所有裸体男女雕像，既然无法摧毁这些作品，他希望公开忏悔自己雕刻它们的悔意。 最后，他敦促同行艺术家绘制和雕刻全身披袍的人物，他说，同样美丽，
just as good a test of the artist’s skill. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Later he wrote to the Grand Duke Ferdinand asking for permission to alter all the naked statues which he had made for the Duke’s father by draping them or by transforming them into illustrations of Christian allegories. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} A conversion of such intensity was, no doubt, exceptional, but to a certain extent most artists of the time were affected by the atmosphere of the CounterReformation. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
同样是对艺术家技艺的良好考验。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 后来他致信大公费迪南德，请求许可将他为公爵之父所作的所有裸体雕像加以改造，或以披袍遮盖，或将其转变为基督教寓意的表现。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 这种程度的转变无疑是例外，但在某种程度上，当时大多数艺术家都受到了反宗教改革氛围的影响。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
The attitude of the critics of the Mannerist period towards the problem of the nude in painting is relevant to the whole relation of Mannerism to the Renaissance. The more puritanical of the Counter-Reformers seem to have been simply insensible to the serious qualities of Renaissance art, but with critics like Gilio da Fabriano the case is different. He not only admits the merits of Michelangelo but enthusiastically praises them. Michelangelo, he says, has restored painting to splendour in its externals; he, Gilio, wishes to restore it in its treatment of religious subjects. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} And of the Last Fudgement he writes that in it Michelangelo ‘has shown all that art can achieve’. He admits, therefore, that on standards of purely artistic achievement Michelangelo is incomparable. But Gilio admits a still higher standard according to which, he maintains, Michelangelo must be condemned, because he ‘has taken more delight in art, to show of what kind and how great it was, than in the truth of the subject’. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} For ‘I consider an artist who fits his art to the truth of the subject far wiser than one who adapts the purity of the subject to the beauty of art’. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} To Gilio, therefore, Michelangelo is to be censured for not treating his subject with sufficient seriousness, and he quite unjustly classes him with those of his Mannerist followers against whom it was a common accusa-
对描绘裸体问题的批评家在矫饰主义时期的态度，与矫饰主义与文艺复兴整体关系密切相关。反宗教改革中较为清教徒式的人似乎对文艺复兴艺术的严肃特质完全无感，但像 Gilio da Fabriano 这样的批评家情况则不同。他不仅承认米开朗基罗的优点，而且热情赞扬。米开朗基罗，他说，使绘画在外在表现上恢复了辉煌；他自己，Gilio，愿意使它在宗教题材的处理上得到恢复。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 他还写到《最后审判》，称米开朗基罗“展示了艺术所能达到的一切”。因此他承认，就纯粹艺术成就的标准而言，米开朗基罗无可比拟。但 Gilio 还认可一个更高的标准，并据此断定米开朗基罗应受谴责，因为他“对艺术的喜爱更多是为了展示艺术的性质与伟大，而不是为了题材的真理”。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 他认为“把艺术适应于题材真理的艺术家，比把题材的纯洁性为了艺术之美而改动的艺术家明智得多”。 因此，对吉利奥来说，米开朗基罗应受到指责，因为他未能以足够严肃的态度对待他的题材，并且他极不公平地将他与那些他的矫饰主义追随者归为一类，而这些人常常被指控——
tion that they introduced as many nudes as possible into their paintings simply in order to show their skill in drawing. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} We cannot accuse critics like Gilio of failing to recognize the technical and formal ability in Michelangelo’s work; we can only regret their blindness to the intense seriousness which inspired it, but which to men of their generation was concealed by the existence of theological errors of detail, of quite minor importance to a Renaissance Humanist mind.
他们尽可能在画作中加入大量裸体，纯粹是为了展示他们的绘画技巧。我们不能指责像吉利奥这样的批评家未能识别出米开朗基罗作品中的技术和形式能力；我们只能为他们看不见那些激发作品的深沉严肃感而感到遗憾，而在他们那一代人眼中，这种严肃感被一些神学细节上的错误所掩盖——这些错误对文艺复兴人文主义者来说其实并不重要。
The critics involved in the disputes about religious art do not always base their views on a direct appeal to morality or to ecclesiastical authority. They sometimes make use of a doctrine invented for quite different purposes, namely, the theory of decorum. We have already come across this theory in the writings of Leonardo, for whom it forms a necessary part of the realistic presentation of a scene. In the sixteenth century it is applied in a more complex manner. It demands that everything in a painting should be suitable both to the scene depicted and to the place for which it is painted. That is to say, the figures must be dressed suitably to their standing and character, their gestures must be appropriate, the setting must be rightly chosen, and the artist must always consider whether he is executing a work for a church or a palace, a State apartment or a private study.
参与宗教艺术争论的批评家并不总是直接以道德或教会权威为依据。他们有时会利用一套为完全不同目的而发明的学说，即得体理论。我们在莱昂纳多的著作中已经遇到过这一理论，对他而言它构成逼真呈现场景的必要部分。到了十六世纪，这一理论的应用更为复杂。它要求画面中的一切既要适合所描绘的场景，又要适合其被绘制的场所。也就是说，人物的服饰必须符合其地位和性格，姿态须当得体，布景要恰当选择，艺术家还必须时刻考虑自己是在为教堂还是为宫殿、为国家陈设还是为私人书房创作。
In religious painting the theory provides another reason for demanding accuracy in detail, but on some occasions it even seems to form a higher test than literal exactness. It is used, for instance, by Gilio to justify his condemnation of the figure of Christ in Michelangelo’s fresco of the Conversion of St. Paul in the Cappella Paolina. One of the speakers in the dialogue argues that this figure, rushing down from heaven, symbolizes the irresistible and sudden force of grace, but Gilio answers that this is unimportant compared with the fact that the figure of Christ is lacking in the dignity suitable to him. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
在宗教绘画中，该理论为要求细节准确提供了另一个理由，但在某些情况下，它甚至似乎形成了比字面精确性更高的考验。例如，Gilio 就用它来为自己谴责米开朗基罗在卡佩拉·保利纳（Cappella Paolina）中《圣保禄归信》（Conversion of St. Paul）壁画里基督形象的批评辩护。对话中的一位发言者认为，这个从天而降的形象象征着恩典那不可抗拒且突如其来的力量，但 Gilio 回答说，与基督形象缺乏适合其身份的庄严相比，这一点并不重要。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
The theory of decorum, however, is most extensively applied in the one contemporary attack on Michelangelo which remains to be considered. I have left it till this point because it must be carefully distinguished from all the criticism inspired by the Council of Trent. The attack in question was launched by Aretino and carried on in his name by his friend, Lodovico Dolce. It was inspired by purely personal motives and was in no way connected with the serious and religious criticisms of the Last Fudgement, though later Gilio da Fabriano seems to have borrowed arguments from Dolce’s work. The story of Aretino’s relations with Michelangelo has been told at length by various writers, 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} and need only be summarized here. Aretino, who greatly admired Michelangelo, did everything to gain the latter’s good graces. But his flattering letters, in which he begged for a drawing, received no reply, and his attempt to dictate to the artist how he should paint the Last Fudgement was met with insulting evasion. For ten years Aretino persisted, but in 1545 his patience gave way, and he wrote to Michelangelo that letter on the Last Fudgement which is now famous as an example of insincere prudishness. From a man of Aretino’s character it seems strange to hear passionate horror at the indecencies of the Last Fudgement, but they pour out with far more violence than from Gilio or any seriously minded priest. Dolce’s dialogue, L’Aretino, which was published in 1557 , repeats all Aretino’s arguments with the same intensity, and, since the authors were close friends, there is no doubt that they were working in collaboration. We need not examine their accusations in detail, since they are largely the same as those made by Gilio, but what is important is the fact that Aretino and Dolce base their charges on different premisses from those of Gilio. The latter attacks in the name of morality; the former do so when it suits them, but more often it is to the theory of decorum that they appeal. They
然而，得体理论在同时代对米开朗基罗的唯一一篇攻击中被最广泛地运用，这篇攻击还待讨论。我把它留到此处，是因为必须将其与所有由特伦特公会议引发的批评仔细区分开来。所论及的攻击由 Aretino 发起，并由他的朋友 Lodovico Dolce 以他的名义继续。它出于纯粹的个人动机，与对《最后的审判》所作的严肃而宗教性的批评毫无关联，尽管后来 Gilio da Fabriano 似乎从 Dolce 的作品中借用了论点。Aretino 与米开朗基罗的关系经过多位作家的详尽叙述， 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 此处只需概述。极为钦佩米开朗基罗的 Aretino 尽一切努力争取后者的好感。但他的阿谀信件中恳求得到一幅素描，未获回音；他试图指示这位艺术家如何绘制《最后的审判》，却遭到了侮辱性的回避。 十年来阿雷蒂诺一直坚持不懈，但在 1545 年他的耐心耗尽，他给米开朗基罗写了那封关于《最后的审判》的信，这封信如今以虚伪的假道学著称。对于像阿雷蒂诺这种性格的人来说，听到他对《最后的审判》中不雅之处表达出强烈的惊骇似乎有些奇怪，但他的谴责比吉里奥或任何一本正经的神父都要激烈得多。多尔切的对话体作品《L’Aretino》，于 1557 年出版，重复了阿雷蒂诺全部论点且同样强烈，而且由于两人是密友，毫无疑问他们是合作进行的。我们不必详细审查他们的指控，因为这些指控在很大程度上与吉里奥的相同，但重要的是阿雷蒂诺和多尔切基于与吉里奥不同的前提出发。后者以道德的名义进行攻击；前者则在方便时也这样做，但更多时候他们诉诸的是合宜性(the theory of decorum)。他们
are shocked not so much at Michelangelo’s painting an indecent picture as at his painting it in such an important place as the Sistine Chapel: 'Who will dare to assert that it is right that, in the church of St. Peter, prince of the apostles, in Rome where all the world meets together, in the chapel of the Pope, who, as Bembo truly says, is like a god on earth, there should be seen painted so many naked figures, shamelessly uncovered both before and behind. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
他们震惊的并不是米开朗基罗画了一幅猥亵的画，而是他把这幅画画在了西斯廷教堂这样一个重要的地方：“谁敢断言，在使徒之首圣彼得的教堂里，在罗马这个举世汇聚之地，在教皇的礼拜堂里——正如 Bembo 确实所说，教皇在世上如同一位上帝——会被看到如此多的裸体人物，前后都赤裸裸地无耻暴露。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
This theme of the unsuitability of the painting to its position recurs in Dolce, and makes us suspect that his feelings are not based only on morality. This suspicion is confirmed by one extraordinary passage in the dialogue. Fabrini, the second speaker, complains of the indecency of a set of Marc’ Antonio’s engravings after Giulio Romano for which Aretino himself had written a series of sonnets in his most licentious manner. Aretino, however, shifts the blame from Giulio to the engraver, saying that the former never intended to publish them, and adds: ‘It is not wrong for the painter sometimes to produce such works for his own amusement; just as certain ancient poets joked freely about the image of Priapus, to please Maecenas and to celebrate his gardens. But in public . . . one must always behave with decency.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} This defence of what has always been considered a series of calculatedly pornographic engravings, coming immediately after Aretino’s prudish horror at the nudes in the Last Fudgement, leaves no doubt that the writer was inspired by personal anger and not by any high moral feelings. The whole of Aretino’s and Dolce’s attack is, in fact, irrelevant to the theme of religious art at the time of the Counter-Reformation, but since the latter’s dialogue was widely read, and was particularly used by French writers of the following century, it cannot be altogether ignored. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
在 Dolce 的作品中，关于画作与其所处位置不相称这一主题反复出现，这使我们怀疑他的感受并非仅仅基于道德。这一怀疑在对话中的一段非凡的文字中得到证实。第二位发言者 Fabrini 抱怨 Marc’ Antonio 根据 Giulio Romano 的作品所刻的一组版画的不雅，而 Aretino 本人曾以极放荡的方式为其写过一系列十四行诗。Aretino 却将责任从 Giulio 转移到版画师身上，称前者从未打算出版这些作品，并补充道：“画家有时为自己消遣而创作此类作品并无不当；正如某些古代诗人为取悦 Maecenas 并颂扬他的花园而自在地戏谑 Priapus 的形象。但在公共场合……人们必须始终保持端庄。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 这种对一系列历来被视为蓄意色情的版画的辩护，紧随 Aretino 对《最后的审判》中裸体的矫饰性惊恐之后，毫无疑问地表明该作家的动机是出于个人愤怒，而非任何崇高的道德情操。 事实上，阿雷蒂诺与多尔切的全部攻击与反宗教改革时期的宗教艺术主题无关，但由于后者的对话体作品广为流传，且特别被随后一个世纪的法国作家所采用，因此不能完全被忽视。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
We have already come across one survivor of the Renaissance involved in the quarrel over religious art, namely Veronese. Another almost equally out of sympathy with the reform of Trent was Vasari, though he was aware of what was taking place and in general avoided committing himself too far. In the matter of heretical paintings he is a little disingenuous. Referring to Botticini’s Assumption he says that people complained that it contained heretical ideas, and adds: ‘As to whether this is true or false, I cannot be expected to judge; it is enough that the figures painted therein . . . are entirely worthy of praise . . . all varied in diverse ways, the whole being executed with good design.’ 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This is as much as to say that he is not interested in the religious details which he leaves to the theologians. Over decency in painting he is more explicit. He is, of course, enthusiastic about the Last Fudgement and in general he is quite free from prudishness, though he condemns the engravings by Marc’ Antonio which Aretino defends. In the life of Fra Angelico he makes a complete statement of his views, saying that ‘those who work at religious and holy subjects should be religious men’, and blaming those who regard ‘the rude and inept as holy, and the beautiful and excellent as licentious’, since the saints should be ‘as much more beautiful than mortal men as Heaven is superior to earthly beauty’. He even accuses those who are hypersensitive about decency in painting of revealing 'the unsoundness and corruption of their own minds by drawing
我们已经遇到过一位参与关于宗教艺术争论的文艺复兴幸存者，即维罗内塞。另一位几乎同样对特伦特改革不以为然的是瓦萨里，尽管他意识到正在发生的事情，并且总体上避免把自己牵得太远。在有关异端画作的问题上，他有点不够坦率。谈到博蒂奇尼的《升天》时，他说有人抱怨其中包含异端思想，并补充道：“至于这是否真或假，我不能被期望去判断；足够的是其中所画的人物……完全值得称赞……各具变化，整体构图良好。” 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这无异于说他对宗教细节并不感兴趣，把这些留给神学家去处理。关于绘画的端庄问题他则更明确。当然，他对《最后审判》是热衷的，总体上他相当不拘谨，尽管他谴责了马尔克·安东尼奥的版画，而阿雷蒂诺为之辩护。 在方济各修士安吉利柯的一生中，他完整地陈述了自己的观点，认为“处理宗教和神圣题材的人应当是虔诚的人”，并批评那些把“粗鄙和笨拙看作是神圣的，把美好和优秀视为放纵的人”，因为圣人应当“比凡人美丽得多，就如天堂远胜世俗之美”。他甚至指责那些在绘画的端庄问题上过分敏感的人，通过描绘……暴露了“他们自身心灵的不健全与堕落”
evil and impure desires out of works from which, if they were lovers of purity, as they seek by their misguided zeal to prove themselves to be, they would gain a desire to attain to Heaven’. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This all occurs in the 1550 edition and is entirely Renaissance in feeling. But when the second edition was published in 1568 the quarrel over the Last Fudgement had reached a more acute stage, and though Vasari leaves the passages quoted above, and in fact adds to them in the same sense, he also puts in a defensive paragraph in which he covers himself by an appeal to the theory of decorum: 'However I would not have any believe that I approve of those figures that are painted in churches in a state of almost complete nudity, for in these cases it is seen that the painter has not shown the consideration that was due to the place. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} It is hard to tell how sincere this passage is, but in any case it is clear that Vasari had not fundamentally changed his attitude towards religious art.
邪恶和不纯的欲望从那些作品中被驱除出，如果作者们真如他们用误导性的热忱试图证明自己那样，是纯洁的爱好者，他们就会产生向往升入天堂的愿望。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这一切都出现在 1550 年的版本中，完全具有文艺复兴的情感。但当 1568 年第二版出版时，关于最后审判的争论已进入更尖锐的阶段，尽管 Vasari 保留了上面引述的段落，事实上还以相同的意义增加了内容，他也加入了一段防御性的文字，在其中他以体面理论为由为自己辩护：‘不过我不希望有人相信我赞同在教堂里绘制几乎完全裸体的人物，因为在这些情况下可以看出画家没有表现出对该场所应有的考虑。’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 难以判断这段话有多真诚，但无论如何，很明显 Vasari 对宗教艺术的态度并未发生根本改变。
So far the effects of the Council of Trent on the arts which we have considered have been mainly negative, and since the Counter-Reformation was at first a purging movement, it is to be expected that the positive stimulus given by it to painting and architecture should be less direct than its restraining influence. But traces of positive instruction can be found in the propagandists of the Council of Trent.
到目前为止，我们所考察的天特会议对艺术的影响主要是消极的；由于反宗教改革起初是一次净化运动，因此它对绘画和建筑所提供的积极刺激理应不如其约束性影响直接。但在天特会议的宣传者那里仍可发现一些积极教导的痕迹。
The decrees of the Council itself emphasize the value of painted and carved images as incitements to piety, and this theme is developed by Paleotti, who argues that visible representations appeal more vividly to the minds of many than the spoken word, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and by the Lateran Canon Gregorio Comanini, who points out that paintings in a church may catch the eye of even an idle and inattentive person. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} As has already been said, Gilio da Fabriano and other writers consider it more important that the artist should represent the
天特会议本身的法令强调油画和雕刻形象作为激发虔诚的手段的价值，这一主题由 Paleotti 加以展开，他认为可见的表象比口头言辞更能生动地吸引许多人的心灵；Lateran 的 Canon Gregorio Comanini 也指出，教堂中的绘画甚至可能吸引一个懒散且不专心的人的目光。如前所述，Gilio da Fabriano 及其他作者认为艺术家更重要的是要表现出…
truth of his subject than its external and physical beauty. Therefore, in the representation of martyrdoms or of the sufferings of Christ and the saints, which are subjects capable of arousing piety, the artist must not turn the scene into one of calm, statuesque beauty with naked bodies in their physical perfection; he must on the contrary show the full grimness and horror of the scene. If he is painting the Flagellation he must not make it a study in eurhythmics as Daniele da Volterra did in his fresco for S. Pietro in Montorio of which the Counter-Reformers strongly disapproved. He must show Christ as ‘afflicted, bleeding, spat upon, with his skin torn, wounded, deformed, pale and unsightly’. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} If he wants to show a calmer beauty he must choose a calmer subject such as the Baptism, or a more sublime theme like the Transfiguration. In these cases outward beauty is to be encouraged since it is appropriate.
比起外在的物理之美，他要更忠实于题材的真实。因此，在表现殉道或基督与圣徒的受难这些能激起虔敬之情的题材时，艺术家不应把场景处理成宁静、雕像般的美，亦即裸露身体的物理完美；相反，他必须展示场景的全然严酷与恐怖。如果他在画鞭笞，不应把它处理成优美韵律的习作，正如 Daniele da Volterra 在蒙特罗里圣彼得堂（S. Pietro in Montorio）所作的壁画那样，后者遭到反宗教改革者的强烈不满。他必须把基督表现为“受苦、流血、被唾弃、皮肤被撕裂、受伤、畸形、面色苍白且不美观”。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 如果他想表现较为平和的美，应选择较为平静的题材，如洗礼，或选择更崇高的主题，如变容。在这些情况下，外在之美是可取的，因为它是适当的。
In general the positive as well as the negative advice of the followers of Trent is conspicuous for its minuteness rather than for any generalized emotional argument such as this opinion of Possevino. This is particularly true of Molanus, who devotes the last two books of his treatise to exact instructions for the painting of any figure or scene from religious history. Every detail is considered-what persons should be present, how they should be dressed, how placed, what attitude they should be given-so that under his guidance the painter cannot make a mistake. It will be seen later that Mannerist critics applied just the same method to classical and mythological scenes as to religious subjects.
总体上，特伦特派追随者的正面建议和反面训诫都以其细致入微而显著，而不是以像波塞维诺那样的任何泛化的情感性论证为特征。对莫拉努斯尤其如此，他把论著的最后两卷专门用于对宗教史中任何人物或场景的绘制给出精确指示。每一个细节都被考虑到——应当有哪些人物在场、他们应当如何着装、如何摆放、应赋予何种姿态——在他的指导下，画家就不可能犯错。后文将看到，矫饰主义批评家对古典和神话题材采取的正是同样的方法，对待这些题材如同对待宗教题材一样。
No less precise is St. Charles Borromeo, who is the only author to apply the Tridentine decree to the problem of architecture. His Instructiones Fabricae et Supellectilis Ecclesiasticae, composed soon after 1572, dealt with extraordinary care with all the problems concerning church building. The book centres round one idea which is typical
同样精确的还有圣查理·博罗梅奥，他是唯一将特伦特法令应用到建筑问题的作者。他在 1572 年后不久撰写的《Instructiones Fabricae et Supellectilis Ecclesiasticae》（教堂建筑与陈设指示），以非凡的谨慎处理了关于教堂建造的所有问题。该书围绕一个典型的思想展开。
of the Counter-Reformation and which was to be of even greater significance in the seventeenth century: that the Church itself and the services held in it must be as dignified and as impressive as possible, so that their splendour and their religious character may force themselves even on the casual spectator. The fact that the Protestants, reacting against the worldliness of Roman ceremonies, went to the opposite extreme of denying any importance to outward show in church services must have provided one reason for the Counter-Reformers to make their own services more and more splendid, but they must also have realized the emotional effect which a big religious ceremony can exert on a congregation. In his prologue to the Instructiones Borromeo praises the ancient tradition of ecclesiastical splendour, and demands that priests and architects shall combine to keep it up.
在反宗教改革运动中有一项影响在十七世纪更为重大的观点：教会本身及其所举行的礼拜仪式必须尽可能庄重和令人印象深刻，以便其华丽与宗教特性能够强烈地作用于偶然的观众。新教徒为了反对罗马礼仪的世俗化而走向否认教堂礼仪外在表现重要性的极端，这一事实必然成为反宗教改革者愈加华美地装饰其礼拜的一种原因，但他们也必须意识到大型宗教仪式对会众所能产生的情感影响。在他的《Instructiones》序言中，Borromeo 赞扬了教会华美传统，并要求司铎与建筑师协力维持这一传统。
He begins by recommending that the Church should be built in a prominent position, if possible on a slight hill and in any case with steps leading up to it, so that it may dominate its neighbourhood. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Its façade must be decorated with figures of saints and with ‘serious and decent ornament’. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Internally great attention is to be paid to the High Altar, which must be raised on steps 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} and stand in a chancel spacious enough for the priest to be able to officiate with dignity. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} The sacristy should lead into the main body of the Church, not directly into the chancel, so that the priest can make an effective procession to the High Altar. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} The transepts may be converted into chapels with further big altars for particular masses. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} Rich vestments add dignity to a service, 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} and, since the whole ceremony must be properly lit, the windows of the church must in general be filled with white glass. 8 8 ^(8){ }^{8}
他首先建议教堂应建在显眼的位置，最好坐落在一座小山丘上，至少应建有通向教堂的台阶，以便教堂能主宰其周围环境。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 其正立面必须以圣人像和“庄重得体的装饰”来装饰。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 在内部应特别注意高祭坛，祭坛必须建在台阶上 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} ，并置于一处足够宽敞的圣坛，使神父能够庄严地主持仪式。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 圣器室应通向教堂主体，而不应直接通向圣坛，以便神父能够有效地列队行进至高祭坛。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 横耳墙可以改建为小礼拜堂，并设有用于特定弥撒的更大祭坛。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 华贵的祭服能为礼拜增添庄重， 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} 并且由于整个仪式必须有适当照明，教堂的窗户通常应装以白色玻璃。 8 8 ^(8){ }^{8}
But all this effect must be obtained by proper means. There must be no vain show, and above all nothing secular
但所有这些效果必须通过适当的方式来实现。不可有虚浮的炫耀，最重要的是不可有任何世俗的东西
or pagan. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Everything must be strictly in the Christian tradition. The church should be in the shape of a cross, not in the form of a circle which is a pagan practice. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Incidentally Borromeo recommends the Latin rather than the Greek cross, and thereby eliminates the favourite Renaissance form. No doubt he had in mind the new type of Latin-cross plan which had already been evolved by Vignola for the Gesu and was ideally suited to the Counter-Reformation desire for spectacular effects. Even in matters of detail the appeal to ancient Christian tradition is final; doors, for instance, must be square-headed and not arched, because the former kind is found in early Christian basilicas, whereas the latter is a pagan design. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} In every case ecclesiastical reasons predominate, and purely artistic considerations are only allowed in questions which are ecclesiastically indifferent. Borromeo’s attention to detail hardly needs further emphasis, but it is illuminating that he devotes a whole pamphlet to the cleaning of church decoration and furniture. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
或异教。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 一切都必须严格遵循基督教传统。教堂应为十字形，而非圆形——圆形是异教的做法。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 顺便说一句，Borromeo 推荐拉丁十字而非希腊十字，从而排除了文艺复兴时期常见的那种形式。他无疑想到的是 Vignola 为 Gesu 所设计并已形成的新型拉丁十字平面，这种平面非常适合反宗教改革时期对壮观效果的追求。即便在细节问题上，对古代基督教传统的诉求也是最终的裁决；例如门应为方头而非拱形，因为前者见于早期基督教的长方形圣堂（basilicas），而后者是异教的设计。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 在每一种情况下，教会方面的理由占主导地位，纯粹的艺术考量仅在教会上无所谓的问题上被允许。Borromeo 对细节的关注几乎不需更多强调，但有意思的是他专门撰写了一整本小册子，论及教堂装饰和家具的清洁。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
To understand the significance of Borromeo’s instructions for the building of churches it may be useful to compare them with those of architects in whom the ideas of the High Renaissance survived in the middle of the sixteenth century. The forms of Church plan which the latter evolved were also based on religious principles, but their theology was of another kind. Borromeo condemned circular churches because they were pagan. Palladio recommends them because the circle is the most perfect form and is therefore suitable to the house of God. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Moreover, the circle is symbolical of the unity of God, His infinite essence, His uniformity, and His justice. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} After the circle the most perfect form and there-
要理解博罗梅奥关于建造教堂指示的重要性，比较一下十六世纪中叶仍然保有盛期文艺复兴思想的建筑师们的做法可能会有帮助。后者所发展的教堂平面形式也建立在宗教原则之上，但他们的神学属于另一类。博罗梅奥谴责圆形教堂，因为它们是异教的。Palladio（帕拉第奥）则推荐圆形教堂，因为圆是最完美的形体，因此适合做为上帝的居所。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 此外，圆象征上帝的统一、祂的无限本质、祂的恒常性以及祂的公正。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 在圆之后，最完美的形体是—
fore the most suitable plan is the square. Finally comes the cross, which is appropriate because it symbolizes the crucifixion. Borromeo would have approved of this argument, though he would have been shocked at the low place which Palladio allows to the cruciform church. He would have been even more shocked at Palladio’s advice in a later chapter that the rules for building churches are those for the construction of temples, with a few modifications to allow for the introduction of a sacristy and a belfry. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
最适合的平面是方形。最后是十字形，因为它象征着受难，这种形式是合适的。博罗梅奥会赞同这个论点，尽管他会对帕拉迪奥将十字形教堂置于如此卑微位置感到震惊。帕拉迪奥在后一章中建议建造教堂的规则应当是建造寺庙的规则，只需做少量修改以便引入教具室和钟楼，这会让他更加震惊。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1}
Cataneo, in his Quattro Primi Libri di Architettura, published in Venice in 1554, argues in a slightly different way about church building. He maintains that the principal church in a city should be cruciform, because the cross is the symbol of redemption. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} The proportions of the cross should be those of a perfect human body, because they should be based on those of the body of Christ, which was more perfect than that of any other man. Cataneo also adds a very curious and characteristic argument about the decoration of churches. The interior, he says, should be richer than the exterior, because the interior symbolizes the soul of Christ and the exterior the body, and the soul is more beautiful than the body. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Therefore the exterior should be built in a plain order like the Doric and the interior in a more ornamental such as the Ionic. The symbolism of the orders was evidently widespread and is referred to by Serlio. He wishes the orders to be chosen according to the kind of saint to whom the church is dedicated: Doric for those dedicated to Christ, St. Peter, St. Paul, and the more virile saints; Ionic for the gentler male saints and the more matronly female; Corinthian for maiden saints. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} (Plates 11 a 11 a 11 a11 a and b b bb.)
卡塔内奥（Cataneo）在他于 1554 年在威尼斯出版的《Quattro Primi Libri di Architettura》中，以略有不同的方式论述了教堂建筑。他主张城市中的主要教堂应为十字形，因为十字是救赎的象征。十字的比例应当像完美的人体，因为应以基督的身体为准，而基督的身体比任何其他人的都更为完美。卡塔内奥还补充了一个非常奇特且具有特征性的论点，关于教堂的装饰。他说，内部应比外部更为华丽，因为内部象征基督的灵魂，外部象征肉体，而灵魂比肉体更美。因此外部应以朴素的秩序建造，如多立克式，而内部应采用更具装饰性的如爱奥尼亚式。柱式的象征意义显然非常普遍，塞尔里奥（Serlio）也曾提及。他希望根据教堂奉献给的圣人类型来选择柱式：奉献给基督、圣彼得、圣— 保罗，以及更为阳刚的圣徒；爱奥尼亚柱式用于较温和的男性圣徒和较为端庄的女性；科林斯柱式用于处女圣徒。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} （图版 11 a 11 a 11 a11 a 和 b b bb 。)
All these arguments about church building are typical of the way of thought of the High Renaissance. Since beauty was a divine quality, the proper offering to God was a build-
关于教堂建造的所有这些论点都是高文艺复兴思维方式的典型。既然美是神圣的品质，那么献给上帝的恰当供奉就是一座极为美丽的建筑。

ing of great beauty. Combined with this was a strong feeling for the symbolism of certain forms and ornaments. The minute demands of ecclesiastical usage, which for Borromeo weighed above all else, were not yet taken into consideration.
与此相结合的是对某些形式和装饰象征意义的强烈感受。教会礼仪的细微要求——对博罗梅奥而言这些要求高于一切——尚未被考虑进来。
Throughout his Instructiones Borromeo emphasizes the importance of collaboration between priests and artists. This principle had been laid down by the Council of Trent, and we know that in painting at any rate it was generally put into practice. The themes of most Mannerist fresco-cycles are so obscure that they can only have been chosen by a trained theologian, and in some cases we know the names of those who planned the programme. The subjects for the decoration of the Pauline Chapel in S. Maria Maggiore, for instance, were selected by two members of the Oratory. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The same method was generally used in mythological and historical paintings, as, for instance, in the decoration at Caprarola, which were planned by Annibale Caro. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} But from this dictation of ecclesiastical authorities to artists we see that art had, in the most literal sense, returned to its medieval position and had become once more the handmaid of religion.
在他的《Instructiones》中，博罗梅奥反复强调神职人员与艺术家之间合作的重要性。这个原则已由特伦特会议确立，我们知道至少在绘画领域它通常得到了实施。大多数矫饰主义壁画系列的主题如此晦涩，只有受过训练的神学家才能选定，有些情况下我们知道是谁规划了这些方案。例如，圣玛利亚大教堂（S. Maria Maggiore）保禄礼拜堂（Pauline Chapel）的装饰题材就是由两位祈祷会（Oratory）的成员选定的。神话和历史题材的绘画通常也采用同样的方法，例如卡普拉罗拉（Caprarola）的装饰由安尼巴莱·卡罗（Annibale Caro）规划。但从这种教会当局对艺术家的指示中我们可以看到，艺术在最字面意义上已经回到了其中世纪的地位，再次成为宗教的侍从。
This alteration in the position of the arts is brought out by Paleotti, who says that ‘The art of making images is among the noblest arts if it is directed by Christian discipline’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} But the question is more fully discussed by Comanini in his dialogue, Il Figino, published in 1591. The speakers are Ascanio Martinengo, Abbot of S. Salvatore, Brescia; Stefano Guazzo, a literary and artistic patron; and Ambrogio Figino,
这种关于艺术地位的改变由帕莱奥蒂（Paleotti）提出，他说：“如果受基督教规范的指导，造像艺术是诸艺术中最崇高的。” 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 但这一问题在科马尼尼（Comanini）于 1591 年发表的对话录《Il Figino》中讨论得更为详尽。对话者包括布雷西亚圣萨尔瓦托雷修道院院长阿斯卡尼奥·马尔蒂内恩戈（Ascanio Martinengo）；文学与艺术赞助人斯特凡诺·瓜佐（Stefano Guazzo）；以及安布罗焦·菲吉诺（Ambrogio Figino），
a Milanese painter. In the first part of the dialogue Guazzo argues that the aim of painting is simply to produce pleasure, and maintains an art-for-art’s-sake theory. Martinengo, the priest, opposes him and says that though painting produces pleasure by means of imitation, yet it is subject to moral philosophy, and its real end is utility not pleasure. Art, he maintains, has always been controlled by the State, as in Egypt, Greece, and Rome, and has been directed by the State towards good ends. In Christian times the control of art as a useful activity belongs to the Church, which generally has directed it and always should direct it towards the support of religion. In the end Guazzo gives in and admits that the primary end of painting is utility and that the pleasure which it produces is only of secondary importance. The speakers then turn to other matters and Figino maintains that painting is capable of more perfect imitation than poetry, and is therefore more useful than poetry. But the main theme remains clear: painting should aim at moral improvement by means of instruction according to the principles of the Church, not at pleasure by means of aesthetic stimulus. In this thesis is summed up the whole view of the CounterReformation on the position and function of the Fine Arts.
一位米兰画家。在对话的前半部分，Guazzo 认为绘画的目的仅仅是带来愉悦，并坚持为艺术而艺术的理论。牧师 Martinengo 反对他，指出尽管绘画通过模仿产生愉悦，但它受道德哲学的约束，其真正目的不是愉悦而是有用。Martinengo 认为，艺术历来受到国家的控制，如在埃及、希腊和罗马，并且国家已将艺术引向良善的目标。在基督教时代，作为有用活动的艺术的控制属于教会，教会通常并且始终应当把艺术引导用于支持宗教。最终，Guazzo 屈服，承认绘画的首要目的在于有用，而它所产生的愉悦只是次要的。随后话题转向其他事项，Figino 主张绘画比诗歌更能实现更完美的模仿，因此比诗歌更有用。但主要主题仍然清晰：绘画应以按照教会原则的教导手段来实现道德改良为目标，而不是通过美学刺激来追求愉悦。 在这篇论文中，总结了整个天主教反宗教改革对美术地位与功能的看法。
The theories so far discussed in this section are those of the most austere Counter-Reformers on the arts. They would have been endorsed by the ascetic Popes Paul IV or Pius V and by the great saints of the spiritual regeneration like St. Charles Borromeo. But these were not the only figures involved in the Counter-Reformation, and in both the religious and artistic development of the period there were other movements and other individuals of a quite different temper.
到目前为止本节讨论的理论，都是在美术问题上最为严格的反宗教改革者的观点。这些观点会得到禁欲主义教皇保禄四世或庇护五世以及像圣·查尔斯·博罗梅奥那样致力于灵性再生的伟大圣人的赞同。但这些并非参与反宗教改革的唯一人物，在该时期的宗教与艺术发展中，还存在其他运动和性情迥异的个人。
The aim of the severe reformers just mentioned was to recapture a medieval purity of doctrine and a monastic simplicity of life. Their ideas were drawn from the past in which they saw many good features which the men of
上述严厉改革者的目标是恢复中世纪的教义纯洁性和修道式的生活简朴。他们的思想来源于过去，在过去他们看到了许多美好之处，这些是当代人所缺乏的。
their own day might profitably imitate. In the curing of abuses their work was of great value, but in some ways they were out of touch with modern conditions and towards the end of the sixteenth century it became clear that their reactionary reforms would not give the Church that vigour which it needed if it was to re-establish its power after the attacks of Protestantism. Gradually, therefore, there grew up, parallel with the harsher institutions of reform, bodies which aimed at adapting the Catholic Faith to the needs of modern life. The principal agents of this transformation were the Jesuits, but other organizations such as the Oratory contributed their share, and Popes like Pius IV and Clement VIII, more worldly in their outlook than a Paul IV or a Sixtus V, encouraged the movement. The principle on which these new missionaries worked was that religion must not be made so grim in its appearance and so discouraging in its unattainable ideals that ordinary people would be frightened away altogether from the Church. So they set about making religion more accessible, not by giving it a more rational foundation as the Protestants had done, but by making it appeal to the emotions.
他们认为同代人可以从中有益地效仿。在纠正弊端方面，他们的工作非常有价值，但在某些方面他们与现代情况脱节，到了十六世纪末，显然他们那种保守的改革不足以为教会在遭受新教冲击后恢复其权威提供所需的活力。因此，渐渐地，在那些更严厉的改革机构并行发展的，是一些旨在使天主教信仰适应现代生活需要的团体。推动这一转变的主要力量是耶稣会，但诸如 Oratory 等其他组织也做出了贡献，像庇护四世（Pius IV）和克莱孟八世（Clement VIII）这样的教皇，比保禄四世（Paul IV）或西斯图斯五世（Sixtus V）世俗性更强，鼓励了这一运动。这些新传教士所遵循的原则是，宗教不应在外表上显得如此严峻、其不可企及的理想如此气馁，以致普通人完全被教会吓退。因此，他们着手使宗教更易接近，并非像新教徒那样给它一个更理性的基础，而是通过使其诉诸情感来实现。
It is hardly necessary to prove in detail how much the Jesuits relied on an appeal through the senses for the excitement of religious emotion. The Exercises of St. Ignatius are evidence enough. In them the neophyte is urged to use all his five senses to realize, almost to re-enact, the scenes of the Passion, the torments of Hell, or the bliss of Heaven. He is not only to acknowledge these things with the mind, he is to feel them with the heart through the senses. The Jesuits, however, were by no means alone in using these methods. St. Philip Neri attached, much value to music as a means of heightening the appeal of pious words, and the music which he preferred for performance at the Oratory was neither the old frivolous music of the Renaissance, nor the simple setting of the words which the Tridentine decrees demanded, but the
无需详细证明耶稣会士在激发宗教情感方面有多么依赖通过感官的呼唤。《圣·伊纳爵灵修操练》本身就足以证明这一点。在这些操练中，新教徒被敦促动用他的五官去体会，几乎是重新演绎，受难的场景、地狱的折磨或天堂的福乐。他不仅要在理智上承认这些事，而要通过感官用心去感受它们。然而，使用这些方法的并非只有耶稣会士。圣·菲利波·内里非常重视音乐，认为音乐是增强虔诚言辞感染力的手段，他在祷告堂偏好的演奏音乐既不是文艺复兴时期那种轻浮的旧音乐，也不是特伦特会议法令所要求的仅对词句作简单伴奏，而是...
rich and impressive work of Palestrina’s later period. It was neither intellectual nor ascetic, but sensuous, and it fits in with St. Philip’s character, with its curious mixture of practical sense and mysticism.
帕莱斯特里纳晚期丰润而令人印象深刻的作品。它既不理智也不苦行，而是感官性的，符合圣菲利普的性格——那种实用理智与神秘主义奇妙混合的特质。
The quarrel between the old and the new in the CounterReformation came to a head in the dispute between the Jesuits and the Dominicans which occupied the last ten years of Clement VIII’s pontificate and was only silenced, not settled, by Paul V. The Dominicans considered themselves the heirs of St. Thomas Aquinas, whose system they strove to maintain in every detail. The Jesuits, on the other hand, found the rigidity of these doctrines a handicap in their proselytizing work, and in particular considered that the gloomy Thomistic theory of grace and free will was a hindrance to many potentially good Catholics. Through two of their official spokesmen, Aquaviva and Molina, they began to enunciate a more optimistic belief according to which man’s will is freer than St. Thomas admitted, so that he can to some extent work out his own salvation. The dispute which arose out of this difference was in effect the conflict between the supporters of a medieval doctrine and those who wished to modify this doctrine in order to make of it a more efficient weapon in propagating the Faith. As has already been said, Paul V cut the dispute short without making any decision; but this was practically a victory for the Jesuits, for they were the challengers and had avoided condemnation. They only had to wait till the accession of Gregory XV in 1621 for their views to be fully accepted, at least in practice. One of this Pope’s first acts was the canonization of St. Ignatius and St. Francis Xavier, and this may be taken as typical of the policy of submission to Jesuit control which he and his successor Urban VIII consistently followed.
反宗教改革时期的新旧之争在耶稣会与多米尼加会之间的争论中达到高潮，这场争论占据了克莱门特八世教宗在位的最后十年，直到保禄五世才平息，但并未解决。多米尼加会自视为圣托马斯·阿奎那的继承者，努力在各个细节上维护其体系。另一方面，耶稣会认为这些教义的僵化妨碍了他们的传教工作，尤其认为托马斯那阴郁的恩典与自由意志理论阻碍了许多本可成为好天主教徒的人。通过他们的两位官方代言人阿奎维瓦和莫利纳，耶稣会开始阐明一种更为乐观的信念，认为人的意志比圣托马斯所承认的更为自由，从而人在某种程度上可以自己争取救赎。由此产生的争论事实上是中世纪教义的支持者与那些希望修改该教义以使其成为更有效传福音工具的人之间的冲突。 正如前面所说，保禄五世在不作任何判决的情况下草草结束了争论；但这实际上是耶稣会的胜利，因为他们是挑战者，却避免了被谴责。他们只需等到 1621 年格里高利十五世即位，他们的观点便至少在实践上得到完全接受。这位教皇的首批举措之一就是将圣依纳爵和圣方济·沙勿略封为圣人，这可以视为他与其继任者乌尔巴诺八世始终如一地奉行向耶稣会控制屈从的政策的典型表现。
This worldly, emotional, anti-intellectual kind of religion produced its equivalent in the arts. In the seventeenth century the whole Baroque movement must be closely associated
这种世俗的、情绪化的、反智的宗教在艺术上也产生了它的对应物。在十七世纪，整个巴洛克运动必须与此紧密联系起来
with the Jesuits, but even before that time there was a branch of Mannerist painting in which many of the same qualities could be found as in the methods and writings of Jesuits and members of the Oratory. Parallel with the academic and aristocratic Mannerism of Florence, and with the didactic style which flourished under the more severe Popes and is perhaps best shown in the frescoes of Sixtus V’s library in the Vatican, there was a current of emotional and ecstatic painting, particularly associated with the name of Barocci, but including a whole group of artists in Rome and elsewhere. In Barocci the ecstatic subject is common; it is rendered with a whirl of floating figures and sweeping draperies which anticipate Bernini, and in intense colours which appeal directly to the eye and not to the mind. This irrational use of colour recalls the frescoes of Pontormo in the Certosa. Now, however, the colours are applied not to grim, gothicizing, spiritualized forms, but to fleshy figures which smile only too sweetly, or express their emotions of terror in gestures which appeal to the senses like the coy movements of Greuze’s virtuous girls. It is typical of the connexion between this kind of art and bodies like the Jesuits and the Oratory that St. Philip Neri had a particular predilection for the painting of Barocci, and was on one occasion found in an ecstasy in front of his altar-piece of the Visitation in S. Maria in Vallicella. It was for Pius IV, the supporter of the Jesuits, that Barocci first worked in Rome, where he decorated for him the Casino in the Vatican gardens. Further, almost all the artists employed in the original decoration of the central church of the Jesuits, the Gesù, such as Giovanni de’ Vecchi, Salimbeni, and Muziano, belong to that group of Mannerists in whom anticipations of the Baroque are most evident.
与耶稣会有关，但甚至在那之前，就已有一种矫饰派绘画分支，其中许多与耶稣会及祈祷会成员的做法和著述中所见的特质相同。与佛罗伦萨的学院派与贵族式矫饰主义并行，以及在较为严厉的教皇统治下盛行、或许在西斯图斯五世在梵蒂冈图书馆的壁画中表现得最为明显的教训式风格，并存着一种情感和狂喜式的绘画潮流，特别与巴罗奇的名字相关，但也包括一整群活跃于罗马及其它地方的艺术家。在巴罗奇作品中，狂喜题材很常见；他以漂浮的人物和飞扬的衣褶构成的漩涡来表现这种主题，预示了贝尼尼，并以直接诉诸于眼睛而非理性的强烈色彩呈现。这种非理性的色彩运用让人想起庞托尔莫在卡尔托萨的壁画。只是如今这些色彩不再施用于严峻、哥特化、灵性化的形象上，而是用于那些面带过分甜美微笑的血肉之躯，或以像格鲁兹（Greuze）贞洁少女那样含蓄的动作来传达恐惧情绪，从而触动感官。 这种艺术与耶稣会及奥拉托里奥等团体的联系有一个典型例证：圣菲利浦·内里特别偏爱巴罗奇的绘画，曾有一次在圣玛利亚·因·瓦利切拉（S. Maria in Vallicella）他那幅“访礼”（Visitation）祭坛画面前陷入狂喜。正是为支持耶稣会的庇护四世（Pius IV），巴罗奇首次在罗马工作，为他装饰了梵蒂冈花园内的别墅（Casino）。此外，几乎所有参与耶稣会中央教堂——圣依纳爵堂（the Gesù）最初装饰的艺术家，如 Giovanni de’ Vecchi、Salimbeni 和 Muziano，都属于那类在风格上最明显预示巴洛克的矫饰主义者（Mannerists）。
This new emotional kind of painting was not of a sort to produce much theorizing. Artists so consciously opposed to the intellect and relying so little on rational appeal would be
这种新的情感化绘画并非那种会产生大量理论化成果的流派。如此有意识地反对理性、又极少依赖理性诉求的艺术家们会是
unlikely to evolve any systematic doctrine about their art, and the only equivalent to this painting is to be found in details of certain expositions of the Tridentine decrees. For instance, the advice of Gilio da Fabriano to the painter that he must show to the full the horrors of any scene of martyrdom which he may have to depict corresponds to the desire of these forerunners of the Baroque to make their appeal as direct and unavoidable as possible. More remarkable, however, is the addition which the Jesuit Possevino makes to this idea, when he says that the painter must himself feel these horrors if he is to convey them to the spectator. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This seems an almost direct application of the methods of the Exercises to the practice of the arts.
不太可能形成关于他们艺术的任何系统性学说，而与此绘画唯一可比较的东西可在某些关于特伦特法令的阐述细节中找到。例如，Gilio da Fabriano 对画家的建议——他必须充分展现任何他要描绘的殉道场景的恐怖——对应于这些巴洛克先驱者希望他们的诉求尽可能直接和不可抗拒的愿望。然而，更为引人注目的是耶稣会士 Possevino 对这一观念的补充，他说画家若要将这些恐怖传达给观众，自己必须亲身感受这些恐怖。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这似乎是《灵修操练》方法对艺术实践的几乎直接应用。

Chapter IX  第九章

THE LATER MANNERISTS  后期矫饰派

A T A T A^(T)\mathbf{A}^{\mathrm{T}}T the end of the sixteenth century Mannerism gradually ceases to be the dominant style in Italian painting, and its place is taken by the Eclecticism of the Carracci and the Bolognese Academy. It is generally said that the Carracci mark a sharp reaction against the Mannerists with all of whose ideas and methods they disagreed. It is true that there is little in common between the Carracci and Mannerists of the Florentine tradition or those of the Beccafumi type, but there is one group of artists, always described as Mannerists, whose doctrines anticipate the methods of the Eclectics so accurately that one is tempted to regard the Bolognese Academy as the realization in practice of ideas evolved by those very Mannerists which the Academy officially condemned.
十六世纪末，矫饰主义在意大利绘画中逐渐不再是主导风格，其地位被卡拉奇家族及博洛尼亚学院的折衷主义所取代。人们常说卡拉奇家族对矫饰主义发起了强烈反击，他们与矫饰主义者的所有思想和方法均不相容。这话虽有道理：卡拉奇家族与佛罗伦萨传统的矫饰主义者或贝卡富米式样者几乎没有共通之处，但有一群艺术家，始终被称为矫饰主义者，他们的学说准确地预示了折衷派的方法，以至于令人倾向于将博洛尼亚学院视为那些被学院正式谴责的矫饰主义者所发展思想在实践中的实现。
Compared with the aristocratic and emotional kinds of Mannerists so far considered the group now referred to may be described as academic and eclectic-the two adjectives usually reserved for the Carracci and their school. These Mannerists were deeply conscious of the decline which had come over Italian art since the days of Leo X, and they hoped like the Carracci to stop this decline not by new discoveries but by the intelligent imitation of the works which the masters of the Renaissance had left behind. For them, as for the Bolognese, painting was a science which could be taught according to fixed rules, and these rules could be discovered by studying the example of good masters.
与迄今所论的那种贵族化与感情化的矫饰派相比，现称之为的这一派可被描述为学术的并兼采众长——这两个形容词通常用于形容 Carracci 及其学派。这些矫饰派艺术家深刻意识到自 Leo X 时代以来意大利艺术所出现的衰落，他们希望像 Carracci 那样遏止这种衰落，不是通过新的发明，而是通过对文艺复兴大师遗留下来的作品进行有意识的模仿。对他们而言，与博洛尼亚学派一样，绘画是一门可以按既定规则教授的科学，而这些规则可以通过研究优秀大师的范例来发现。
These academic Mannerists can be considered in two main groups. One centred round the Academy of Drawing in Rome, and the most important member of it was Federico Zuccaro, who was elected president in 1593. The other, a
这些学术性的矫饰派大致可分为两大类。一类以罗马的素描学院为中心，最重要的成员是 Federico Zuccaro，他于 1593 年当选为院长。另一类是一个
Milanese group, was less important in painting but more significant in theory since it produced the treatises of Lomazzo, in which the doctrines of later Mannerism are set out at full length.
米兰派，在绘画方面不那么重要，但在理论上更有意义，因为它产生了 Lomazzo 的论文，在这些论文中后期矫饰主义的学说得到了详尽阐述。
Of the practice of these two schools it is not necessary to say much. In spite of differences due to the local traditions out of which they sprang, Lomazzo and Federico Zuccaro in his later period belong to the same stage of painting. Both were highly self-conscious in their outlook and calculating in their methods. Both learnt more from other painters than from the study of nature, and each combined in himself stylistic elements taken from many different sources: Zuccaro drawing mainly on the Roman and Venetian traditions, Lomazzo borrowing directly from Leonardo, Raphael, and Michelangelo, and, through his master Gaudenzio Ferrari, deriving qualities from Mantegna and Pontormo. Both artists avoided the almost caricatural extreme of Mannerism which some of their immediate predecessors had reached, and made some return towards the principles of classical composition and drawing practised by Raphael and his contemporaries. But, though it is necessary to emphasize these new qualities in their art, it remains nevertheless true that these two artists are fundamentally Mannerists. Compared with the paintings of Vasari’s Florentine followers their work may seem simple and unaffected, but, put side by side with any panel of the Farnese Gallery, their use of repoussoir figures, of double contraposto, and of obscure allegorical allusions reminds us that they were still deeply involved in the habits of the later sixteenth century. They belong, in fact, to that transitional stage from Mannerism to the seventeenth century which is best represented in the frescoes of the Cavaliere d’Arpino, an artist who, deriving from Mannerism and working independently of the Carracci, yet developed many of the characteristics of the latter’s style.
关于这两派的创作实践无需多言。尽管因发源地的地方传统不同而存在差异，Lomazzo 和 Federico Zuccaro 在其晚期均属于同一绘画阶段。二人都具有高度的自觉性并以计算性的手法行事。二者从其他画家那里学到的东西多于从自然研究中获得的，各自将来自多种不同来源的风格元素融为一体：Zuccaro 主要借鉴罗马和威尼斯的传统，Lomazzo 则直接取法于 Leonardo、Raphael 和 Michelangelo，并通过他的师傅 Gaudenzio Ferrari 从 Mantegna 与 Pontormo 那里汲取特质。两位艺术家都避免了某些前辈已达到的近乎夸张的矫饰主义极端，并在某种程度上回归到 Raphael 及其同时代人所实践的古典构图与素描原则。但即便必须强调他们艺术中这些新的品质，仍然无法改变这样一个事实：这两位艺术家在根本上属于矫饰主义者。 与瓦萨里那些佛罗伦萨追随者的画相比，他们的作品或许显得简朴而不做作，但如果与任何一块法尔内塞美术馆的画板并列观察，他们对挡景人物（repoussoir figures）、双重反对立姿（double contraposto）以及晦涩寓言暗示的运用都会提醒我们，这些画家仍深受十六世纪后期习俗的影响。事实上，他们属于从矫饰主义向十七世纪过渡的那个阶段，而这一阶段在阿尔皮诺骑士（Cavaliere d’Arpino）的壁画中得到了最好的体现——这位艺术家虽源于矫饰主义且独立于卡拉奇派（Carracci）而行，却发展出许多后者风格的特征。
Something must be said of the individual writers whose
必须对那些个别作家作些说明，他们...
theories will be discussed. With the Roman group two names are to be associated-Federico Zuccaro and Giovanni Battista Armenini. The former published a number of small treatises of which much the most important is the Idea de’ Pittori, Scultori e Architetti, printed in 1607. A shorter expression of his views is to be found in Romano Alberti’s Origine e Progresso dell’ Academia del Disegno, published in 1604. This nominally contains the minutes of Academy discussion for the years 1593-4, but since no one but Federico Zuccaro seems to have been allowed to speak, the book is simply a sort of preliminary to the Idea. Armenini was a native of Faenza whose views on the arts, however, were entirely coloured by his six years’ training in Rome between 1550 and 1556. It is significant that he seems to have been more impressed with the works of Raphael’s followers, Polidoro da Caravaggio and Perino del Vaga, than with the newly painted cycles of full Mannerism like Vasari’s Sala de’ Cento Giorni in the Palazzo della Cancelleria, or Salviati’s paintings in the same palace and in the Oratory of S . Giovanni Decollato. On leaving Rome in 1556 Armenini travelled through Italy studying the masters of every school -Giulio Romano at Mantua, Correggio at Parma, Perino del Vaga at Genoa, Titian in Venice. In later life he became a priest. He published his only work on painting in 1586 1 1586 1 1586^(1)1586^{1} and called it Dei Veri Precetti della Pittura-a title which already reveals the academic outlook of its author.
将讨论这些理论。在罗马派中应关联两个名字——Federico Zuccaro 和 Giovanni Battista Armenini。前者出版了若干小型论著，其中最重要的是 1607 年印刷的 Idea de’ Pittori, Scultori e Architetti。他观点的简短表述见于 Romano Alberti 于 1604 年出版的 Origine e Progresso dell’ Academia del Disegno。该书名义上包含了 1593–94 年学院讨论的记录，但除 Federico Zuccaro 外似乎没人被允许发言，因此这本书只是 Idea 的一种前奏。Armenini 出生于 Faenza，但他对艺术的看法完全受他在 1550 到 1556 年间在罗马六年训练的影响。值得注意的是，他似乎对拉斐尔门徒如 Polidoro da Caravaggio 和 Perino del Vaga 的作品印象更深，而不是对像 Vasari 在 Palazzo della Cancelleria 的 Sala de’ Cento Giorni 或 Salviati 在同一宫殿及 S. Giovanni Decollato 礼拜堂中的那些完全风格主义（full Mannerism）新绘画周期印象深刻。 1556 年离开罗马后，Armenini 周游意大利，研习各派大师——曼图亚的 Giulio Romano、帕尔马的 Correggio、热那亚的 Perino del Vaga、威尼斯的 Titian。晚年他成为了一名牧师。他在 1586 1 1586 1 1586^(1)1586^{1} 发表了关于绘画的唯一著作，题为 Dei Veri Precetti della Pittura——这一书名已透露出其作者的学术取向。
The interest of the Milanese group centres entirely round Lomazzo. He was born in 1538 and was trained mainly under Gaudenzio Ferrari. He went blind in 1571 and was therefore forced to give up painting and take instead to the theory of the arts. He evidently fancied himself a master in every intellectual field and was proud of being president of a local
米兰学派的兴趣完全围绕 Lomazzo。他生于 1538 年，主要师从 Gaudenzio Ferrari。1571 年他失明，因此不得不放弃绘画，转而从事艺术理论。他显然自视为各个知识领域的大师，并以担任当地一所学校的主席为荣。
organization, the Accademia della Valle di Bregno. Apart from his poems, some of them in dialect, and his autobiography in verse, he published two major works on the arts. The first was entitled Trattato dell’ Arte della Pittura, Scultura, et Architettura and was printed in 1584. The second, which appeared six years later, was called Idea del Tempio della Pittura. The Trattato, which will be described in detail later, is an exhaustive volume, of which the Idea is a sort of summary, containing less detailed advice and more abstract aesthetics.
组织，即布雷尼奥山谷学院。除了一些方言诗和以诗体写成的自传外，他还出版了两部关于美术的重要著作。第一部题为 Trattato dell’ Arte della Pittura, Scultura, et Architettura，发表于 1584 年。六年后出版的第二部名为 Idea del Tempio della Pittura。Trattato（后文将详细描述）是一本详尽的著作，而 Idea 则有点像其概要，包含较少的具体建议和更多抽象的美学论述。
In the theories of the late Mannerists the same division is visible as in their paintings. They are half in sympathy with earlier Mannerism and half in reaction against it. At one moment they speak like Vasari; at the next they seem nearer to the classical critics of the seventeenth century. In general they are novel in their practical teaching, but still fully Mannerist when they write of aesthetic questions and of beauty in the abstract. It will therefore be convenient to treat these two sections of their writings separately.
在晚期矫饰主义者的理论中，正如他们的绘画一样，也可见相同的分裂。他们一方面对早期矫饰主义抱有同情，另一方面又对其反动。有时他们的论调像瓦萨里；而下一刻又更接近十七世纪的古典评论家。总体而言，他们在实用教导上具有新意，但在论述审美问题和抽象之美时仍完全属于矫饰主义。因此将他们著作的这两部分分别讨论会更为合适。
It has already been said that just as the CounterReformation in its earlier stages was a reaction towards feudalism, so Mannerism was in many respects a return towards Medievalism in art. The direct effect of this in connexion with religious art was discussed in the last chapter. In Lomazzo and his contemporaries the influence of the Middle Ages was no less important, but it appears in a different form. They all agree with the officials of the Church that art must be subservient to religion, but this is not a matter to which they devote much space, and it is in their abstract discussions of aesthetics that their anti-classical tendencies appear most clearly.
前面已经提到，正如反宗教改革在其早期阶段在许多方面是对封建主义的一种反动一样，风格主义在艺术上在许多方面也是对中世纪主义的某种回归。上一章讨论了这在宗教艺术方面的直接影响。在洛马佐及其同时代人那里，中世纪的影响同样重要，但以不同的形式出现。他们在是否同意教会官员主张艺术必须服从宗教这一点上是一致的，但他们并未在这方面投入大量篇幅，反而在他们对美学的抽象讨论中，他们的反古典倾向最为清晰地显现出来。
Lomazzo and Zuccaro differ in many details of their aesthetic views, but one important feature is common to both, their systems. Whereas for the writers of the Early and High Renaissance nature was the source from which all beauty was
洛马佐和祖卡罗在许多美学观点的细节上存在差异，但两人的体系有一个共同的重要特征。对于早期和盛期文艺复兴的作家来说，自然是所有美的源泉，然而…
ultimately derived, however much it might be transformed by the artist’s imagination, for these Mannerists beauty was something which was directly infused into the mind of man from the mind of God, and existed there independent of any sense-impressions. The idea in the artist’s mind was the source of all the beauty in the works which he created, and his ability to give a picture of the outside world was of no importance, except in so far as it helped him to give visible expression to his idea. The relation of the artist to nature, which was immediate in the Early Renaissance and important, though not so dominant, in the case of Michelangelo, has here been almost broken off. Lomazzo and Zuccaro both perfunctorily define painting as the imitation of nature, but neither refers to the matter at any length, and both had in mind more particularly the Scholastic idea that art works according to the same principles as nature, rather than the view that painting copies the individual works of nature. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} That is to say, they mean that both painting and nature are controlled by intellect-in the one case human and in the other divine intellect-that both obey certain laws of order, and so on. Zuccaro attacks the view that painting copies nature in one of his lectures to the Roman Academy, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} and when Armenini comes to define painting nature is not mentioned at all. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} In both cases the emphasis is on the idea in the artist’s mind, which is the proper object of imitation.
然而无论被艺术家的想象如何改造，对于这些矫饰派艺术家来说，美是直接从上帝的心灵注入到人的心灵中并独立于任何感官印象而存在的。艺术家心中的观念是一切他所创作作品中美的源泉，而他描绘外部世界的能力并不重要，除非这种能力有助于他把心中的观念以可见形式表达出来。艺术家与自然的关系在早期文艺复兴时期是直接的、重要的——在米开朗基罗的情况下虽不那么占主导地位，但仍然重要——而在这里几乎被切断。洛玛佐（Lomazzo）和佐加罗（Zuccaro）都草率地将绘画定义为对自然的模仿，但两人对这一问题都没有详细论述，更特别的是，他们心中考虑的是经院哲学的观点：艺术遵循与自然相同的原理，而不是绘画复制自然的个别作品。也就是说，他们的意思是，绘画和自然都受理性支配——前者为人类理性，后者为神性理性——二者都服从某些秩序法则，诸如此类。 Zuccaro 在他对罗马学院的一个讲座中抨击了绘画模仿自然的观点 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} ，而当 Armenini 试图对绘画下定义时，根本没有提到自然。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 在这两种情况下，强调的是艺术家头脑中的观念，这是模仿的恰当对象。
For Zuccaro ideas exist in three different stages: first in the mind of God, secondly in the mind of angels, and thirdly in the mind of man. Since he is writing for artists, he chooses to avoid the word idea, and prefers to it the phrase disegno interno. By this device he is able to argue that everything
对 Zuccaro 来说，观念存在于三个不同的阶段：首先存在于上帝的心中，其次存在于天使的心中，第三存在于人的心中。既然他是为艺术家而写，他选择避免使用“idea”一词，而更喜欢用短语 disegno interno。通过这一手段，他能够论证一切
derives ultimately from disegno interno, and that drawing is the foundation of all intellectual pursuits. Disegno interno is entirely without substance and is a reflection of the divine in us. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} This scheme and the account which Zuccaro gives of the workings of the intellect are exactly in accordance with Scholastic doctrines, and in many cases are explained in passages copied directly from St. Thomas. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Many of the ideas which Zuccaro expresses are Aristotelian in origin, but they are combined with elements of Christian doctrine to form a typically medieval Scholastic blend. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
最终源自 disegno interno（内在构思），而素描是所有智力活动的基础。Disegno interno 完全没有物质性，是我们体内神性的映照。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 这一体系以及 Zuccaro 对智力运作的描述完全符合经院哲学教义，且在许多情形下直接引用了圣托马斯的段落进行阐释。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Zuccaro 表达的许多思想源自亚里士多德，但它们与基督教教义的元素相结合，形成了典型的中世纪经院派混合体。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
With Lomazzo the scheme is in many ways similar, but flavoured with a strong addition of Neoplatonism. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Whereas Zuccaro is more concerned with the intellectual idea, in Lomazzo the concept of beauty plays a far greater part. For to the Neoplatonist beauty is a visible manifestation of the good. According to Lomazzo beauty is a spiritual grace, ‘una certa grazia vivace e spiritale’, which springs from God and appears in three ways; in angels, where it forms ideas; in the human soul, where it is called reason or knowledge (ragione or notizie); in matter, where it creates images or forms (imagini or forme). The means by which beauty is infused into matter or into the human soul are not logically explained, but the process is compared with that of light
在洛马佐这里，这一体系在许多方面相似，但带有强烈的新柏拉图主义色彩。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 而祖卡罗更关注智性观念，在洛马佐那里，美的概念占据了更重要的地位。因为对新柏拉图主义者而言，美是善的可见显现。根据洛马佐的观点，美是一种属灵的恩宠，“una certa grazia vivace e spiritale”，它来自上帝并以三种方式显现：在天使身上，形成观念；在人类灵魂中，被称为理性或知识（ragione or notizie）；在物质中，创造形象或形式（imagini or forme）。美被注入物质或人类灵魂的方式并未作出逻辑上的解释，但这一过程被比作光

图 8：Federico Zuccaro。《绘画的寓意》。Palazzo Zuccaro，罗马
