streaming from the face of God and absorbed by spiritual and material beings. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
从上帝面颜发出并被属灵与物质存在吸收的流动。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }}
Although Zuccaro and Lomazzo differ about the general problems of aesthetics, it appears that they have in common certain important qualities: both are strongly anti-rationalist and mystical, and in both the scientific spirit characteristic of Renaissance thought is entirely absent. In both the idea from which the work of art is copied derives from God and not from the outside world. Both writers have their eyes turned inward, not outward, and they would have sympathized with the feelings of another Mannerist, El Greco, as recorded in a story, perhaps apocryphal, told of him by Giulio Clovio. Clovio went to see him on a summer day and discovered El Greco sitting, inactive, in a room with the curtains drawn, because he found the darkness more conducive to thought than the light of day, which disturbed his inner light. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
尽管 Zuccaro 和 Lomazzo 在美学的一般问题上意见相左，但他们似乎有一些共同的重要特质：两人都强烈反理性主义且带有神秘主义色彩，而且两人都完全缺乏文艺复兴思想特有的科学精神。在两人的观点中，艺术作品所复制的观念都源自上帝，而非外在世界。两位作者的目光向内而非向外，他们会支持另一位矫饰主义者 El Greco 的感受，这在 Giulio Clovio 所记述的一个故事中有所反映，该故事可能是伪托。Clovio 某个夏日去看望他，发现 El Greco 坐着，静止不动，房间里拉着窗帘，因为他觉得黑暗比白昼的光更有助于思考，白昼的光会干扰他内在的光。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
Further, the ideas of both Zuccaro and Lomazzo discussed above are all strongly medieval. The Neoplatonist Christianity of the latter and the Scholasticism of the former are both signs of the tendency in the Mannerist period for theorists as well as artists to give up the rational ideals which had dominated the Renaissance in its pure manifestations and to return to the non-humanist theological values of medieval Catholicism. In the case of Lomazzo the Gothic effect is greatly increased by the form in which he expresses his ideas. His fondness for astrology led him to use a complicated system of symbolism, according to which every quality in painting and every division of the mental faculties are placed under
此外，以上讨论的 Zuccaro 和 Lomazzo 的观点都具有浓厚的中世纪色彩。后者的新柏拉图主义基督教和前者的经院哲学都表明，在矫饰主义时期，理论家和艺术家都有放弃在其纯粹表现中曾主导文艺复兴的理性理想、回归中世纪天主教非人文主义神学价值的倾向。在 Lomazzo 的 case 中，这种哥特式影响因他表达思想的形式而大大增强。他对占星术的偏爱使他采用了一个复杂的象征体系，根据该体系，绘画中的每一种品质和精神能力的每一个划分都归属于
the protection of a particular planet. The types of proportion in the human body and the different emotions which the painter must depict are divided into seven planetary groups, and the painters chosen as Governors of the Temple of Painting are each connected with a heavenly body-Raphael with Venus, Leonardo with the Sun, and so on. There is also considerable play in Lomazzo with the symbolism of numbers, with the seven circles of heaven, and with all the apparatus of medieval astrology. Even Zuccaro, who is in general clear of this particular lumber, when he compares drawing with the sun as the source of all light, cannot resist dragging in Mercury, Jupiter, and the rest to complete the picture, I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} and some of Vincenzo Borghini’s letters about painting are obscured with the same symbolism. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} His namesake, Raffaello Borghini, however, avoids this method and is able to satisfy his urge for complicated comparisons in Christian and mythological terms. It is not surprising that this medieval tendency appears more strongly in Lomazzo than in the other writers, for Milan had never been as fully conquered by the Renaissance as the towns of central Italy. There was always a certain connexion kept up between Lombardy and the countries north of the Alps, and throughout the sixteenth century the influence of Gothic painting was strong in Milan, even in Leonardo’s immediate followers, but more particularly in Lomazzo’s master Gaudenzio Ferrari.
对某一特定行星的保护。人体的比例类型以及画家必须描绘的不同情感被划分为七个行星组，而被选为“绘画神殿”守护者的画家各自与一个天体相联系——拉斐尔与金星、莱昂纳多与太阳，等等。Lomazzo 在数字象征、七重天球以及中世纪占星术的全部装置上也玩味颇多。即便是通常不受此类繁冗影响的 Zuccaro，当他将素描比作一切光的源头太阳时，也忍不住把水星、木星等牵扯进来以完善图景， I I ^(I){ }^{\mathrm{I}} 而 Vincenzo Borghini 关于绘画的一些信件也被同样的象征主义所掩蔽。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 然而，同名的 Raffaello Borghini 避免了这种方法，能够用基督教和神话的术语来满足他对复杂类比的冲动。Lomazzo 比其他作家更明显地展现出这种中世纪倾向并不令人惊讶，因为米兰从未像意大利中部的城镇那样被文艺复兴完全征服。 伦巴第地区与阿尔卑斯山以北各国之间始终保持着某种联系，整个十六世纪哥特式绘画在米兰影响颇深，即便在莱昂纳多的直接追随者中亦然，但在洛马佐的师傅高登齐奥·费拉里身上尤为明显。
The almost mystical doctrines held by the later Mannerists about the nature of beauty and the foundations of art were accompanied by many other anti-rational features, of which perhaps the most important is the new attitude towards the relation of painting to mathematics. Lomazzo admits that proportion and perspective are based on actual measurement and on the certain methods of mathematics, 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} but he reminds
晚期矫饰派关于美的本质和艺术基础所持的几乎神秘主义的学说伴随了许多其他反理性特征，其中也许最重要的是他们对绘画与数学关系的新态度。洛马佐承认比例和透视是基于实际测量和确定的数学方法，但他提醒
the artist that this is only a foundation, and that in the last resort he must rely on his eye and not on his compasses. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Zuccaro goes much further and denies the connexion with mathematics altogether:
艺术家这只是一个基础，归根结底他必须依靠自己的眼睛而不是圆规。祖卡罗走得更远，完全否认与数学的联系：
‘But I say-and I know that I speak the truth-that the art of painting does not derive from the mathematical sciences, nor has it any need to resort to them to learn rules or means for its own art, nor even in order to reason abstractly about this art: for painting is not the daughter of mathematics but of Nature and of Drawing.’ 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
“但我说——我知道我所言为真——绘画的艺术并非源自数学科学，也不需要借助它们来学习本艺的规则或方法，甚至不需要借助它们来对此艺术进行抽象推理：因为绘画不是数学的女儿，而是自然与素描的女儿。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
So mathematics, which had been to the early Humanist artists one of the chief weapons in the scientific study of the outside world, is in the Mannerist period almost driven out of painting. The certainty of scientific observation has given place to a conviction directly inspired by God: reason has given way to faith.
因此，对于早期人文主义艺术家来说曾是研究外部世界科学手段之一的数学，在矫饰主义时期几乎被逐出绘画。科学观察的确定性让位于一种直接来自上帝的信念：理性让位于信仰。
Certain writers of this period go farther and deny not only the validity of mathematics as a foundation for painting but the possibility of the arts being based on any certain rules at all. Giordano Bruno says that poetry does not spring from rules, but rules from poetry, and that there are therefore as many different kinds of rule as there are different kinds of poets. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Zuccaro writes that the mind of the artist 'must be not only clear but free, and his invention unfettered and not compelled to the mechanical slavery of such rules; for this noble profession demands judgement and skilful execution which are its rules and standards of working. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} And for Zuccaro judgement is no longer a rational and intellectual faculty but the weapon which ‘chooses that which is most pleasing to the eye’. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
这一时期的某些作家更进一步，不仅否定数学作为绘画基础的有效性，而且否定艺术可以建立在任何确定规则之上的可能性。乔尔达诺·布鲁诺（Giordano Bruno）说，诗歌不是源自规则，而是规则源自诗歌，因此规则的种类与诗人的种类一样多。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 祖卡罗（Zuccaro）写道，艺术家的心灵“必须不仅清晰而且自由，他的创造力不受束缚，不被强迫屈从于此类规则的机械奴役；因为这一高尚的职业要求判断力和娴熟的技艺，这些才是其工作准则和标准。 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} ” 对于祖卡罗来说，判断已不再是一个理性和智力的能力，而是那把“选择最悦目者”的武器。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
It has already been said in connexion with Vasari that the
关于瓦萨里（Vasari）已经在相关处提到，
rising importance which attached to the quality of grace in the sixteenth century was a sign of an anti-rational attitude towards the arts. In the later Mannerists this quality plays a great part. It is in general treated by Lomazzo in the same way as by Vasari: it appeals to the eye and cannot be attained by mere study. I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} Zuccaro is even more explicit: 'Grace is… a soft and sweet accompaniment which attracts the eye and contents the taste . . .; it depends entirely on good judgement and good taste. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} This coupling of grace with taste (gusto) is another sign that it is a sensuous and not an intellectual quality, a fact which is brought out even more clearly in a passage where it is put with spirito and sapore as the vital qualities which a too great subservience to the rules of mathematics will destroy.
十六世纪对“优雅”品质日益重视，表明对艺术存在一种反理性态度。在晚期矫饰主义者中，这一品质起了很大作用。总体上，Lomazzo 对它的处理方式与 Vasari 相同：它诉诸于视觉，不能仅靠学习获得。 I I  ^("I "){ }^{\text {I }} Zuccaro 更为直白：“优雅是……一种柔和甜美的伴随，使目光为之吸引、使趣味得到满足……；它完全依赖于良好的判断力和良好的品味。” 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 将优雅与品味（gusto）联系在一起，进一步表明它是一种感官性的而非理性的品质；在另一段文字中，这一点更为清楚——将其与 spirito 和 sapore 一并列为生命性的品质，而对数学规则的过分服从会摧毁这些品质。
So far the ideas of Lomazzo and his contemporaries considered in this chapter have been those which are generally in agreement with Mannerist principles. It is not till we leave their explanations of the nature of beauty and the function of the arts and come to the methods which they recommend for the training of artists and for the actual practice of painting that the new features in their theories appear.
到目前为止，本章所讨论的洛马佐及其同时代人的观点，与矫饰主义原则大体一致。只有当我们不再局限于他们对美的本质和艺术功能的解释，而转而考察他们为艺术家训练和绘画实际操作所推荐的方法时，他们理论中新出现的特征才显现出来。
It has been said above that these later Mannerists were aware of the decline which had taken place in Italian art since the generation of Raphael, Michelangelo, and Titian, and the feelings which this decline aroused in them receive clear expression in their writings. Armenini speaks of the horror which these masters would feel if they could come back and see the works of their followers. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Lomazzo attributes the decay of the arts to the fact that artists will not think out their works with enough care in advance, 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} nor take enough trouble in making themselves perfect in their art. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Zuccaro makes
前文已指出，这些后期矫饰主义者意识到自拉斐尔、米开朗基罗和提香那一代以来意大利艺术所发生的衰落，这种衰落在他们的著作中得到了明显表达。Armenini 谈到如果那些大师能复生看到他们追随者的作品会感到的惊恐。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Lomazzo 将艺术的衰败归因于艺术家在事前对作品缺乏充分的思考， 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 也不在使自己在艺术上臻于完善方面下足功夫。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Zuccaro 指出
the poor state of the arts his main theme in the Lamento della Pittura. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Painters wish only to please the eye and neglect all the intellectual side of their art. Their principal qualities are capriccio, frenesia, furore, and bizzaria, whereas they should display disegno, grazia, decoro, maestà, concetti, and arte. These demands seem not to be entirely in agreement with Zuccaro’s belief in the importance of gusto, but contradictions like this are common in the writers of this group, and only bring out more clearly the transitional position which they held.
在《绘画的哀歌》中，他把艺术的糟糕状况作为主要主题。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 画家只求取悦于眼睛，忽视了他们艺术的所有智力层面。他们的主要特征是 capriccio、frenesia、furore 和 bizzaria，而他们本应展现 disegno、grazia、decoro、maestà、concetti 和 arte。这些要求似乎与 Zuccaro 对 gusto 重要性的信念并不完全一致，但此类矛盾在这一群体的作家中很常见，只是更清楚地显现出他们所处的过渡性立场。
The hope of the later Mannerists was to save the arts from falling to a yet lower point by academic methods. They were academic in both the particular and general senses of the word. In the particular sense, they actually used the existing academies as weapons for attaining their ends, and they show particular pride at being members of different academies, even when the latter had nothing in particular to do with their own professions. Lomazzo, for instance, was president of the Accademia della Valle di Bregno, the main business of which was to preserve a local dialect; and Zuccaro was not only President of the Academy of Drawing in Rome, but also of the Accademia Insensata at Bologna and of the Innominata at Parma, and he made efforts to found other academies in Venice and elsewhere. These academies of drawing, which had been founded as a demonstration of the fact that painting was a liberal art, were gradually changing their character in the later sixteenth century. They were no longer simply meeting-places where those interested could discuss the general problems of the arts, but they had become institutions in which every detail of instruction was supervised and fixed by rule.
晚期矫饰派的希望是通过学术的方法把艺术从进一步堕落中拯救出来。他们在“学术”的狭义和广义两层含义上都是学究式的。狭义上，他们确实把现有的学院当作实现目的的武器，并且为成为各种学院的成员而感到特别骄傲，即便这些学院与他们自身的职业并无直接关联。例如，洛马佐（Lomazzo）曾担任 Accademia della Valle di Bregno 的会长，该会的主要事务是保护一种地方方言；祖卡罗（Zuccaro）不仅是罗马绘画学院的会长，还是博洛尼亚的 Accademia Insensata 和帕尔马的 Innominata 的会长，并曾努力在威尼斯及其他地方创办学院。这些最初为表明绘画属于自由艺术而创立的绘画学院，在十六世纪后期逐渐改变了性质。它们不再只是利于相关人士讨论艺术总体问题的聚会场所，而变成了对教学每一个细节均由规则监督和固定的机构。
But the late Mannerists were also academic in the wider
但晚期风格主义者在更广泛的意义上也是学术的
sense of the word. Their doctrine was exclusive. They scorned the idea of making a wide or popular appeal and deliberately directed their work towards a select, educated public 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} of men who could understand the subtleties of painting and would not be taken in by technical brilliance like the ignorant crowd. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Even in appreciating human beauty training and a knowledge of painting are necessary if one is not to judge it like an animal. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} If knowledge and learning are important in the spectator, it follows that they are even more necessary in the painter himself, who must be learned in all the sciences connected with his art-and in many, such as astrology or philosophy, which do not to us seem directly relevant to it. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4}
“sense of the word. Their doctrine was exclusive. They scorned the idea of making a wide or popular appeal and deliberately directed their work towards a select, educated public 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} of men who could understand the subtleties of painting and would not be taken in by technical brilliance like the ignorant crowd. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Even in appreciating human beauty training and a knowledge of painting are necessary if one is not to judge it like an animal. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} If knowledge and learning are important in the spectator, it follows that they are even more necessary in the painter himself, who must be learned in all the sciences connected with his art-and in many, such as astrology or philosophy, which do not to us seem directly relevant to it. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} ”
The demand for knowledge in the painter is a manifestation of one of the fundamental tenets of the late Mannerist system, namely, a belief that the arts can be taught by precept. This assumption runs all through the Trattato of Lomazzo, which is a Handbook to Painting in a much more thorough sense than any of the earlier treatises. Armenini is quite explicit on the point. The title of his book, D e ′ D e ′ De^(')D e^{\prime} Veri Precetti della Pittura, is in itself evidence of his faith, but he leaves no doubt when, in the concluding reflections of the work, he speaks of those who maintain that painting ‘is so difficult that it cannot be taught by the written word except in certain confused, feeble, and poor principles, and they add that it is a virtue and a grace poured from heaven into human bodies which cannot be acquired by other means’. Armenini comments on this: ‘How stupid are those who have got into their heads the idea that this is one of those speculative or occult sciences which are only revealed and comprehensible to the deepest and most acute minds.’ Rules are for him ‘the unchangeable foundations of the art’. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
画家的求知欲是晚期矫饰主义体系一项基本信条的体现，即艺术可以通过训诫来教授。这一假设贯穿于 Lomazzo 的《Trattato》，该书在更深入的意义上是一本绘画手册，远胜于任何早期的论著。Armenini 在这一点上相当明确。他著作的书名 D e ′ D e ′ De^(')D e^{\prime} Veri Precetti della Pittura 本身就证明了他的信念，但当他在作品的结语中谈到那些主张绘画“如此艰深，书面文字除了某些模糊、薄弱和贫乏的原则之外无法教授它，并且他们补充说它是一种从天上倾注到人体的美德与恩赐，无法通过其他手段获得”的人时，他毫无疑问地反驳了这种观点。Armenini 对此评价道：“那些脑中装着这种观念的人是多么愚蠢——认为这是那些只有最深刻、最敏锐的头脑才能揭示和理解的推理或秘学之一。”对他而言，规则是“艺术不变的基础”。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5}
The Mannerists do not, of course, maintain that the whole
矫饰主义者当然并不主张整个
of painting can be taught, and they frequently refer to the fact that the painter must be born with a natural genius if he is to achieve any good at all. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} But having said this, they devote all their attention to the minutiae of his training.
绘画的某些方面是可以教授的，他们经常提到画家如果要取得任何成就，必须天生具有自然的天才。但话虽如此，他们却把全部注意力都放在训练的细枝末节上。
It is no new doctrine to maintain that much useful advice could be given to the painter by means of the written word. Alberti and Leonardo had both put down their views in writing for the benefit of other artists and many had profited by them. But the Mannerists approached the matter in a different spirit. The theorists of the Early Renaissance believed that a student could be helped to learn the art of painting by the application of reasonable methods; the Mannerists wished him to learn it by absolute rules.
认为通过文字可以向画家提供许多有用的建议并不是一种新观点。Alberti 和 Leonardo 都曾将他们的观点以文字形式记录下来，供其他艺术家参考，许多人因此受益。但矫饰主义者（Mannerists）以不同的精神处理这一问题。早期文艺复兴的理论家们相信，通过应用合理的方法可以帮助学生学会绘画；而矫饰主义者则希望学生通过绝对的规则来学习绘画。
At first sight reason seems to play quite an important part in the theories of Lomazzo and Armenini. Painting, says the former, does not appeal to the eye, but to the reason. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} However, his argument in favour of this view reveals what he really means; for he argues that beauty must appeal to the reason and not the eye, because no one would deny that beauty exists in angels and, since they are invisible to the eye, their beauty must be recognizable by other means-according to him, by reason. This explanation makes clear the gulf which exists between the reason of Alberti and the reason of Lomazzo. For the latter is, in effect, only repeating the view of St. Thomas that beauty appeals to the mind and not to the senses, and he is going no farther than Armenini, who makes painting appeal to ‘the eye of the understanding’ (l’occhio dell’ intelletto). 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Neither the reason of Lomazzo nor the understanding of Armenini has anything in common with the reason of the early Humanists which was a weapon for studying the real world, and the foundation of the scientific method.
乍看之下，理性在 Lomazzo 和 Armenini 的理论中似乎扮演着相当重要的角色。前者说，绘画不是诉诸于眼睛，而是诉诸于理性。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 然而，他为这一观点所做的辩护揭示了他的真实含义；因为他论证道，美必须诉诸于理性而不是眼睛，因为无人会否认天使是美的存在，而既然天使对眼睛是不可见的，它们的美就必须通过其他方式被识别——在他看来，通过理性。这个解释清楚地表明了 Alberti 的理性与 Lomazzo 的理性之间存在的鸿沟。后者实际上不过是在重复圣·托马斯的观点：美诉诸于心智而非感官，而且他并没有比 Armenini 更进一步，后者将绘画诉诸于“理解之眼”（l’occhio dell’intelletto）。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Lomazzo 的理性和 Armenini 的理解与早期人文主义者的理性毫无共同之处，后者是研究现实世界的工具，也是科学方法的基础。
When analysed, Lomazzo’s idea of reason comes down
经过分析，Lomazzo 的理性观归结于
roughly to the knowledge and observance of certain fixed rules. Moreover, these rules are based on authority, not on experience. With Alberti, and even more particularly with Leonardo, the scientific approach led to observation of actual facts about painting or about natural beauty. From these observations were deduced the rules which made up the treatises of these writers. The rules were put down only in a tentative way, to be abandoned if a new experimental test went against them. They were a means by which one artist could hand on to another the practical knowledge which he had gained at first hand. With the Mannerists all this is changed. Rules are laid down as final, and the reason that they are final is not that they are the outcome of the writer’s own observations but that they have been deduced from his study of some other master’s work. The argument now is that such and such a method is to be followed because it was followed by such and such an artist. In the conclusion to his work Armenini explains that he travelled all round Italy to study the work of all the best artists so that he might draw up his rules of study; and we shall see later that the whole method of instruction suggested by Lomazzo in his Idea del Tempio della Pittura is based on the same doctrine.
大致上依赖于对某些固定规则的认知与遵守。而且，这些规则是基于权威而不是基于经验。到了 Alberti，甚至更明显地在 Leonardo 那里，科学方法引向了对关于绘画或自然之美的实际事实的观察。从这些观察中推导出了构成这些著作的规则。这些规则只是以试探性的方式写下的，如果新的实验性检验与之相悖就会被放弃。它们是艺术家之间传授亲身获得的实践知识的一种手段。在矫饰派（Mannerists）中，所有这些都发生了变化。规则被规定为最终的，而它们之所以被视为最终的理由并不是因为它们出自作者自身的观察，而是因为它们是从他对某位或某些大师作品的研究中推导出来的。现在的论点是，应当遵循某种方法，因为它曾被某位或某些艺术家所遵循。 在他的结论中，Armenini 解释说他周游了全意大利，研究所有最优秀艺术家的作品，以便拟定他的学习规则；我们稍后将看到，Lomazzo 在其《Idea del Tempio della Pittura》中所建议的整个教学方法也是基于相同的学说。
This return to the principle of authority appears in one curious form, in connexion with ancient art. Although in general the Counter-Reformation and Mannerism were movements opposed to the influence of classical antiquity, yet the ancients are quoted as authorities whose example must be followed, particularly by Armenini, whose connexion with Rome brought him into close contact with ancient remains. The explanation is connected with a point which has already been discussed in connexion with religious art. The Church was only opposed to the philosophical systems of the ancients and was prepared to allow the use of classical themes and classical forms as long as they were divorced from that element of individual rationalism which gave them their
这种回归权威原则在与古代艺术相关的情况下出现为一种奇特的形式。尽管总体上反宗教改革和矫饰主义是与古典古代影响相对立的运动，但古人仍被引用为必须效仿的权威，尤其是 Armenini，其与罗马的联系使他与古代遗迹有密切接触。其解释与此前在宗教艺术讨论中已涉及的一点有关。教会仅反对古人的哲学体系，并愿意允许使用古典题材和古典形式，只要它们与赋予这些形式以个体理性主义成分的元素相分离。
point in the Early Renaissance. This appears in the art of the period, for instance in fresco-cycles like Zucchi’s decoration in the Palazzo Ruspoli in Rome, in which the themes and apparatus are all classical but the spirit and forms in every way anti-rational and Mannerist. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Another example is the Mannerist fondness for grotesques-a fantastic and therefore harmless form of ancient art-which were developed with great originality by the Mannerists in their decoration.
文艺复兴早期的一个转折点。这在当时的艺术中有所体现，例如罗马 Ruspoli 宫中 Zucchi 的连环壁画装饰，其主题和手法皆为古典，但精神和形式在各方面都反理性且带有矫饰风格（Mannerist）。另一个例子是矫饰派对 grotesques 的偏爱——一种奇诡而因此无害的古代艺术形式——矫饰派在装饰中以极大的独创性对其加以发展。
As students of antiquity concentrated more and more on the details of classical antiquity and less on the recovery of its spirit, respect for the authority of the ancients increased and became almost servile. Alberti admires classical antiquity and uses it constantly; but only when it suits him. He is never tied by it and he advises the young artist to break away from its limits if he can. In the later sixteenth century it is accepted as a final authority in all matter of detail. In architecture, for instance, the only matter in dispute was the relative importance of Vitruvius and of surviving buildings as means of deciding what was right and what was wrong. Palladio, for instance, a great practising architect, whose methods still had much in common with the classical architects of the beginning of the sixteenth century, relied more on his study of the buildings themselves than on the rules of Vitruvius; 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Serlio, on the other hand, who was primarily a theorist, pins all his faith on the latter. His belief in him is so great that he is ready to admit that other Roman architects sinned when they did not follow his precepts. For instance, speaking of the theatre of Marcellus, he says:
随着古代学者越发专注于古典古代的细节，而较少关注其精神的恢复，对古人的权威的尊重增加并几乎变得奴颜婢膝。Alberti 敬仰古典古代并不断借鉴它；但仅在它适合他的时候。他从不被其束缚，并且建议年轻的艺术家在可能时突破其局限。到十六世纪后期，古典已被视为在一切细节问题上的最终权威。例如在建筑学中，唯一的争论点是维特鲁威（Vitruvius）与现存建筑哪一种更为重要，哪一种能作为判断对错的依据。比如 Palladio，作为一位伟大的执业建筑师，其方法与十六世纪初的古典建筑师仍有许多共同之处，他更依赖对建筑本身的研究，而非维特鲁威的规则；相反，主要作为理论家的 Serlio 则把全部信念寄托在后者。他对维特鲁威的信仰如此之深，以至于愿意承认其他罗马建筑师在不遵循维特鲁威教条时犯了罪。 例如，谈到马尔切卢斯剧场（the theatre of Marcellus）时，他说：
if this ancient architect was licentious that is no reason why we should be so: for, unless reason tells us to the contrary, we must always follow the teaching of Vitruvius as an infallible rule and guide. T T  ^("T "){ }^{\text {T }}
如果这位古代建筑师放荡，这也不意味着我们应当效仿：因为，除非理性告诉我们相反，否则我们必须始终将维特鲁威的教导作为不容置疑的规则和指南。 T T  ^("T "){ }^{\text {T }}
Vignola harmonized the models provided by the surviving works of antiquity with the rules of Vitruvius, and produced for the first time a set of absolute proportions for the Five Orders, based solely on the authority of the ancients. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
维尼奥拉将古代遗存所提供的范式与维特鲁威的规则协调起来，首次仅以古人权威为依据，提出了一套针对五大柱式的绝对比例。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
At the same time Armenini took an important step in the same direction in the theory of painting. When he comes to give the correct proportions for the human figure he does not base his measurements entirely on the most beautiful specimens in life, but he checks the results arrived at in this way by ‘the most perfect statues in Rome’. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} No doubt Alberti and his contemporaries had been influenced in their choice of natural beauty by their taste for Roman sculpture, but this is the first 'occasion on which a writer actually makes ancient statues the final test for natural beauty.
与此同时，阿尔梅尼尼在绘画理论上朝同一方向迈出了重要一步。当他给出人体的正确比例时，他并不完全以生活中最美的范本为测量标准，而是用“罗马最完美的雕像”来检验由此得出的结果。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 毫无疑问，阿尔伯蒂及其同时代人在选择自然之美时受到了他们对罗马雕塑的审美影响，但这是首次有作者真正将古代雕像作为自然之美的最终检验。
In the system of the later Mannerists, therefore, the individual reason, which was the foundation of all Renaissance progress, was replaced by an acceptance of authority, exactly as the individual conscience had been crushed in religion by the Counter-Reformation.
因此，在后期矫饰主义者的体系中，那种作为所有文艺复兴进步根基的个人理性，被对权威的顺从所取代，正如反宗教改革中个人良知在宗教领域被压制一样。
This servility and the study of the great masters to which it led produced the intricate scheme of rules which is most fully developed by Lomazzo in his Trattato. In this book, which contains some seven hundred crowded pages, every possible problem which may confront the painter is discussed and settled. The treatise is divided into seven books dealing respectively with Proportion, Motion, Colour, Light, Perspective, Practice, and History. Each book is systematically subdivided so that nothing escapes analysis. In the book on
这种奴颜婢膝以及由此导致的对伟大大师的研习产生了复杂的规则体系，而这一体系在洛马佐（Lomazzo）的《Trattato》中得到了最充分的发展。在这本约七百页的巨著中，画家可能面临的每一个问题都被讨论并加以解决。该论著分为七卷，分别论述比例（Proportion）、运动（Motion）、色彩（Colour）、光（Light）、透视（Perspective）、实践（Practice）和历史（History）。每一卷又按系统细分，确保无一遗漏。在论及...
Proportion, for instance, details are given for drawing figures of men and women of seven, eight, nine, and ten heads in height. The proportions of children and horses are also added. In the book on Motion, which includes Expression, all the possible human emotions are classified, the gestures and facial movements which they produce are described, and episodes are mentioned which illustrate the effects of each. In the last book, of History, Lomazzo describes the Forms of all the gods, of the elements, and of everything that the painter may want to depict. It is interesting in this context to notice that he uses the word ‘Form’ in its medieval and Scholastic sense, meaning that which gives any particular thing its being, that which distinguishes it from other things. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} For him, therefore, the form is not simply the outward shape of a thing; it is the sum of its distinguishing characteristics. The form of Jupiter, for instance, includes his eagle and his thunderbolts. In the case of a saint it includes his traditional attributes. So that the last book of the treatise contains a complete handbook to Christian and Classical iconography. To paint Mars or the Archangel Michael the artist need not use his imagination; he need only turn up the relevant passage in the Trattato.
例如，在“比例”一章中，给出了绘制身高为七、八、九和十头身的男女人体的详细尺寸。还补充了儿童和马匹的比例。在包含“动作”的那本书中（其中包括“表情”），将所有可能的人类情感进行了分类，描述了由这些情感产生的手势和面部动作，并提及了说明每种情感效果的情节。在最后一本“历史”中，Lomazzo 描述了所有诸神、四大要素以及画家可能想要描绘的一切的形象。有趣的是，在此语境下他使用“形”（Form）一词采用了中世纪和经院哲学的意义，意指赋予任何特定事物其存在的东西，使其区别于其他事物的那些特性。因此，对他而言，形不仅仅是事物的外在形状；它是其区分性特征的总和。例如，朱庇特（Jupiter）的形象包括他的鹰和雷电；对于一位圣人，则包括他的传统标志。因此，该论著的最后一卷包含了一部完整的基督教与古典宗教图像学手册。 要画火星或大天使米迦勒，艺术家无需动用想象力；他只需在《Trattato》中找出相关段落。
This method is carried to its extreme point by Lomazzo, 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} but it is also used in a milder way by the other late Mannerists, particularly Armenini. The latter covers a smaller range than Lomazzo, but within it he is no less final in his statements and no less dictatorial in his tone. In the first book of the Veri Precetti his treatment is rather general, but in the second, in which he discusses the different parts of painting -proportion, colour, light, and shade-his approach is just like that of Lomazzo, and in the last book, devoted to the
这种方法被洛马佐(Lomazzo)推到极致， 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 但其他晚期矫饰派画家也以较温和的方式采用，尤以阿尔梅尼尼(Armenini)为著。后者涵盖的范围不及洛马佐，但在其范围内论断同样绝对，语气同样专断。在《Veri Precetti》的第一卷中，他的论述较为概括；但在第二卷中，当他讨论绘画的不同部分——比例、色彩、明暗——时，他的方法正如洛马佐一样，而在最后一卷，专论
kind of decoration required in different buildings, his instructions recall those of St. Charles Borromeo, though the authorities appealed to here are the masters of the Renaissance, not the early Christian Fathers.
在不同建筑中所需的装饰类型，他的指示让人想起圣卡洛·博罗梅奥的做法，尽管此处引用的权威是文艺复兴大师，而不是早期基督教教父。
Enough has been said to show in what sense the later Mannerists were academic, and it remains to consider their Eclecticism. According to Lomazzo the process of artistic production could be divided into two parts: the formation of the idea in the mind of the artist, and the expression of this idea in material form in paint, marble, or line. The first of these stages was the business of the mind and the imagination. For the second it was essential to acquire a ‘good manner’; and it is in the acquisition of a good manner that the method of Eclecticism becomes important.
上文已足以说明后来的矫饰派在何种意义上是学术的，接下来需考察他们的兼收并蓄。根据洛马佐的观点，艺术创作过程可以分为两部分：艺术家心中观念的形成，以及以颜料、大理石或线条将该观念表现为物质形态的过程。第一阶段属于心智和想象力的范畴。至于第二阶段，掌握“良好风格”是必要的；正是在获得良好风格的过程中，兼收并蓄的方法变得重要。
First of all it is important to see approximately what Armenini means by ‘manner’. Vasari often talks of the maniera, and it is from this word that the whole school of the late-sixteenth-century Italian painting now takes its name. It is therefore a quality of considerable importance, but it is not easy to isolate its meaning. Vasari usually qualifies the word, and talks of maniera secca, or gran’ maniera. Raffaello Borghini appears to be the first critic to say simply that a painter possesses or lacks ‘manner’. When he does so he seems to understand by ‘manner’ what Vasari meant bygran’ maniera, which is connected with the terribiltà for which Michelangelo was famous and with our idea of the sublime. At any rate he contrasts it with cose finite e delicate. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Armenini is more explicit. His conception of the maniera depends on the distinction which he draws between exact imitation and good drawing. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} There was nothing new in making such a distinction, for all the critics of the earlier Renaissance, except Leonardo, the supreme naturalist, had made it. But Alberti has quite different reasons from Armenini for distinguishing these aspects of painting. For Alberti good drawing is one
首先，大致弄清楚 Armenini 所说的 “manner”（风格/手法）是什么意思是很重要的。Vasari 经常谈到 maniera（风格），而正是由这个词，整个十六世纪末意大利绘画流派才得名。因此这是一种相当重要的品质，但要把它的含义单独提取出来并不容易。Vasari 通常会限定该词，会谈到 maniera secca（干涩的风格）或 gran’ maniera（宏大风格）。Raffaello Borghini 似乎是第一个干脆说某位画家“有”或“没有”‘manner’的评论家。其言下之意，他似乎把 ‘manner’ 理解为 Vasari 所说的 gran’ maniera，这与 Michelangelo 著名的 terribilità（可畏感）以及我们对崇高的观念有关。无论如何，他把它与 cose finite e delicate（细致而精巧的事物）相对立。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Armenini 则更为明确。他对 maniera 的概念依赖于他在精确模仿（exact imitation）与良好素描（good drawing）之间所作的区分。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 把这样的区分提出并不新鲜，因为除了作为最高自然主义者的 Leonardo 之外，早期文艺复兴的所有评论家都曾作过这样的区分。但 Alberti 对于区分绘画这些方面的理由与 Armenini 完全不同。对阿尔伯蒂来说，良好的素描就是准确的构图
stage beyond exact imitation, since to arrive at the former the artist has to go through the process of selecting and combining the best elements in natural beauty. Armenini conceives of another stage beyond this, for he tells the story of Zeuxis choosing the most beautiful features of five Crotonian girls to paint his Venus-the anecdote always chosen by earlier critics to illustrate Alberti’s selection process-and then adds: 'If Zeuxis . . . had not possessed a particular manner (singolar maniera), he would never have harmonized the different features which he had chosen for their beauty from the several girls. T T  ^("T "){ }^{\text {T }}
超越精确模仿的阶段，因为要达到前者，艺术家必须经历从自然之美中挑选并组合最佳元素的过程。Armenini 设想了另一个更高阶段，他讲述了泽克西斯（Zeuxis）从五位克罗托尼亚姑娘中选出最美的五官来画他的维纳斯的故事——这一轶事一直被早期评论家用来阐明 Alberti 的选择过程——并补充道：“如果泽克西斯……没有拥有一种特殊的风格（singolar maniera），他就不可能将他从几位姑娘身上为其美丽而挑选出的不同特征和谐地结合起来。” T T  ^("T "){ }^{\text {T }}
Now Michelangelo also went a stage beyond Alberti’s selection, but with him the further process was a transmutation of the selected material by means of the imagination. Armenini’s method is different. His final stage consists not of a transmutation but of an addition-the addition of maniera.
米开朗基罗在阿尔伯蒂的选择之上又迈进了一步，但对他而言，进一步的过程是通过想象力对所选素材的易位（transmutation）。阿尔梅尼尼的方法则不同。他的最后阶段不是一种易位，而是一种添加——风格（maniera）的添加。
A first approximation to a translation of maniera in this context might be style. There is, of course, nothing unusual in the idea of an artist’s having style. All artists have style, naturalism itself being a style as much as Gothic or Baroque. But, in general, naturalistic artists do not talk about style; they talk more in terms of what they are interested in painting, or of the accuracy with which they think they can paint it. It is a characteristic of non-naturalistic, mannerist periods of art that people talk explicitly about style. In this way Armenini is typical of his time. He evidently thinks that there is one and only one style; for when he discusses the painters of the Quattrocento he does not say, like Vasari, that they have a maniera secca, but simply that they lack la bella maniera, as if it was something discovered by his contemporaries. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} It is this confidence in the absolute rightness of their particular style, and the undue importance which they attribute to it as an end in itself, that justify the name of Mannerists, as opposed to Stylists, for the painters and
在此语境中，对 maniera 的一种初步翻译可能是“风格”。当然，艺术家拥有风格这一观点并不奇怪。所有艺术家都有风格，自然主义本身与哥特式或巴洛克一样也是一种风格。但一般而言，自然主义艺术家并不谈论“风格”；他们更多谈论自己感兴趣去画什么，或他们认为自己能多准确地去描绘它。非自然主义的、矫饰主义的艺术时期有一个特点：人们明确谈论风格。从这个角度看，Armenini 具有其时代的典型性。他显然认为只有一种风格；因为当他讨论十五世纪的画家时，他不像 Vasari 那样说他们具有 maniera secca（枯燥的风格），而只是简单地说他们缺乏 la bella maniera（美丽的风格），好像那是他的同时代人发现的东西。正是这种对其特定风格绝对正确性的自信，以及他们将其作为目的本身而赋予的不当重要性，使得将这些画家称为 Mannerists（矫饰派）而不是 Stylists（风格派）成为合理的叫法，后者用于指代那些画家和
theorists under consideration, and bring us to the more obvious translation manner as the closer approximation to the meaning of maniera.
我们所讨论的理论家，并将我们引向更明显的“maniera”一词的翻译方式，作为对其含义的更接近的逼近。
In training himself to acquire a good manner, the first essential is that the artist should decide in what direction his natural talent draws him. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Lomazzo is quite clear about this point, and frequently reminds the artist of the disasters which will come upon him if he imitates other painters slavishly, without stopping to consider whether they are the right kind of painter for him personally to imitate, or if he tries to force his style into a certain line because he has been told that it is the right line. This basic proposition distinguishes Lomazzo’s Eclecticism from the rigid system of borrowing usually connected, though not quite fairly, with the Carracci. Once the artist has decided in what direction he is naturally drawn, there are two methods by which he can develop his talent: by sheer study and effort, or by the imitation of other artists. The former is a serious way of advancing, but it has one disadvantage, that too concentrated work leads to dryness of manner and consequently prevents the artist from displaying grace in his work. Since the loss of grace is of the greatest importance the second method is the better, and Lomazzo explains it at length. His Temple of Painting is controlled by seven Governors, each of whom represents a particular kind of perfection in painting. They form a curious list to our eyes. First the four great names of the High Renaissance: Leonardo, Raphael, Michelangelo, and Titian; then Lomazzo’s master, Gaudenzio Ferrari; and finally Polidoro da Caravaggio, presumably as the continuer of the Raphaelesque tradition, and Mantegna, who perhaps owes his position in the list to the influence which he seems to have exerted on Gaudenzio. The particular achievements of these seven Governors are then analysed under the seven parts of paint-
在训练自己以获得良好风格时，首先要紧的是艺术家应当决定他的天赋自然倾向于哪个方向。洛马佐在这一点上相当明确，并且经常提醒艺术家，如果他盲目模仿其他画家，而不去考虑这些画家是否适合他个人去模仿，或者如果他仅仅因为被告知某种路线是正确的就试图把自己的风格强行纳入某一线路，那么灾祸将降临于他。这一基本命题将洛马佐的折衷主义与通常与卡拉奇（尽管并不完全公平地）联系在一起的僵化借鉴体系区分开来。一旦艺术家决定了自己自然倾向的方向，可以通过两种方法来发展他的天赋：靠纯粹的学习与努力，或通过模仿其他艺术家。前者是严肃的进步方式，但有一个缺点，即过度专注的工作会导致风格的枯燥，从而妨碍艺术家在作品中展示优雅。既然失去优雅至关重要，第二种方法更为可取，洛马佐对此作了详细阐述。 他的绘画之庙由七位统治者掌管，每一位都代表绘画中一种特定的完美。他们在我们看来构成一个奇特的名单。首先是盛期文艺复兴的四个伟大名字：Leonardo、Raphael、Michelangelo 和 Titian；接着是 Lomazzo 的师傅 Gaudenzio Ferrari；最后是 Polidoro da Caravaggio，可能作为拉斐尔传统的延续者，和 Mantegna，他在名单中的位置或许归因于他对 Gaudenzio 似乎产生的影响。这七位总督的具体成就在随后的七部分绘画中分别进行了分析——
ing (proportion, motion, colour, &c.) in a confusion of astrological symbolism. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The young painter has, therefore, simply to decide which elements he finds congenial in each of these painters and, by carefully studying them, to nourish his own talent. By this method he will be saved the excessive fatigue which will overcome him if he tries to work out everything for himself and he will make the best use of the work of his predecessors.
构图（比例、运动、色彩等）被占星术象征混杂在一起。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 因此，年轻的画家只需决定在这些画家中各自有哪些要素与他志趣相投，并通过仔细研究这些要素来滋养自己的天赋。通过这种方法，他可以避免如果试图独自解决一切时会压倒他的过度疲劳，并能最大限度地利用前人的成果。
This scheme represents, in effect, a full system of Eclecticism, which is summed up in the description which Lomazzo gives of his ideal painting. It was to consist of two panels; on the first Adam drawn by Michelangelo and painted by Titian, using the proportions of Raphael; on the other, Eve drawn by Raphael and painted by Correggio. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} But in spite of passages like this, it must be remembered that Lomazzo tempered his Eclecticism by his constant warning against mere plagiarism and by his advice to the artist only to imitate those masters for whom he feels a natural sympathy. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
这个方案实际上代表了一个完整的折衷主义体系，正如 Lomazzo 对他理想画作的描述所总结的那样。它应由两幅画面组成；第一幅是由 Michelangelo 起稿、Titian 作画、并采用 Raphael 的比例绘制的亚当；另一幅是由 Raphael 起稿、Correggio 作画的夏娃。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 但尽管有这样的段落，必须记住 Lomazzo 通过不断警告反对纯粹的剽窃并建议艺术家只模仿那些他自然同情的大师，从而对他的折衷主义进行了调和。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
The method recommended by Armenini is similar in its general lines, but rather less complicated. He agrees with Lomazzo that it is vital for the artist to possess a good manner, more precisely una bella e dotta maniera. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} This can only be acquired if the artist has a natural gift as a painter, but this gift must be cultivated by study. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} The first stage of study is to consist simply of copying progressively more difficult models: first drawings and engravings, then paintings, in chiaroscuro and in colour, and finally ancient sculpture and Michelangelo’s Last Fudgement. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} The student is then offered two alternative methods: either to follow one master, or to draw what he needs from the study of many different masters. Armenini does not finally decide which is the better of these
Armenini 所推荐的方法在总体上类似，但要简单些。他同意 Lomazzo 的观点，认为艺术家必须具备一种良好的风格，更确切地说是 una bella e dotta maniera。这只有在艺术家具有作为画家的天赋时才能获得，但这种天赋必须通过学习来培养。学习的第一阶段仅由逐步临摹更难的范本构成：先是素描和铜版画，然后是在明暗法和色彩中的绘画，最后是古代雕塑和 Michelangelo 的《最后的审判》。随后，学生面临两种可选的方法：要么追随一位师傅，要么从对多位不同师傅的研究中汲取所需。Armenini 最终并未决定哪一种更好。
two methods, but he evidently favours the latter, since he quotes Michelangelo’s remark that a man who always follows another never overtakes him, and laments the bad effect which the universal imitation of even so great an artist as Michelangelo has had on painting.
两种方法，但他显然偏爱后者，因为他引用了米开朗基罗的话：总是跟随别人的人永远赶不上别人，并且为即便像米开朗基罗这样伟大的艺术家被普遍模仿对绘画造成的恶劣影响而感到惋惜。
However, the important difference between the schemes of Lomazzo and Armenini lies in the position which the latter gives to ancient sculpture as a model for the artist. His admiration for antiquity thrusts itself even into his definition of painting. For in this, after saying that the painter must first conceive an idea in his mind, he goes on to talk of the manner which the painter must adopt to express it, and this manner he calls not maniera buona but maniera antica. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} His feeling for the ancients has already been mentioned in connexion with his treatment of proportion, but it appears throughout his discussion of the artist’s training. Ancient sculpture is quoted as the best possible model, and nature, which is only to be imitated at all after the painter has acquired his good manner, is said to be beautiful in proportion as it approaches the works of antiquity. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} It is, however, to be expected that the Roman-trained Armenini should show a greater enthusiasm for ancient sculpture than the Milanese Lomazzo.
然而，Lomazzo 与 Armenini 体系之间的重要差别在于后者将古代雕塑置于作为艺术家范本的位置。他对古代的仰慕甚至渗入到他对绘画的定义中。因为在这方面，他在说画家首先必须在脑海中构思一个观念之后，继续论及画家为表达该观念必须采用的方式，而他称这种方式为 maniera antica 而非 maniera buona。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 他对古人的情感在他处理比例问题时已被提及，但它贯穿于他对艺术家训练的整个论述。古代雕塑被引用为可能的最好范本，而自然——只有在画家获得其良好方式之后才可模仿——被认为其美在于越接近古代作品便越美。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 然而，可以预料，受罗马训练的 Armenini 对古代雕塑应比米兰的 Lomazzo 表现出更大的热情。
Lomazzo and Armenini are, therefore, academic and eclectic in their method, but they could not free themselves from Mannerist views even in their practical advice to the painter. For though they favour this very elaborate training and urge the artist always to work out carefully in his head and on paper what he intends to do before he actually sets to work on a painting, yet they accept Vasari’s compromise that in the execution itself he should be as rapid as possible so that he may not destroy the grace of his painting by overelaboration. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
因此，Lomazzo 和 Armenini 在方法上是学术的且折衷的，但即便在对画家的实际建议中，他们也无法摆脱矫饰主义的观点。因为尽管他们主张进行这种极为精细的训练，并一再敦促艺术家在真正动手绘画之前，先在脑中和纸上仔细推敲他打算做的事，然而他们接受了 Vasari 的折衷意见：在具体的执行过程中，画家应尽可能快速，以免因过度精雕细琢而毁掉作品的优雅。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
However, in the practical advice which these theorists give to the painter these few Mannerist features are more than counterbalanced by those which they have in common with the Carracci. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Some of these common features also go back to the earlier forms of Mannerist practice. The Eclecticism advocated by Lomazzo, and by the Carracci, for instance, was the common habit of many painters in the middle of the sixteenth century, and even sometimes received conscious formulation, as, for instance, by Tintoretto, who aimed at combining the colour of Titian and the drawing of Michelangelo, or by Tibaldi, who wished to harmonize the terribiltà of Michelangelo with the elegance of Raphael. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
然而，在这些理论家给画家的实用建议中，这些少数的矫饰主义特征已被他们与卡拉奇家族共有的那些特征所大大抵消。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 其中一些共同特征也可追溯到早期的矫饰主义实践形式。例如，洛马佐和卡拉奇主张的折衷主义，是十六世纪中叶许多画家的共同习惯，甚至有时被有意识地表述出来，比如丁托列托旨在将提香的色彩与米开朗基罗的素描相结合，或提巴尔迪希望将米开朗基罗的 terribilità与拉斐尔的优雅相协调。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2}
It in no way lessens the importance of the Carracci in the development of the arts in Italy to say that in their method of teaching they applied many of the methods worked out by their Mannerist predecessors. It means only that the name of ‘Eclectic’ usually applied to them is not an adequate description of their achievement. Their Eclecticism was not new, but in many other ways their teaching revolutionized Italian painting. As all their biographers in the seventeenth century agree, their great work was that they brought painting back to the imitation of nature after the wanderings of the Mannerists. In our view their naturalism is so mild, particularly in comparison with that of Caravaggio, that it is hard to think of them as anything but academic. But in their day they seemed to be getting back to a simple and direct rendering of nature, after a period of almost abstract stylization.
说卡拉奇家族在意大利艺术发展中的重要性，并不因为他们在教学方法上采用了他们那些矫饰派前辈所发展的许多方法而减弱。那只是意味着“折衷主义者”这一常用于指称他们的名称，并不能充分描述他们的成就。他们的折衷并非新创，但在许多其他方面他们的教学革新了意大利绘画。正如十七世纪所有传记作者一致认为的，他们的伟大之处在于，在矫饰派的游移之后，他们将绘画带回了对自然的模仿。在我们看来，他们的自然主义是如此温和，尤其是与卡拉瓦乔相比，使人很难把他们看作不是学院派。但在他们那个时代，他们似乎是在经历了几乎抽象化程式化的时期后，回归到对自然的简单而直接的呈现。

    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} In a sense he was only giving systematic form to a tendency already visible in Italian architecture of the fourteenth century. Many north Italian towns, such as Cremona and Piacenza, had central squares round which were grouped the principal public buildings. But it was not till the fifteenth century that we find a standard design repeated round a square, as in the Piazza of St. Mark’s in Venice, or that in front of the Annunziata in Florence, both of which were in great part laid out in the Quattrocento. Pius II’s plans for Pienza show something of the same spirit, and Nicholas V’s idea for linking up St. Peter’s with the Castel S. Angelo, in which Alberti was involved, is an even more ambitious scheme of the same kind.
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 从某种意义上说，他只是在把十四世纪意大利建筑中已显现的一种倾向系统化。许多北意大利城镇，如克雷莫纳和皮亚琴察，都有围绕中央广场分布的主要公共建筑。但直到十五世纪，我们才看到在广场周围重复使用标准设计的例子，例如威尼斯圣马可广场或佛罗伦萨圣母领报教堂前的广场，这两处在很大程度上都是在 Quattrocento 时期规划的。教皇皮乌斯二世为皮恩察所做的规划也体现了类似精神，而尼各拉五世关于将圣彼得大教堂与圣天使堡相连的构想（阿尔伯蒂参与其中）则是同类方案中更为雄心勃勃的一例。
    5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} De Re Aed., bk. viii, ch. 5.
    5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 《论建筑》（De Re Aed.），第八卷，第五章。

    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Ibid., bk. ix, ch. 1. By leading citizens Alberti means those who are responsible for the government of the city; and the qualifications which he demands for this are highly typical: either wisdom, which will fit a man for making laws and for supervising the religious life of the town; or experience, which will give him a place in the executive; or wealth, which brings prosperity to the city, and alone makes it possible for the other two groups to perform their functions. (Cf. bk. iv, ch. 1.)
    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 同上，卷九，第 1 章。Alberti 所说的“领导公民”是指那些负责城市治理的人；他对这些人的资格要求具有高度代表性：要么具有智慧，使人能够制定法律并监督城镇的宗教生活；要么具有经验，使人能够在行政部门担任职务；要么具有财富，为城市带来繁荣，且只有财富才能使另外两类人履行其职能成为可能。（参见卷四，第 1 章。）
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Ibid., bk. ix, ch. 1.
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 同上，卷 ix，第 1 章。

  10. 1 ‘Della Pittura’, ed. cit., p. 143. This naturalism is reflected in certain examples which Alberti gives; as, for instance, when he refers to Narcissus as the first painter, since his image reflected in the water was an exact likeness of himself on a flat surface (ibid., p.91).
    1 ‘Della Pittura’，同上，第 143 页。这种自然主义反映在阿尔贝蒂给出的某些例子中；例如，当他提到纳耳喀索斯是第一个画家时，因其在水中的影像是在平面上对他自己的精确再现（同上，第 91 页）。

    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Ibid., p. 101. In the ‘De Statua’ Alberti supplies the sculptor with an apparatus by means of which he, too, can attain the mathematical certainty which realism demanded. It consisted of a series of circles and plumb-lines which allowed the sculptor to measure in terms of height and projection the contour of any figure or three-dimensional object.
    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} 同上，页 101。在《论雕像》中，Alberti 为雕塑家提供了一套装置，使他也能达到现实主义所要求的数学确定性。它由一系列圆和铅垂线组成，允许雕塑家以高度和投影来测量任何人物或三维物体的轮廓。

    要补充四十五世纪直接与艺术相关的作家名单，我们必须增加两类人。首先是一群关于透视和建筑的著作家，例如 Piero della Francesca 和
  40. Francesco di Giorgio, whose works are entirely technical and contain no general ideas about painting or the other arts. Secondly there are certain artists, like Foppa and Bramante, who are known to have written on their arts, but whose works are lost. The accounts of them that survive are too general to provide any material for the present history.
    Francesco di Giorgio，他们的著作完全是技术性的，并不包含关于绘画或其他艺术的一般性观点。其次有一些艺术家，如 Foppa 和 Bramante，已知曾撰写过关于他们艺术的著述，但这些著作已经失传。现存的关于他们的记述过于笼统，无法为本史提供任何材料。

    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Ibid. i, § 13. It is typical of Leonardo’s method that this should not be an original passage, but should be copied from a medieval writer on perspective, John Peckham (Perspectira Communis, Milan, 1482, Introduction). Peckham had not, of course, in mind any connexion between perspective and painting, and was thinking of the former as a purely optical study; but Leonardo almost certainly copied the passage for its relevance in the quarrels about the liberal arts. For in several notes dealing with these quarrels he refers to the superiority of the eye over the ear among the senses, which was a common Neoplatonic doctrine based on the dignity of light of which Peckham speaks here.
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 同上，卷一，第 13 节。典型的列奥纳多的做法是，这并非原创段落，而是摘自一位关于透视的中世纪著作家约翰·佩克汉（John Peckham，《Perspectira Communis》，米兰，1482，导言）。佩克汉当然并未考虑透视与绘画之间的任何联系，他将透视视为纯粹的光学研究；但列奥纳多几乎可以肯定是为其在有关自由艺术争论中的相关性而摘抄此段。因为在几则处理这些争论的笔记中，他提到感官中眼睛优于耳朵，这是一个基于光之尊严的常见新柏拉图主义学说，佩克汉在此处也谈到了光的尊严。
    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} The dignity which architecture derives from its reliance on the certainty of mathematics is alluded to at an early date, in a patent given by Federigo da Montefeltro in 1468 in which he speaks of ‘La virtù dell’Architettura fundata in l’arte dell’ Aritmetica e Geometria, che sono delle sette arti liberali e delle principali, perchè sono in primo gradu certitudinis’ (cf. Gaye, Carteggio Inedito d’Artisti, i, p. 24). The writers of this time were of course able to point to an ancient example for the connexion of painting with mathematics, and Equicola (Instituzioni, Milan, 1541) refers to the view of Eupompus, that painting could not exist except on a basis of arithmetic and geometry (Pliny, Nat. Hist. xxxv. 76, attributes this view to Pamphilus).
    建筑由于依赖于数学的确定性而获得的尊严早有所指，1468 年 Federigo da Montefeltro 颁发的一份专利就提到“建筑的美德建立在算术与几何艺术之上，这些是七艺中最主要的，因为它们首先是确定性的层级”（参见 Gaye, Carteggio Inedito d’Artisti, i, p. 24）。当时的作家当然可以引用古代将绘画与数学关联的例子，Equicola（Instituzioni，米兰，1541）提到 Eupompus 的观点，即绘画不能脱离算术与几何而存在（Pliny, Nat. Hist. xxxv. 76 将此观点归于 Pamphilus）。

Whosoever conceives otherwise is mistaken. This Idea alone lifts my eyes to those high visions which I set myself to paint and carve here below. If men of rash and foolish judgement drag sense-ward the beauty which moves and transports every right intelligence to Heaven, it is because weak and wavering eyes, and even eyes fixed steadily on things above, cannot pass from the mortal to the divine, for without grace it is a vain thought that one may rise thither.’
    同上。xciv。1541–1544 年：“作为我天职中的可靠向导，‘美的理念’，它既是镜又是灯，赐予我两门艺术，自我出生时就被赋予。凡有不同看法者，皆误。惟有此理念把我的目光提升到那些高远的幻象，正是我决心在此世绘画与雕刻之对象。若鲁莽愚昧的判断将那使一切正当智慧升向天堂的美拉向感官，乃因软弱摇摆的眼，甚至定睛于上方之眼，亦不能从凡人升及神圣；因为无恩典，欲上升彼处为徒然之想。”
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Ibid. cix. 105, ‘To Cavalieri’, 1536-42: ‘Nowhere does God, in his grace, reveal himself to me more clearly than in some lovely human form, which I love solely because it is a mirrored image of Himself.’
    同上。cix。105，“致 Cavalieri”，1536–1542 年：“在任何地方，上帝以上他的恩典向我显明自己，都不如在某个可爱的人的形体中更为明显；我爱那形体，仅因为它是他的映像。”

    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 例如，Alberti 提到“quella gratia ne’ corpi quale dicono bellezza”（《论绘画》，卷二，第 109 页），并补充说他不知道有其他获得它的方法，除了对自然的近距离研究。文艺复兴早期的柏拉图主义者在优雅与美之间作出与 Vasari 类似的区分，但他们仅将其应用于肉体之美，而不适用于艺术之美。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Lives，iv，第 81 页。
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} In his Discorso della Bellezza e della Grazia Benedetto Varchi makes roughly the same distinction between beauty and grace as that madc by Vasari, though, as he is concerned mainly with the beauty and grace of women, not of works of art, what he says only bears indirectly on the point under discussion here.
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} 在他的《论美与优雅》（Discorso della Bellezza e della Grazia）中，Benedetto Varchi 对美与优雅作了大致与 Vasari 相同的区分，尽管他主要关注的是女性的美与优雅，而不是艺术作品，因此他所说的内容仅间接与此处讨论的问题有关。

  86. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} The fact that this passage stands out from the general line of Vasari’s thought is explained by its being a direct borrowing from another writer. Scoti-Bertinelli discovered a page of manuscript by Vincenzo Borghini containing a draft of this passage (see Giorgio Vasari, Scrittore, p. 82). Vasari was certainly indebted to many of his friends for information and ideas used in the Lives, but the difficulties of distinguishing the different contributions are so great that I have thought it better to treat the Lives as a homogeneous work. In this case the ideas expressed by Vasari may well have been common property among the circle in which he moved in Florence. His definition of drawing can be paralleled in Varchi’s exposition of the meaning of concetto in his Lezione on Michelangelo’s sonnet beginning: ‘Non ha l’ottimo artista alcun concetto’.
    这一段与瓦萨里的总体思想路线有所不同，可归因于它直接借用了另一位作家的著作。Scoti-Bertinelli 发现了一页由 Vincenzo Borghini 所写的手稿，包含了该段落的草稿（参见 Giorgio Vasari, Scrittore, p. 82）。瓦萨里确实在《列传》中向许多朋友借取了资料和观点，但要区分这些不同贡献的来源极为困难，因此我认为把《列传》视为一部内部统一的作品更为妥当。在这种情况下，瓦萨里所表达的观念很可能在他在佛罗伦萨活动的圈子中是共有的。他对素描的定义可以与 Varchi 在其关于米开朗基罗开头为“Non ha l’ottimo artista alcun concetto”的十四行诗的 Lezione 中对 concetto 的阐述相类比。

  106. Michelangelo in Venice. Apart from the fact that nothing but personal spite could account for the tone of Dolce’s attack, there is evidence that in general Michelangelo was admired in Venice at this time. Biondo and Pino both praise him highly in their dialogues; Doni, writing to Aretino in 1549, does the same (Disegno, p. 60); and there is even a letter from Dolce himself to Gaspero Ballini, in which Michelangelo is described as divine and is said to have raised the arts to the level they attained in antiquity (Bottari-Ticozzi, op. cit., v, p. 175). In proof of his influence on Venetian artists it is enough to recall Tintoretto’s motto: ‘Il disegno di Michelangelo, e il colorito di Tiziano.’
    米开朗基罗在威尼斯。除了多尔切的攻击语气只能用个人怨恨来解释之外，有证据表明在当时米开朗基罗在威尼斯总体上是备受钦佩的。比翁多和皮诺在他们的对话录中都高度赞扬他；多尼在 1549 年给阿雷蒂诺的信中也如此写道（Disegno，第 60 页）；甚至还有多尔切本人写给加斯佩罗·巴里尼的一封信，信中称米开朗基罗为神圣，并说他使艺术达到了古代的高度（Bottari-Ticozzi，前引书，第五卷，第 175 页）。为了证明他对威尼斯艺术家的影响，只需回想丁托列托的格言：“Il disegno di Michelangelo, e il colorito di Tiziano.”

    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Caro’s instructions to Taddeo Zuccaro for these paintings are given in full by Vasari (Lives, viii, p. 245). They are worth studying to see how far painters at this time were prepared to have everything dictated to them. The tone is set by Caro’s opening remarks: ‘It is not enough for them to be explained by word of mouth, because, besides the invention, we must look to the disposition of the figures, the attitudes, the colour, and a number of other considerations, all in accordance with the descriptions that I find of the subjects which seem to me suitable.’
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 卡罗给塔德奥·祖卡罗关于这些画作的指示由瓦萨里完整记载（《名人传》，卷八，第 245 页）。这些指示值得研究，以观察当时的画家在多大程度上愿意让一切被人指示。基调由卡罗的开场话语定下：“仅凭口头解释是不够的，因为除了构思之外，我们还必须考量人物的布局、姿态、色彩，以及许多其他事项，所有这些都应与我所找到的、我认为合适的题材描述相一致。”

  116. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} He describes it as scintilla della dirinità (Idea, bk. i, ch. 7). To emphasize this point he makes a characteristically Mannerist pun, deriving the word disegno as segno di Dio (di-segn-o).
    他把它形容为 scintilla della dirinità（Idea，卷一，第 7 章）。为了强调这一点，他做了一个典型的矫饰派双关，将 disegno 一词解释为 segno di Dio（di-segn-o）。
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} This has been noticed by E. Panofsky (cf. Idea, Ein Beitrag zur Begriffsgeschichte der älteren Kunsttheorie, Studien der Bibliothek Warburg, 1924, pp. 39 ff), who gives a full analysis of Zuccaro’s and Lomazzo’s views on the nature of beauty.
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 这一点已被 E. Panofsky 注意到（参见 Idea, Ein Beitrag zur Begriffsgeschichte der älteren Kunsttheorie，Studien der Bibliothek Warburg，1924 年，第 39 页及以下），他对 Zuccaro 和 Lomazzo 关于美的本质的观点做了全面分析。
    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Zuccaro used his theory of disegno as the basis for a series of decorations in his own house in Rome (cf. Körte, ‘Der Palazzo Zuccari in Rom’, Römische Forschungen der Biblioteca Hertziana, 1935, pp. 35 ff.). The central panel of the ceiling is reproduced on Plate 12.
    3 3 ^(3){ }^{3} Zuccaro 在他位于罗马的宅邸中以他的 disegno 理论为基础进行了一系列装饰（参见 Körte，《Der Palazzo Zuccari in Rom》，Römische Forschungen der Biblioteca Hertziana，1935 年，第 35 页及以下）。天花板中央的画框复制见版面 12。
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Zuccaro is at times inclined towards Neoplatonism, but only rarely. He gives Plato himself as the source for his theory of Ideas, though it is more exactly Neoplatonic (Idea, bk. i, ch. 5), and he talks of light in a Neoplatonic manner towards the end of the Idea (bk. ii, ch. 15).
    4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Zuccaro 有时倾向于新柏拉图主义，但很少。他把柏拉图本人作为其观念理论的来源，尽管更准确地说是新柏拉图式的（Idea，第 i 卷，第 5 章），并且在 Idea 的结尾处（第 ii 卷，第 15 章）以新柏拉图式的方式谈论光。
  117. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Tempio della Pittura, ch. 26. The greater part of this passage is a verbatim borrowing from Ficino (see Panofsky, Idea, Appendix I). In the Trattato Lomazzo constantly refers to Ficino or to earlier Neoplatonists like the Pseudo-Dionysius for ideas (e.g. in bk. iv, ch. 3).
    1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} Tempio della Pittura，第 26 章。本段大部分是从 Ficino 逐字借用（见 Panofsky，Idea，附录 I）。在 Trattato 中，Lomazzo 不断引用 Ficino 或早期的新柏拉图主义者如伪狄奥尼修斯作为观念来源（例如在第 iv 卷，第 3 章）。
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Cf. Panofsky, Idea, p. 56. As another example of the Mannerist love of darkness the studiolo of Francesco de’ Medici in the Palazzo Vecchio may be quoted. It is a small room, completely shut in, with no windows, so that it can only be lit up artificially.
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 参见 Panofsky，Idea，第 56 页。作为矫饰派（Mannerist）喜爱黑暗的另一个例子，可以引用 Palazzo Vecchio 中 Francesco de’ Medici 的 studiolo。那是一个小房间，完全封闭，没有窗户，因此只能靠人工照明。

  132. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} It is worth noticing that both Armenini and Federigo Zuccaro were in personal contact with Lodovico Carracci (cf. a letter from Zuccaro to Carracci, Bottari-Ticozzi, op. cit. viii, p. 516). But the two Mannerists were of an altogether older generation than Lodovico Carracci, and what influence there was must have gone from the theorists to the painter.
    1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 值得注意的是，Armenini 和 Federigo Zuccaro 都曾与 Lodovico Carracci 有私人接触（参见 Zuccaro 致 Carracci 的一封信，Bottari-Ticozzi，op. cit. viii，第 516 页）。但这两位矫饰派画家与 Lodovico Carracci 相差整整一代，人们所能察觉到的影响很可能是从理论家流向画家。
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} Niccolò dell’ Abbate’s eclecticism, as celebrated in the famous sonnet attributed to Agostino Carracci, may be rather a construction of the later artist than the conscious intention of the master himself.
    2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} 人们常以归于 Agostino Carracci 的那首著名十四行诗来颂扬 Niccolò dell’ Abbate 的折衷主义，但这更可能是后世艺术家的构建，而非该大师本人有意识的意图。
